News.title: Russell Brand's author wife Laura Gallacher - sister of TV star Kirsty - stood by her partner throughout his trial
News.content:
Russell Brand's wife appeared on the verge of collapse as the disgraced star was convicted of one rape and three sex assaults against four different women.

Laura Gallacher, 39, had to be held up by a security guard while leaving Court Three at Southwark Crown Court after a foreman delivered the jury's bombshell verdicts on Thursday afternoon. She had earlier looked tearful and as though she was struggling to breathe while a female pal held her hand while they waited for the verdicts to be delivered.

Ms Gallacher later turned her head and body towards a wall and held her hand over her mouth in shock after hearing her husband was being remanded in custody ahead of his sentencing this Monday. The verdicts eventually came after eight hours and 30 minutes of deliberations, after she had again bravely accompanied her husband to court.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



View 5 Images Russell Brand's wife Laura Gallacher is pictured outside the court (Image: James Manning/Press Association)

The children's author and illustrator had stood by her man day-after-day during his almost month-long trial, which included shocking and at times harrowing testimony from six different complainants.

She sat directly to Brand's right handside inside court throughout all the evidence so that the pair could constantly see each other through the dock's door, which was permanently left open throughout the trial until the verdict hearing when the pair could no longer see each other from their seats.

View 5 Images Brand was remanded in custody and will be sentenced on Monday (Image: Elizabeth Cook/Press Association)

‌



It was obvious Ms Gallacher, whose dad is golf legend Bernard Gallacher and older sister is broadcaster Kirsty Gallacher, was a constant support to Brand both inside and outside the courtroom. At times she made a point of waiting next to the door of the dock in order to greet her embattled husband as he walked out of the courtroom.

She was seen smiling widely towards him and appeared to offer words of encouragement after they both listened to some of the most bruising evidence. And she appeared to find comfort by holding her wedding ring and smiled towards members of her and Brand's entourage for signs of assurance.

Unlike her husband, who showed almost no emotion inside court, Ms Gallacher showed far more expression. At times she appeared frustrated while straining to hear the evidence.

View 5 Images Laura stood by her husband throughout the trial (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

‌



At other points she smiled while listening to what was being said, including when looking at other members of their entourage, including his lookalike manager and producer Jake Smith, security guard Joe McCann, personal assistant Sara Watson and podcaster pal David Fields.

On at least one occasion, Brand and Ms Gallacher were seen linking arms while walking in a corridor on the third floor of the court building. Brand was also seen putting a protective arm around his wife while waiting outside the courtroom doors, asking her: “You alright, darling?".

It was clear the during the trial that the pair were very much united, with even their outfit choices regularly appearing to be in sync. Ms Gallacher's valuable support continued outside the courtroom when the pair reportedly retired to rented accommodation in London's Waterloo area, as well as at weekends, when they returned to their rural home in Henley-on-Thames., Oxfordshire.

The couple first got together in 2006 before splitting up in 2007 before Brand wed US pop star Katy Perry. They got back together again in 2015 and got married in a ceremony near the picturesque Oxfordshire town in 2017. They now have three children together, all of primary school age, including their eldest child who the court heard celebrated their tenth birthday on Wednesday.

‌



View 5 Images Laura had to be supported after the verdict (Image: James Manning/Press Association)

Speaking on the couple's own ironically named podcast, Stay Free, during the trial, Ms Gallacher gave an insight into the couple's chauffeur-driven journeys to court in a black Mercedes people carrier each day, including on the approach road Battle Bridge Lane.

She also spoke about how the couple and their entourage found solace in reading psalms together during the journeys. She said: "As soon as I see the name of the street I get nervous, I think this is it now. On Battlebridge Road you don your armour, that's what I feel. That when i think you need to get into your shape get into your strength."

Ms Gallacher is 13 years her husband's junior, but he has previously told how he calls her "100 per cent the boss". He will need her to lead him and their family now more than ever.

News.title: Massive bomb hoax impact flights at Heathrow Airport and Birmingham Airport
News.content:
Massive bomb hoax impact flights at Heathrow Airport and Birmingham Airport

Mystery flight bomb hoaxers spread chaos across Europe in vicious campaign against passengers as police launch probe into who triggered the alarm and if it was state-sponsored

View 3 Images Finnair plane taking off from Fiumicino Airport after being diverted due to a bomb threat (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A massive wave of more than two dozen hoax bomb threats against flights swept through Europe on Thursday leading to emergency landings and planes being escorted by warplanes.

‌



‌



Both Heathrow and Birmingham airports received threats that were assessed as not credible, it is understood, as flights were diverted across Europe in reaction to bomb alerts.

‌



EasyJet said one of its flights from Newcastle and another from Glasgow were met by police on arrival in Prague as a "precautionary measure due to a security-related matter."

‌



A Ryanair flight from London Stansted heading for the Bulgarian capital, Sofia was diverted and landed safely in Plovdiv, Bulgaria, it is believed. One flight from Dublin to Rome was diverted to an airfield in northern France.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Finnair plane hit by bomb hoax on tarmac at Fiumicino Airport (Image: Alessandro Serranò/AGF/Shutterstock)

‌



Zelensky defies Trump with revenge hits as Russia steps up 'double-tap' attacks READ MORE :

Most of the impacted flights were diverted to other airports for emergency landings while others landed safely at their destinations.

A Heathrow spokesperson said: "Safety and security are our top priority. There are robust UK aviation security standards in place to assess and safely manage these types of situations.

‌



"Upon receiving the threat, a multi-agency response is initiated to assess the information and determine the response. The threat received today was deemed not credible and there was no risk to passengers, colleagues or the aircraft at Heathrow."

The alert, thought to be the biggest to hit Europe, followed another slew of similar threats during the previous week as police in multiple countries launched a hunt for the perpetrators.

‌



So far, no hazardous or suspicious materials have been found in any of the planes in what a British official called "malicious" hoaxes as an investigation continues.

The cost of re-routing of planes, emergency landings, the scrambling of military planes as escorts, plus the pan-Europe investigation may run into hundreds of millions of pounds

‌



It has sparked fears the warnings could have been launched by malicious actors or gangs linked to state sponsored plots on behalf of hostile states Iran or Russia.

View 3 Images Aer Lingus plane heading from Dublin to Rome, rerouted and escorted by military aircraft after a suspected bomb threat at Evreux-Fauville Air Base (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



But there were also reports from European officials that an anti-feminist group had claimed to have emailed a bomb threat.

Authorities in Rome said they received a bomb threat by email by a group claiming to be called “The Fighters of the Male State.” Britain's Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said flights across Europe have been hit by "malicious hoax threats."

‌



European Union Transport Commissioner Apostolos Tzitzikostas said in Dublin that it was "too early to draw conclusions on whether the reported incidents are linked." He added: "National investigations remain ongoing.”

Italian air force fighter jets escorted a Finnair flight that departed Helsinki bound for Rome after an email threat was received, the air force said in a statement.

Article continues below

Finnair said that two of its flights, including the one that received the military escort and landed safely in Rome, "faced unfounded hoax bomb scares."

Several flights across Europe received hoax bomb threats earlier this week, officials said. They included flights operated by Polish airline LOT, Scandinavian Airlines, Wizz Air and Ryanair. The hoax threats came after a plane headed for Bulgaria was diverted to Hungary after receiving a similar bomb threat while in the air.

News.title: Six killed and nine injured as massive fire rips through New York home
News.content:
Six killed and nine injured as massive fire rips through New York home

Huge flames ripped through a two storey home in Brooklyn, New York, with six people killed and a further nine injured, including firefighters and police.

View 4 Images Firefighters tackling the blaze in New York (Image: FDNY via AP)

Six people have been killed and nine injured including three firefighters and two police officers after a horror fire ripped through a New York home.

‌



‌



Emergency services rushed to the property in Sunset Park on 58th Street in Brooklyn, between 6th and 7th avenues, following reports of a fire shortly after 1.30am.

‌



The fire department has told of finding the house engulfed in flames with 200 personnel tackling the blaze which left six dead and a further nine injured.

‌



A cause has not been determined yet.

View 4 Images Two hundred firefighters tackled the blaze in the early hours of this morning (Image: FDNY via AP)

“Upon arrival, we had fire on every floor,” Kevin Woods, the department’s chief of fire operations, said at a news conference near the severely charred wood home. “Fire blowing out every window, meeting us at the front door.”

‌



Footage showed huge flames coming from a second-storey window while glass could be heard breaking. Residents nearby were kept away from their properties due to the thick black smoke and the threat of the fire spreading.

At one point a person could be seen being given CPR on a stretcher outside the building. Firefighters rescued four people, getting through a rear entrance in the two-unit home to get to two people who were trapped behind window bars, said Woods.

‌



View 4 Images Six people were killed and nine others injured in the fire (Image: @FD4D via AP)

The fire, which also damaged an adjoining home, was brought under control in about three hours. Eight neighbours were evacuated and were taken to hotels.

‌



“This was a devastating fire,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani said at the news conference. “It will take a long time for this neighbourhood to mourn the neighbours they lost this morning and to recover from this immense grief.”

The nine people who were injured were expected to survive, including the three firefighters and two police officers who had minor injuries, the department said. No names have been released.

‌



View 4 Images Fire crew and police officers were among the injured (Image: AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)

Fire marshals were investigating. A lithium-ion battery was found at the scene, but it was unknown whether it was related to the cause of the fire, the department said.

Article continues below

The home was built in 1915, according to city property records. Last week, an e-bike battery fire killed a boy in the Bronx. It is among more than 400 fires in the city that have been linked to lithium-ion batteries this year, leading to at least six deaths and more than 70 injuries, according to fire officials.

News.title: E-bikes clampdown hailed as clunky hire cycles make pavements 'impassable'
News.content:
E-bikes clampdown hailed as clunky hire cycles make pavements 'impassable'

Newly-announced plans to tackle the scourge of E-bikes cluttering pavements and clamp down on cyclists jumping red lights have been hailed by riders, pedestrians and campaigners

E-bikes clampdown hailed as clunky hire cycles make pavements 'impassable'

Plans to bring in new rules on hired E-bikes have been welcomed after years of clunky cycles clogging up pavements across the UK.

‌



The Department for Transport launched a consultation on Thursday which could see cyclists fined for riding drunk or cycling on pavements.

Firms which run the schemes would also be subject to penalties if they fail to stop riders blocking footpaths.

‌



Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "This is a small but important everyday fix to make our streets safer."

On one busy street near the London Eye, the Mirror found dozens of E-bikes from a range of different hire companies lining both sides of the road.

Several of them were left directly in the middle of the pavement, which combined with scaffolding from a nearby building created a difficult, narrow channel that pedestrians struggled to pass through.

‌



View 4 Images Mirror reporter Benedict Tetzlaff Deas went E-bike spotting (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Ed, who did not want to give his surname, was parking a rented E-bike in one of the designated bays. The 31-year-old Londoner said he liked to use them on occasions where he'd left his motorcycle at home, as they were easy to use and preferable to taking the "crowded" Underground.

‌



But he admitted he'd seen plenty of examples of bad behaviour by fellow cyclists - and said more oversight of the sector would be welcomed.

He said: "It's crazy. It really is an arms race between the E-bike companies, you see hundreds of them in one space.

‌



"I don't really know if all of them are really being used. You see plenty of people on Lime bikes, but you can go down any street in Central London and it's like 40 or 50 parked on any one street, it's crazy."

"And of course you shouldn't be riding around drunk - though I see plenty of people getting on bikes after a few pints. So yeah, I think it's probably a good thing."

‌



View 4 Images Ed, 31, is an E-bike user - but spoke in support of closer regulation (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Ann Leo, 72, from Orpington, said she believed the capital was still struggling to catch up with the E-bike boom.

‌



She explained: "This many people using bikes is relatively new. I spent of my time growing up in Belgium - people there go at a sedate pace, they use it just to get from A to B, and kids go to school and grow up with it. They learn the etiquette and the safety, but here it's all happening quite quickly.

"It's dangerous. I saw two locally yesterday, when was quite windy, and they'd fallen over across the pavement. I thought, 'well, this is everywhere now' - I get it, but it's an accident waiting to happen. That, and the fact that people don't wear helmets."

‌



View 4 Images Ann Leo, 72, said fallen and badly parked E-bikes are 'dangerous' (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Nurse Victoria Cleary was visiting London to see Witness for the Prosecution at the old County Hall building with her friend Jean - and said E-bikes were a big problem in her home city of Liverpool too.

‌



She said: "It's just as bad - and scooters are the worst.

"In my area, they're just left on pavements, not even anywhere near a parking space."

‌



View 4 Images Nurse Victoria Cleary, from Liverpool, said that the problem was 'just as bad' in her home city (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Campaigners warn that disabled people and parents with prams suffer most from the growing amount of 'street clutter' in recent years, such as E-bikes, scooters and delivery robots.

‌



Tanya Braun, Director of External Affairs at Living Streets, said: "Our pavements are for people and should be safe and accessible for everyone to use.

"Discarded e-bikes obstruct our pavements, which is dangerous for everyone but especially for wheelchair users, those who are blind or partially sighted or families with young children.

"This can prevent people from enjoying the many health and social benefits of walking and wheeling."

News.title: Cocaine deaths overtake heroin for the first time, government figures show
News.content:
Cocaine deaths overtake heroin for the first time, government figures show

Some 5,519 drug poisoning deaths were registered in England and Wales last year - and 1,233 of these were linked to cocaine

View 3 Images Deaths linked to cocaine have overtaken heroin for the first time (Image: Getty Images)

Cocaine deaths have quadrupled in a decade - overtaking heroin for the first time, government figures show.

‌



‌



The substance claimed 1,233 lives last year - 1.9% more than heroin, which killed 1,210. Some 5,519 drug poisoning deaths were registered in England and Wales overall, up 55% on a decade ago and the equivalent of 92.4 fatalities per a million people.

‌



Robin Pollard, of drug and alcohol support charity WithYou, warned cocaine has become cheaper, purer, and far easier to get hold of. He said: “Across almost all areas where WithYou deliver services, we hear that cocaine has become far more prevalent. Whereas before 2020, we typically would have seen the price of a gram of cocaine being around £100, it is much more common to hear it being available for £60 a gram or less now, and available to buy in ever smaller amounts.

‌



View 3 Images Cocaine claimed 1,233 lives in 2025

“It has also become easier to purchase in all parts of the country, has become increasingly socially acceptable, and of higher purity. We also know that cocaine use tends to be associated more with men, but they can be more hesitant to access support for their drug use.

"There is often a perception that there is no treatment for cocaine use, but there are many support options available, and anyone who is worried about their drug use, or that of someone close to them, we are here to help."

‌



Forty-somethings were hit the hardest, with 147 registered deaths per million, while youngsters in their 20s faced 46 deaths per million. Broader opioids – including heroin and methadone – remained the deadliest overall substance group, mentioned on 2,324 death certificates. Men accounted for the vast majority of fatalities, dying at more than double the rate of women.

Drug poisoning mortality rates remain highest in the North East, with 135 deaths per a million people registered in 2025. London recorded the lowest rate nationwide at 58.3 per million.

‌



The south west saw a jump of 6.3% to 96.5 deaths per million, and rates in the South East hiked by 13.4%. Middlesbrough, north Yorks, suffered the worst casualty rate in the country, recording 118 drug poisoning deaths between 2023 and 2025, including 27 in 2025 alone.

View 3 Images Drug poisoning mortality rates remain highest in the North East (Image: PA)

Article continues below

Zaheen Ahmed of national addiction treatment provider The UKAT Group said: “This is a stark reminder that the UK's drug crisis is far from over, and that where you live can determine the level of support available to you.

"The Government must look beyond the national headlines and act on the worsening picture in areas like this. A marginal national improvement means nothing to the communities still losing lives at an alarming rate. Every figure is a life lost and a devastated family, and we must never forget that.”

News.title: What now for Trump's kingdom? The cracks in the 'Trump cartel' are showing as his VP and son turn
News.content:
What now for Trump's kingdom? The cracks in the 'Trump cartel' are showing as his VP and son turn

Donald Trump and his cronies once appeared to be an unstoppable in the American right-wing, but the massive midterm humiliation has led to some key allies starting to turn their back on the President

View 9 Images JD Vance publicly distanced himself from Donald Trump following the midterm wipeout (Image: Shutterstock)

Donald Trump's once blindly loyal inner circle appears to be falling apart after he was dealt a humiliating blow at the US midterms elections this week.

‌



‌



The finger pointing has already begun as senior figures within the Republican party look to find someone to blame for the party's massive losses. Trump has attempted to pin the blame the losing candidates, despite spending weeks telling people to vote as if his name was on the top of the ballot paper.

‌



The Trump kingdom that has ruled Washington and right-wing US politics for years appears to be crumbling, as a new bombshell report suggests the President's close allies expressed their frustrations over his war and controversial ballroom.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 9 Images The pressure is now on Trump following the huge midterms blow (Image: Getty Images)

Vance sensationally turns on Trump's war as VP fights for his political future READ MORE :

US midterms 2026 live: Donald Trump starts MAGA blame game with Hegseth facing axe READ MORE :

Trump once appeared to be an unstoppable force on the right-wing as he hijacked the Republican party with his MAGA movement, family and gang of loyal cronies.

‌



In the wake of the embarrassing loss, which led to the Democrats gaining control of both the Senate and House of Representatives, Vice President JD Vance publicly broke from Trump's defence of the Iran war and even the President's own son agreed.

A report, from the New York Times, has claimed members of Trump's inner circle grew frustrated at the President for allegedly refused to sign off on fundraising money until August. It claimed Trump called the funds "my money".

‌



House Democrat leader Hakeem Jefferies branded the administration "the Trump Cartel" and said anyone "stealing from the American people" can "no longer hide", adding: "We are going to hold the crooks accountable."

The Trump dynasty is showing cracks, but could this be the beginning of the end?

‌



JD Vance

Trump's vice president was noticeably quiet on the campaign trail in the run up to these midterms, not making as many public appearances or headlines as he had in the past.

View 9 Images JD Vance threw Trump under the bus in a post following the election results (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



JD Vance publicly criticised Trump's war in Iran, attempting to distance himself from a clear rebuke of the president by voters. In a lengthy social media post after the results, he wrote: "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so."

Vance, in his post, said Republican voters cast their ballots for Democrats due to the war, the cost of living, America not being prioritised and the US relationship with Israel. The VP, unlike Trump, declined to endorse Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for re-election.

‌



This comes as Vance is widely expected to run to be the Republican candidate for the presidential election in 2028.

Don Jr.

Even more surprising than Vance's social media rant was Donald Trump's own son, who agreed with the VP that the Iran war was behind the Repubicans' shocking losses. The US President's family members have played a big part in both of his presidential terms.

‌



View 9 Images Donald Trump Jr.'s response to JD Vance (Image: @DonaldJTrumpJr/X)

Don Jr. threw his dad under the bus by reposting Vance's rant and wrote: "Every word of this is 100." While Don Jr. has never held a role in an elected public office, he was an executive vice president in the families real-estate company, the Trump Organization, and was a key figure in his father's election campaigns.

‌



Pete Hegseth

Trump's loud and brash Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth could reportedly be Trump's fall guy after the embarrassing election results. The army veteran and TV personality, who changed his title to Secretary of War, has backed Trump in his controversial military actions - including the Iran war and bombing alleged drug boats in international waters.

Reports have suggested Hegseth is on the chopping block as Trump looks to blame someone for the election humiliation. A Republican source close to the White House, speaking to CNN, said: "If the president is serious about anyone taking responsibility for it, it's Pete Hegseth."

‌



Trump however yesterday defended his war in Iran saying, "If I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again," with insiders adding Trump personally likes Hegseth but could find himself with nowhere else to look as some Republicans turn on Hegseth and the war.

View 9 Images Pete Hegseth could reportedly be Donald Trump's fall guy (Image: Samuel Corum - Pool via CNP/Shutterstock)

‌



Elon Musk

Musk had a brief stint as Trump's face behind the DOGE initiative to cut federal spending, which saved little and caused chaos, but the billionaire has played his role in the MAGA movement.

The Tesla boss pumped nearly $500million of his own money in these midterms, breaking an individual spending record, but saw little for his investment. $45million went to support Republican Ken Paxton for a Senate seat but he was beaten by Democrat James Talarico, in the historically red state.

‌



View 9 Images Elon Musk's relationship with Trump could cost him and his businesses lots of money (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

On Tuesday night Musk joked that his "election-interfering space lasers didn't work" but the tech mogul could face serious issues with his own companies.

‌



Musk's SpaceX has been awarded around $10bn in government contracts since the start of Trump's second term and this could be at risk with a Democratic-controlled Congress. Also, businesses owned by Musk struggled on the stock markets after the midterms, as investors worry he could be among possible targets for investigations by Congress.

Family

The Trump terms have been a family affair with not only Don Jr being involved politically but also son-in-law Jared Kushner, as US Special Envoy for Peace, and even wife Melania Trump brokering a ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia for the front-line city of Oleshky.

‌



View 9 Images Donald Trump's kids and wife Melania (Image: AP)

The House Democrats oversight committee, which can launch investigations, posted an apparent warning to the Trump's which said: "Good morning to everyone except: —The Trump Crime Family." Rep. Robert Garcia, who will lead the powerful House Oversight Committee, issued a cryptic two word statement: "Lawyer Up."

‌



It has been reported that House and Senate Dems are planning to probe the Trump family's crypto venture, Don Jr's close ties to a Russia oligarch who paid for part of his wedding and property deals by the Trump Organization, according to the New York Times.

View 9 Images A House Democrats oversight committee post (Image: @OversightDems/X)

‌



Old Trump allies turned foes

This is not the first time hardcore Trump allies have turned on the US President. Former-Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene was a key MAGA movement member but broke with Trump last year.

She has now become an outspoken opponent of the President, on the handling of the Epstein Files and the Iran war. She yesterday posted: "This election is a referendum on Donald Trump and the Republican Party’s complete and total failure."

Article continues below

View 9 Images Marjorie Taylor Greene had a huge fallout with Trump last year (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

American conservative news anchor Tucker Carlson was once key in pushing Trump and MAGA messages out but has turned on Trump over Iran and Middle East policy. Last month, speaking to NPR, Carlson said Trump should be removed from office.

News.title: Henry Nowak killer Vickrum Digwa has sentence increased after claiming it was 'excessive'
News.content:
Henry Nowak killer Vickrum Digwa has sentence increased after claiming it was 'excessive'

Vickrum Digwa, 23, who murdered 18-year-old student Henry Nowak in Southampton last year, had been challenging the length of his sentence at the Court of Appeal

View 3 Images Vickrum Digwa was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years in June (Image: Hampshire Police/Solent News)

Vickrum Digwa's bid to reduce the minimum term of his life sentence for murdering Henry Nowak has failed.

However, a challenge by the Attorney General to increase his sentence was successful, with his minimum term raised from 21 to 25 years.

Digwa, 23, was jailed in June after fatally stabbing the 18-year-old in Southampton on December 3 last year with a 21cm ceremonial knife.

In their ruling on Thursday, three senior judges said it was "unarguable" that Digwa's original sentence was too long. They found the minimum term should be increased as it "fell outside the range reasonably open" to the sentencing judge.

Lady Chief Justice Baroness Carr said: "A minimum term of 21 years did not adequately reflect the overall seriousness of the murder. It was not only lenient, but unduly so."

Digwa falsely accused Henry of racially abusing him, leading police to handcuff the student as he lay dying from his injuries. There was widespread anger following the release of police body-worn footage showing Henry, from Chafford Hundred, Essex, being placed in handcuffs.

Baroness Carr, sitting with Mr Justice Nicklin and Mr Justice Wall at the Royal Courts of Justice in London, heard Digwa's barrister argue that the length of his sentence was "manifestly excessive", alongside Attorney General Ellie Reeves's argument that it was "unduly lenient".

View 3 Images Henry Nowak was killed in Southampton on December 3, 2025 (Image: Family/Solent News)

Security guard killed by plane propeller seconds after stepping off flight in Somalia READ MORE :

In written submissions on behalf of the Attorney General, Jonathan Polnay KC said Digwa "abused the privilege" afforded to Sikhs to carry a knife in a public place for religious reasons.

He said: "The offender was carrying a substantial bladed weapon in public, immediately available for use, which he repeatedly deployed against an unarmed and defenceless stranger. He abused a statutory religious exemption permitting him to carry that weapon."

Mr Polnay continued: "There were significant additional aggravating factors: the offender’s sustained attempts to pervert the course of justice, his false allegation of racism against the deceased, his procurement of his mother’s assistance in concealing evidence, his degradation of the dying victim by filming him, and his conduct in misleading responders."

He added that the minimum term imposed failed to "reflect the combined weight of those features".

Digwa watched proceedings via video link from HMP Frankland in County Durham, wearing a dark suit, shirt and tie.

He appeared to show no reaction as his minimum term was increased. Members of Henry's family attended the hearing at the Royal Courts of Justice in London, with one relative wiping away tears as the judgment was delivered.

Speaking to ITV before the hearing, Henry's stepmum, Katie Nowak, said: "It’s another process that we’ve got to go through. It’s another fight that we have to have. It was a very clear verdict. It’s not right that he’s allowed to do this."

View 3 Images Katie Nowak said Digwa being allowed to challenge his sentence 'doesn’t feel fair to us at all' (Image: Yui Mok/PA Wire)

‌



Digwa's use of dagger was ' analogous to an abuse of trust'

At Digwa's sentencing hearing at Southampton Crown Court, Judge William Mousley KC said he had been carrying two knives on the night of the murder.

One was a small knife hidden from view, known as a kirpan, which Sikhs are required to carry at all times. The other was a "large dagger in a sheath", which he carried because of his membership of the Nihang order of Sikhs, who have a tradition of having a second knife.

‌



Mr Polnay told the court on Thursday that the bid to increase the sentence "is not about the lawful possession of a kirpan" or the laws allowing Sikhs to carry blades, but "about what followed". He said that Digwa’s use of the dagger was "on at least one level, analogous to an abuse of trust".

He continued: "When a person who has the benefit of that accommodation uses the article protected by law for repeated lethal violence, that is an aggravating factor of particular weight."

‌



Imran Khan KC, for Digwa, said the sentence could only be increased in "exceptional, rather than borderline cases, and directed to gross error by the sentencing judge". He added: "Where is the gross error?"

He acknowledged the law allowing Digwa to carry the knife "plainly did not" allow him to use it to murder Mr Nowak, but also said Judge Mousley had "already expressly aggravated [the sentence] for both the dangerous weapon and the abuse of religious privilege", as well as other factors.

‌



He said: "There must be vigilance for using the same underlying facts repeatedly."

Mr Khan also said carrying a knife for religious reasons "should not of itself" cause Sikh offenders to be given longer sentences.

‌



Challenging the length of the sentence, Mr Khan said while Digwa's lies to first responders "unquestionably affected the dignity with which Mr Nowak was treated", his wounds were unsurvivable.

"The false account therefore did not worsen the fatal injury or deprive Mr Nowak of the prospect of survival," he said.

Article continues below

Digwa is also separately seeking to overturn his conviction, but a decision has yet to be made on whether that challenge will be allowed to proceed.

News.title: Jesus de Miguel's teammates carry his coffin at funeral of tragic Tenerife footballer
News.content:
The funeral of Jesus de Miguel has taken place, with his Tenerife teammates carrying his coffin at an emotional ceremony on Thursday.

De Miguel passed away at the age of 30 in hospital on Tuesday morning after colliding with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off, in a Spanish Segunda clash on Monday night.

The Tenerife striker suffered head and chest injuries, with a preliminary autopsy report revealing he died of "accidental chest trauma". The football world has been plunged into mourning, with tributes paid around this week's Champions League matches, while thousands of fans gathered at Tenerife's stadium to pay their respects.

De Miguel is survived by his girlfriend Maria and their one-year-old daughter Carla. They were joined at the funeral in Navahermosa, Toledo by De Miguel's teammates, as well as a whole host of club staff and other mourners.

‌



Jesus de Miguel's cause of death revealed after fatal collision with goalkeeper READ MORE :

The Tenerife players wore black suits and ties and carried his coffin into the ceremony. Manuel Hernandez, De Miguel's agent and a spokesperson on behalf of the family, then read a statement to reporters.

"In these difficult times for us, we want to sincerely thank everyone for the kind words and expressions of affection we are receiving," he said.

"We don't have enough words to thank you for every message, every call, and every gesture of affection that we are receiving. Thank you to everyone who has remembered him, to his team-mates, friends, fans and all the clubs who have wanted to convey their condolences and accompany us in this painful moment.

View 4 Images The funeral took place on Thursday in Navahermosa, in Toledo province, Spain (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Feeling such love for Jesus and witnessing the impact he has had on so many people is something we will always carry with us. Therefore, we respectfully request that our privacy and that of all those accompanying us at this time be protected.

"We need to grieve in the peace and quiet that this situation requires. We understand the affection, concern, and support that her loss is generating, and we are deeply grateful.

View 4 Images Tenerife players and club staff attended the funeral (Image: Europa Press via Getty Images)

"Jesus leaves a void impossible to fill, but also an immense memory in all of us who have been lucky enough to share our lives with him. Thank you for loving him, for remembering him, and for being with us. His family."

‌



According to a neighbour of the De Miguel family in Navahermosa, a village in Toledo, his father had been watching the match against FC Andorra in a bar on Monday night. He immediately started crying after the collision with Owono and gathered his family to fly to Tenerife to be with him immediately.

Tragically, De Miguel's friend Fernando Roman told Spanish outlet Vamos a Ver that they had been planning a family trip before tragedy struck.

"We have to send our love to his family, to Maria, to his daughter Carla, who is a year and a few months old," he said. "It was unbelievable because we were talking about traveling to Disney with the girls, with my daughter too, and look what's happened."

‌



Andorra goalkeeper Owono was forced to disable his social media accounts after receiving abuse in the wake of the incident. The 25-year-old released a statement on Wednesday.

"These are the most difficult days of my life," he said. "I struggle to find the words, and it is very hard for me to come to terms with what has happened. I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him.

"I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are all experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus."

News.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault
News.content:
Russell Brand has been convicted of rape and sexual assault, and is now expected to face a substantial prison sentence.

A jury found the entertainer guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, following a four-week trial at Southwark Crown Court in London.

He was found not guilty of two other counts of rape, and one count of attempted indecent assault. The jury deliberated for eight-and-a-half hours.

Brand was taken into custody after the verdicts were delivered, and was refused bail. He is due to be sentenced on Monday.

It can now be reported that Brand is also facing further rape allegations made by two women and the 51-year-old has already been questioned by officers in relation to the complaints. The Metropolitan Police said its investigation "remains ongoing".

During the trial, Brand faced allegations from six women spanning the decade between 1999 and 2009, when he rose to fame as one of Britain's most high-profile entertainers.

The women came to court to reveal how Brand used his immense fame to force them into sexual activity.

Brand, who told his wife Laura Gallacher "I love you" after entering the dock, displayed no emotion as the jury delivered its verdicts.

Afterwards he mouthed "I'm good, I'm good" to his defence counsel as he left the dock. His walk was steadily paced, and he continued to show little emotion.

The judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, told Brand to expect "a significant custodial term" after the verdicts were delivered.

News.title: Watch: Met Police release Brand interview footage
News.content:
Comedian and actor Russell Brand has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

Brand has been remanded in custody and will be sentenced on Monday.

Video released by the Metropolitan Police shows Brand being interviewed by officers in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

More on this story.

News.title: Henry Nowak’s killer has minimum term increased to 25 years by Court of Appeal
News.content:
A man jailed for life for murdering Henry Nowak has had his minimum prison term increased to 25 years by the Court of Appeal.

Vickrum Digwa was serving a minimum of 21 years for stabbing 18-year-old student Nowak with a large dagger in Belmont Road, Southampton, on 3 December 2025.

The Attorney General referred the case to the Court of Appeal on the grounds it was "unduly lenient", while Digwa also challenged his jail term as "manifestly excessive".

The Lady Chief Justice quashed the sentence, ruling the original term "did not adequately reflect the overall seriousness of the murder".

Digwa, who was also refused permission to appeal, told police Henry had attacked and racially abused him, which led to Henry, from Chafford Hundred in Essex, being handcuffed as he lay dying.

The trial judge later found Digwa's accusations of racism to be a lie. Then 22, he was jailed for life at Southampton Crown Court in June.

News.title: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years
News.content:
Interest rates have risen for the first time in more than three years and the Bank of England has signalled a further increase is likely unless the US-Iran war is resolved.

Rates rose to 4% from 3.75% in a bid to curb inflation mainly driven by the conflict's impact on global oil prices.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank's governor, said the decision "shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes", but warned "unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase".

The higher level will increase the cost of borrowing for things such as mortgages, loans and credit cards, but will also lead to higher returns on savings.

The Bank's rate-setting committee all backed increasing interest rates, with eight out of nine voting in favour of the rise to 4%. One member wanted an even bigger increase to 4.25%.

Bailey said the hike was warranted due to higher energy prices and pointed to what happens in the Middle East as the main factor in future decisions.

"Put simply, it requires real progress towards settling the conflict in the Middle East," the governor said.

Bailey said he could "see the argument" for a further rate hike, before taking a "more conditional approach" dependent on the path of energy prices and inflation in the coming months.

However, the views of members on the rate-setting committee differed on the path forward.

Clare Lombardelli agreed there was "likely to be a case for a further increase in rates in the near term", while Megan Greene went further, suggesting "additional hikes" might be likely depending on how inflation impacted wages, prices and the jobs market.

However, Alan Taylor said the rate rise was a "a risk-management 'one-for-now' insurance hike".

News.title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo arrives in UK for treatment
News.content:
A British man who tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been flown back to the UK.

The man, who is a health worker and has not been identified, landed at RAF Northolt before being transported to a specialist infectious diseases unit at the Royal Free Hospital in north London.

It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths.

Speaking earlier this week, a UK government spokesperson said there were "well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and that the risk to the public remains low.

News.title: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
News.content:
The US first lady said she had "reviewed demining plans, aerial images, assessed roadways, and discussed evacuation routes, hospital access, vehicles, and medical resources" during the truce.

"Last week in Oleshky and neighbouring areas of Kherson, people experienced the simple joys of life for the first time since 2022," Trump said. "They walked down familiar streets without fear of explosions."

She thanked both Volodymyr Zelensky and Vladimir Putin, making no reference to the origins of the war, which began when the Russian president launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and which has caused thousands of civilian casualties and the displacement of millions.

Dmitriev, a businessman and Kremlin special envoy who has previously represented Moscow during peace talks with Ukraine, thanked Trump for "saving and touching so many lives".

"Let us continue making a humanitarian contribution together; this is within our power," Dmitriev said, before gifting Melania Trump a framed drawing by an 11-year-old Oleshky evacuee.

He also praised Trump for her work on reuniting children separated from their families by the war. These include children allegedly abducted by Russia.

Arakhamia, a Ukrainian MP who heads Zelensky's party in parliament who has also been part of the Ukrainian negotiating team, said the Oleshky ceasefire had constituted the "biggest de-escalation since 2022".

"We are creating a momentum where both sides are learning theâ¦ mechanics of how to actually keep the peace when the peace comes," he added.

He acknowledged that the "political track" of negotiations to end the conflict was "complex" but said Ukrainians were asking Melania Trump "to keep going and find new missions and de-escalate more."

At the end of the event, Trump handed Dmitriev and Arakhamia two letters to be hand-delivered to their respective presidents.

The White House later said Melania Trump had invited her guests to view two historic artifacts which she had "personally selected as powerful symbols of peace".

One was an 18th Century medicine chest which was removed from the White House when the British set it on fire in 1812. "Once adversaries, the United States and Great Britain ultimately established a strong alliance," the White House said.

The second artifact was a cup gifted in 1899 to the French ambassador in recognition of his efforts to bring the Spanish-American war to an end.

Melania Trump has generally remained discreet on foreign policy matters, and neither Moscow nor Kyiv have elaborated on the nature or extent of her involvement in coordinating the delicate ceasefire - the most enduring and widespread of the war so far.

A source who works in the local government of the Kherson region told the BBC that work on the Oleshky evacuation had been ongoing for almost a year.

News.title: Married at First Sight UK cancelled after BBC revealed rape allegations
News.content:
Married at First Sight UK will not return, Channel 4 has said, following a BBC investigation into the hit reality TV show.

The Channel 4 show was plunged into crisis earlier this year, after Panorama revealed rape allegations from two female cast members on the show, while a third woman alleged a non-consensual sex act. The men involved have denied all the allegations against them.

A review was commissioned by Channel 4 shortly after the BBC first contacted the broadcaster, with details of the allegations we had heard.

On Thursday, the completed review recommended extra safeguards on the show. But Channel 4 said the programme had "run its course" and apologised to the women involved in the investigation.

The broadcaster's chief executive Priya Dogra said she was "very sorry for the distress those women have clearly felt", adding that the show's budget would be reinvested in "distinctive new programming".

The Panorama investigation in May, in which three women made allegations about the men they were partnered with - claims the men deny, made the following allegations:

One woman said her onscreen husband raped her and threatened her with an acid attack.

A second woman told both Channel 4 and CPL, before broadcast, about being allegedly raped by her onscreen husband. Her episodes were still aired.

A third woman - Shona Manderson, the only woman who was identified - accused her onscreen husband of sexual misconduct.

All three women accused the show of not doing enough to protect them.

Lawyers for CPL, the independent production company that makes the UK version of the show, previously said its welfare system is "gold standard" and industry-leading, and that it acted appropriately in all these cases.

Channel 4 had initially told Panorama that all the allegations were "wholly uncorroborated".

Dame Caroline Dinenage MP, chair of the House of Commons culture and media committee, said the decision to axe the show "makes sense" given the review's findings and the "seriousness of the allegations".

"Reality TV contestants have often been treated as a commodity, with duty of care a slogan rather than a genuine principle. Everyone involved in producing and regulating reality TV must now learn and act," she added.

A spokesman for Ofcom said the broadcast regulator would "carefully consider the reports published today as we move to strengthen our guidance for broadcasters".

"We are clear that broadcasters have a duty of care towards members of the public who participate in their programmes."

News.title: A bitter end for Ronaldo - the icon who transformed Portugal announces international retirement
News.content:
When a young Ronaldo first joined the squad, he arrived at camp with his baseball cap on backwards, enormous sunglasses and headphones turned up so loud they could be heard from a distance.

He would not take the cap off to eat among veterans like Luis Figo and Rui Costa. Luiz Felipe Scolari saw an extraordinary player who was immature and obsessed with showing off. He reprimanded him in public, then told him privately that if he changed his attitude, he would one day captain Portugal.

The first great disappointment came early, and it came at home. At 19, Ronaldo played in the final of Euro 2004 at the Estadio da Luz in Lisbon, in front of a country that had convinced itself the trophy was already on its way.

A single headed goal by Angelos Charisteas was enough for unfancied Greece to win it by surprise. When the final whistle went, Ronaldo could not hold back the tears, and the image of the teenager crying on his own pitch travelled everywhere.

It was a painful way to learn what a final costs, and it left him with a hunger that never really went away.

Figo owned the number 7 at the time, so Ronaldo had to have 17. Figo helped him settle but had no intention of making it easy. When he left the national team in 2006, the shirt and the team became Ronaldo's.

In September 2005, before a qualifier in Russia, Scolari and Figo went to his room to tell him his father had died. Scolari offered to send him home. Ronaldo chose to play, asked his team-mates to behave as normal, and spent time in the dressing room doing ball tricks.

That was his way to cope with the expected but still hugely hurtful passing of his alcoholic dad. He later called Scolari "father". That way the national team had become the place that held him together.

Things went sour with Carlos Queiroz. After the 2010 World Cup exit against Spain, asked to explain a poor performance, Ronaldo told journalists to ask the coach. His influence in the camp had grown so large it changed routines and habits, which explains why the coach felt undermined.

The sociologist Joao Nuno Coelho offers the best lens on how Portugal sees him. In his analysis, the national team became a representation of Portuguese identity and of the country's need to be seen internationally.

In years of economic hardship and a crisis of confidence, a team that won admiration abroad was important beyond football.

Ronaldo stood at the centre of that need and created contradictory feelings. Some Portuguese questioned his individualism and his ego, and not everyone saw themselves in his personality.

Coelho explains criticising him became more difficult as time went by. The country wanted to be proud of him and sometimes felt uneasy at the same time.

The former international Jorge Andrade told me some supporters preferred figures like Figo, Eusebio, Paulo Futre or Rui Costa. Even so, Portugal was proud to have him. And with the titles, the doubts eased.

News.title: Farage says he is worried Trump will step up Iran war after midterm 'disaster'
News.content:
Nigel Farage has said he fears Donald Trump will "aggressively" continue his war with Iran after his "disaster" in the US midterm elections.

The Reform UK leader said the US president was still a friend, but accused him of having "broke a promise" to the American electorate by launching the war.

The war in Iran, which the US began in February 2026, weighed heavily in the midterm election results earlier this week in which the Democrats swept Trump's Republicans out of power in Congress.

Farage, who had initially urged people to support the war, said that following the election results he worried Trump would respond with more strikes on Iran.

Asked how he thinks President Trump will respond, Farage told broadcasters on Thursday: "I suppose I worry that the president will continue aggressively attacking Iran.

"That worries me because that would have even more serious implications for the price of oil, for inflation, for the whole western world".

He acknowledged he had initially supported the war but stressed he "never supported endless war".

Asked if the war was a mistake, he said: "There's no question about it."

The US president had "always kept his promises," added Farage, but "in this case, he said no more foreign wars and here we are in month eight of a war with no sign of ending."

"That and the resulting fuel prices are what in the end has done the damage."

Trump said on Tuesday that the poor results for Republican congressional candidates were partly due to the war and the related surge in oil prices.

But he insisted he did not regret launching a joint attack with Israel on Iran.

News.title: Pound rises to its highest level since the Brexit referendum
News.content:
The pound has risen to its highest overall level since the Brexit referendum over a decade ago.

Sterling has risen notably in recent weeks against the euro and the dollar, ahead of an expected rise in interest rates.

The most-watched measure of the value of the British currency against a basket of 18 of the world's main currencies this week reached its joint highest level since the June 2016 referendum, according to Bank of England figures.

The value reached 86.4 on an index where 100 equals the value in 2005. The Bank will officially confirm the calculation on Thursday.

News.title: New £200m fleet of publicly funded trains in Wales barely used after three years
News.content:
A new fleet of publicly funded trains that cost more than Â£200m still remain mostly unused more than three years after the first one was delivered.

They were initially promised to be fully up and running by 2022 but Transport for Wales' (TfW) boss has said he expects all of the tram-trains will be in full service by the end of 2027.

Data obtained by the BBC reveals that less than half of the 36 fleet - what TfW call the "final piece" in their Â£2bn South Wales Metro project - have passed rigorous statutory testing.

TfW chief executive James Price said he wants trains that work "100% well, 100% of the time" before putting them into full service.

News.title: 'Flawed' training contributed to officer's death
News.content:
An Army officer's accidental death during a training exercise was contributed to by "flawed" training and a faulty alarm system, a coroner has concluded.

Second Lt Max George, 26, died on Salisbury Plain after struggling with a piece of "snagged" kit as he left a Warrior armoured vehicle, which then reversed into him, an inquest into his death heard.

Victoria Neale, who represented George's family, said the inquest provided his loved ones with "important answers" and provided a "degree of accountability".

The Ministry of Defence (MOD) vowed to respond to points raised during the inquest and said it had already made several safety improvements.

The inquest heard that George, from Durham, was stood by the open rear door of the Warrior on 21 June 2022 when the exercise commander gave the order to reverse the armoured vehicle.

The 26-year-old died at the scene near Everleigh from multiple traumatic injuries, Wiltshire and Swindon Coroner's Court was told.

Recording a narrative conclusion, Coroner Ian Singleton said the training of the student commander who gave the command had been flawed.

Brigadier Giles Malec, head of the Army Safety Group, said the service recognised "the seriousness of the failures which led to Max's tragic death" and would "look to rectify any additional failures identified". He apologised to the family on the second day of the inquest.

Warrior vehicles are no longer allowed to reverse with the rear door open and visual checks are required before any movement.

News.title: Zimmer frame thrown at train attacker, jury hears
News.content:
Passengers were "chucking everything" including a toaster and a woman's Zimmer frame at a man who was stabbing people on a busy train, a court has heard.

Anthony Williams stabbed 10 people on the train which made an unscheduled stop in Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, on 1 November last year.

One of the victims, Raza Aslam, told Cambridge Crown Court he was handed a frying pan to defend himself as "all hell's broken loose".

Williams, 33, of Langford Road in Peterborough, denies 10 counts of attempted murder, and four other alleged attempted murders in earlier incidents in Peterborough and London.

Jurors have been watching video interviews with the stabbing victims, who were attacked on the York to London King's Cross LNER service.

Aslam said that not long after the train left Peterborough "someone just burst through the back door" of the carriage he was in and said "everybody run".

He said he helped a mother and child into a toilet, which they locked themselves in, as he remained in the carriage.

Aslam described how train staff member Samir Zitouni "was rushing backwards and forwards like a busy beaver trying to get different things" like trolleys and pans to defend the passengers.

Williams then appeared, "seeing if I was hiding something behind my back", Aslam recalled, before he felt "the knife stabbing".

He remembered Zitouni and another man "chucking stuff" - including a woman's Zimmer frame - and said the staff member had "saved me".

Williams was the "calmest person I've ever met", he said, adding: "If he had wanted he could have stabbed all of us in the back afterwards, he had plenty of opportunity and he didn't."

News.title: Met PC who taunted and hurt homeless man is sacked
News.content:
Farok ignored requests from the man to explain why he was being accused of resisting, and footage showed the officer manipulating the handcuffs in a way that caused pain while continuing to accuse the man of resisting.

Because he was handcuffed behind his back, the man was unable to break his fall when Farok shoved him to the floor and he landed face-first on the pavement. The man suffered a cut near his right eyebrow that required hospital treatment and "left a pool of blood on the pavement".

Farok was cleared of assault by beating in a criminal trial in November 2025.

However, a misconduct panel found Farok to have breached police standards of professional behaviour relating to use of force and authority, respect and courtesy.

He will be placed on the College of Policing barred list, preventing him from working in policing in the future.

The IOPC said criminal trials and disciplinary proceedings served two different purposes.

It said criminal proceedings were held to decide whether a criminal offence had been committed, while police disciplinary proceedings determined whether an officer had breached professional standards and, if so, what sanction should be imposed.

News.title: Could this be the last Bonfire Night for noisy fireworks?
News.content:
Bangers, rockets and screamers have long been part of Bonfire Night - but the traditional celebrations might sound a little different next year.

The government is currently considering reducing the noise limit for fireworks by 50% for those bought in shops for private use, after pressure from campaigners concerned about the impact on nervous animals and people with Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD).

Professionally organised displays would continue to have no maximum limit provided the noise level is not harmful to human health.

About 20 million people enjoy fireworks at home every year, according to industry figures.

Andy Hubble, of the British Fireworks Association (BFA), said displays had already been getting quieter and a balance must be struck to prevent a black market in noisy fireworks springing up.

The end of October sees the start of several celebrations traditionally marked by fireworks and bonfires, including Halloween on 31 October, Guy Fawkes Night on 5 November, and Diwali, which is on 8 November this year.

The government has said an outright ban on the public buying fireworks would not be proportionate.

But Business Minister Kate Dearden said her department was considering "reforms to fireworks legislation, focused on their key harms associated with their misuse - their noise, and contribution to antisocial behaviour â whilst still allowing individuals to enjoy fireworks safely and responsibly for the important community and cultural celebrations they play a part of."

It is already illegal to sell fireworks to under 18s, or to set fireworks off after 23:00, with exemptions for special occasions including Bonfire Night, Diwali, New Year's Eve and Chinese New Year.

But campaigners have raised concerns about the impact of loud bangs on nervous pets.

Dog owner Katherine Alderson, from Clacton-on-Sea, told BBC Breakfast: "It's a nightmare every single year.

"This year I've actually barricaded my bedroom window with numerous layers of insulation to try and keep out the noise of fireworks."

Asked whether reducing the bangs would take the fun out of fireworks, she said she believed displays "should be about the lights and colours" and suggested "a complete ban" on the sale of fireworks to the general public could be the solution.

News.title: Southport and Nottingham attack victims demand end to data breaches
News.content:
Families affected by the Southport and Nottingham attacks have called for stronger safeguards against NHS staff improperly accessing confidential patient records.

In an open letter, they described the breaches as a "flagrant abuse of power" and urged ministers and NHS leaders to take further action.

More than 30 people have signed the letter, including those affected by the maternity scandals.

Health Secretary, Yvette Cooper, has described the NHS data breaches as a "disgrace" and in cases where it has happened she said she expected action to be taken. The BBC has also contacted NHS England for comment.

Grace O'Malley-Kumar, Barnaby Webber, both 19, and grandfather Ian Coates, 65, were stabbed to death in the street by Valdo Calocane in Nottingham in 2023.

The authors of the letter highlighted how, in the wake of the attack, "staff began prying, while parents were still coming to terms with the deaths of their children. Other victims were still in hospital fighting for their lives when their records were breached".

Last month, Nottingham University Hospitals (NUH) NHS Trust said a total of 15 people had now been sacked as part of its investigation for inappropriately accessing medical records of the Nottingham attacks victims.

News.title: Russell Brand behind bars after being found guilty of raping fan and sexually assaulting three women
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in
