Insiders say United decision-makers are not fully sold on available coaches Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann. A well-placed source told SunSport, “The best ones won’t come.”

United did not make a formal approach for Conte, but former Newcastle boss Howe has done due diligence amid the prospect of an offer from the club.

United’s director of recruitment Christopher Vivell worked with Nagelsmann in the Red Bull group and was the driving force behind him being shortlisted.

Fabian Hurzeler has all but been discounted due to the lofty compensation fee Brighton would receive for the German and the same school of thought applies to the equally admired Unai Emery at Aston Villa.

Sports.title: ‘I wanted just one thing’ – Forgotten Chelsea outcast reveals ‘horrible’ Stamford Bridge spell and ‘no sign of life’
Sports.content:
Next

MAMADOU SARR has opened up on his “rollercoaster” time at Chelsea after being sent out on loan for the second straight season.

The centre-back, 21, joined the Blues last summer for around £12million but was immediately sent on loan to sister club Strasbourg.



Sarr was recalled to the squad in February but suffered a nightmare display during their 3-0 defeat to PSG the following month.

The youngster gifted possession away and allowed Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to open the scoring before being hooked at half time by Liam Rosenior.



The Senegal international, who is now on loan at Real Sociedad, has shed light on his struggles after admitting he saw “no sign of life” for his career following “horrible” criticism.

He told L’Equipe: “It was really very difficult – a rollercoaster. I was coming back from the AFCON and I was on a cloud.

“I started to play, have some good matches, [but] the one against PSG and that error came quickly. [Then] no news. No sign of life.

“The first week was horrible regarding the criticism. And Rosenior, who brought me, was quickly ejected.

“No longer doing your job, staying on the bench and watching your teammates play was very hard to experience, especially without any explanation.

“And then, at the World Cup, I thought that I’d be playing, but, without rhythm, I didn’t.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Sarr found himself far down the pecking under Rosenior’s successor Xabi Alonso this summer, with Levi Colwill, Maxence Lacroix, Josh Acheampong and Wesley Fofana all ahead of him.

The former Lyon defender was forced to agree another season-long loan as he headed to LaLiga but is now reaping the benefits.

He’s started nine games in all competitions and helped the team rise to fifth in the table after 11 matches.

And after picking up some much-needed minutes, Sarr believes he has regained confidence again.



He added: “I am living again. I had to be patient and find the best way out [of Chelsea].

“I was hungry, very hungry. I wanted just one thing: to play football. I have rediscovered a bit of the Lyonnais atmosphere.

“A very good club on a sporting level and a family club, too, that trusts in young players. Real Sociedad is the perfect club for me.”

Sarr started his career with boyhood Lyon before moving to Strasbourg in 2024.

Since signing for Chelsea, he has made a total of seven appearances in all competitions.

Sports.title: Daniel Levy & Joe Lewis to go head-to-head to buy London team in shock £7.6BILLION venture after bitter Tottenham split
Sports.content:
Next

DANIEL LEVY and Joe Lewis are battling it out to buy a London team in NBA Europe.

The NBA has planned to invest around £7.6billion over 10-years to launch a European basketball super league.



Already, the response has been huge with many of the teams expected to come from football clubs, including Barcelona, Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich.

But, it’s the London team that has seemingly caused the biggest clamour, with experts predicting a franchise based in the capital could be worth over £1billion.



Levy has formed a consortium with Liberty Global and MSP Sports Capital, who once backed McLaren Racing and have submitted a bid.

The Lewis family are part of a separate consortium led by the Checketts family, who have owned or invested in the likes of MLS team Real Salt Lake and the NHL’s St Louis Blues.



The Eccles family, who have shares in Burnley FC and LaLiga side Espanyol, have joined forces with Lewis and the Checketts.

The race for the London franchise has further intensified in recent weeks with reports suggesting former Chelsea chairman Todd Boehly, as well as Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, are all embroiled in a bidding war.

SunSport delves into the battle for launching the London team, the NBA’s plan for basketball in Europe, as well as venues touted for the franchise’s base.

Boardroom rivaly

Levy and Lewis were long-time business partners whose multi-decade alliance propelled Tottenham into one of the world’s wealthiest clubs.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

They joined forces in 1995 as the investment trust ENIC International Ltd. Levy was the executive face of the group, while Bahamas-based billionaire Lewis was the financial muscle.

In 2022, currency trader Lewis stepped away from the club after pleading guilty to insider trading.

However, his family members became beneficiaries of a trust fund that now owns around 75 per cent of Enic Sports Inc, which owns roughly 89 per cent of the North London giants.



Last year, Levy’s 25-year tenure as executive chairman came to an end when he was dismissed by Lewis’s children, Vivienne and Charles Lewis in a brief 10-minute phone call.

Levy is still a minority shareholder, but his equity and influence in the club have steadily shrunk.

Incredibly, after the post-Spurs fallout, Levy and the Lewis family are now being pitted against each other in what could be the ultimate corporate grudge match.

NBA’s plans

NBA Europe is predicted to become the world’s biggest sporting start-up competition.

The launch date has been set for 2028 with a 16-team league.



12 of those teams will be permanent franchises, while four temporary members will be found from a pre-qualifying competition planned for next year.

The NBA is said to have received multiple offers that have exceeded their initial targets.

Mark Tatum, the deputy commissioner of the organisation, has held talks with senior executives from Barcelona, Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Milan.



London, Manchester, Rome, Athens, Istanbul and Lyon are also expected to be homes to permanent franchises.

Buss Sports Capital, who sold their 17.8 per cent stake in the LA Lakers to Joshua Kushner this year, are believed to have submitted a bid for the Manchester-based franchise.

However, according to reports Manchester City and Manchester United have no plans to enter the bidding.

Tatum revealed that the league will follow a pyramid system, like European football leagues.

He said: “Our vision for basketball is to bring everybody with us – EuroLeague, the governing body, Fiba and the clubs – to revamp the European basketball scene.



“One of the things that we’ve learned from European football is the power of the pyramid. In football every single club understands the clear pathway to play at the top level. That doesn’t exist in basketball.”

Venues are being scouted

According to reports, the NBA is already looking at where they could house the London franchise.

One location said to be under consideration is Battersea Power Station, which Chelsea once considered as a site for a Stamford Bridge upgrade.



The Athletic claims that discussions between intermediaries regarding the Battersea Power Station proposals have taken place and the site is one of the many locations being considered for the franchise.

The report adds that the land that’s being considered is part of the wider Battersea Power Station redevelopment, and not the Grade II-listed power station building itself.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium has also been mooted as a potential home, which could give the Lewis family the edge in the bidding war.



But, just imagine if Levy’s consortium are successful. How much satisfaction could that give him walking into the stadium he helped build with a new team?

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s seven biggest moments for Portugal – from infamous wink to ‘coaching’ team to Euro 2016 glory
Sports.content:
Next

CRISTIANO RONALDO has brought the curtain down on an extraordinary international career spanning 23 years, 234 appearances and 146 goals.

But beyond the astonishing world record numbers lies the story of a man who transformed the fortunes of an entire footballing nation.



When Ronaldo made his Portugal debut in August 2003, the country had never won a major international trophy.

More than two decades later, he leaves with three winners’ medals, the gratitude of a nation and perhaps one lingering regret, never lifting the World Cup.



From the boy who grew up on the small island of Madeira to becoming one of the greatest footballers of all time, Ronaldo’s journey has been anything but ordinary.

There have been tears, controversy, unforgettable goals and moments of sheer brilliance that helped define an entire generation.

Some have questioned whether he stayed on the international stage for too long, particularly as his influence began to fade in the twilight of his career.

But Ronaldo has never been a man willing to settle for what he has already achieved.

Even after conquering Europe and rewriting the record books, his hunger to represent his country remained as fierce as ever.

And as he finally walked away from international football, he left his beloved nation with one final message: “Portugal will always be inside me.”



As one of football’s greatest-ever players bids farewell to the international stage, SunSport looks back at seven moments that defined his remarkable Portugal career…

7. Portugal 1-0 Kazakhstan — The beginning (2003)

Every great story has a beginning, and Ronaldo’s started on August 20, 2003.

Just 18 years old and fresh from completing his move to Manchester United, the teenager was introduced at half-time in a friendly against Kazakhstan, replacing Portuguese legend Luis Figo.



His fearless running, quick feet and willingness to take on defenders offered a glimpse of the superstar he would eventually become.

Few watching that evening could have imagined the teenager would go on to become the most prolific goalscorer in men’s international football history.

6. Portugal 0-0 England (3-1 pens) — The infamous wink (2006)

It was the moment that turned Ronaldo into public enemy No1 among England supporters.



During Portugal’s World Cup quarter-final against England in Germany, Wayne Rooney was sent off following an incident involving Ricardo Carvalho.

Ronaldo, then Rooney’s Manchester United team-mate, was accused of influencing referee Horacio Elizondo’s decision after rushing towards the official.

Television cameras subsequently caught Ronaldo appearing to wink towards the Portugal bench, sparking outrage back in England.

To make matters worse for English supporters, Ronaldo stepped up to score the decisive penalty as Portugal won the shootout 3-1.

He returned to Manchester United facing hostility from opposition supporters across the country.



But rather than allowing the controversy to derail his career, Ronaldo used the criticism as motivation and went on to enjoy one of the most remarkable periods of his club career.

5. Portugal 1-0 France — The heartbreak (2016)

It was supposed to be the biggest night of Ronaldo’s international career.

Twelve years after Portugal suffered a heartbreaking defeat to Greece in the Euro 2004 final on home soil, Ronaldo finally had another opportunity to become a European champion.



But his dream appeared to be slipping away when he suffered a knee injury following a challenge from Dimitri Payet.

Despite attempting to continue, the Portugal captain was forced off after just 25 minutes, leaving the pitch on a stretcher with tears streaming down his face.

For a player who had dedicated so much of his career to winning a major trophy for his country, it was a devastating moment.

Yet the night would eventually produce one of football’s most extraordinary stories of redemption.

4. Portugal 3-3 Spain — The masterpiece (2018)



If ever there was a performance that captured Ronaldo’s extraordinary ability to carry his country, this was it.

Facing Spain in Portugal’s opening match of the 2018 World Cup in Russia, Ronaldo produced arguably his finest individual display on the international stage.

He opened the scoring from the penalty spot before adding a second goal just before half-time.

But with Portugal trailing 3-2 and time running out, Ronaldo delivered a moment of pure genius.



Standing over a free-kick in the 88th minute, he curled an unstoppable effort beyond David de Gea to complete his hat-trick and rescue a dramatic draw.

It was a performance that underlined his ability to deliver when the pressure was at its greatest.

3. Sweden 2-3 Portugal — The one-man demolition (2013)

With a place at the 2014 World Cup on the line, Ronaldo produced one of the most devastating performances of his international career.



Portugal faced Sweden in a two-legged play-off, with much of the build-up dominated by the battle between Ronaldo and Zlatan Ibrahimovic.

Having scored the only goal in the first leg, Ronaldo travelled to Stockholm knowing his country was just 90 minutes away from securing a place in Brazil.

What followed was a breathtaking display.

Ronaldo scored a stunning hat-trick in the second leg, repeatedly tearing through the Swedish defence with his pace, power and clinical finishing.

Ibrahimovic responded with two goals of his own, but even the Swedish superstar could do little to stop Ronaldo.



His four goals across the two matches secured Portugal’s qualification and provided another reminder of his ability to rise to the biggest occasions.

2. Hungary 3-3 Portugal — The great escape (2016)

Portugal’s historic Euro 2016 triumph might never have happened without Ronaldo’s heroics against Hungary.

Having drawn their opening two group matches, Portugal entered their final fixture knowing another disappointing result could send them home.



And with Hungary repeatedly taking the lead, Ronaldo was forced to drag his country back into the contest.

He produced a moment of brilliance with an audacious backheel to level the scores at 2-2 before heading home another equaliser to make it 3-3.

The draw was enough to send Portugal through to the knockout stages as one of the best third-placed teams.

It was not the most glamorous performance of Ronaldo’s career, but it proved one of the most important.

Without his two goals that afternoon, Portugal’s journey to European glory could have ended before it had truly begun.



1. Portugal 1-0 France — The ultimate redemption (2016)

For all the goals, individual awards and records, this was the moment Ronaldo had been waiting for throughout his international career.

Portugal faced hosts France in the Euro 2016 final, hoping to win the first major trophy in their history.

But when Ronaldo was forced off injured after just 25 minutes, it seemed his chance of finally lifting silverware with his country had been cruelly taken away.



What followed, however, was an extraordinary display of leadership.

Unable to influence proceedings on the pitch, Ronaldo became Portugal’s most passionate supporter on the touchline.

He encouraged his team-mates, shouted ‘coaching’ instructions and celebrated every tackle as Portugal battled to keep the French at bay.

Then, in the 109th minute, substitute Eder unleashed a stunning strike from outside the penalty area to give Portugal the lead.

Ronaldo could barely contain his emotions as the final whistle confirmed Portugal’s first major international trophy.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Twelve years after leaving the pitch in tears following defeat to Greece at Euro 2004, Ronaldo was finally a European champion.

It was the crowning moment of his international career — and proof that even football’s greatest individual talents sometimes need their team-mates to deliver the ultimate prize.

Sports.title: 27 reasons we love Cristiano Ronaldo after Portugal retirement from charity donations to no tattoos so he can give blood
Sports.content:
Next

FOOTBALL fans don’t know if they’re going to get Jekyll or Hyde when Cristiano Ronaldo appears in front of the cameras.

From his early days at Manchester United, then Real Madrid, before Juventus and United again – the 41-year-old has become one of the most divisive athletes in the world.



And now, the Al-Nassr ace has made headlines again to announce his retirement from the international stage.

His fans treat him with god-like admiration – some have tattoos, copy his hairstyles, even buy CR7 pants in honour of his ridiculous skill and achievement.



But for every fan, there’s a critic.

For every Piers Morgan, there’s a Roy Keane calling out his petulant behaviour and obsession with appearance and brand.



And while the entire world are aware of the five-time Ballon d’Or winner’s divisive antics like walking out on the Portugal team, less are watching his kindhearted work behind the scenes.

SunSport looks back on how Ronaldo’s heart has grown and grown – and that despite the sometimes outwardly grumpy persona, there’s much more to CR7.

JESUS DE MIGUEL

UD Almeria, a Spanish club partly owned by Ronaldo, announced that they will donate the money from ticket sales for their game versus Tenerife to the family of Jesus de Miguel.

The 30-year-old tragically died on Tuesday morning after suffering a heavy blow during a LaLiga 2 match between Andorra and Tenerife.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

THE AMBASSADOR

Ronaldo continues to be an ambassador for major charities like Unicef and World Vision, and has spoken up for several more.

He made a point of mentioning a group of children he had met with leukemia during his 2014 Ballon d’Or speech.



In 2016, he recorded a message to the children affected by the Syrian conflict, calling them “true heroes” and stating “I am with you”.

He also made a donation which he asked Save the Children to stay top-secret.

Ronaldo’s Ice Bucket Challenge video – the viral sensation that raised hundreds of millions of pounds in 2014 – was seen by more than a hundred million people across his social media platforms.

HOSPITAL HELP

In 2020, Ronaldo teamed up with his agent Jorge Mendes to donate £1m to hospitals in Portugal to fight the coronavirus pandemic – according to various reports.

Fans, monitors, infusion pumps and beds were shipped into hospitals in Porto and Lisbon as they attempted to cope with their ever-increasing number of Covid-19 patients.



The president of Lisbon’s Santa Maria Hospital, Daniel Ferro, pulled the curtain back on the generous act stunned at their kindness.

GOLDEN BOOTED

Who needs another Golden Boot? Not Ronaldo.

In 2011, Ronaldo was awarded the European Golden Boot after scoring 40 goals under Jose Mourinho.

Los Blancos only finished second in LaLiga and crashed out in the semi-finals of the Champions League.



But rather than cramming it in the trophy cabinet, Ronaldo sent it to auction where it raised £1.2m to build schools in war-torn Gaza.

Cristiano's big donations Selling his 2011 European Golden boot – £1.2milion Selling his 2013 Ballon d’or – £530,000 Donating to the Nepalese earthquake – £5million* (reported) Uefa Team of the Year bonus – £100,000 Champions League 2014 win bonus – £450,000 Portuguese cancer centre – £120,000 Helping Erik Oritz Cruz – £55,000

BLOOD DONOR

The 41-year-old is remarkably tattoo-free compared to a growing number of his peers.

And this is said to be because Ronaldo regularly donates blood and has been involved in numerous campaigns, including Be The 1, to encourage others to do the same.

People with tattoos can donate blood, but are not able to do so immediately after getting new ink to reduce the risk of infection.



Ronaldo also donated bone marrow after a former team-mate Carlos Martins revealed he had a son who needed bone marrow.

And Ronaldo has been a donor since.

He said donating bone marrow is “something a lot of people think is a difficult thing to do but it’s nothing more than drawing blood and doesn’t hurt”.

THE MILLION DOLLAR QUESTION

In April 2015, Ronaldo wrote another cheque to aid relief efforts following the Nepalese earthquake that killed 9,000 people, and injured another 22,000.

Ronaldo is said to have given £5MILLION to Save the Children’s disaster relief fund.



And even though those reports have stayed unverified and were even denied by the charity – it’s likely he did make a mystery donation.

PANDEMIC PAYCUT

Ronaldo’s estimated net worth clocks in at an eyewatering £891million, so it’s not all that surprising that there is some to spare.

In 2020, in the middle of the pandemic, the Portugal star agreed to waive four months wages to ensure Juventus could pay their staff – while the world waited to see what happened.



That’s said to have cost Ronaldo £3.8m personally.

BERNARDO BONUS

Bernardo Silva spilled the beans when he told everyone that his fellow Portugal team-mate asked the Portugal squad to donate 50 per cent of their qualification bonus for Euro 2020.

The donation went to helping battle the coronavirus pandemic.

Silva said: “So we qualified to the 2020 Euros, which now is in 2021.

“And he gave us the idea let’s donate part of our bonus, so I think our national team, our players will donate 50 per cent of our qualifying bonus.”



BALLON D’MORE

Ronaldo headed to the auction house again in 2017 but this time towing his 2013 Ballon d’Or.

The Make-A-Wish Foundation raked in a massive £530,000 for the golden prize, while the gala dinner was a roaring success.

HELPING A CANCER CENTRE

Dolores Aveiro, Ronaldo’s mother, survived breast cancer in 2007.



The United man thanked the care centre in Portugal that treated his mum, while chipping in £120,000 to their purse.

INVITATION TO AN ORPHAN

Real Madrid fan Haidar was orphaned when both of his parents were killed by a suicide bomber in Beirut, Lebanon.

When a local reporter got in touch with the 15-time European champions, the boy was eventually invited to the club, where he burst into tears as he squeezed CR7.

COST COVERED

Ronaldo sent a car to bring the family of nine-year-old Nuhazet Guillen, who had terminal cancer, to the Real Madrid hotel in 2009.

Inviting the kid to his private Bernabeu box, Ronaldo dedicated a goal to Nuhuzet and even handed him his match shirt post-game.



The star then went a step further to pay for experimental treatment in the US before he covered all his medication and private treatment as Nuhuzet’s condition worsened.

Ronaldo paid that for over a year, until the boy’s tragic passing in March 2013.

FLOOD RELIEF

Following the devastating 2024 floods in Spain, Ronaldo and his wife reportedly helped fund truckloads of food, water, and essential supplies directly to the affected towns.



They also helped families replace furniture lost in the floods.

LAY THE FOUNDATION

In 2024, the CR7 foundation was born, built and tailored exclusively for youth education and health.

They host scholarships and fund sports programs to give vulnerable children an improved access to medical care.

EARTHQUAKE RELIEF

After catastrophic earthquakes in Turkey and Syria struck the region, Ronaldo chartered a whole plane filled to the brim with around £260,000 worth of tents, blankets, food, baby food, and medical supplies en-route.

He also auctioned a signed shirt in a collection alongside Leonardo Bonucci and Paulo Dybala to raise more than £196,000.



NEVER FORGETS A KIND GESTURE

Ronaldo, a shy kid, would beg for food at the back of McDonald’s and returned the favour to one of the generous employees in 2019 when he took Paula Leca out for dinner.

Ronaldo revealed he was given free burgers by three women when he used to beg for food as a child.

After a massive appeal, Leca came forward to say she was one of the three women – calling Ronaldo “timid”.



PAYING FOR LIFE-SAVING TREATMENT

Ronaldo and Georgina helped pay for Portuguese youngster Tomas’ cancer treatment in 2019.

After the youngster suffered a relapse of the rare cancer neuroblastoma in October 2020, Tomas’ parents appealed to try and get funding for their brave child’s operations.

And it was none other than Ronaldo and Georgina who discreetly stepped up to cover the costs, according to Georgina’s sister Ivana.

The brave kid then checked in to D’Hebron Hospital in Barcelona for tests and oncology consultations.

INVITATION FOR RICKSEN

In 2013, Rangers legend Fernando Ricksen was suddenly diagnosed with motor neurone disease meaning he was wheelchair-bound and heavily reliant on his wife and carers.



After his condition became well-known, Ronaldo contacted the Scottish title winner to invite Ricksen and his family to a match at the Bernabeu.

Ronaldo also presented a shirt to the former right-back after a Champions League win over Legia Warsaw in October 2016

Unfortunately the star passed away in September 2019.



SUPER TEAM-MATE

Ronaldo – the player of the tournament – handed out personalised Bvlgari watches to each of his Real Madrid team-mates after La Decima.

They were said to have cost him £5,000 apiece.

BIG BROTHER IS WATCHING

Like his dad Denis, older brother Hugo Aveiro battled addiction for years.

As Ronaldo grew in fame, the star decided to help boot out his destructive habits, promising to dedicate La Decima to his brother if he pulled through.



Once he did, the two brothers – ten years apart – embraced at full-time of the Champions League final and he’s now popped up at several other events, including the 2016 Ballon d’Or ceremony.

Ronaldo is also godfather to Hugo’s son, while Hugo has been tasked with looking after the Ronaldo Museum in Madeira.

EARLY BIRDS

Ronaldo popped out to an exclusive party spot at 9.30pm for a pre-Christmas dinner with his now-wife Georgina Rodriguez and son Cristiano Jr in 2018.

But it turned out they were 90 minutes early, and they were forced to watch the clock for the best part of an hour for a table.



But the striker didn’t throw a hissy fit at chef Davide Fiore but waited it out calmly, the Turin local described Ronaldo as a “decent boy”.

A GREAT TIPPER

The luxury Costa Navarino resort in southern Greece hosts two five-star hotels, as well as luxury private residences, conference facilities, spas, golf courses.

And they will even enforce a media blackout for their biggest stars.

Ronaldo & Co were so thankful for some privacy, he left a huge tip for the staff who took great care of him, adding £20,000 on top of his bill to be shared across ten staff both times he stayed.



SELFIE TIME

CR7 is one to bat away heavy-handed security when they tackle his pitch-invaded fans to the floor.

Ronaldo also loves to interact with supporters inside stadiums – staying to throw his shirt into the crowd, sign autographs and take lots of selfies.

SURGERY SUPPORT

Ten-month-old Erik Ortiz Cruz’s mum pleaded with Ronaldo for a shirt for her son, who has cortical dysplasia – a condition that causes up to 30 seizures a day.

But after the international superstar heard about his difficult story, Ronaldo chipped in £55,000 for his initial brain surgery before promising the full cover for any follow-up treatment.



He also helped raise extra money for Erik by donating a signed kit to sell at auction.

BROKEN WRIST

Unlucky Charlie Silverwood had his wrist broken when Ronaldo blasted a trademark free-kick into the Vitality Stadium crowd at Bournemouth in 2013.

Shortly after, the 11-year-old kid got a call from Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, while Ronaldo gave him a signed shirt.



And it happened again in a Champions League clash when a young boy burst into floods of tears when Ronaldo dashed the ball into the masses – but he leapt into the stands to give him a training top.

BEST FRIEND EVER

Super-agent Mendes was gifted a £40m Greek island by his best man, Ronaldo, when he married Sandra in 2015

BACK TO SCHOOL

Partnering with the Peter Lim Scholarship in Singapore, Ronaldo expanded his educational philanthropy to hand out Singapore Youth Scholarships.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The scheme offered increased funding for young student-athletes to chase their wildest dreams.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal farewell match ‘set to take place with different manager’ after furious Jorge Jesus bust-up
Sports.content:
Next

CRISTIANO RONALDO will have a new manager in the dugout for his Portugal farewell match after announcing his retirement.

Ronaldo, 41, revealed the shock news he was walking away from the Portuguese national team following his fallout with boss Jorge Jesus.



It comes just weeks after Jesus dropped the veteran for the team’s clash against Norway in September.

The former Manchester United star quit the camp in fury and has now decided to retire from Portugal duty.



The forward – who scored 146 goals in 234 appearances – won’t be saying goodbye immediately as he’s set to play in one final match to cap off over a decade with the team.

But according to ESPN, Jesus won’t be leading the team for Ronaldo‘s last game after their bitter row.

Instead, former Portugal boss Luiz Felipe Scolari – who gave Ronaldo his debut back in 2004 – could return to the dugout.

Ronaldo had a close relationship with Scolari during his youth after supporting him following the death of his father aged 20.

The report also claims Ronaldo’s old Portugal coach Fernando Santos is not in the running to lead the team for the match.

Ronaldo worked under Santos between 2014 and 2022 and – while he won Euro 2016 – the pair are not on good terms after the coached benched the legendary star during the 2022 World Cup.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Ronaldo's Portugal career Debut: Portugal 1-0 Kazakhstan (August 20, 2003) Last match: Portugal 1-0 Wales (September 24, 2026) Appearances: 234 Goals: 146 Accolades Euro 2016 winner

Nations League winner 2018-19, 2024-25

Ronaldo said he considered quitting Portugal before insisting he was still “ready to play” for his team.

But now he has made a U-turn and has decided to close his chapter following an incredible reign.

Ronaldo said in a statement: “The day has come back for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team.

“I never felt it belonged to me alone. But for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.



“Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision. Because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart.

“A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.

“When I look back at everything with the national team, I don’t just see the matches, goals, records or trophies.

“I see people. I see the Portuguese people living abroad who, for 90 minutes, felt a little closer to home. I see millions of Portuguese people I have never met but who became part of my life.

“Because at the end of the day, football is so much bigger than a game. Football is about people.”



Jesus opted to keep things civil despite their feud as he added: “Cristiano is a global icon, an example for Portugal and the national team.

“I had a huge photo of him put up in our auditorium so that all the young players could look up to him every single day.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I asked him to continue with me because I needed him by my side. “But I have to accept his decision.

“He will always have a place in the hearts of the Portuguese people. “He will always be an icon of Portuguese football.”

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson was so impressed by Unai Emery that he told him Wayne Rooney secret – but he’s not right for Man Utd
Sports.content:
Next

UNAI EMERY first encountered Sir Alex Ferguson as a 38-year-old managing Valencia.

Manchester United won 1-0 at the Mestalla in September 2010 and Emery could barely speak any English. Yet he was granted an audience with Ferguson, partial to a post-match glass of red, for more than an hour.



Emery was curious as to why Wayne Rooney was not in the United squad. Ferguson, usually economical with the truth regarding team news, had publicly said Rooney was injured. He had been dropped.

Remarkably, Ferguson told Emery the truth: “He has to know who the boss is.”



Rooney had questioned Ferguson’s failure to sign Mesut Ozil and informed United he would not sign a new contract.

At Aston Villa, Emery is the manager. Not the head coach, the manager. It would make any approach from United, whenever they have the nerve to dismiss Michael Carrick, a possible non-starter amid their insistence on the title ‘head coach’.

Villa have taken measures to keep Emery, in line for a new contract. The Football Association did similarly with Thomas Tuchel five weeks after United dismissed Ruben Amorim in January.

Emery, Mikel Arteta and Enzo Maresca are the only three ‘managers’ in the Premier League. Their clubs all lifted silverware last season.

Friday marks Emery’s first match in charge of Villa, a 3-1 victory against United and the club’s first home victory against them since August 1995. Emery’s mentality ensured that would not be as good as it would get.

Villa, 17th when Emery took over, have since come seventh, fourth, sixth and fifth. They have helped render that awful old phrase ‘big six’ obsolete and finished above United twice.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Europa League glory in May marked Villa’s first trophy in 30 years. However long Emery remains in the midlands, he merits a permanent tribute at Villa Park.

The BBC commentator Ian Dennis noticed after Villa thrashed Freiburg in the Europa League final that Emery has won the competition with three clubs with ‘Villa’ in their name: Sevilla, Villarreal and Villa.

It is the biggest reason why Emery would be ill-fitted to managing United. The Spaniard has succeeded at clubs with little or no scrutiny and low expectations.

Jamie Carragher said Villa will never be United before his cringing climbdown on social media last week.

Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Emiliano Martinez and Youri Tielemans moved to bigger English clubs in the summer. Tielemans accurately told us in August that “there are still clubs above Villa, and Manchester United is one of them”.



Embarrassingly, Tielemans then apologised for his comments on Instagram amid a hissy fit from deluded online Villa fans. Martinez wanted to join United last year after they had finished ten places below Villa.

At clubs where there is significant scrutiny and lofty expectations, Emery has failed. His time at Paris Saint-Germain is best remembered for the extraordinary 6-1 Champions League shellacking by Barcelona after winning the round-of-16 first leg 4-0 in 2017.

Emery was always an unusual choice to succeed Arsene Wenger in 2018. His 18 months at Arsenal even included his one Europa League final defeat, a 4-1 thumping by Chelsea.



During this borderline golden era for Villa, with their best team in 30 years they have won one trophy. During the same period, United have won two and their worst team in 51 years reached a Europa League final.

Uefa have unwittingly rigged the Europa League and Conference League for English clubs. The drab league format reduces jeopardy and the budgets of English top seven sides or cup winners blow their overseas counterparts out of the water.

Champions League teams do not drop down when eliminated from the group stage to up the standards. The Premier League has monopolised the two Europas since the format change in 2024.

Villa’s knockout run last year read Lille (3-0 on aggregate), Bologna (7-1 on aggregate) and Nottingham Forest (4-1 on aggregate) before Freiburg were pummelled 3-0. It was theirs to lose.

Emery’s triumph with Villarreal against United in 2021 has its own caveat, given it was achieved amid the soullessness of pandemic-era football.



United require an authoritarian in charge. They always have done and it is on director of football Jason Wilcox that he compromised and settled on the safe option of Carrick. His tactics were publicly questioned by the club captain 11 games into the season and Bruno Fernandes is already back in the side.

Emery’s experience, authority and longevity understandably appeal to many United fans. As does his Premier League nous.

Yet Villa’s record at United under Emery is another red flag: four games and four defeats, two against the worst United teams in living memory.



Villa were the poorest team at Old Trafford in 2024-25 – the season United finished 15th. They bottled Champions League qualification on the final day against a United side reeling from their meek Europa League final defeat to Tottenham.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Overall, Emery has managed nine times at Old Trafford, lost six and drawn three. His only ‘win’ was in Rio Ferdinand’s testimonial in 2013.

Sunday is his chance to show United who’s boss.

Sports.title: 'I went full out!' - Antonelli reveals title celebrations and 'special' messages
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli has revealed details of his celebrations after being crowned Formula 1 world champion, along with some of the messages he received in the aftermath of his historic triumph.

The 20-year-old Italian finished third in Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix to become the sport's youngest-ever drivers' title winner, achieving the feat with four rounds of the 2026 season still remaining.

Despite having the final leg of a triple-header to come this weekend with the Sao Paulo Grand Prix in Brazil, a party was held on Sunday night in Mexico at which Antonelli said he did not hold back.

Asked whether Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord had been the "biggest party animal", Antonelli told Sky Sport Germany: "Bradley's good. But I was not joking either.

"I never drink. I try to avoid that as much as possible, also because I prefer eating pasta ragu from my mother.

"But that night, I was like, it's such a special occasion, I've got to go full out.

"The thing is, because I'm not used to it, after very little I was already feeling it. But I just kept going, all the way until the end. But it was a fun night.

"It was not easy to wake up. And my body wasn't in the best of states, let's say.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player How Antonelli's Drivers' Championship sounded with Italian commentary!

"But it was good. We had a lot of fun together with the team. Also, my dad was there, some of my friends were there.

"It was the best way to celebrate such a special day. But now we're back at it again, and the focus is to try and win."

'Vettel message was really cool'

The extremely popular Antonelli was inundated with congratulations after sealing the title, starting with fellow world champions Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, who shared the podium with the Italian in Mexico.

Antonelli revealed he had received further messages from Verstappen and Hamilton, along with reigning world champion Lando Norris and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

He also confirmed he had been congratulated by fellow Italian sports stars Valentino Rossi and Jannik Sinner.

However, Antonelli was particularly enthused by a video message he received from retired four-time F1 world champion Sebastian Vettel.

"I have to be honest, many, many people reached out and they were super nice," Antonelli told Sky Sports F1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli watches back a montage of videos from his journey from go-karting, to F1's youngest champion

"Max, Lewis, Lando was very nice as well, Charles. Everyone within the paddock reached out and they were super, super nice.

"The message from Seb was really cool. But I got messages from all over. I'm very lucky to have so much support and to see so many people that were happy. Valentino Rossi, Jannik Sinner - there's so many people that I could list.

Sports.title: Family, friends and Tenerife players gather for De Miguel's funeral
Sports.content:
Jesus de Miguel's funeral took place in the village of Navahermosa on Thursday; the Tenerife striker died after a collision; LaLiga confirmed ⁠that fixtures in the first and second divisions would go ahead, apart from games involving Tenerife, FC Andorra and Castellon vs Eibar

Jesus de Miguel funeral: Family, friends and Tenerife players gather to remember striker who died following on-field collision

The funeral of footballer Jesus de Miguel took place on Thursday

The funeral of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel has taken place after the footballer died following an on-field ‌collision.

De Miguel was involved in a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono on Monday and was taken to intensive care, after which his death was announced on Tuesday.

The Tenerife squad, club staff and majority shareholder Rayco Garcia attended the funeral. Also in attendance were Spanish FA (RFEF) ​president Rafael Louzan, Spain coach Luis de la Fuente, Real Madrid president ‌Florentino Perez and Atletico Madrid chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin.

The funeral took place at the San Miguel Arcangel ​church after a procession.

Image: A procession took place before the funeral

"Feeling so much affection for Jesus ​and seeing the impact he had on so many people is something ⁠we will always carry with us," the family ⁠said in a statement read out by the player's agent Manuel Hernandez before the funeral.

"Jesus leaves a void that is impossible to fill, but also cherished memories for all of us ‌who were fortunate enough to share our lives with him. Thank you for loving him and for standing by us."

Image: Real Madrid president Florentino Perez attended the funeral

Image: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente attended the funeral alongside Aitor Karanka

Spanish police have opened an investigation into De Miguel's death.

Meanwhile, FC Andorra goalkeeper Owono said he is going through the most difficult ‌days of his life in a statement released by his club on Wednesday.

"These are the most difficult days of my life," ‌Owono said. "I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to ​process what has happened. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

"But right now, honestly, ​I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the ⁠pain we are experiencing. Rest in ⁠peace, Jesus."

Tenerife's match against Granada and FC Andorra's game with Mallorca have been postponed this weekend.

Las Palmas, will play their against Eldense on Sunday in blue and white colours, traditionally ⁠worn by their main rivals Tenerife, as a tribute to De Miguel.

Meanwhile, Tenerife owner Garcia invited fans to ​Tenerife's stadium on Saturday to pay their respects to De Miguel ​in what he called "the last goodbye".

LaLiga games to go ahead this weekend

LaLiga have confirmed ⁠that fixtures in the top two tiers will go ahead, with a few exceptions. Those exceptions being FC Andorra vs Mallorca, Granada vs Tenerife and Castellon vs Eibar.

This is despite the Spanish Footballers' Association calling for the suspension of this weekend's round of matches on Thursday.

De Miguel spent two-and-a-half years at Castellon before moving to Tenerife in 2025, and LaLiga accepted ⁠the club's request to postpone their match.

A minute's silence ​will be observed before each game that goes ahead, while the referee will stop ​play at the first interruption after the ninth minute, in recognition of the number nine shirt De Miguel wore for Tenerife.

Sports.title: Is Rashid still England's No 1 spinner in ODI cricket?
Sports.content:
Through the ups and downs of England's white-ball cricket in the last decade or so, one of the constants has been Adil Rashid.

The leg-spinner was recalled after the 2015 World Cup debacle, a tournament at which the side were dumped out in round one, and played a major part in the rebuild that culminated in the unforgettable victory over New Zealand in the 2019 final at Lord's.

Rashid was there, too, for the high of the 2022 T20 World Cup title in Australia and the nadirs of the 2023 ODI World Cup in India and 2025 Champions Trophy in Pakistan, when England failed to make it out of their group after some pitiful performances.

Image: Rashid is in England's squad for the white-ball tour of Australia later this month

Only James Anderson (269) has more one-day international wickets for England than Rashid (244) and on many occasions we have heard from inside and outside the camp that the Yorkshireman is the team's most-important player. But is that still the case?

Anderson's future has been a hot topic following his surprise release from Lancashire and so has Rashid's with England after he was left out of their final three games of the ODI tri-series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka in the subcontinent last month.

The reason for the 38-year-old's omission given publicly by head coach Brendon McCullum was tactical - the New Zealander saying Liam Dawson's left-arm darts were more beneficial in Pakistani conditions than Rashid's leg-breaks.

The stats bear that out with the most prolific spinners in the tri-series - Pakistan's Arafat Minhas (nine wickets at 23.22), Dawson (seven wickets at 21.42), Sri Lanka's Dunith Wellalage (four wickets at 48.25) - all southpaws.

Image: Liam Dawson impressed in the ODI tri-series in Pakistan after taking Rashid's place

Is Rashid suffering from a lack of cricket?

Still, England leaving out Rashid a few years ago, even a few months ago, would have been anathema whatever the conditions. That call, coupled with his central contract ending before the next 50-over World Cup in late 2027, raised questions and eyebrows.

For perhaps the first time since his return to the white-ball set-up 11 years ago, Rashid's spot is not a given. He has been great for England but not so great of late in one-day internationals.

He has nine wickets in seven games in that format in 2026, at an average of 36.22 and strike-rate of 37.50, after a 2025 when he averaged two wickets a game (30 in 15 fixtures at an average of 23.63 and strike-rate of 24.10).

In his sole game in the recent ODI tri-series, against Pakistan in Rawalpindi, he recorded figures of 1-55 from eight overs at an economy rate of 6.87.

Image: Rashid's numbers have slid in ODIs in 2026

Sky Sports' Michael Atherton said of Rashid, who will be hoping to return to the XI for the three-match ODI series in Australia from next Friday, starting in Perth: "He plays so little outside of international cricket so you don't get a sense of where his game is at outside of those matches to see if there is a drop off.

"I think it will be absolutely fascinating in Australia. That is where you think a wrist spinner would come into his own so one assumes he will play. They will be important ODIs for him."

Whether Rashid's lack of matches, and maybe the hand injury he picked up towards the end of the English summer, hindered him in the subcontinent, you could not help but feel Harry Brook's side missed him in the tri-series, however well Dawson may have bowled.

The middle-overs magic Rashid is able to deliver at his best was sorely missed as Sri Lanka chased down a monster 430 at Rawalpindi and Pakistan then recovered from 154-9 to successfully pursue 242 in Lahore three days later.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Rawalpindi as Sri Lanka stunned England by reaching 430 and completing the second-highest ODI run chase of all time

Can Dawson and Rashid fit in same XI?

So a big question now for England is whether they pick Dawson, Rashid or both. If the spinners are in the same XI, there will be knock-on effects elsewhere. It is a tricky juggling act.

If Rashid came in for seam-bowling all-rounder Sam Curran, then Dawson would probably have to move up to No 7. Dawson is a good batter but that feels a spot high. The same could be said if Jamie Overton were to bat at No 7, above Dawson.

If Rashid were to replace one of the main fast bowlers, then Curran would have to serve as third seamer and on the evidence of the tri-series - four wickets at 54.75, an economy of 7.50, and periods where he looked rather anodyne - that would be a risk.

Image: Having Sam Curran as England's third seamer in ODIs could be a risk

There is no easy fix balancing a side when you do not have Ben Stokes' all-round abilities at your disposal, a problem England's Test team are now discovering.

With Will Jacks, Joe Root and potentially the returning Jacob Bethell offering slow-bowling options, it may ultimately be that only one of Dawson and Rashid can play.

The identity of that one is not as clear as it once was.

Sports.title: Fury's camp deny injury claims ahead of Joshua fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury's camp have denied claims their fighter is injured ahead of his eagerly-anticipated clash with Anthony Joshua next month.

Fury and Joshua will finally face each other on December 11 in Cardiff for the WBA (Super) heavyweight title after years of back and forth.

However, former British heavyweight boxer Frank Bruno has cast doubt on the fight and suggested Fury could be injured.

"I looked at him the other day and I think someone was talking to me in the gym that he's got some injury, which may stop him from going into the fight with Anthony Joshua? And having that on your head ain't nice," said Bruno on the Fight Your Corner podcast.

Fury's camp have denied the claim to Sky Sports News, so the Fury-Joshua fight is set to go ahead as scheduled.

Image: Frank Bruno made the injury claim about Fury

The fight is due to begin at around 1am in the early hours of Saturday December 12, with the Principality Stadium remaining open until 3.30am.

Last week, Fury said he intends to carry on boxing after December's blockbuster clash, even though at 38 he is at a late stage in his career.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Johnny Nelson expects things to heat up between Fury and Joshua as we get closer to the fight

"I'm going to continue. I've got two fights left on my contract. I'll finish the contract off and then probably sign another 10-fight deal. Who knows?" he said when speaking to WSVN Miami from his training camp.

"If the money's right sign another 10 fights, but they've got to be quick because I'm getting older. And when it's gone it's gone. I'm coming up to fight No 40."

Sports.title: Bentley reveals tough route to world title as he prepares for Mosley Jr fight
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley's route through boxing has never been smooth.

The Battersea fighter is smarting from the WBO stripping him of his hard-won middleweight world title, but has to focus on a dangerous bout with Shane Mosley Jr on Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

Bentley fights Mosley Jr on the Zuffa Boxing 12 bill, headlined by Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chev Clarke refuses to shake Chris Billam-Smith's hand ahead of their Zuffa Boxing 12 main event this Saturday

The WBO required Bentley to box his mandatory challenger, Yoenli Hernandez next. It was a fight Bentley was willing to take, but he had committed to fighting Mosley Jr, which he wanted to do as a voluntary defence or even a non-title bout.

"We put up a really good case and everything we mentioned was kind of ignored," Bentley told Sky Sports. "The reasons as to why they stripped me are their reasons.

"[WBC middleweight champion Carlos] Adames is able to do a non-title fight and box.

"I was happy to fight Hernandez next year," he added. "They just want to seem like they're doing justice, but they're not."

The son of boxing legend Shane Mosley, Junior is coming off a tremendous stoppage victory over Serhii Bohachuk. He is also rated No 6 in the WBO's own rankings.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Billam-Smith and Clarke share a first fight week face-off

"If this was for a world title, everyone would be like this is a good defence. He's No 6 with the WBO, everyone knows his resume, he's fought top fighters and I'd say he deserves a title shot if I'm being honest," Bentley said.

"I deserve to defend my title. I'm being criticised for my move but that's because a lot of people out there are putting out narratives to try and take a hit on Zuffa as a promotional company. I'm just in the middle of the crossfire.

"It's not [fair] but life is not fair. You've just got to take it as it is."

Bentley has vowed to use all this antagonism to fuel his motivation for Saturday's fight.

"I'm expecting a dogfight at some point, it should be good. I get excited about these fighters. He's a good fighter and if I turn up I can put on a good performance," he said.

"I'm free of all this circus and I can just move forward and box like I want to do."

Bentley has overcome setbacks in life and career before. He has faced adversity becoming a three-time British middleweight champion. He lost his first world title fight, but came back eventually to win the WBO's interim belt that was upgraded to the full world championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Billam-Smith and Clarke will box in the headline event of Zuffa Boxing 12 at London's Copper Box Arena

He was out of action for more than a year before his crucial fight with Endry Saavedra that saw him secure the interim strap. That was a struggle. He was looking for work outside of the sport, but could not even get jobs as a delivery driver.

"I was out for 16 months," Bentley said. "During that time there was no income because I wasn't fighting.

"It's hard for boxers to get sponsors and I just couldn't get anything going so I was trying to apply for Amazon delivery, like a zero-hour contract one, you just download the app put in your details and it just gives you jobs and you just do it whenever you can.

"And there were just no jobs in my area at the time. That's the only reason why I didn't do it.

"I just couldn't get any work. I just had to sit tight and wait for a fight date.

"I don't think I take enough time to sit back and think about my journey. When you put it like that it is quite incredible."

Watch Bentley vs Mosley Jr this Saturday live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: WTA takes 'full responsibility' after Pegula labels Andreeva a 'diva' during practice
Sports.content:
The WTA Tour says it takes "full responsibility" after Mirra Andreeva was labelled a "diva" who "needs to be humbled" by Jessica Pegula during a conversation with her coach in practice at the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells.

American star Pegula is at the centre of controversy after being picked up on a hot mic criticising 19-year-old French Open champion Andreeva and her coach Conchita Martinez at the year-end tournament in California.

The practice session at Indian Wells was live streamed by the Women's Tennis Association on its YouTube channel with the WTA Tour Finals starting on Sunday.

All the practice streams from this year's event have since been removed from the platform.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at Andreeva's 2026 season

"Conchita's always been very nice to me, but I lost a little respect for her, because I'm just like, this girl, she's a nice girl. She's a diva. She needs to be humbled. Conchita eggs on her behaviour," the American was heard saying about her rival to one of her coaches, Mark Knowles.

"If I were her coach and my player had just played four great games, she's up 4-0, she gets mad at me and chases me down... I'd tell her not to talk to me like that.

"She's bad... I feel like she needs to be provoked to get fired up and react."

Spaniard Martinez, the 1994 Wimbledon champion, began working with Andreeva in 2024.

Andreeva reached the Wimbledon quarter-finals last year before sealing her first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros in June.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Naomi Osaka, Pegula and Coco Gauff weigh in on influencers disrupting matches at the US Open

Pegula, who is a member of the WTA players' council, went on to claim that, were Andreeva to adopt Coco Gauff's mentality, she would become a much better player:

"It's so funny 'cause if you see her and Coco's mentality, if she had Coco's mentality, she's better than her. Serve and everything and moves just as good," she said.

But Pegula, runner-up at the 2024 US Open, also praised Andreeva, saying the world No 3 is "wonderful" and "smart".

In a statement issued on Thursday, the WTA Tour said it takes "full responsibility for failing to inform our players and their teams that microphones, in place to give fans a livestream of the players' practice, were active on the courts. We sincerely apologise for failing to meet our responsibility to ensure players and coaches were properly informed".

The WTA went on to explain: "The microphones were intended to capture the ambient sounds of tennis, not player or coach conversations. However, conversations were captured, and we recognise that we failed to ensure the appropriate safeguards were in place.

"We are continuing with live streaming of practice but there will not be any audio."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the 2025 mixed doubles semi-final when Pegula teamed up with Britain's Jack Draper

Pegula has been drawn to face Gauff, world No 1 and defending WTA Finals champion Elena Rybakina, and Linda Noskova, who won her maiden Grand Slam singles title at Wimbledon this year.

Andreeva will avoid Pegula having been drawn alongside Aryna Sabalenka, Elina Svitolina and Karolina Muchova.

The WTA Finals is set to take place between November 8-15 at Indian Wells, before it moves to its new, permanent location of Charlotte, North Carolina in 2027.

The tournament had been hosted in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia for the past two seasons, with Gauff and Rybakina lifting the title in 2024 and 2025 respectively.
