Sports.title: Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football
Sports.content:
Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier.

Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments.

“Of course, we plan to submit documents,” the Sevastopol CEO Valery Chaly told local media last month. “According to the regulations we should advance to the next stage.” The RFU remains a member of Uefa and Fifa but there would be fresh calls for it to be ejected if Sevastopol’s ascent is not blocked. It is understood no decision about their potential admission has been made.

Football’s governing bodies were given a similar dilemma in 2023 when Sevastopol and another Crimean club, Rubin Yalta, were accepted into FNL 2B even though sides from the occupied territory have not been allowed to compete in Russia since its annexation in 2014.

The Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) asked Uefa and Fifa to consider ejecting Russia, alleging a “gross violation” of their statutes and Uefa’s ruling, made in 2014, that Crimean clubs must not compete in RFU-run events. Uefa claimed it would assess the situation but the authorities appeared to turn a blind eye, the RFU saying it had created a workaround by making FNL 2B an amateur competition that it did not operate. At the time, several clubs at that level contacted by the Guardian confirmed informally that they were fully professional. No such blurring of the lines exists for FNL 2A, which has never denied its clubs are professional.

That unwillingness to act led to escalation when, in April 2024, an imitation of the Ukrainian club Zorya Luhansk – whose home city in Donbas is illegally occupied by Russia – was admitted to FNL 2B. This year they were joined by a fake Shakhtar Donetsk, mimicking the current Champions League side who have been forced to play elsewhere since 2014. Five of the 15 teams who completed the recent FNL 2B group one season played in or claimed to represent occupied areas, the Simferopol-based club Kyzyltash Bakhchisaray completing the quintet.

View image in fullscreen FC Sevastopol’s logo at their home in Crimea. Photograph: Vasiliy Batanov/AFP/Getty Images

Should the RFS decide, of its own accord or under pressure from international bodies, to bar Sevastopol from promotion an even bigger flashpoint may await. The imitation Shakhtar finished runners-up in group 1, securing that spot by winning 2-0 at Sevastopol on the season’s final day last Saturday, and are next in line to go up. Unlike Sevastopol their home matches are played on Russian territory, in Taganrog, rather than an occupied area. The club is, however, registered to an address in Donetsk.

In October 2025 the UAF asked Uefa to review and explain the imitation clubs’ legal positions but, as with any assessment of the Crimean clubs’ participation, the results are still awaited. It warned of a“coordinated political attempt to legitimise the occupation and erase the identity of Ukrainian football”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Last month Russia competed in a Fifa-run event for the first time since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, finishing 19th in the new under-15 World Cup. Teams at under-15 and under-16 levels have continued to play in smaller Uefa development tournaments, largely against invited opponents on home soil, during the war in Ukraine.

None of Uefa, Fifa, the RFU, the FNL, Sevastopol or the imitation Shakhtar Donetsk offered comment when contacted by the Guardian.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo to be blocked from emotional Portugal farewell as he blindsides Jorge Jesus
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo to be blocked from emotional Portugal farewell as he blindsides Jorge Jesus

Portugal manager Jorge Jesus had planned to call-up Cristiano Ronaldo for the upcoming international break.

Ronaldo announced his retirement from the Portugal national team on Thursday after 23 years and 146 goals in 234 games.



3 Ronaldo scored was also Portugal captain for 19 years Credit: AFP

It follows a well publicised fallout between the 41-year-old and manager Jesus.

Ronaldo received a sanction of 30 days for walking out the national camp, which had already been served, and a fine of €255.

Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda told talkSPORT that Jesus had intended to call-up the five-time Ballon d’Or winner.



“Ronaldo knew that Jorge Jesus had his name on the list for tomorrow and Jorge Jesus was expecting to call Ronaldo for this next international break," Sepulveda said on Hawksbee and Jacobs.

“So Ronaldo wanted to make this statement because he thinks there are no conditions for him to return to the national team of Portugal while Jorge Jesus is the coach.



“He knows Jorge Jesus is going to stay more than one year and he knows that in one year Ronaldo probably is not going to be playing even football.”

No Ronaldo farewell?

Sepulveda revealed there will be no Portugal farewell for Cristiano Ronaldo while Jesus is the manager.



This is in stark contrast to the send-off that Lionel Messi got after announcing his retirement from the Argentina national team.

World Cup winner Messi played in front of tens of thousands of people in Buenos Aires in October for his 208th and final match.

Sepulveda said: “I can guarantee you that Ronaldo won't dress officially, let's say like that, in the Portuguese jersey again.

3 Jesus planned to call-up Ronaldo to the November international break Credit: AFP



“I can guarantee you that until Jorge Jesus leaves the national team of Portugal that last friendly game for everyone to say goodbye to Cristiano Ronaldo won't happen.”

He added: “The thing is, Ronaldo feels that he wanted to retire after the World Cup. He made that decision and then Pedro Proenca, the new president of the federation, with Jorge Jesus, they both convinced him to stay.

“In the head of Ronaldo, after they convinced him, they took the decision to make this to Ronaldo without defending him.”

What did Ronaldo say?

Ronaldo confirmed the news in a very lengthy and emotional social media post, with the caption 'Portugal will always be in me.'



"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team," he said.

"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.

3 Ronaldo's international career has etched him a permanent place in Portugal's history

"Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone - they are also made with the heart.



"A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end."

Sports.title: Tottenham can still re-sign Harry Kane despite massive new Bayern Munich deal
Sports.content:
Tottenham can still re-sign Harry Kane despite massive new Bayern Munich deal

Tottenham have been offered increased hope of possibly re-signing Harry Kane, despite his new Bayern Munich contract announcement.

The 2026 Ballon d'Or winner has extended his stay at Bayern to 2029 and will now earn around £400,000-a-week.



2 Kane has penned terms on a new deal at Bayern to 2029 following three years of consistent goalscoring success Credit: Getty

Kane has scored 156 goals in 161 appearances across all competitions since joining in 2023, an outstanding tally that confirms he is one of the best strikers in world football.

Once the terms of his new deal end, the England captain and legend will approach his 36th birthday and be in the latter stages of what is an iconic career.

However, whilst retirement will likely be considered at this point, he may have one last dance at former club Spurs before calling it quits.



As per the Daily Telegraph, the north Londoners have kept hold of their first-option matching rights on Kane despite his new Bayern deal.

Spurs negotiated these rights with Bayern before the finalisation of the £100million deal to sell him in August 2023.



This agreement covers his entire stint at the German club and is not affected by any contract changes or extensions.

The Spurs-Bayern agreement is said to remain active and be separate to Kane's extension.



Will Kane return to Spurs?

With 280 goals in 435 appearances, Kane became the all-time record scorer at Spurs during a glittering spell from 2009 to 2023.

He was their Player of the Year on three occasions and named in six different Premier League Team of the Year squads.

Kane is the English top flight's second-highest scorer on 213 goals, 47 shy of leader Alan Shearer.

2 Kane could still be set for a second spell at Spurs as they have retained their first-option matching rights Credit: Getty



And the forward's ex-boss Tim Sherwood hinted to talkSPORT that a return could well be on the cards.

"I think when he comes back, he's going to come back to a team he thinks can win. He's used to winning trophies now, he's enjoying his time over there at Bayern.

"I don't think he comes back to a team that he thinks can't win, so it narrows it down.

"He's not going to go to Chelsea, he's not going to go to Arsenal, so where is he actually going to end up?



"It's probably not going to be Man City, so you're only looking at Liverpool, Man United and possibly Tottenham.

"I mean, Tottenham have got more chance of winning something at the moment, as you look at it, than Man United certainly have."

Sports.title: Cesc Fabregas has little-known incentive to stay at Como despite inevitable exit for Premier League
Sports.content:
Cesc Fabregas has little-known incentive to stay at Como despite inevitable exit for Premier League

While Cesc Fabregas’ personal project at Como tempts him to remain in Italy, a romantic return to the Emirates Stadium feels all-but inevitable.

The former Arsenal and Chelsea player's side produced a stunning performance away to Lens as they put nine goals past the French club in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

3 Como are also the first team to score nine goals in an away European Cup match since Feyenoord won 9-0 at Olympiakos Nicosia in 1971 Credit: Getty

Having already defeated RB Leipzig and Manchester United, they have lifted themselves fourth in the league phase table. A 3-2 defeat to Feyenoord is their only stain on their stunning European campaign so far.

Como's rise in the last decade has been staggering, with the club playing in the fourth tier of Italian football as recently as 2019.

The Serie A side was taken over by the London-based media company Sent Entertainment which dramatically changed the trajectory of the club.

In 2022, Fabregas was revealed as a new Como player as the club sat in Serie B.

He invested a minority ownership share when he joined, partnering alongside former Barcelona teammate Thierry Henry with the exact percentage not being publicly disclosed.

Following the news of his retirement one year later, he was appointed the Italian side's under-19 and B-teams manager and was promoted to be the first-team's boss four months later on an interim basis.

In his first season in charge in 2023/24, he guided Como to promotion which became their first time in the top flight in 21 years.

Last season, he helped the Italian side secure European qualification for the first time in the club's history as they overtook AC Milan in Serie A on the final day.

The 39-year-old has rapidly become one of the most sought-after managerial minds in Europe since he transformed Como.

However, Italian sports reporter Greg Whelan believes the ex-Barcelona midfielder is committed to the project with the Italian club, for the foreseeable at least.

3 Fabregas' reputation continues to grow after Como's historic 9-1 win in the Champions League Credit: Getty

Whelan said: "He has done extremely well, his reputation stands before him now and he has spoken to other clubs.

"He spoke to Inter 15-16 months ago when [Simone] Izaghi left and I think Roma made a play for him as well at the time before [Gian Piero] Gasperini came in.

"But he said, ‘I am part of something at Como and I want to try and see it through’ and he did have a stake in the club when he joined as a player back in 2022, this is something that is very important to him. Where it goes and how long it takes is another question."

Fabregas to leave Como?

The Spaniard is contracted with Como until June 2028; however, reportedly he pushed to include a specific clause in his deal which allows him to leave on favourable financial terms if an offer arrives from one of his three former clubs (Arsenal, Chelsea, Barcelona).

Mikel Arteta recently signed a four-year contract extension which will keep him as manager at the Emirates until June 2030.

However, Whelan didn't rule out Fabregas working as a successor to Arteta.

3 Arteta's new Arsenal deal will see him earn almost £70,000-a-day Credit: Getty

He responded: "I think it’s inevitable that he will end up at a big club eventually, for sure.

"You only have to see the way Como play and the whole of Europe is seeing it, they play some of the best football in Serie A. If that’s not an advert for a head coach, I don’t know what is."

Sports.title: Why are there so few Premier League fixtures on Saturday
Sports.content:
Why are there so few Premier League fixtures on Saturday

It will go from feast to famine for Premier League fans this Saturday.

Top-flight supporters were treated to a rare jam-packed Saturday of action last weekend with eight games taking place.

3 Mikel Arteta's Arsenal play on Saturday but not many other teams are Credit: Getty

Chelsea got the day underway with a 2-0 win over Manchester United in the 12:30pm kick-off.

Brighton, Coventry, Bournemouth and Brentford then picked up wins in the five-strong 3pm slate.

Tottenham beat Crystal Palace at 5:30pm and Aston Villa and Fulham played out a 1-1 draw in the Saturday evening clash.

With more games on television than ever before, it’s quite unique to get such a busy single day in the Premier League schedule.

And the fixture gods have changed things up dramatically this weekend.

Why are there so few Premier League fixtures on Saturday

While last Saturday saw eight games held, this coming Saturday will see half that amount with just four matches in the schedule.

Everton vs Coventry kicks off Matchweek 10 on Friday night, live on talkSPORT.

From there, Leeds vs Tottenham is the lunchtime game - again live on talkSPORT - while Manchester City travel to Nottingham Forest for the 5:30pm game.

3 Brighton are back to Thursday - Sunday games Credit: Getty

There are then just two 3pm matches as Arsenal host Hull and Fulham entertain Newcastle.

The reason for the stripped back Saturday is to do with the return of European football this week.

Crystal Palace, Bournemouth, Sunderland and Brighton are all playing in Europe again on Thursday so top-flight rules prevent them from returning to action on Saturday.

Instead, those four teams will play on Sunday, with their games all scheduled for 2pm.

Brighton, who face Getafe in the Conference League on Thursday, host Brentford on Sunday.

Palace take on Hoffenheim in the Europa League in midweek before hosting Liverpool this weekend.

3 Another international break is coming up Credit: Getty

Similarly, Bournemouth face Sparta Prague away before then making the trip to Ipswich on Sunday and Sunderland host Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday before welcoming Chelsea to Wearside this weekend.

Clubs set for another break

Following a busy week for top-flight clubs, the Premier League will break for another set of international fixtures.

England take on Croatia and Spain in the Nations League next week before the domestic season returns on November 21.

And that Saturday will see normal service resume with seven fixtures scheduled including Man City vs Fulham and Newcastle vs Arsenal.

Sports.title: Unai Emery to ‘shut up’ Man United fans with new Aston Villa deal and win Premier League title
Sports.content:
Unai Emery to ‘shut up’ Man United fans with new Aston Villa deal and win Premier League title

Manchester United fans must give it a rest as Unai Emery looks set to commit his long-term future to Aston Villa.

That's according to Gabby Agbonlahor, although his talkSPORT colleague Simon Jordan has tipped the Spaniard to win a Premier League title - but not at Villa Park.

3 Villa are set to keep hold of Emery by offering him a new deal beyond 2029 Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands Emery will sign a new deal to keep him at Villa beyond the 2029 expiry date of his current contract following sustained success as their head coach.

The former Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain boss ended their 30-year wait for a major trophy by winning last season's Europa League and is in a second Champions League campaign.

With Michael Carrick struggling as the United head coach, Emery has been tipped as a potential successor should he be dismissed.

However, a new deal at Villa will surely end any prospect of him going to Old Trafford, and club legend Agbonlahor will be happy to see the back of the speculation.

Agbonlahor message to the 'idiots'

"He's a fantastic manager, and I'm so happy that this is going to shut up all the idiots," he said on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"'He should go to Man United... he should go there, because he could do what he did at Villa with Man United, he could bring these people', he doesn't want to go to Manchester United.

"Players might want to go because they can maybe pay more money. (Youri) Tielemans is there sitting on the bench, eating some humble pie.

"But Aston Villa can pay the same amount for a manager as Manchester United. The money he's going to be earning at Villa on his new contract, you're talking £16/17million-a-year.

"So, why would he leave? He's got a fantastic project, a club that loves him, the fans love him, the owners love him. Why would you go to a toxic football club in Manchester United that's a mess?"

Can Emery win the Premier League?

When reacting to Agbonlahor's question at the end of his passionate plea, former Crystal Palace owner Jordan stated: "Because you've got ambition."

3 Villa legend Agbonlahor sent a message to United fans amid the news of Emery's new contract as Villa boss Credit: talkSPORT

White and Jordan host Jim White said Emery has ambition to do well at Villa, but Jordan insisted: "Villa will not, while I've got a hole in my backside, win the Premier League, they won't win the Champions League.

"We might be able to have a street celebration like we did for Newcastle if Villa win the League Cup."

"Villa won't win the Premier League and won't win the Champions League under Unai Emery?" White asked.

"Unai Emery is capable of winning the Premier League I think, yeah," Jordan responded.

"But I think with the restrictions that are put on Aston Villa unfairly by the construction of the league and the finances that go around it, I think it's very difficult for them to do so."

On whether United would make a move for Emery if they part with Carrick, he replied: "I don't know if they'll move for Unai Emery because, if Unai Emery is signing a new contract, I think it's fantastic for Aston Villa and well done him for doing it.

3 Whilst Jordan doesn't think Villa can win the Premier League, he reckons Emery can do so elsewhere Credit: Getty

"He's been given a lot of support, he's been given a great job, they're a great football club. But it doesn't alter the parameters.

"What Jamie Carragher said ('Aston Villa will never be Manchester United'), that I fundamentally agree with and most sensible people do, rather than sensitive little souls up in Birmingham that somehow have got some right not to be observed upon."

Sports.title: Man United ‘sources’ reveal Michael Carrick will make huge selection call on Sunday
Sports.content:
talkSPORT host Andy Goldstein has been told that Michael Carrick will hand Shea Lacey his first-ever Premier League start against Aston Villa this weekend.

The 19-year-old, who made his first-team debut away to Villa last term, enjoyed a game-changing cameo in the win over Roma.



3 Academy graduate Lacey could be in line for first Premier League start on Sunday Credit: Getty

On Tuesday, Lacey was trusted to make only his third outing since scoring against Brighton in the Carabao Cup in September.

The teen impressed after his 75th-minute introduction, and grabbed an assist for Matheus Cunha's winner in the 3-2 comeback victory.

The result gave Man United their first win in ten matches, and seemingly rescued boss Carrick from getting his marching orders.



The Red Devils had been two goals down to Roma before their fightback, with protests against the club's ownership ongoing as well.

Man United are still in huge trouble in the Premier League, with the club only outside of the relegation zone in 17th on goal difference.



Shea Lacey to start against Aston Villa?

talkSPORT presenter Goldstein, who previously revealed that Bruno Fernandes would be dropped for United's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth for criticising Carrick's tactics in a post-match rant, has now revealed that Lacey is in line to start against Aston Villa.

He told Darren Bent on Drive: "I've heard, by the way, it's the same person that told me that Bruno Fernandes was going to be dropped, that Shea Lacey starts against Villa.



"How about that? He was so good for Man United [against Roma], and when the crowd watch him, they're on the edge of their seat.

"Genuinely, you can hear that 'gasp'."

3 Lacey's impactful cameo off the bench against Roma has shown he's ready to play a bigger part for Man United Credit: AFP

"I like Amad, but there's obviously something that we're missing with his game. Maybe his finishing's not that great," Goldstein added.

"Shea Lacey looks like a really, really good player."

Lacey, previously dubbed by United fans as 'the Scouse Lionel Messi', only made his senior debut under Ruben Amorim in December.



Fittingly, that was against Unai Emery's Villa, having played six minutes as a second-half sub in the 2-1 loss, days before Christmas.

The England Under-20 international also featured in both matches during Darren Fletcher's short stint as interim boss earlier this year.

Lacey has since hit several senior milestones under Carrick this term, opening his goalscoring account on his first start against Brighton.

3 Lacey, who is yet to start a Premier League game, has only made two top-flight appearances this term Credit: Getty



Man United's No.31 had only a week earlier made his first appearance in the Champions League against Sabah at Old Trafford.

But he has only made two cameo outings in the Premier League this term, the first of which came in the opening-day defeat to Hull City.

Lacey was also a late introduction in the Bournemouth loss, with his only appearances in a senior win coming in the Champions League.

Following his first senior assist for Cunha's second goal, the Liverpudlian then filled in at full-back after the Brazilian's red card.



“It was new, I haven’t done it before,” Shea said about his newfound role, to MUTV.

“But just to see games out like that, sometimes you’ve got to do those things, and I thought it worked in the end; it worked well.”

Sports.title: Top five pound-for-pound managers in the Premier League right now
Sports.content:
Top five pound-for-pound managers in the Premier League right now

With the era of Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp over, who are the current outstanding managers in the Premier League?

Well, talkSPORT's Max Scott has managed to pick out who he believes are the leading bosses currently in charge in the top flight.



6 Guardiola is one of the greatest Premier League managers of all-time - but who are the best right now? Credit: Getty

In the latest edition of his weekly Mount Rushmore or Less series, he has whittled his list down to the top five in the division.

But why five when Mount Rushmore famously features just four of the most influential US presidents? That's why it's Mount Rushmore or Less - sometimes, four simply just isn't enough.

So, here are the best current Premier League managers...

Arteta on his way to all-timer status

"It's simple, it's obvious, it's Mikel Arteta."

Scott selected Arsenal manager Arteta to take a spot in his list, lauding him for his achievements amid constant backlash.



"Like him or loathe him, like their brand of football or not, Arteta has been an absolute revolutionary force for Arsenal," he added.

"It's his first senior job in management, taking a club where fans were fuming at the Kroenkes, fuming at what had happened at the back end of Arsene Wenger's tenure.



"And in a time of Man City's fraudulent dominance, he finds a way to win the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years.

"Yes, there's an argument he should have done it earlier, and I think the accusations of Arsenal's mentality or the language of them 'bottling it' has truth to it - but he put all of that to bed.



"The strength of feeling that Arteta has managed to claw back, the passion within the fanbase, has to be respected, it's absolutely incredible.

6 Arteta led Arsenal to their first Premier League title in 22 years last season and could well have his side on track for another this term Credit: Getty

"People might not like his football, but it's effective.

"Arsenal should have won the Champions League last season and they could well go and win it this season. They're a fabulous, effective football team.

"What he's achieved, he doesn't get enough respect for, as people might dislike his antics on the touchline, dislike fans on social media or don't like their brand of football."



He then concluded: "Arguably, if he carries on at this rate, he will be in the conversation soon as one of the best Premier League managers of all time."

English football's Robin Hood

Up next is 'the man who pulls rabbits out of hats', Unai Emery.

Scott explained: "Aston Villa has been created in the image of Emery.

6 Villa boss Emery achieved European glory with Aston Villa and has them challenging the Big Six despite huge losses to his squad Credit: Getty

"He took over the football club when they were threatened with relegation back to the Championship and the fact that he has managed to make them European champions once again, regulars in the Champions League, getting Big Six scalps, is probably one of the best stories in the Premier League in recent years.



"He's done this with two hands tied behind his back with these draconian financial regulations limiting what Aston Villa can do. The ladder's been pulled up by Chelsea and Man City.

"Unai Emery is like a freedom fighter, like a Robin Hood, stealing from the rich and giving to the poor Midlands fans, who have been bereft of a team that once conquered Europe.

"He's gone and done it again and I know it's the Europa League, but the fact he's managed to do it is absolutely unbelievable.

"And this season, regaining the energy to reinvent and reinvigorate a side that had their heart ripped out of it - Emi Martinez, Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa.



"The fact they are playing so much brilliant football now with new signings is all down to Unai Emery."

What is Mount Rushmore? The faces of George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln are carved into the stone in South Dakota, chosen for their representation of the most important events in the United States' history. As a result, fans use the idea to create their own version to list the most influential or iconic games and people that define their selected categories. Here, though, talkSPORT argues five is not enough, so more or less this is Mount Rushmore.

A controversial pick

Next up in this Mount Rushmore or Less is former Crystal Palace and now Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner.

"This shouldn't be controversial, and if I wasn't saying this as a lifelong Forest fan, I think people would probably have no issue with it," Scott began.

"Oliver Glasner is one of the best Premier League managers right now, he has to be in it.



"Not because of what he's done at Forest where wins have been hard to come by - but he can't finish Liam Delap's dinner, so we won't blame it on him.

"The only silverware Crystal Palace had was in their canteen when Glasner came along and he's gone and got them the Conference League, the FA Cup... such a storied history of that competition.

"Just because he might have got off to a slow start at Forest, it doesn't take away what he achieved at Crystal Palace. A side that had no major silverware in their history.

6 Glasner has made a slow start at Forest, but his achievements with Crystal Palace have done wonders for his reputation in Europe Credit: Getty



"Everyone was shocked he came to Forest and yes, he probably came to Forest as he was getting paid as one of the best five managers in the division. But it's because he is.

"If he'd have gone to Bayern Munich or a big European club like Manchester United, nobody would have been surprised... we've got to put respect on his name and we can't look at recency bias."

The antidote to the 'boring' Premier League

"This is where it gets difficult because we've not got some of these huge names at big football clubs."

Scott admitted that after the first three, managers were harder to select, but he found another in Andoni Iraola.



He explained: "What he achieved at Bournemouth, qualifying them for Europe, absolutely unbelievable.

"Some people will have said: 'Well he's not managed at a big club'. He has now, he's at Liverpool and the fact that someone like Liverpool went for Iraola, not, for example, a Fabian Hurzeler, says everything that you need.

6 Scott thinks Iraola's entertaining style and impressive start with Liverpool means he has to be one of the best in the Premier League Credit: Getty

"If you need big club bias to validate how important and how good a manager is, well you've got it, because Liverpool employed him.



"The brand of football he plays, the intensity of which he plays, the attacking nature of his sides, makes it one of the most entertaining brands of football in the Premier League in an age that the Premier League can be accused of being a little bit boring.

"Andoni Iraola is the antidote to that."

Andrews and Brentford 'a breath of fresh air'

Honourable mentions were handed out for Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca and Brighton manager Hurzeler.

However, Scott landed on a different man to finish up his Mount Rushmore or Less, saying: "I've got to give it to Keith Andrews.

"Last season, he was pound-for-pound manager of the season. At the start, everyone was laughing at Brentford employing a set-piece coach, everybody had them to go down.



6 Brentford manager Andrews was doubted by almost everyone, but he has quickly become one of the best managers in the top flight with Brentford Credit: Getty

"And they were a point or two off European qualification, and this season they have been a breath of fresh air.

"Notwithstanding the pressure that was on him, but he succeeded Brentford's greatest ever manager in Thomas Frank and he's taken them, no doubt, to another level.

"He's got Igor Thiago a Brazil call-up and made him look like one of the best strikers in the Premier League.



"I love the way he communicates, I love what he's building at Brentford, that it's disrupting the establishment.

"I sincerely hope they qualify for European football, I think last season, not getting it could have been a blessing in disguise.

"It's all down to Keith Andrews, I think he's magnificent...I think he will get picked up by a bigger club, but he's done a terrific job and rightly deserves to be in the Mount Rushmore-or-less."

Sports.title: ‘Stop moaning’ – Arsenal have no excuses as Christmas fixture reality exposed
Sports.content:
‘Stop moaning’ – Arsenal have no excuses as Christmas fixture reality exposed

Gabby Agbonlahor has claimed Arsenal can have no complaints about fixture lists after organisers served up a festive treat.

The reigning Premier League champions and current leaders will play nine consecutive matches in London during December and January.

3 The Gunners are three points clear at the top of the Premier League Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta's men have already played away at Villa Park, Anfield, the Amex and even the Allianz Arena during a tricky start to the season.

However, Arsenal's fixtures flip into a highly favourable run during what is typically the toughest part of any Premier League campaign.

And talkSPORT's Agbonlahor claimed that he doesn't want to hear any complaints from anyone within the club about the schedule.

Declan Rice pulled out of the England squad in September over load management concerns, having confirmed during the World Cup that he'd been battling nerve pain in his hamstring since December.

Arsenal's fixtures in December

"It is non-stop," Agbonlahor admitted to Alan Brazil on Breakfast.

"But when you've got a squad like Arsenal, I don't wanna hear no moaning; they've got so many players they can rotate, and he's moaning about fixtures and stuff.

"Here's Arsenal's fixtures in December: Brentford away, Spurs away, Real Madrid at home, Bournemouth at home, Man United at home, Palace away, Fulham away, all in London; they don't play out of London in December.

"So shut up and stop moaning; you've spent a billion pounds, you've got one of the best squads in world football.

"Your squad's that good you had to send [Ethan] Nwaneri out on loan because he couldn't get into the squad of players.

3 Arteta led Arsenal to their first Premier League title in 24 years last season and could well have his side on track for another this term Credit: Getty

Agbonlahor continued on talkSPORT: "Stop moaning; you've got enough players for your positions that you've got.

"It's football; they've got 25, 26 top international players, get on with it. What about the teams that have got 19, 20 players? Come on!"

Arsenal don't play outside of London after a trip to Newcastle on November 21 for nearly two whole months.

Their run of 12 matches in the capital across league and Europe finally comes to an end away to Hull City on January 16.

By that time, the Gunners could be flying towards claiming back-to-back titles, with Agbonlahor declaring the title race is already over.

"Arsenal have conceded five goals. Three of those were against Brighton. They're fantastic defensively.

3 Agbonlahor claimed Arsenal have one of the best squads in world football, so have no excuse not to cope with the fixture list Credit: talkSPORT

"Liverpool didn't have a shot on target. So defensively, Arsenal are the best in the league by a country mile.

"That's what will win them the Premier League. I look at Manchester City.

"[Gianluigi] Donnarumma - I don't know what's happened to him. PSG have made the right decision on him.

"I look at [Matheus] Nunes. He's not a right back; he's filling in there. You can tell when you watch him. His positioning isn't right at times."

Sports.title: Newcastle star Amar Dedic sparks six-car police swoop after being spotted with a BOW AND ARROWS in Northumberland beauty spot before weapon is seized
Sports.content:
Newcastle United star Amar Dedic was at the centre of a major police operation after he was spotted carrying a bow and arrows at a Northumberland beauty spot – with at least SIX patrol cars involved in the search for the £30million defender.

The Bosnia international sparked alarm when a concerned member of the public reported seeing him and a friend walking with the weapon near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the area in Harlow Hill, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were finally intercepted around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Sources have described the dramatic swoop on Dedic's vehicle before officers searched the car and seized a bow and arrows, with the 24-year-old questioned about his activities.

In a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic. It is understood the pair were in the area by chance and stopped to offer assistance.

After speaking to the two men, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public, with police subsequently stating that the equipment was believed to have been intended for recreational use.

Amar Dedic played in Newcastle's 1-0 defeat by Everton on Monday evening

Dedic signed from Benfica on a five-year deal this summer, and was reunited with former Salzburg coach Matthias Jaissle

Dedic was spotted with a crossbow off Military Road, the 61-mile B6318 in Northumberland

However, enquiries remain ongoing into the incident, which happened on Wednesday afternoon. It is understood that Dedic and his friend had fired some arrows while in the countryside, although it remains unclear what they were aiming at. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in the UK.

Dedic joined Newcastle from Benfica during the summer and has impressed at right back despite the club's difficult start to the season.

Daily Mail Sport understands he will not face disciplinary action from Newcastle over the incident, although there is a feeling that the player was naive to believe he could walk around the countryside carrying such weaponry.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: 'Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

'Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows. At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing.'

Dedic is expected to be available for Saturday's Premier League trip to Fulham, where Newcastle will attempt to halt a run of four defeats in five matches across all competitions.

Sports.title: Ex-Man United star Clayton Blackmore is forced to apologise for encouraging Mason Greenwood to 'come home to us' after winger beat Liverpool with Fenerbahce
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United footballer Clayton Blackmore has apologised after being criticised on social media for asking Mason Greenwood to 'come home' to Old Trafford.

Greenwood, 25, played a pivotal role for Fenerbahce during their 3-2 victory over Manchester United's archrivals Liverpool in the Champions League on Wednesday, scoring the Turkish giants' first-half equaliser.

The English forward broke through the ranks as a youngster at Manchester United and looked destined to become a key long-term player, but his career spiralled after he was arrested and charged in 2022 with suspected attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault causing actual bodily harm.

Although those charges were subsequently dropped by the Crown Prosecution Service in February 2023, United decided Greenwood could not continue to ply his trade at Old Trafford after undertaking an internal six-month investigation.

Since his exit, which came after disgruntled Manchester United supporters groups heaped pressure on the club to cut ties with the forward, Greenwood has represented Spanish club Getafe on loan, French giants Marseille and Turkish side Fenerbahce, who he joined this summer for a reported €39million (£33.27million).

Blackmore, who played for Manchester United between 1982 and 1994, was met with backlash on Thursday after he heaped praise on Greenwood for his role in Fenerbahce's 3-2 win over Liverpool.

Mason Greenwood (centre) celebrates after scoring in Fenerbahce's 3-2 win over Liverpool

Former Man United star Clayton Blackmore pleaded for Grenwood to 'come home to us'

The 62-year-old Welshman apologised after his post was met with a furious backlash online

Greenwood's Manchester United career ended after he was charged with attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault causing actual bodily harm in 2022

'Well done Mason Greenwood beating Liverpool. Come home to us please,' the Welshman, 62, posted on X.

Two hours later, after receiving a slew of disparaging comments on the platform, he said: 'Sorry I've offended anyone but I heard he had been cleared of any wrongdoing I apologise to everyone I've upset with my comments like I said I thought he had been cleared of everything and he’s had a baby with his girlfriend. Big sorry.'

Blackmore had previously come under fire for expressing his sadness that both Greenwood and Angel Gomes, another former English prodigy who was sold to Lille by Manchester United in 2020, no longer play for the club.

When the duo were both playing at Marseille last season, Blackmore said on X: 'Good to see Angel Gomez and Mason Greenwood score Marseille in first 26 mins. Sad they're not still at United.'

After landing himself in hot water with the post, he clarified to those commenting: 'Sorry I understand what you're saying but sometimes everything you hear is not always the truth why did his girlfriend stay with him I'm just looking at the football side.'

He later doubled down and wrote: 'Sorry didn't see or hear any of that I will do my home work next time just looking at it from the football side sorry if I've offended anyone especially his girlfriend and her family.'

While there was noisy resistance to Greenwood joining Marseille in the summer of 2025, he found no such opposition in Turkey, where one prominent journalist claimed 95 per cent of the population would not know or care about his past.

He didn't face any questions about the dropped charges or his public image in his first press conference and outside of brief post-match comments, has not conducted any interviews of note.

Greenwood has been hiding from the limelight a record signing would usually bask in, especially in the football-crazed city of Istanbul.

He found a home in a district called Sarıyer, a favourite among footballers, who largely live in gated communities.

Greenwood is said to count team-mates N'Golo Kante and Marco Asensio as neighbours and was seen in a rare online post after securing his new home, posing with the all-female team of estate agents who helped him with the purchase.

The former United starlet completed his move to Turkish giants Fenerbahce in the summer

Blackmore had previously come under fire for expressing his sadness at Greenwood leaving

Since the big-money move, Greenwood has only posted a handful of times on his Instagram profile, all of which were generic action shots after matches.

His latest offering came after Fenerbahce's stunning win over Liverpool, as he posted a gallery of photographs celebrating in the club's yellow and black jersey.

His partner, Harriet, 26, is also selective with how much she shares from their new life.

She only has four posts in total, with around 20 photos in each 'round-up', offering a glimpse into the high-life, though Greenwood himself only appears twice.

One of the images is of him looking exhausted in hospital at the birth of their second daughter in 2023 and another shows him holding hands with their eldest, Summer, who is three.

Sports.title: EDDIE JONES: This is what happened inside this week's Windsor summit where the world's best coaches decided how the game should be played. From what Steve Borthwick said, there's one thing England will focus on - it won't be running rugby!
Sports.content:
At the beginning of this week, all of us coaches in the Nations Championship gathered at a hotel in Windsor to discuss the shape of the game.

We were split into panels with the referees to chat through officiating matters and how we want the games to be controlled and managed.

Steve Borthwick and South Africa supremo Rassie Erasmus were given the maul as their specialist subject, so they took a couple of stools out in front of us and got into the topic. I'll come back to that but you couldn’t find two more different blokes. I don’t think they’re the next Ant and Dec!

Usually the teams ranked No 1 and No 2 in the world are the loudest when we all get together and this week was no exception. Rassie and New Zealand boss Dave Rennie had a fair bit to say and everyone files in behind that and I said my bit as Japan coach.

I honestly think World Rugby missed a trick by not bringing cameras to show all the coaches in the same room discussing the laws of the game. It would have made great TV.

These meetings are interesting because everyone goes in with different agendas. I always remember one before the 2003 World Cup. Clive Woodward was coaching England and I was coaching Australia.

England boss Steve Borthwick had his say on mauls when all us coaches got together to discuss officiating in the Nations Championship with the referees

South Africa supremo Rassie Erasmus joined Borthwick - they are not exactly the next Ant and Dec though!

We used to play a few decoy runners at the time and Clive accused us of obstruction. He turned up with this massive presentation, all shining and sparkling, and we got into a pretty robust debate. In the end, the referees backed us to do it legally. You could say the Australians won that battle – but England won the World Cup!

This week, Borthwick went in with an agenda around the maul. It’s gone through quite a considerable law interpretation change, making it harder to stop the drive of powerful attacking teams.

England are heavily in favour of that. They want to keep the status quo, while teams like Japan, who aren’t as strong, want to see a bit of a change.

Reading between the lines, that’s one area England will be focusing on this autumn. It’s created a lot of tries in the PREM. The tries have come thick and fast in English club rugby but that won’t translate to the international game.

Northampton against Bath finished 71-48 last month. Given there are around 35 minutes of ball-in-play time, that’s almost four points every minute. That’s not good to watch.

I don’t think we’ll be seeing 120-point Test matches. Look at English Test cricket. ‘Bazball’ was not successful. The best teams in the world have that balance between their attack and defence. At the moment, the advantage is with the attacking team and we’re seeing a lot of tries.

Around the goal-line, referees have only really been officiating the defending team. We’ve seen a lot of supporting players going off their feet in attack to secure the ball and I think that will be tidied up in these Tests. The PREM teams have been scoring bucket-loads of tries but Test rugby is different. It’s more intense and the defences are better.

In most sports around the world, defences have become more aggressive. If you think about football's Premier League, the best teams are much more aggressive, pressing the ball. Rugby is no different. South Africa have made an art form out of it.

With Maro Itoje leading the way, England have a very impressive pack but after five defeats in seven, they will be looking to sharpen up their attack

If you look at South Africa, they've got two superb centres. If there’s any sort of fracture in the opposition's defence line, World Cup winner Damian de Allende can find it

After five defeats in seven, England will be looking to sharpen up their attack. They look like they need to develop a better way of playing off kick return.

With Ellis Genge, Maro Itoje, George Martin, Tom Curry and Jamie George, they have the nucleus of a very good pack. It’s the backline where they’ve got major issues. There’s no one in the centres saying: 'Right, pick me!' There’s no Manu Tuilagi who you simply cannot ignore.

If you look at South Africa, they've got two superb centres. If there’s any sort of fracture in the opposition's defence line, Damian de Allende can find it. He's got great feet, he's strong and he just suits the South African system.

Who can do that for England? Seb Atkinson looks like a handy player but can he make that jump to world class? That’s what he needs to show now.

Henry Slade's proven himself over a long period of time to be a good Test player. When he was younger, he certainly had great running skills. We haven't seen much of that recently. Maybe he’s lost that pace or maybe he’s just not getting the opportunities to use it.

You need someone at 13 who can convert opportunities into points. I’ve seen Will Joseph play a little bit for Gloucester. When I was England boss, we took him on tour to Australia and gave him his first cap back in 2022.

He’s always looked like a player who can really make it at Test level. He's big, strong and fast. He probably hasn't matured as fast as you’d like but he looks like he can make it.

Outside of Fin Smith and Tommy Freeman, it’s quite hard to pick England’s backline. Alex Mitchell looked like he would be the Test No 9 for a long time but he’s consistently injured. Manny Feyi-Waboso is dynamite but he’s injury prone, too.

Outside of Fin Smith and Tommy Freeman (above), I find it quite hard to pick England’s backline

Manny Feyi-Waboso is dynamite but, like scrum-half Alex Mitchell, he's injury-prone

Full-back is a conundrum. Do they go for a sturdy No 15 like Freddie Steward or a second playmaker like George Furbank? Furbank is another who is injured all the time. That’s a problem for English rugby. Their players play too much. They don’t get enough rest and recovery and that’s hurting them.

The RFU have given Borthwick full support for the World Cup now. And rightly so. They have got to give him all the support to get the players right. They need to find out who is going to be in the tent and who is going to be outside of it because the clock is ticking.

Four years ago, when I was coaching England, we hadn't developed the attack to where we needed it to be at this point of the cycle. We were a very good kicking team.

At times we were a good attacking team, particularly when we had Manu. When we didn’t have Manu, we had to find other ways of trying to get forward and most of that revolved around kicking. The grand plan was to develop a better attacking game for the World Cup but the RFU got rid of me and we never got there.

England are a high kicking team at the moment. If Smith weren't fit to play, I suspect they would have picked George Ford at No 10. They don't like to play a lot out of their own half. They seem to be very strict about the number of rucks they play. They want to keep the number of jackal opportunities for the opposition to a minimum.

These games are important but teams will be thinking, 'Right, what do I need to do for the World Cup?' Maybe that is part of Borthwick’s thinking but the fans don’t like to hear that.

England versus Australia at Twickenham in November is usually a tight game. England’s preparation has been minimal, while Australia are coming in on the back of the Bledisloe Cup. Their new coach, Les Kiss, has given them a bit of a lift and guys like massive prop Taniela Tupou are on form. At his best, Tupou is a force of nature, but England should have an advantage at set-piece.

Australia are struggling at 10 with Carter Gordon injured. Declan Meredith and Ben Donaldson are good players but they lack that real creativity of a Test No 10. Australia could struggle to score enough points, so I’m backing England to sneak home.

Full-back is a conundrum for England. Do they go for a sturdy No 15 like Freddie Steward or a second playmaker like Harlequins' George Furbank (pictured)

Australia are struggling at No 10 with Carter Gordon injured. Declan Meredith (pictured) and Ben Donaldson are good players but they lack that real creativity of a Test No 10

WHY ENGLAND IGNORED EDWARDS

There’s been a lot of talk about Shaun Edwards joining the Argentina coaching team. He’s a hugely successful English defence coach but he’s never had the chance to coach his country in men’s rugby.

I had a meeting with Shaun in 2020 but he was already in the process of being offered the French job. We were keen on bringing him in but the timing wasn’t right.

Particularly in international coaching, everyone says you should get this person or that person. But sometimes your window of need doesn’t match up to contract situations.

Borthwick is now in his second rotation of coaching staff so he probably wants to cement those guys in for the World Cup. Generally speaking, it's pretty hard to bring a bloke in 12 months before the sport's biggest tournament.

DUO DOWN UNDER WOULD BE FINE RECRUITS

We recently had Justin Holbrook, the Newcastle Knights rugby league coach, come and spend some time in camp with Japan. It was great to pick the brains of someone from Australia’s thriving NRL competition.

They’ve got a good English winger called Dominic Young. He’s from Huddersfield originally and he’d be an incredible union player. He’s big, good in the air, fast, aggressive. Along with Herbie Farnworth, I think he would be a top-class recruit for English rugby union.

Dominic Young (pictured scoring in the Rugby League World Cup) would be a fine pick-up for Borthwick's side

AT LAST, ABSURD KNOCK-ON RULE IS CHANGED

Intentional knock-ons were a big talking point at our coaching meeting. We’ve been through a period where if you stuck out your hand or tried to catch the ball and you didn't catch it, it was almost automatically a yellow card.

Everything was deemed intentional. It was quite absurd. Now I think we've got to the realisation that you can stick out one hand to try to catch the ball.

Some of the best interceptors, like Cheslin Kolbe, come in late, stick out their hand and try to knock the ball up. South Africa defend high so they go for intercepts more. Kolbe is a genius at it.

A good player can just anticipate the flight of the ball. It comes down to the ability to see what the passer is doing, where they’re looking to pass the ball, and then find the right time for the intercept.

South Africa winger Bryan Habana was superb at it, too. You need exceptional speed, meaning you can accelerate on to the ball and time your run. There was a really good agreement for this autumn that unless the motion is hitting the ball down, then it's not an intentional knock-on.
