Sports.title: LIV Golf is dead: Lawyers confirm winding down process in bankruptcy court as last-gasp $300m revival fails
Sports.content:
LIV Golf is dead: Lawyers confirm winding down process in bankruptcy court as last-gasp $300m revival fails

LIV Golf is shutting down after a tumultuous five-year, $5 billion saga that tore golf in two.

Some of golf's biggest names, including Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson, Phil Mickelson and Brooks Koepka, signed mega-money deals to turn their back on the PGA Tour.

But the future of the breakaway tour has been in doubt ever since Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced earlier this year that it would stop funding LIV Golf beyond the 2026 season.

The PIF ​had spent more than $5 billion since the rebel tour launched in 2022. It was hoped that, with new investment, LIV 2.0 could survive without being bankrolled by the Middle East.

LIV Golf's lawyers confirmed in a hearing in New Jersey on Thursday, however, that the entity was shifting its plans from restructure to full liquidation. 'We believe the wind down path is the best path,' attorney Matthew Williams said, per Golfweek, with the league slated to begin liquidating assets from Monday.

In a statement, LIV later confirmed it 'intends to transition to an orderly wind-down of its operations' claiming it is 'the most responsible path forward for the League at this time.' But LIV 'will remain open to, and continue to consider, any value-maximizing alternatives with third parties that may arise.'

LIV Golf's lawyers confirmed on Thursday that league was shifting plans to full liquidation

The Saudi Public Investment Fund pulled its massive funding in LIV Golf earlier this year

It comes after BC Partners Credit decided to drop its $300 million backing of a new iteration of the league.

After the Saudi PIF announced plans to cut funding, the league's 2026 season ended earlier than expected due to financial difficulties.

In September, the league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September, with BC Partners committing to investing around $300 million as long as certain conditions were met.

But they had a deadline to show it had enough player support for a 2027 league and reports emerged on Wednesday that BC Partners had shelved its backing due to a lack of player commitments.

According to Sports Business Journal, none of DeChambeau, Johnson, Joaquin Niemann or Cameron Smith had signed up, while other big names including Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton had declared they would not return.

In fact, only four players had publicly committed - Cameron Tringale, Richard Bland, Brendan Steele and Ben Campbell.

Speaking to Bunkered last month, BC chief, Ted Goldthorpe, said: 'The players are everything. They're our partners and they're very, very important to our future.'

The league, originally run by Greg Norman, spent more than $5 billion. But a few months after the start of the Iran war, PIF changed its investment strategy in April and said it would no longer pay for LIV Golf after the 2026 season.

Some of golf's biggest names - including Dustin Johnson - signed mega-money deals with LIV

In a statement to The Athletic on Thursday, BC Partners said: '[We] supported a transaction that aligned the interests of players and investors, offering a credible path toward building a sustainable future for LIV Golf.

'While there was great support for the league, we are disappointed that mutually acceptable terms could not be reached among the various stakeholders.

'We commend LIV Golf’s management for their tireless efforts and thank the players who supported the future of LIV and engaged constructively throughout.

We wish them every success as they continue their careers.'

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk is spot on: Liverpool's brittle defence leaves them looking like a vulnerable mess - it is unsustainable and MUST be fixed, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Liverpool's defensive woes are not sustainable, insists skipper Virgil van Dijk who says the team cannot accept losing in the way they did at Fenerbahce.

The Reds lost 3-2 having twice led in Istanbul, with individual errors and lapses in concentration costing them.

Andoni Iraola’s men have now suffered back-to-back defeats after also losing to Arsenal – and they have conceded three goals in each of their last three European games, against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce.

When this statistic was put to Van Dijk, he said: ‘(Our defending) is definitely not sustainable. That’s why it is a very disappointing night, for many reasons but definitely the goals we conceded and the manner we conceded them as well. There is work to do.

‘It is very, very tough. Three set pieces as well. We have been very good at them so far this season but we switched off and were not ready for the first and second balls. Yeah, it is a tough one to take.

‘I mentioned after the last game, we as a group have to go through good moments but also lesser good moments. That will only form a bigger bond, it will be only beneficial.

Liverpool suffered a disappointing 3-2 Champions League loss to Fenerbahce on Wednesday

Captain Virgil van Dijk insisted Liverpool's poor defending is not 'sustainable' after the game

‘No one wants to lose games especially how we did today but it should only help us in the near future. We should not accept losing, especially in the manner we did today.’

Asked if he was angry, the Dutchman said: ‘Yes. But I didn’t show it today because everyone looked disappointed and they have a reason to be, they should be disappointed. We cannot lose in the manner we did today. But we did that and it is down to Fenerbahce as well.’

Analysis: Reds' defence is a mess

By LEWIS STEELE

Van Dijk is right. The defence has been all over the place at times this season – especially in Europe.

Iraola thought he had won the game with a masterstroke triple substitution just after the hour mark when Cody Gakpo assisted Alexander Isak two minutes after the pair joined Florian Wirtz in entering the field.

But in trying to win the game – which is commendable – Iraola left the back door open. It felt ajar all night as Fenerbahce continually had joy down the flanks.

Van Dijk was asked if the deafening atmosphere of the Istanbul crowd played a part and said: ‘It is very difficult for everyone on the pitch because you can’t communicate easily.’

That could be an excuse but these players are world class and cannot put too much blame on the atmosphere.

Jeremy Jacquet has been imperious since joining from Rennes but the Frenchman had his first bad game in a Liverpool shirt, while Van Dijk was not too much better.

Milos Kerkez (above) and Kostas Tsimikas are proving a serious problem at left back

Leaky Liverpool's defensive record November 3: Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool October 20: Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal October 14: LASK 3-6 Liverpool September 9: Liverpool 2-1 Atletico Madrid *In the Champions League this season

Alisson, too, has left questions to be asked over his performances of late. After giving the ball away cheaply for Arsenal’s winner on Sunday, he was at fault for Fenerbahce’s decisive goal by dilly-dallying over whether to come for a cross. He should have gobbled it up.

But the real problem is at full back. Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas are not good enough – not now, anyway. That should be first on the priority list in future transfer windows.

Ronald Araujo, rested on the night, was missed.

The approach of ‘you can score, we will score more’ has been used – intentionally or not – in most European games this term. When it comes off, as it did in 6-3 and 4-3 wins over LASK and Villarreal respectively, it is exciting.

When it doesn’t, Liverpool just look a vulnerable mess. Work to do for Iraola ahead of a trip to Selhurst Park and Crystal Palace on Sunday, where Pierre Sage is fighting for his life.

Sports.title: No more excuses, England - Steve Borthwick's side must be bold, brave and adventurous this autumn... or kiss goodbye to their World Cup dreams
Sports.content:
The presence of top British sprinter Amy Hunt at England camp this week felt appropriate – because Steve Borthwick and his players face the equivalent of a 100-metre dash to put themselves in genuine contention to win the World Cup.

With less than a year to go until the next global showpiece in Australia, England have significant work to do in a short period of time. This month’s Nations Championship matches are vital. Genuine signs of progress have to be seen now – or England can pretty much kiss goodbye to their dreams of glory Down Under.

There can be no excuses either. England have everything they need to be successful – the player quality, squad depth, financial clout and backroom resources.

Borthwick and his players lack for nothing. Now, they must deliver. England enter their November Tests against Australia, Japan and New Zealand ranked fifth in the world. They are World Cup outsiders – a team with hopes of taking down the mighty South Africa, New Zealand and France, but only a small chance of actually doing so.

For that to change, England need to not only string a run of victories together, but also show the team’s loyal supporters they have a clear identity.

England can win the World Cup. But the clock is ticking.

England have everything they need to be successful – the player quality, squad depth, financial clout and backroom resources. Steve Borthwick (right) and his players lack for nothing

Team GB sprinter Amy Hunt came into England's camp on Wednesday to meet Maro Itoje and Co - now Borthwick's side must fire the starting gun on their World Cup assault

Ahead of a must-win game with the Wallabies, Tommy Freeman and Joe Heyes – both expected to start at Twickenham on Sunday – expressed ‘full confidence’ in the team’s direction of travel. RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney placed his full faith in Borthwick for the foreseeable, extending his head coach's contract to the middle of 2028 regardless of what happens in the next 12 months.

‘We're committed to Steve, we believe in what he's doing,’ said Sweeney. ‘We had a difficult Six Nations this year, we accept that, but we just want to see continued progress. We're backing him to get that done.’

Sweeney’s statement could be considered a means of taking the pressure off Borthwick. His job is safe, regardless of what happens in the months to come.

But it could actually increase the expectation. After England’s worst ever Six Nations this year ended in a fifth-place finish and a first defeat by Italy, Sweeney and the RFU suits will look foolish if England fall further adrift of the world’s top-ranked sides in the weeks to come. That cannot be allowed to happen.

‘We have been a bit up and down. We want results,’ Northampton wing Freeman admitted. ‘It’s fine margins in international rugby. It's all about winning. If we lose a couple of games, we're not going to do very well at the World Cup – that’s how the outside might view it.

'It might upset confidence, but we’re always going with the plan. We’ll be very focused on performance.’

After England’s disastrous Six Nations, the summer was slightly better – wins over Fiji and Argentina following a defeat by South Africa. But there can be no doubt that in the past 12 months, England have not been the sum of their parts, losing five of their last seven Tests.

That has to change this month and Borthwick, thankfully, has reinforced that message to his players. There are just three campaigns and 12 matches until England begin their World Cup bid.

After a disastrous Six Nations, England were thumped in South Africa in July - but the likes of Tommy Freeman (left) are adamant the team is on the right track

There can be no doubt that in the past 12 months, England have not been the sum of their parts, losing five of their last seven Tests

WORLD CUP COUNTDOWN 2026 Nations Championship Sunday, Twickenham Australia Nov 14, Twickenham Japan Nov 21, Twickenham New Zealand Nov 27-29, Twickenham Finals weekend 2027 Six Nations Feb 5, Dublin Ireland Feb 14, Twickenham France Feb 20, Twickenham Italy Mar 6, Cardiff Wales Mar 13, Twickenham Scotland 2027 World Cup warm-ups September (dates TBC), Twickenham Ireland , France , Italy 2027 World Cup Pool F Oct 2, Brisbane Tonga Oct 8, Adelaide Zimbabwe Oct 16, Sydney Wales

South Africa showed in 2019 you can go from an international rugby also-ran to global champions in the space of a year, so all is not lost for England. Their forwards look in good shape, even if there is a lack of challenge to hookers Jamie George and Luke Cowan-Dickie.

England have a strong scrum, a powerful, mobile pack and young tyros such as Henry Pollock who can cause havoc in a game's latter stages. There is hope captain Maro Itoje can get back to his best too after being rested in the summer.

There can be no doubt that Borthwick, a former second row, is an expert at getting a tune out of the forwards. The questions remain behind the scrum.

England need to be bold. Brave. Adventurous. The rest of the rugby world are playing an attacking game and England are behind the eight ball. ‘It’s more prescribed rugby, as opposed to instinctive,’ Ronan O’Gara, the former Ireland fly-half and one of the game’s great thinkers, told Daily Mail Sport.

Borthwick has to flip that narrative, allow highly rated attack coach Lee Blackett to have more of an impact on the team, and settle on an established centre pairing that can bring the best out of world-class wingers Freeman and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso.

The news that first-choice No10 Fin Smith is likely to be available for Australia is a big positive. England do have injuries to the likes of Alex Mitchell and Guy Pepper, and Tom Curry is now a doubt for the Wallabies too. But Borthwick has more than adequate replacements.

Two non-negotiables for England are to improve their shocking disciplinary record and breakdown work.

The team received eight yellow cards and one red in five Six Nations matches, a result of a regular concession of penalties. In the summer, there were two more yellows in defeat by South Africa and a mammoth four – all in one half – against Argentina. No team is going to win a World Cup doing that.

England's disciplinary issues have cost them dear in 2026 - Sam Underhill (centre) was shown one of eight yellow cards they received in five Six Nations matches

Tom Curry's injury is a significant blow to England's breakdown work

Borthwick has pointed out that the way PREM Rugby is officiated at the contact area is very different to how it is done so internationally. That cannot be a reason for England not to perform, even if Curry’s fitness setback is a blow in that area.

Yes, the avalanche of tries and poor defence we’ve seen in the PREM doesn’t mirror the international game. But the top domestic league doesn’t exist solely to prepare England to win. The players meet regularly for ‘alignment camps’ outside of Test windows to get up to speed with each other, so Borthwick and his players should be able to adapt quickly enough and if they don’t, that’s on them.

This time last year, England won all four of their autumn Tests to stretch their winning run to 11 matches in an eventual 12-game streak. Back then, confidence was high before the team capitulated in the Six Nations. There is no reason why four wins can’t be another realistic goal again, but three is an absolute minimum requirement.

Over to you England. The clock is ticking. Like Hunt on the track, it’s time for Borthwick’s team to hit the accelerator and get up to top speed.

Sports.title: Liverpool Confidential: Billionaires' investment set to beat deadline, new deal for Trey Nyoni, the academy kids who shone in Istanbul and Mor Talla Ndiaye's visa issues
Sports.content:
Liverpool Confidential: Billionaires' investment set to beat deadline, new deal for Trey Nyoni, the academy kids who shone in Istanbul and Mor Talla Ndiaye's visa issues

The deal for a group of billionaires to buy a minority stake in Liverpool remains on track to pass a deadline set by the new independent football regulator.

The consortium led by Amit Bhatia, known as 1892 Holdings, agreed to purchase a 38 per cent stake in Fenway Sports Group’s controlling interest in the club earlier this season. And despite some anxieties externally and in the fanbase about a lack of updates, I have been told this week that everything is moving in the right direction.

Sources close to Bhatia and his consortium insist the process takes time but there are no hitches and it is still expected to beat the deadline. It is understood the date in question is in December and in accordance with the new regulator, who must take within 90 days to issue a final suitability determination for prospective new owners or senior executives.

Indeed, this week brought the news that FSG are in exploratory talks to buy a significant stake in Formula One team Cadillac. Both FSG and Cadillac were contacted for comment around that story – and insisted it is an ongoing process.

One source pointed to the fact that FSG clearly expect to have some ‘spare pennies lying around’ – hinting the Liverpool investment will go through.

Senior FSG staff have constantly stressed that selling 38 per cent of the club does not mean they are losing interest and that they are as committed as ever, though the potential for the buy-in to become a full-scale takeover at some point in the future remains.

Bhatia is backed by his billionaire father-in-law Lakshmi Mittal, plus Jeff Bezos and Eduardo Saverin.

Amit Bhatia (second left) is heading up a consortium to buy a stake in Liverpool from John Henry (second right) and his Fenway Sports Group

Liverpool supporters hope the deal will transform the club's fortunes on the pitch

Frimpong nears return

Jeremie Frimpong has had rotten luck with injuries since he joined Liverpool – and Andoni Iraola ruled him out for more than a month with a problem he suffered at Brentford on October 17.

I understand the Dutch international is now all-but fit and could play this weekend if needed – however, given his high number of injuries, a decision has been made to delay his return.

Liverpool were recently punished for bringing back Dominik Szoboszlai too quickly as the Hungarian pulled up shortly after his first start upon his return, which set him back a fortnight.

Frimpong missed only seven Bayer Leverkusen games through injury in four years at the club according to Transfermarkt, but has already sat out nearly 30 Liverpool matches. Most of those absences have been hamstring related, so Frimpong is not being rushed back and will be given the international break to continue working on his recovery.

Jeremie Frimpong has had rotten luck with injuries since he joined Liverpool and went down again against Brentford last month. However, the Dutch international is now close to a return

Trey bien!

Trey Nyoni has been offered a bumper new contract to reward him for his fine progress.

The 19-year-old, who scored his first Liverpool goal in the defeat in Istanbul against Fenerbahce on Wednesday night, has had a stellar rise since Iraola took over at Liverpool.

Nyoni, signed from Leicester City in 2023, was in many matchday squads and featured sparingly last season but has come of age this campaign and has already doubled his first-team minutes – with three quarters of the season still to play.

Nottingham Forest made a £30million bid in the summer but Iraola identified him as a key asset and he will be rewarded handsomely for his progress.

Trey Nyoni scored his first Liverpool goal on Wednesday night in the Champions League loss against Fenerbahce

Your question answered: What's the January priority?

One topic fans have asked me about this week is which position is a priority in the January and summer transfer windows.

The first area to mention is midfield. I have reported in the past how Chelsea are currently ahead of Liverpool in the race for Bournemouth's Alex Scott, so let’s keep an eye on that – and the situation of Lamine Camara of Monaco. But I think the priority has to be a left-back.

Are Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas good enough? Neither have performed at the required level so far this season and bringing Tsimikas back from a loan at Roma – where he barely played – felt like a bit of a cop-out. It has to be a priority position in the next 12 months.

Red-eye Reds

Liverpool flew straight home from Istanbul after the loss to Fenerbahce and did not land on Merseyside until past 2am. It is a departure from last season, when Arne Slot would often have his squad stay for two nights on European away days.

Players are said to be big fans of the extra night at home with most preferring to sleep in their own beds.

Iraola did not hold a post-match team talk after Fenerbahce but will debrief the squad when back in training, having branded the defeat ‘cheap’ and ‘messy’.

Kop Kids: Wright is a gem

Another UEFA Youth League game, another hat-trick for Will Wright.

I was in place on the outskirts of Istanbul on Wednesday afternoon to watch the 18-year-old bag his second treble in four European matches this term, making it 13 goals for the season in all competitions.

Wright had a heated exchange with Josh Sonni-Lambie over who would take a penalty but the pair have smoothed things over now after Wright took it and scored. The striker’s assist for Finn Inglethorpe was also a notable moment that showed he is a team player and not a greedy No9.

Liverpool's Will Wright scored another hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League on Wednesday, against Fenerbahce Under 19s

I was also impressed by right back Oliver O’Connor, who looks like a real athlete. He aced every physical pre-season test for the academy and is versatile, with a quality delivery into the penalty area.

The Scouser joined the club aged six and has been a midfielder for most of his career. Boss Rob Page does not necessarily see him as a right back long-term but he caught the eye up and down that flank.

Mor's visa hitch

Those who did watch the academy game – and the first-team later on – would have been wondering where defender Mor Talla Ndiaye was. He is a mainstay in the Youth League XI and has been on the seniors’ bench several times.

It is believed the Senegalese defender had a visa issue and could not feature in the game in Turkey, though next month’s away match in Bruges is not expected to pose the same problem.

Liverpool's Mor Talla Ndiaye (centre) was nowhere to be seen in Istanbul due to visa issues

Also in academy news, young midfielder Michael Laffey has signed with the OmniSports agency who represent the likes of Wright and Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton. Under 21s captain Laffey, whose dad owns the Glenbuck pub in Anfield, made the first-team bench a fortnight ago.

Reds fans pay for priciest pints!

Liverpool supporters have drawn the short straw and will pay more than any of their English counterparts for a pint while following their team in Europe this season.

That’s according to data from LiveScore, who have worked out that Reds will pay an average of £4.91 per pint on their travels.

Still, £4.91 for a pint? Better than most places at home. You might need one after watching Liverpool’s defending this week!

Sports.title: Long balls are NOT banned at Newcastle! Matthias Jaissle insists his criticism after Everton defeat was lost in translation - having said stars were failing to follow tactics
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle says his criticism of Newcastle’s players was lost in translation and has clarified that long balls are not forbidden under his management.

The head coach also believes that his squad understands what is being asked of them, although he says his door remains open to any player seeking clarity over his instructions.

In the wake of Monday’s 1-0 home defeat by Everton, Jaissle said that the players had failed to follow his instruction and bemoaned their use of long balls when the plan was to keep it on the floor.

Asked if those comments had been addressed with the squad this week, Jaissle said: ‘I don't know if it's a misinterpretation or a language barrier, but there is an element of that when I explained that in the press conference.

‘But it is indeed (something) we address, because we talked sometimes about the no-risk zone, where we had previously critical-ball losses leading to goals. Of course, if there is a clear risk for ball loss, then I prefer playing a long ball to our striker and protecting the ball and develop the game from there.

‘It (my comments) are not to point any fingers, not at all. Sometimes you are willing to do something, but on that day it just did not work and you make the wrong decisions. It comes also with confidence.

Matthias Jaissle, pictured giving instructions during Newcastle's defeat by Everton, has insisted long balls are not banned

'If you have scenarios where you can find easily your team-mate on the ground and we build up from there with our patterns, then you should for sure also prefer that.

‘But it's not easy, it's easier said from outside. If the confidence is missing, then you prefer to be really safe and shooting maybe even more the long ball.’

Daily Mail Sport was told this week that some players are ‘confused’ by exactly what it is Jaissle wants from them, but the head coach said: ‘The fundamental thing is that we can count on unity and togetherness.

'The door is always open if ever there is anything unclear. If you see the training then I’m pretty sure everyone understands and is fully committed. There was never a question, at least I’m not aware of it.

‘It’s important we listen to the players. If there is anything unclear, they will drop in.’

Meanwhile, Jaissle says he retains the support of the club’s hierarchy after a run of four defeats in five matches.

‘The nice part is that I got even more the feeling from within the club how committed they are (this week),’ he said.

‘That just shows me that everyone believes in the long-term project and that everyone is also aware and realistic about the journey and where we are right now.’

Sports.title: Leicester City spark backlash after club's sponsor announces deal with porn star
Sports.content:
Leicester City spark backlash after club's sponsor announces deal with porn star

Leicester City's front-of-shirt sponsor BC Game, an unlicenced online cryptocurrency gaming platform, has signed up porn star Eva Elfie as an ambassador

View 3 Images Leicester City's sponsor BC Game has partnered with porn star Eva Elfie (Image: BC Game)

Leicester City are facing a backlash from supporters after the club's sponsor announced a controversial partnership with a porn star.

‌



‌



Leicester have had BC Game, an unlicenced online cryptocurrency gaming platform, as their front-of-shirt sponsor since 2024. The company's presence on the Foxes' shirts as they plummeted from the Premier League to League One in successive seasons was already a bone of contention for some fans.

‌



And now BC Game has sparked renewed anger by teaming up with Eva Elfie, a Russian adult content creator. In a video which is packed full of porn references and has been viewed 6 million times on X, Elfie is seen accepting her BC Game contract.

‌



The post has caused a stir among BC Game's eSports fanbase, as well as Leicester supporters. One fan group, called Foxes Trust, has released an angry statement condemning the move. "Most Leicester City supporters will know by now the Trust's dismay and discontent with BC Game being our front of shirt sponsor," it reads.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"BC Game have now announced a new partnership with 'international content creator and Esports personality' Eva Elfie... who just happens to be an international porn star.

"From the moment the Club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company, we felt Leicester City were ditching its values. Our first article in July 2024 said that 'It doesn't feel like who LCFC are to have a gambling website on our shirts and seems to be another step away from our well run family club reputation'.

‌



"The Club has not only partnered with a gambling company, but chosen one that is unlicensed to operate in the UK, has unanswered questions about the legitimacy of its funding and its origins, and allows clients to 'game' using cryptocurrencies.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 3 Images Leicester have been sponsored by BC Game since 2024 (Image: Stephen White/Getty Images)

"Now throw into the mix that BC Game have entered into a partnership with someone who continues to make their name via adult content. Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people. Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?

‌



"Our end of season survey showed 73% of fans felt negative about the relationship, and only 5% were content with it. As always our message is, if you're purchasing an LCFC replica shirt, opt for one that doesn't have the BC Game logo on it."

Mirror Football contacted Leicester City but has not received a response. But in the press release announcing the partnership in the summer of 2024, the club proudly boasted about BC Game being "community-based", "safe", "fair and secure".

‌



View 3 Images BC Game is unlicenced in the UK

The real reason behind their enthusiasm was plain for all to see, with the first line saying the deal was "one of the most valuable in Leicester City’s history", while chief executive Susan Whelan noted the club's "ability to attract high-value partners" after they were promoted to the Premier League.

‌



Leicester were relegated after one campaign in the top flight in 2024/25 and subsequently dropped another division to League One. Had they stayed in the Premier League, then the partnership with BC Game - which lost its licence to operate in the UK in December 2024 - would no longer be allowed.

Premier League clubs voted to get rid of front-of-shirt gambling sponsors in April 2023 and the ban came into effect at the start of the 2026/27 season. Before that ban began, obscure gambling companies had become part of the furniture of elite football, often targeting clients in markets where gambling is illegal.

Sports.title: Real Madrid chief pays tribute to Jesus de Miguel's heartbroken family at funeral
Sports.content:
Real Madrid chief pays tribute to Jesus de Miguel's heartbroken family at funeral

As the funeral of Jesus de Miguel took place, Real Madrid president Florentino Perez was there to represent his club and offer his respect

View 5 Images Real Madrid chief Florentino Perez was amongst the mourners at Jesus de Miguel's funeral (Image: AFP or licensors)

Real Madrid president Florentino Perez paid his respects to the late Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel, who died after a mid-football match collision.

‌



‌



De Miguel passed away on Tuesday, one day after a collision with Andorra FC goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who struck the Tenerife forward in the chest as he ran out to clear the football. The striker died the following morning in hospital from "accidental chest trauma" a preliminary autopsy report has stated.

‌



On Thursday, his funeral took place in his hometown of Toledo, where hundreds of mourners lined the streets to pay their respect. It was also attended by Rafael Louzan, president of the Spanish football federation, World Cup-winning Spain manager Luis de la Fuente, Atletico Madrid CEO Miguel Angel Gil Marin and Perez.

‌



The Spanish football figureheads all paid tribute to the striker, who died at the age of 30 years old. As well as the La Liga bosses, Real legends Jose Antonio Camacho, Emilio Butragueno and Pedrag Mijatovic were also amongst the mourners.

‌



Louzan spoke to the media at the funeral, saying: "Thank you to everyone here. Today was the day to be here, supporting Jesus’ family. Our solidarity is with you because I believe this is an irreparable loss.

"This tragedy should show us the path that still needs to be corrected regarding media prevention, so that they are always in the right place. It is a very difficult day. Football must stand united today.”

‌



View 5 Images Jesus de Miguel died following an on-pitch collision (Image: Andres Gutierrez/Anadolu via Getty Images)

View 5 Images Jesus de Miguel's funeral took place in his hometown (Image: AFP or licensors)

‌



De La Fuente also said: "I echo the president’s words. With deep sorrow and emotion, we convey our condolences and respect. It is the best way to demonstrate that football is united. A very warm embrace to all his loved ones.”

Many tributes around Europe have been paid to De Miguel, with this week's Champions League matches beginning with a moment of silence for the striker. Owono, the Equatorial Guinea international who was sent off for the collision against Miguel, also conveyed his sorrow in a recent statement.

‌



View 5 Images The funeral took place on Thursday in Navahermosa, in Toledo province, Spain (Image: Getty Images)

View 5 Images De Miguel's team-mates carried his coffin into the church (Image: AFP or licensors)

‌



He said: "These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words, and it is very hard for me to process anything that has happened.

"I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I am thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many matters to address, and I will face whatever comes with complete respect.

Article continues below

"But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything other than Jesus and the grief we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.”

Sports.title: Didier Deschamps' brutal reply to offer of replacing Michael Carrick at Man Utd
Sports.content:
Didier Deschamps' brutal reply to offer of replacing Michael Carrick at Man Utd

Manchester United are moving forward with Michael Carrick for the time being, but reports continue to suggest they are quietly sounding out his eventual replacement

View 2 Images Didier Deschamps has turned down the chance to manage Man Utd (Image: Getty Images)

Didier Deschamps has told Manchester United he has no interest in becoming their next manager.

‌



‌



It’s understood United bosses sounded out the former France manager about replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. Carrick is fighting to save his job after picking up just one win from their opening nine Premier League matches.

‌



Deschamps was viewed as having the winning credentials and experience to take on the challenge of restoring United to former glories. He also appealed to United because he is available for nothing.

‌



But Deschamps, who led France to World Cup glory in 2018, has no desire to take on the poisoned chalice that is managing United.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Deschamps stood down as France boss following the summer’s World Cup and is taking a break from the game before weighing up his next options.

The 58-year-old hasn't been a club manager since leaving Marseille in 2012 and will continue to assess his options before taking on his next role.

‌



United’s owners are also interested in appointing Unai Emery. But the Spaniard, who takes Aston Villa to Old Trafford on Sunday, is said to be close to agreeing a new and improved deal to remain at Villa Park instead.

Julian Nagelsmann has also been on United’s radar but has little desire to talk to the fallen giants. While Eddie Howe remains a leading contender to replace Carrick, should he be sacked during the international break.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick turned it around at half-time against Roma (Image: Getty Images)

Many expected Carrick to be axed before the fortnight break, with United putting a together a winless run stretching to nine games in all competitions.

‌



And that run looked certain to be extended when Roma opened up a 2-0 goal in front of an increasingly toxic Old Trafford home crowd. But United completed a stirring comeback, with Matheus Cunha scoring a dramatic late brace to ease some pressure on his manager.

Speaking after their win in the Champions League, Carrick said: "I don't have a crystal ball to know what happens next. We move on to the weekend. We've got a really important game here against Aston Villa, which we need to prepare for right."

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola's failed Bradley Barcola experiment leaves Liverpool with £123m dilemma
Sports.content:
It was once the envy of European football. Liverpool's consistency excellent recruitment was the key to Jurgen Klopp's glittering reign and set Arne Slot up for a quick-fire title win.

But Andoni Iraola hasn't been dealt such a favourable hand. The Spaniard has inherited an unbalanced squad, whether that be in terms of age or areas of the pitch.

Iraola's priority in his first summer was to sign an elite winger to replace Mo Salah - and Bradley Barcola was top of the list. After weeks of deliberation, Liverpool shelled out £123million on the Paris Saint-Germain star, who'd just won the Champions League for the second year running.

Barcola didn't take long to announce himself, bagging a hat-trick in Liverpool's 6-3 victory over LASK. So why did his next start in the Champions League come as a striker?

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"We thought it would work well," Iraola explained after their 3-2 loss away to Fenerbahce on Wednesday. "I think Bradley, in terms of speed [and] the match-ups, it could be good for him.

"He hasn't found the position too hard... all season he has been better when he has played outside wide, and then obviously with Cody [Gakpo], with Alex [Isak], I think we've been more dangerous."

‌



The Liverpool's manager comments suggest that Barcola won't be playing up front again. His performance does, though, leave Iraola with a dilemma.

Should Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool? Let us know your XI in the comments section.

View 5 Images Andoni Iraola hasn't figured out his best attack (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Two of Liverpool's best players this season have also been wingers: Gakpo and Rio Ngumoha. The pair compliment each other well, as seen in the Reds' swashbuckling 4-3 win against Villarreal last month when Barcola was notably benched.

‌



With nine goal contributions in 11 games this season - including one against Fenerbahce as a substitute - Gakpo has been prolific from the left wing, Barcola's preferred position. On the right, Ngumoha is chomping at the bit and completed seven dribbles (the most of any player) in Istanbul.

So where does Barcola fit in? On the left, where he's played most of his career and performed best for PSG and France? Or the right, a position which he's got plenty of experience in but means that he's unable to cut inside on his stronger foot?

Awkwardly for Iraola, all three of Gakpo, Ngomoha and Barcola have performed better than Florian Wirtz, but the German appears to have the No.10 role nailed down despite his consistently underwhelming displays. Could Barcola be used there for Iraola's next experiment?

Likely not. In October, the Reds boss said: "He probably has played more as a left winger but has played a little bit as a striker, has played even more as a right winger. I think he can cover the three positions up front."

‌



5 View 5 Images Cody Gakpo is enjoying a prolific season (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) 5 View 5 Images Rio Ngumoha's stock is rising rapidly (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher warned Anfield chiefs that Barcola wasn't a like-for-like replacement for Salah on the right flank, and after Wednesday's defeat, he once again criticised the club's squad-building. "The squad Liverpool have got is very expensive but not as good as it should be, and not as balanced as it should be," Carragher told CBS Sports.

"When you think of some of those players that have come in, what's a little worry for - not so much the manager - but the people who run the club, I spoke about Trey Nyoni being the best player for Liverpool. Well him and Rio Ngumoha, another young player, were the best players for Liverpool and they were a week or so ago against Chelsea.

‌



"But they also play in the position of players where Liverpool have spent big money. So Barcola has come in for £120million; he played up front tonight, didn't play well, but the younger players are playing better than him."

With the international break approaching, Iraola and his coaching staff will soon time to mull over Liverpool's setup and perhaps find a solution. Against Crystal Palace on Sunday, however, Barcola may well have to settle for the right-hand side - or the bench.

View 5 Images Bradley Barcola struggled in a new position against Fenerbahce (Image: OZAN KOSE/AFP via Getty Images)

But what does Barcola himself have to say? "I don't think I'm at my best yet," the 24-year-old admitted in an interview with Sky Sports this week.

‌



"You still haven't seen the best version of me. On top of that, we're working with my team-mates so that they can make the most of my strengths.

"So yes, I think once we really develop that understanding, things will get much better. And I think things are improving all the time. People are beginning to understand my style of play much better. I think it's going much better."

Sports.title: Real Madrid plan to avoid JJ Gabriel mistake that cost Arsenal star after Man Utd swoop
Sports.content:
Real Madrid plan to avoid JJ Gabriel mistake that cost Arsenal star after Man Utd swoop

Real Madrid's previous record with signing wonderkids isn't perfect as they close in on Manchester United wantaway JJ Gabriel

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel is close to joining Real Madrid (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Real Madrid are looking to avoid a repeat of the blunder they made with Martin Odegaard as they edge closer to signing JJ Gabriel. The Manchester United youngster is poised to join the La Liga giants following his shock request to quit the club.

‌



‌



Gabriel has been absent from Carrington since his camp demanded his registration be cancelled. While United rejected that request, he has since secured a European Union passport, clearing the path for him to join a club in mainland Europe.

‌



Real are leading the race to sign the youngster, who also drew attention from other European heavyweights, including Barcelona, Bayern Munich and PSG. If finalised, the transfer would mirror Odegaard's switch to the Bernabeu as a 15-year-old.

‌



Everyone involved will be hoping it works out better than that, considering the Norwegian managed just 11 first-team outings for Real amid multiple loans before ultimately moving to Arsenal in 2021 and becoming a title-winner.

Man Utd prepare for Real Madrid conflict as JJ Gabriel nears Old Trafford exit READ MORE :

JJ Gabriel rejects PSG transfer offer as wantaway Man Utd wonderkid picks next club READ MORE :

Odegaard wasn't wanted by then-boss Carlo Ancelotti, who labelled the signing a "PR exercise" by club president Florentino Perez. He was also afforded minimal playing time under Zinedine Zidane.

Spanish journalist Guillem Balague reckons Los Blancos will have taken lessons from that saga as they prepare to bring in Gabriel. Speaking on Match of the Day, Balague said Real hope not to alienate his team-mates by giving him a first-term contract but making him train with their B side, as was the case with Odegaard.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Martin Odegaard's move to Real was a complete disaster (Image: NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



That caused tensions for the young Norwegian, whose peers would supposedly refuse to pass him the ball in training given he wouldn't be playing with them at the weekend.

United still retain Gabriel's registration, despite the player failing to return to Old Trafford or Carrington since departing after scoring a hat-trick against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League in September. The club's subsequent efforts to contact his family about his well-being have been ignored.

‌



View 3 Images United haven't heard anything from Gabriel or his family recently (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Gabriel was poised to become United's youngest-ever first-team player against Brighton in the Carabao Cup, only to be withdrawn from the club three weeks before he turned 16, with his family dissatisfied with his development plan.

‌



They had insisted that Gabriel appear against Sabah in the Champions League and the Carabao Cup, while also making his Premier League debut. He would've become United's youngest-ever player.

Sports.title: Jesus de Miguel's heartbroken family issue emotional first statement on footballer's death
Sports.content:
Jesus de Miguel's heartbroken family issue emotional first statement on footballer's death

Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed after a collision with another player and his heartbroken family has issued their first statement

View 3 Images Jesus de Miguel's family has released a statement (Image: CD TENERIFE/AFP via Getty Images)

Jesus de Miguel's family has issued their first statement following his tragic death. The Tenerife forward died after a tragic collision with Andorra FC goalkeeper Jesus Owono in a second division match this week.

‌



‌



The two players competed for a loose ball during a game on Monday and De Miguel was knocked to the ground after Owono charged out of his goal, only to hit the striker in the chest when attempting to clear. Owono was sent off and the challenge caused De Miguel to go into a cardiorespiratory arrest on the pitch.

‌



De Miguel received immediate treatment but he passed away in hospital on Tuesday morning. His cause of death has been ruled as "accidental chest trauma" in a preliminary autopsy report.

‌



Tributes poured in and the 30-year-old's funeral took place today (November 5) in his hometown, Navahermosa, Toledo, in mainland Spain. His family had remained silent after his death, but offered their first public statement since the tragedy.

Jesus de Miguel's cause of death revealed after fatal collision with goalkeeper READ MORE :

Manuel Hernandez, a spokesperson for the family, has read a statement on their behalf: "In these difficult times for us, we want to sincerely thank everyone for the kind words and expressions of affection we are receiving.

View 3 Images De Miguel's family have spoken out (Image: Instagram/@martitamig)

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

"We don't have enough words to thank you for every message, every call, and every gesture of affection that we are receiving. Thank you to everyone who has remembered him, to his team-mates, friends, fans and all the clubs who have wanted to convey their condolences and accompany us in this painful moment.

‌



"Feeling such love for Jesus and witnessing the impact he has had on so many people is something we will always carry with us. Therefore, we respectfully request that our privacy and that of all those accompanying us at this time be protected.

"We need to grieve in the peace and quiet that this situation requires. We understand the affection, concern, and support that her loss is generating, and we are deeply grateful.

‌



"Jesus leaves a void impossible to fill, but also an immense memory in all of us who have been lucky enough to share our lives with him. Thank you for loving him, for remembering him, and for being with us. His family."

View 3 Images Tributes have been paid to the striker across the continent (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Both De Miguel's girlfriend Maria and his infant daughter Carla were tragically at the stadium for Monday's game and a family friend, Fernando Roman, gave an interview with Spanish outlet Vamos a Ver. He opened up about how De Miguel's girlfriend was left alone in the hospital following his passing. The player's parents travelled in after hearing the news.

"Yesterday, my girlfriend and I were talking all afternoon and all night with Maria, his girlfriend, who was alone in the hospital," Roman said. "I've spoken with his girlfriend, and you can imagine how she is. Now we have to be with the family. We have to send our love to his family, to Maria, to his daughter Carla, who is a year and a few months old."

Article continues below

Goalkeeper Owono broke his silence on the tragic ordeal on Wednesday. He said: "These are the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

"I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo ends Portugal career with emotional five-minute retirement speech
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo ends Portugal career with emotional five-minute retirement speech

Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football

View 3 Images

Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football as he 'hands back' his number seven shirt. The forward confirmed the news in a five-minute speech released on his social media accounts.

‌



‌



The 41-year-old played 234 times for his country, scoring 146 goals. During that time, he won the European Championships and the Nations League with Portugal.

‌



His final appearance for the national team came in the 1-0 Nations League victory against Wales back in September. Ronaldo was an unused substitute for the next game against Norway, which led to a major spat with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus. The five-time Ballon d'Or winner refused to train following the game and then left the Portugal camp.

‌



Speculation arose that Ronaldo was considering international retirement following Portugal's exit from the World Cup in the summer, with the manager reportedly convincing him to stay. But posting on his social media accounts, the former Real Madrid and Manchester United man has confirmed the decision.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team," he said. "I never felt it belonged to me alone.

"But for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defining it, and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world. Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future.

‌



"It was not an easy decision. Because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart.

"A journey that began in August 2003, and changed my life forever, has come to an end. When I look at everything I experienced with the national team, I don't just see matches, goals, records or trophies. I see people.

‌



"I see Portuguese people living abroad, who, for ninety minutes, felt a little closer to home. I see millions of Portuguese people I have never met, but who became part of my life.

View 3 Images Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his international retirement. (Image: Matthias Hangst/Getty Images)

‌



"Because, at the end of the day, football is so much bigger than a game. Football is about people.

"Throughout my entire career with the national team, I always pushed myself beyond my limits. I wanted to win, I wanted to be better. I wanted to make history. I always demanded the most of myself. I always wanted more.

‌



"I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this shirt. There were perfect afternoons and nights. There were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember.

"I made mistakes, I suffered. There were also moments when I couldn't give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

‌



"Over the years I learned a few very simple things: Goals fade, trophies end up in museums, records are eventually broken. But there is something that time can never erase: The place we hold in people's hearts.

‌



"If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you embrace someone, forget a worry, or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also about this. We suffer together, we rise together. We believe again.

"Portugal will always need young people who dare to dream, players who never give up. New generations who believe it is possible to go where no one has gone before. Because a country that keeps creating new heroes is a country that never stops believing in itself.

‌



"To my teammates, I want to say something special, thank you for every run, for every embrace, for every argument, for every silence before stepping onto the pitch, for every victory we celebrated together and every defeat that made us stronger.

"I had the privilege of being your captain, but no captain walks alone and you will always be part of my story.

‌



"To all the coaches, directors, doctors, physiotherapists, kit managers, staff members, and so many others who worked alongside me throughout these years, thank you. Many of you never appeared in the photographs, but without you none of those photographs would have been possible.

"To my family. Thank you for sharing this dream with me. Thank you for understanding the absences, the sacrifices, and the moments when the national team had to take up a space in my life that also belonged to you. If I came this far, it was because we always walked hand in hand.

‌



View 3 Images Portugal and Cristiano Ronaldo lost to eventual champions Spain in this summer's World Cup. (Image: Lars Baron/Getty Images)

"And to the people of Portugal, to every Portuguese person, wherever you are in the world, there is one last thing I want to tell you. There is an image I will carry with me forever. The moment our national anthem begins, I look around; I see my teammates, I see the stands, I see children, mothers, fathers and grandparents, I see Portuguese people who have travelled so far just to be there.

‌



"And for those few minutes, all our differences disappear. There are no clubs, there are no colours, there are no classes, there are no professions, there are no opinions, there is only one passion: Portugal. That is the feeling I will carry with me for the rest of my life.

"Today, my journey on the pitch with the national team comes to an end, I will leave with my head held high, proud of the path I have taken, and knowing that I gave everything I had for Portugal. But I will never stop being one of you. I will keep suffering, cheering and celebrating every Portuguese victory with a siuuuuu.

‌



"I spent my life working to become the best player in the world. Today, I realise that my greatest victory was earning the honour of representing the best country in the world.

"Thank you for these 23 years, thank you for believing in me, thank you for allowing me to live a dream that began when I was just a little boy in Madeira running after a football. The number seven shirt will remain, the pride of having worn it will be mine forever. Portugal will always be a part of me.

‌



"Farewell, until we meet again. Cristiano Ronaldo. "

Portugal are back in action later this month as they face Denmark and Wales in the Nations League in the upcoming international break. Ronaldo, meanwhile, will not be involved in Al Nassr's AFC Champions League clash in Uzbekistan due to security concerns.

Article continues below

He also missed Monday night's clash vs Pakhtakor, a game which Al-Nassr won 6-2.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca makes Gianluigi Donnarumma stance clear after latest Man City error
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca makes Gianluigi Donnarumma stance clear after latest Man City error

Gianluigi Donnarumma was at fault for another goal as Manchester City beat RB Leipzig 3-2 in the Champions League, prompting some to call on Enzo Maresca to drop him

View 2 Images Gianluigi Donnarumma made an error against RB Leipzig (Image: Odd ANDERSEN/AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is firmly behind Gianluigi Donnarumma, stating that his recent mistakes aren't a 'concern'. City goalkeeper Donnarumma was caught out for Ridle Baku's equaliser during their 3-2 win away to RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday.

‌



‌



It came 11 days after the Italian's mistake against Aston Villa which cost City their unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign. Donnarumma also hasn't kept a clean sheet in his last six appearances.

‌



But Maresca is unlikely to drop him for City's trip to Nottingham Forest on Saturday, even though he acknowledged the 27-year-old's error. The City manager replied after being asked if he was concerned about Donnarumma's form: "Not a concern but it's a mistake.

‌



"We recognise that it's a mistake. At the moment I'm not thinking about the goalkeeping situation. A few minutes before the goal he's done a save that no 'keeper in the world makes. Gigio knows he was not good with the first goal. He's going to do better.

"Both goals are quite silly goals we can avoid. We are creating many chances in each game but we need to avoid silly goals. It's about working more. Understand and analyse.

"I'm new here, I need to know the players and they need to know me. We can only improve. I don't think in this moment it's a matter of balance.

‌



"In the last five or six games we concede in all competitions [and] they are individual mistakes so it's not about the system or a midfielder to the offensive line. It's more individual mistakes that we need to do better to avoid."

Should Enzo Maresca drop Gianluigi Donnarumma? Have your say in the comments section.

‌

Donnarumma's backup, Geronimo Rulli, has made two appearance since re-signing for City in the summer transfer window, both in the Carabao Cup. The Argentina international is expected to reclaim his place when Maresca's side face Bradford City in the quarter-finals next month.

‌



For now, Donnarumma will keep the gloves with his manager's backing. City travel to Nottingham looking for their first Premier League win since October 17, having suffered back-to-back defeats away to Villa and at home to Brighton, consequently losing their grip on first place.

Wednesday's victory was much needed, as Erling Haaland scored the winning goal to down Leipzig. The win moved City onto nine points after four games in the Champions League. History suggests that they only need one more win to secure at least a play-off spot.
