Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Climbs Rankings After Barely Surviving Wallace
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker holds the mandatory rankings to demand a world title shot right now, yet his shaky finish against Wallace shows he is nowhere near ready for that step up. Owning two top spots does not prove he can last twelve rounds with Dmitry Bivol. Wallace had him out on his feet and clinging for life in the closing seconds, exposing flaws that an elite operator would punish without mercy.

Whittaker is now ranked at #1 WBO, #1 IBF, and #3 WBC at light heavyweight. Promoter Eddie Hearn suddenly holds multiple paths to steer his fighter toward a strap. The problem is those gaudy rankings build up heavy expectations that Whittaker simply failed to justify against Wallace.

He won the October 3 IBF final eliminator by scores of 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113, building his lead behind the jab before Wallace hurt him late. The way Whittaker fell apart physically in the later rounds showed that he’s not ready for Bivol or Artur Beterbiev.

Hearn is targeting February or March for Whittaker’s return, with Anthony Yarde and the winner of Joshua Buatsi against Willy Hutchinson among the possibilities.

The problem is that the blueprint is out on how to beat Whittaker. In the 2020 Olympics in Tokyo, Arlen Lopez and Imam Khataev exposed the flaws by walking through the flash, cutting off the ring, and roughing Whittaker up on the inside. Conor Wallace didn’t invent anything new in the late rounds; he just dusted off the same heavy-pressure game plan.

Every solid light heavyweight contender watched Whittaker gas out and resort to clinging once his legs stiffened up. Marinating the Bivol matchup only works if Hearn can keep matching him against fighters who lack the punch or the engine to execute that exact strategy. One slip against a live underdog with a sturdy chin, and the entire cash-out plan evaporates before Bivol even enters the conversation.

Hearn has twelve to eighteen months at most to let the fight marinate. The calendar is working against him far quicker than Matchroom wants to admit.

Whittaker turns 30 next summer. He entered the pros with an Olympic pedigree, but his physical peak as an agile, Reflex-reliant fighter is happening right now. Waiting three or four years completely destroys his own physical advantages. Once his hand speed drops half a step or his legs fade five minutes earlier, he will not have the inside game or the durability to fall back on.

Waiting also assumes Bivol falls off a cliff overnight. Bivol turns 36 in December, but his style is built on footwork, distance management, and textbook fundamentals. Those attributes age far better than reliance on raw athleticism. A 37-year-old Bivol who has lost half a step will still possess the discipline and the tight combinations to pick apart a gassing Whittaker.

The real danger in stalling is the contender pool. Keeping Whittaker busy with fringe contenders or domestic rivals to run out the clock carries massive risk. The light heavyweight division is full of heavy-handed pressure fighters who took copious notes during the Wallace bout. If Hearn matches him with someone who has the engine to walk him down and the power to test his chin in rounds eight through twelve, Whittaker gets clipped before he ever sees a world title purse.

Hearn’s realistic window is late 2027. He can afford two tune-ups to work on conditioning and ring generalship under heavy fire. After that, he has to cash in the ticket, win or lose, before an ambitious contender beats him to the punch and ruins the entire investment.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Responds To Tyson Fury Injury Rumors
Sports.content:
Frank Warren says he knows nothing about Tyson Fury picking up an injury in camp, leaving Frank Bruno’s recent claim completely unbacked ahead of the Anthony Joshua fight.

Warren seemed surprised when asked about the talk surrounding Fury’s preparation for the December 11 date in Cardiff. He gave no support to the injury talk, though he stopped short of officially declaring Fury totally fit.

“That’s news to me. That’s news to me. Absolute news to me,” Warren repeated to the media today when asked about Bruno’s comments.

Bruno spoke publicly about hearing whispers that Fury suffered a setback in training. That remains unconfirmed, with no specific injury mentioned or verified. Casual gym talk happens all the time, and it is a long way from something serious enough to derail a massive bout.

Warren being Fury’s promoter means people naturally pay attention to his words, but observers need to look at the whole picture. Saying he has not heard anything bad is not the same as checking in directly with the trainers or getting an official update from a doctor. Nobody followed up by asking if he had spoken to the gym.

After waiting years for Fury and Joshua to finalize a deal, boxing followers get nervous at the slightest rumor. The bout took ages to put together, so nobody wants to see another delay. Still, nothing Warren said points to the Cardiff date being at risk.

The promoter kept right on talking up the event, including the addition of Deontay Wilder against Jai Opetaia on the undercard. He also fielded a question about Fury’s next move, with Daniel Dubois brought up as a possible future opponent.

“When Tyson wins the fight, he’ll make his choice what he wants to do,” Warren said.

That keeps Fury’s plans after Joshua completely open. Warren made no promises about facing Dubois or going after other champions, which makes sense before his fighter gets through the biggest domestic night of his career.

Right now, the focus is on whether any real facts emerge from the gym. Bruno’s standing ensures the story gets attention, but his name alone does not prove what is taking place in camp. Warren’s surprise does not completely shut down the conversation either.

Until Team Fury comes out with something concrete, there is no real basis for an injury crisis. Warren pushed back on the talk; the fight stays locked in for Cardiff, and the rumor simply lacks the substance to treat it as a done deal.

Sports.title: Vasiliy Lomachenko Signs Top Rank Deal, Chases Undisputed at 130
Sports.content:
The three-division champion plans to fight in early 2027 after signing a multi-year co-promotional deal through Loma Power Promotions.

Vasiliy Lomachenko is coming out of retirement and dropping back to super featherweight. The former IBF lightweight champion will return in early 2027 under a multi-year agreement between Top Rank and his newly formed Loma Power Promotions.

The comeback takes him back to 130 pounds, where he held the WBO belt before moving up to lightweight. Top Rank did not name an opponent, a fight date or a broadcaster in its November 5 announcement.

“I thought I would never step back into the ring again as a boxer,” Lomachenko said. “But our Lord Jesus Christ had other plans for me. I’m happy to be living this boxing life once again.”

Lomachenko Chases Undisputed at Super Featherweight

Lomachenko retired in June 2025 as IBF lightweight champion. He had stopped George Kambosos Jr. for the belt in May 2024, a year after losing his bid for the undisputed 135-pound championship against Devin Haney.

That chase now moves to 130. Top Rank chairman Bob Arum and manager Egis Klimas both identified an undisputed championship as the goal of the comeback.

“He’s accomplished so much, but he’s determined to become undisputed,” Arum said.

Lomachenko returns with an 18-3 record and 12 knockouts. The two-time Olympic gold medalist won his first professional title in his third bout and had claimed belts in three divisions by his 12th, when he stopped Jorge Linares to win a lightweight title in May 2018.

Top Rank has promoted Lomachenko since his professional debut in 2013. This time, his own promotional company will share the bill with the outfit that handled his rise through the divisions.

Lomachenko credited Klimas with pushing for a return after he had decided his fighting days were over.

“Special respect and gratitude to Egis, who, despite my firm belief that my boxing career was over, never stopped believing that we would step into the ring again. He put in a tremendous amount of work and effort to get us back in the race.”

Sports.title: IBF Orders Osleys Iglesias Defense As Canelo Weighs Options
Sports.content:
The IBF just handed Osleys Iglesias a mandatory defense against Malik Zinad at the worst possible time, with Canelo Alvarez still deciding on an opponent for a rumored February return. The Cuban holds a belt that makes him a legitimate unification target, but sanctioning body bureaucracy just dumped an unwanted roadblock in his way.

Iglesias was always an outside shot to get picked by Canelo, but holding the IBF super middleweight title legitimately placed him in that conversation. That makes this ruling sting even more. The IBF is forcing him into a matchup with Zinad, a challenger whose recent resume gives zero indication that he can compete at this level.

The sanctioning body officially ordered the fight, according to Mike Coppinger, who reported that The Ring obtained the IBF letter. Coppinger also highlighted that Iglesias is rated No. 2 by the publication at 168 pounds, meaning an eventual clash between Canelo and Iglesias would crown a new Ring champion.

A fight with Iglesias offers legitimate credibility rather than just another easy paycheck on the calendar. Unifying the division actually means something at 168 pounds. Canelo taking on a heavy-handed southpaw who presents actual danger is another question entirely.

The mandatory order does not mean a unification is dead in the water. Without an official ruling on a proposed Canelo fight, declaring Iglesias unavailable would be jumping the gun. What this ruling actually does is force the Cuban into tedious talks with Zinad while Canelo takes his sweet time sorting through his options.

The timing is worth a close look, but not as proof of backroom coordination. A champion who already faced steep odds to land the division’s golden ticket now has another unwanted complication thrown directly in his path.

Looking at Zinad, this is a glaring mismatch on paper. The 32-year-old challenger has only one career defeat, coming when Dmitry Bivol stopped him in six rounds during their June 2024 light heavyweight title fight. There is no shame in getting stopped by an elite operator like Bivol, but failing at 175 pounds is hardly a valid qualification for a mandatory title shot down at 168.

His recent schedule reveals the real issue. Zinad collected two bounce-back wins against Haris Dzindo and Ante Bilic. BoxRec lists Dzindo as an inactive cruiserweight. Bilic is 43 years old, listed at super middleweight, and currently sits at No. 285 in the BoxRec rankings. Neither victory provides a convincing reason to expect Zinad to give Iglesias an ounce of trouble.

Those bouts padded a record, plain and simple. They do virtually nothing to establish that a fighter deserves to stand at the very front of the line for a world championship.

Iglesias packs one-punch power behind a stinging southpaw jab and an awkward, concussive right hook that obliterates second-tier opposition. Zinad boasts a shiny record on surface inspection, but stripping away the numbers exposes empty padding against overmatched opposition.

The IBF has every right to call its mandatories. Still, handing out a world title shot to a fighter with this level of opposition demands real scrutiny, especially when it disrupts talks for the biggest fight in the division.

Iglesias gets tied up with Zinad while Canelo plays waiting games and takes his time. For a champion trying to turn his belt into life-changing money against the sport’s cash cow, getting derailed by a mandatory nobody wanted is a raw deal.

Sports.title: Zuffa Boxing Promised A Revolution And Delivered The Copper Box
Sports.content:
Zuffa talked a massive game about revolutionizing boxing, but the actual product inside the ring tells a different story. Fans are already questioning whether these initial shows are making any real splash.

The choice of the Copper Box sparked plenty of talk during a talkSPORT preview covering Chris Billam Smith against Cheavon Clarke alongside Denzel Bentley against Shane Mosley Jr. Hardcore boxing followers might appreciate those matchups, yet they hardly signal the massive shakeup Zuffa promised.

During the broadcast, the host questioned whether Zuffa would eventually book an arena bigger than the Copper Box. One panelist pointed out that the promotional powerhouse talked up massive announcements without delivering anything groundbreaking. That prompted the host to recall Dana White asking critics to grade the venture after a full twelve months.

The venue itself isn’t the real issue. A cozy arena creates electric energy when the action heats up. Booking a cavernous stadium means nothing if the seats end up empty or the bouts fall flat.

The real test is whether Zuffa can stage matchups people crave. Billam Smith taking on Clarke brings local intrigue alongside their amateur history, yet Clarke losing to Viddal Riley softened fan enthusiasm. A victory keeps Billam Smith active, though it won’t ignite massive demand for his next appearance.

Bentley versus Mosley offers solid matchmaking, too. Bentley openly praised the financial incentives of signing with Zuffa, which makes total sense for his career. Spectators tune in for compelling drama, not fighter paychecks. Handing out better contracts won’t instantly transform an ordinary bout into appointment viewing.

Zuffa created this problem through its own bold marketing. Staging decent regional fight cards works fine if the goal is modest roster growth. Because White guaranteed a complete overhaul of the business, viewers naturally expect something groundbreaking.

Collecting recognizable athletes gives the banner talent to book. The brand still has to generate genuine excitement around those athletes, ignite heated rivalries, then secure opponents that get fans genuinely invested. The company logo won’t carry the load by itself.

There is definitely runway left for things to click. One modest night at the Copper Box doesn’t seal the outfit’s fate, nor does skeptical radio banter mean the experiment is doomed. What it proves is that early hype won’t cut it anymore. People want hard proof.

White asked for twelve months before everyone delivers a final grade. When evaluation day arrives, the only thing that counts will be a lineup of matchups fans begged to see. Fresh sales pitches simply won’t fool anyone a second time.

Sports.title: Did Callum Smith Take Something Out of Joshua Buatsi for Good?
Sports.content:
Joshua Buatsi insists his loss to Callum Smith prepared him for deep water. His rematch with Willy Hutchinson will test whether that ring education took something out of him physically.

Buatsi showed real grit against Smith, yet his flat showing against Zach Parker raised doubts about what that night took out of him. Hutchinson now steps in with the knowledge that he can push Buatsi into an uncomfortable place.

That question surfaced during talkSPORT’s preview, where pundits questioned whether the Smith war aged the Londoner. The flat outing against Parker gave the debate real traction, even if a single night cannot settle what remains in his gas tank.

Buatsi counters that the Smith setback revealed what he could summon when the going got rough. Going twelve rounds at elite level gave him reference points he plans to use if Hutchinson turns their second meeting into another grueling scrap.

Ring logic backs him up. A tough defeat often teaches a fighter more than a string of easy stoppage wins. Buatsi discovered he can stay in the pocket when an opponent matches his physical strength.

Belief and physical durability are entirely different matters. A boxer can feel mentally bulletproof while his physical reserves are running low, so pure self-belief offers no clue about the version stepping through the ropes.

It also discounts just how punishing their initial collision was. Buatsi got his hand raised, but Hutchinson made him fight for every inch. The Smith clash was hardly the first time Buatsi absorbed heavy damage to stay on course. Surviving a war never wipes away the wear on the odometer.

Hutchinson arrives fresh off an impressive win over Ezra Taylor, an effort that drew heavy praise on talkSPORT. Replicating that success against Buatsi presents a steeper hurdle. Buatsi’s inside work and committed body assault gave Hutchinson fits the first time around, problems the Scotsman must solve.

Hutchinson might not need a massive tactical overhaul. If he took another step forward while Buatsi lost a half-step, the gap between them narrows instantly.

Buatsi laughed off suggestions that anyone forced his hand for the return bout.

“I definitely wasn’t bullied into it,” Buatsi said on talkSPORT. “What I said was that I wanted something on the line. The minute we got it, everything was accepted on our side.”

The vacant WBC light heavyweight crown gives him that target. It puts a world title on the table against an opponent he already solved once, though identical tactics never guarantee an identical finish.

The previous victory feeds Buatsi’s certainty. The lackluster Parker outing gives Hutchinson every reason to believe the timing favors him. Now, Buatsi has to prove those hard-earned lessons still have the physical engine to back them up.

Sports.title: John Fury Fears Humiliation For Fury-Joshua Loser
Sports.content:
John Fury fears the loser of Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua won’t cope with the abuse afterward. That could happen, but these two have waited so long to fight that a defeat shouldn’t carry the weight it would have five years ago.

“They’ll get that much stick, the loser, they won’t be able to cope with it,” Fury said in the BBC documentary Rivals: Fury v Joshua, as reported by talkSPORT.

You can understand a father worrying about that. The losing fighter will have clips of the defeat thrown at him whenever he opens his phone, especially if he gets knocked out. Years of accomplishments can get buried beneath one ugly night when fans want to rub it in.

Still, John is giving that reaction too much power. Neither fighter should have to beat the other at this stage to protect everything he achieved earlier in his career.

The trouble is that Fury and Joshua spent years being compared without getting into the ring together. That allowed their supporters to keep arguing that their man would win. Once they fight, one side will have a result to wave around, and the other will have to live with it.

But it won’t tell us who would have won when both were younger. It will tell us who has more left in December. Those are two different arguments, even if the winning side treats them as the same thing.

John himself accepts that both have declined. That makes his fear of humiliation harder to buy as a reason for the fight never to happen. If neither man is at his best, there should be room to accept a loss without treating the beaten fighter like a fraud.

A bad beating could make retirement the sensible choice for the loser. But where is the winner really going? Beating another aging heavyweight doesn’t suddenly make either man better equipped to face the younger punchers in the division.

My expectation is that the winner looks for another lucrative Usyk fight, if it can be made, or an opponent he believes he can beat. It is difficult to picture either volunteering to face Daniel Dubois. That would mean taking a dangerous fight when a more carefully selected opponent could keep the paydays coming.

That limits what this contest actually settles. The loser could be pushed toward retirement, while the winner carries on choosing his opportunities carefully. Neither outcome makes this the start of a fresh run through the heavyweight division.

John’s fear of the ridicule is understandable. But the winner gets bragging rights over another faded name, and the loser shouldn’t have his whole career dismissed because he came off second best.

Sports.title: Oscar De La Hoya Predicts A Mayweather vs Garcia Fight Won’t Happen
Sports.content:
Rumors of a high-profile fight between Ryan Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs) and Floyd “Money” Mayweather (50-0, 27 KOs) have been circulating, but Garcia’s promoter Oscar De La Hoya believes that on February 6, 2027, Garcia will not be sharing the ring with Mayweather.

The Golden Boy Promotions CEO, Oscar De La Hoya, thinks Mayweather is capable of giving Garcia a good fight. However, he believes that instead of Mayweather, Ryan Garcia will face Teofimo Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) on February 6th.

Back on October 21st, Ryan Garcia posted breaking news on all of his social media platforms. Garcia claimed a Hall of Fame boxer reached out to him to discuss a potential title fight.

“Trust me at first I thought this was bull***,” Garcia said. “But it’s real Floyd, and I agreed to a fight at 147 for the WBC welterweight championship of the world, 50-0 vs. the current champ.”

Garcia doubled down on the claim when he posted a second message on his Instagram account, and this message included a photo of Garcia and Mayweather in what appears to be a FaceTime call.

As time went on, fight fans were becoming skeptical about the Mayweather vs. Garcia matchup actually happening because Garcia was doing all the talking while Mayweather remained silent.

Then, finally, on November 1st, Floyd Mayweather posted the  for his upcoming exhibition bout. Included in the , Mayweather confirmed the Garcia fight when he stated, “This is a lil tune-up before me and Ryan Garcia lock up Feb. 2027.”

At this point, it seemed like the bout was official, but during a recent interview with Sean Zittel, Garcia’s promoter Oscar De La Hoya made a statement that puts the fight in doubt.

“I do love that Teofimo fight, uh, sometime in February on DAZN. And you know the Floyd Mayweather thing, yes, there are a lot of rumors, a lot of speculation.Who knows? I don’t think it will happen, but look if it does, I’ve always said yeah, it’s a 50/50 fight,” De La Hoya stated.

Ryan Garcia has one more fight on his Golden Boy contract. Garcia keeps talking about Floyd, but if his promoter is leaning toward Teofimo, then there’s a good chance we will see a Garcia vs Lopez title bout in February.

Fighting the WBA welterweight world champion Teofimo Lopez makes a lot of sense. If Ryan wins, he will have a victory over a high-level opponent, and the win would equate to Garcia becoming a unified champion.

If he decides to fight Floyd Mayweather he has everything to lose and nothing to gain. If Garcia loses to Mayweather, it’s an embarrassment, and if he defeats Mayweather, nobody is going to give him credit for beating a 50-year-old man.

Ghana News.title: Ablakwa announces new trade and diplomatic initiatives with Caribbean countries
Ghana News.content:
Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has announced significant progress in Ghana's trade and diplomatic relations with Caribbean countries, with new developments in port cooperation, energy investment, tourism, healthcare and air connectivity.

The progress follows a series of bilateral meetings between Mr Ablakwa and his counterparts from Antigua and Barbuda, Jamaica and Trinidad and Tobago on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda.

In a Facebook post on Thursday, November 5, the Minister said the engagements provided an opportunity to assess existing partnerships and explore new areas of cooperation with Ghana's strategic partners.

He disclosed that Antigua and Barbuda has requested additional Ghanaian health workers following the positive impact made by the first batch of 120 nurses deployed to the Caribbean country.

He said the first group of Ghanaian nurses had made an impressive impact on the country's healthcare sector, prompting the Antiguan government to seek more professionals from Ghana.

"My bilateral meeting with host Foreign Minister His Excellency Everly Paul Chet Greene of Antigua and Barbuda confirmed that the first group of 120 nurses from Ghana is making an impressive impact. Antigua has therefore requested more health workers," Mr Ablakwa stated.

The development marks a boost for Ghana's labour mobility programme, which seeks to create employment opportunities for Ghanaian professionals while helping partner countries address shortages in key sectors.

Mr Ablakwa also announced that a new visa waiver arrangement covering all categories of passport holders is expected to strengthen relations between Ghana and Antigua and Barbuda.

He said the agreement would make it easier for citizens of both countries to travel and support increased trade, tourism and people-to-people exchanges.

"Our new Visa Waiver for all categories of passport holders is expected to bring us closer as we deepen trade, tourism and people to people relations," he said.

The Foreign Affairs Minister also announced progress on a major maritime cooperation agreement between Ghana and Jamaica, which is now ready.

The agreement was discussed during his meeting with Jamaica's Foreign Affairs Minister, Kamina Johnson Smith.

Under the proposed partnership, Ghana's Tema Port and Jamaica's Port of Kingston are expected to establish comprehensive cooperation to improve trade, logistics and maritime operations.

The arrangement is also expected to create jobs and strengthen economic relations between the two countries.

Mr Ablakwa described the agreement as an important development in Ghana-Jamaica relations.

"My engagement with Jamaican Foreign Minister, Her Excellency Kamina Johnson Smith highlighted our crucial Ghana-Jamaica Port Cooperation Agreement which is now ready," he said.

He added that the partnership between the two ports would focus on boosting trade, logistics, maritime cooperation and job creation.

The port agreement is expected to provide new opportunities for businesses and strengthen commercial links between Ghana and the Caribbean.

Mr Ablakwa further disclosed that Ghana's latest group of nurses had arrived in Jamaica under the labour mobility programme negotiated by the two countries last year.

The deployment is part of efforts to expand employment opportunities for Ghanaian health professionals while supporting Jamaica's healthcare workforce.

Ghana is also seeking to deepen its economic relations with Trinidad and Tobago, particularly in the oil and gas industry.

Mr Ablakwa said he held a substantive meeting with the country's Foreign Affairs Minister, Sean S.M. Sobers, MP, to discuss new investments and opportunities to expand cooperation in the energy sector.

The two countries are expected to explore further areas of partnership in an industry that remains important to their respective economies.

As part of efforts to strengthen diplomatic relations, Ghana is expected to commission its new High Commission in Trinidad next year.

The establishment of the mission is expected to improve Ghana's diplomatic presence in the Caribbean and provide greater support for trade, investment and cooperation between the two countries.

The government is also working to improve air connectivity between Ghana and Caribbean countries through new air services agreements.

According to Mr Ablakwa, negotiations on the agreements are being finalised to pave the way for direct flights between Ghana and the Caribbean.

He explained that the proposed arrangements would be implemented when the ongoing revival of Ghana Airways is completed.

The move is expected to make travel between the two regions easier, while supporting tourism, trade and business relations.

Direct air links could also strengthen the historical and cultural connections between Ghana and Caribbean countries, many of which share deep ties with Africa.

Beyond his engagements with Caribbean countries, Mr Ablakwa also held discussions with an Australian official on international peace, security and reform of the United Nations.

He met James Buttigieg, Australia's Assistant Secretary for Multilateral Peace, Security and Candidacies, to discuss areas of shared interest as Australia seeks membership of the United Nations Security Council.

The discussions also form part of Ghana's wider diplomatic efforts to build international support for reforms that would give Africa a stronger voice in global affairs.

Mr Ablakwa said Ghana was strengthening its relations with international partners ahead of its role as Chair of the African Union next year.

He stressed the need for Africa to secure permanent representation on the UN Security Council, arguing that the continent must have a stronger role in decisions affecting international peace and security.

"As Chair of the African Union next year we are forging closer ties with international allies to advance Africa's case for UN reforms as we ensure Africa is permanently represented on the UN Security Council," he said.

He further outlined other issues Ghana intends to advance on the international stage, including reforms to the global financial system, artificial intelligence regulation, climate justice, resource sovereignty, reparatory justice and conflict resolution.

Ghana News.title: Martin Kpebu says a 2008 Court of Appeal ruling could determine fate of the seat of detained Asante Akyem North MP
Ghana News.content:
Private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu says a 2008 Court of Appeal ruling involving former Nkoranza North MP Eric Amoateng could influence whether detained Asante Akyem North MP Ohene Kwame Frimpong loses his parliamentary seat.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Top Story, Mr Kpebu said the ruling in Professor Stephen Kwaku Asare v Attorney-General & 3 Others could be relevant because Mr Frimpong has reportedly not obtained written permission from the Speaker of Parliament to be absent from parliamentary sittings.

He argued that the circumstances surrounding the current MP’s absence could place him in a more difficult position than those considered in the earlier case.

“The Court of Appeal held that the Speaker cannot give permission for an MP to be absent for more than 15 sittings. And in this particular case, from what Kweku Asare read, it says the MP has not even sought permission, so it means that his situation is even worse,” he said.

Mr Kpebu questioned whether Mr Frimpong’s detention in the Netherlands prevented him from seeking permission through his lawyers.

“I doubt that being in custody per se could prevent him from seeking permission. He has instructed lawyers to write to the Speaker, but even if they did, now that we've gone past 15 sittings, it appears the Kweku Asare case will be determinative,” he added.

Mr Kpebu also argued that the Asare ruling established that courts have jurisdiction to determine matters involving an MP’s absence from Parliament where questions of law arise.

He said parliamentary procedures do not automatically place such matters beyond judicial scrutiny.

“It says that the court has power to determine this particular matter, and that's how come the court went into it. So this is not one of the cases in which we say what happens in Parliament is a closed book. No, there are many exceptions to that,” he stated.

“When there is a breach of the law, and not just parliamentary procedure, the courts have jurisdiction. So it would appear that the Kweku Asare case would be helpful in determining this matter.”

The case cited by Mr Kpebu arose after Eric Amoateng, then MP for Nkoranza North, was arrested and detained in the United States on narcotics charges in November 2005.

Parliament subsequently granted him indefinite leave of absence, a decision challenged by Professor Stephen Kwaku Asare.

The Court of Appeal rejected the indefinite leave arrangement, holding that an MP could lose their seat after missing 15 parliamentary sittings without the Speaker’s written permission and without providing a reasonable explanation to the Committee on Privileges.

The court also considered whether the MP’s detention and constitutional presumption of innocence justified his continued absence from Parliament.

Mr Kpebu said the ruling was relevant to the current situation because it addressed the relationship between an MP’s detention and the constitutional requirement to maintain parliamentary representation.

What the Constitution says

Article 97(1)(c) of the 1992 Constitution provides that an MP shall vacate their seat if they are absent from 15 sittings of Parliament, without the Speaker’s permission in writing, and are unable to offer a reasonable explanation for their absence to the Committee on Privileges.

Mr Frimpong was arrested at Amsterdam’s Schiphol Airport on May 10, 2026, following an extradition request from the United States.

Two applications for bail have reportedly been unsuccessful, while his extradition hearing in the Netherlands is scheduled for November 18, 2026.

The outcome of the extradition proceedings and any action by Parliament’s Committee on Privileges could shape the next steps in the matter.

However, Mr Kpebu’s comments reflect his interpretation of the earlier ruling. Any determination of Mr Frimpong’s parliamentary status would depend on the applicable constitutional provisions and the relevant legal and parliamentary processes.

Ghana News.title: UCAES SRC president urges young people to embrace agriculture
Ghana News.content:
The newly elected President of the Students' Representative Council (SRC) of the University College of Agriculture and Environmental Studies (UCAES), Prince Amoako Atta, has called for increased youth participation in agriculture and environmental protection.

The 18th SRC President expressed concern over the declining interest in agriculture, despite the sector employing more than 40 per cent of Ghana's population.

He attributed the trend partly to illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, deforestation and the perception among young people that farming is unattractive.

According to him, Ghana's development prospects are closely linked to its ability to strengthen agricultural production and protect the environment.

Using California as an example, Hon. Amoako Atta highlighted the economic benefits of investing in agriculture, noting that communities could achieve significant growth when the sector receives adequate attention, resources and technological support.

“Agriculture has evolved beyond the traditional use of cutlasses and hoes, with emerging opportunities in agribusiness, biotechnology and other technology-driven agricultural practices,” he said.

He therefore urged young people to change their perception of farming and explore the numerous opportunities available across the agricultural value chain.

Hon. Amoako Atta also emphasised the importance of environmental protection, arguing that human survival depends largely on maintaining a healthy and sustainable environment.

He consequently called on individuals, institutions and the government to make agriculture and environmental protection national priorities to safeguard the country's future.

The UCAES SRC President further appealed to the government to extend support to private institutions specialising in agricultural and environmental education, stressing that their contributions to national development should not be overlooked because of their ownership status.

“The government must therefore pay attention to and support institutions that focus on agriculture and environmental studies to help make Ghana a major food hub,” he said.

He maintained that supporting such institutions would strengthen agricultural education, encourage innovation and equip more young people with the knowledge and skills needed to transform the sector.

Mr. Amoako Atta added that prioritising agriculture would not only improve food security but also promote peace, protect the ecosystem and create a sustainable environment for present and future generations.

He reiterated that a renewed national commitment to agriculture and environmental protection was essential to building a stronger and more resilient economy.

Ghana News.title: Prisons Service calls for national policy to support ex-convicts’ reintegration
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Prisons Service has called for a comprehensive National Reintegration Policy to address the stigma, discrimination and unemployment confronting formerly incarcerated persons as they seek to rebuild their lives after prison.

The Service says the challenges continue to undermine efforts to reintegrate former inmates into society, making it necessary for government, the private sector, families and communities to provide sustained support and employment opportunities.

The call was made at the maiden National Ex-Convicts Conference organised by the Crime Check Foundation at the GNAT Hall in Accra on Wednesday, November 4, 2026.

Held under the theme, “Rebuilding Life After Prison: Effective Reintegration for a Better Society,” the conference brought together stakeholders to discuss ways of addressing social exclusion and creating opportunities for people returning to society after serving prison sentences.

Delivering an address on behalf of the Ghana Prisons Service, the Director of Prisons in Charge of Operations and Facility Management, Mr Benedict Bob-Dery, reaffirmed the Service’s commitment to the rehabilitation and reintegration of inmates.

He, however, identified societal stigma, discrimination and unemployment as major obstacles that make it difficult for former inmates to rebuild their lives.

He urged stakeholders to move beyond prison-based rehabilitation by creating an enabling environment for returning citizens to secure jobs, gain social acceptance and access post-release support.

Mr Bob-Dery said such interventions were necessary to reduce reoffending and promote public safety.

Also addressing the conference, the Chairman of the Prisons Service Council, Apostle Ing. Alexander Nana Yaw Kumi-Larbi, highlighted the importance of prison ministry and partnerships with stakeholders in advancing inmate rehabilitation and reintegration.

He encouraged participants to support the Service’s Think Prisons 360 Degrees Agenda and embrace the Employing the Returning Citizen Campaign.

He stressed that having a criminal record should not become a lifelong barrier to employment and social acceptance, urging society to give formerly incarcerated persons a fair opportunity to rebuild their lives.

Some former inmates who shared their experiences at the conference recounted the difficulties they faced after leaving prison, particularly stigma, discrimination and exclusion from economic opportunities.

They appealed for greater public support and inclusive opportunities to help returning citizens reintegrate successfully.

The event was attended by the Director-General of Prisons (Rtd.), Mr Isaac Kofi Egyir, senior officers of the Ghana Prisons Service and other key stakeholders.

The Service's participation reinforces its position that its mandate extends beyond the safe custody of inmates to include their rehabilitation, reformation and eventual reintegration as productive members of society.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaians hold on to cherished food traditions as Christmas approaches
Ghana News.content:
As Christmas approaches, families are preparing to celebrate the festive season with meals that bring them together and keep cherished food traditions alive.

For many households, Christmas is not just about the celebrations but also the special dishes that have become part of their family traditions. Yet, with the cost of food and festive preparations often a concern, some families are finding ways to maintain their favourite meals without giving up what makes the season special.

Speaking in a Christmas series exploring the foods families cannot do without during the festive season, Daniel Thompson said his family would continue preparing eba, describing it as an affordable meal.

He said the family might switch from yellow gari to white gari to manage costs, but eba would remain part of their Christmas menu.

“We will not stop eating eba because eba is cheap in Ghana. I’ll just change the yellow gari to white gari but I’ll never stop,” he said.

For Gordon Amoah, akple remains an important part of his family's Christmas tradition.

He said the family traditionally prepares the meal during the festive season and intends to maintain the practice this year.

“Traditionally, my family loves to prepare akple during Christmas and that is our main food. Akple is so important to my family in such a way that we believe that you find so much carbohydrates in akple,” he said.

Christiana Ekpe, on the other hand, said fried rice, chicken and salad were the special meals her family looked forward to preparing during the festive season.

She described the combination as an important part of their celebrations, making Christmas more memorable.

Grace Acheampong also shared her family's tradition of preparing waakye with chicken, grilled fish, onion, salad, macaroni and gari every Christmas.

She said the tradition dates back to her childhood, making the meal particularly special to the family.

“We prepare that food because we enjoy it when I was a child,” she said.

The accounts highlight how Christmas meals go beyond satisfying hunger, with family traditions, affordability and childhood memories shaping what households choose to prepare during the festive season.

Ghana News.title: Ayariga urges residents to keep surroundings clean as AMA deploys 20 tricycles
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has urged residents to take greater responsibility for sanitation by ensuring waste is properly disposed of rather than leaving refuse outside their homes for government authorities to collect.

He said keeping communities clean should go beyond maintaining individual homes to include the surrounding environment, stressing that sanitation was a shared responsibility.

“Sometimes people clean their home and just put the waste right in front, and then they make it the responsibility of government to come and take the waste right in front of their homes,” he said.

Mr Ayariga made the remarks while commending the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) for procuring 20 tricycles to support waste collection and sanitation activities across its 20 electoral areas.

He urged other metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies to emulate the initiative by investing their Internally Generated Funds (IGF) in projects that address sanitation challenges.

“I urge your Assembly and others to emulate this example and try and put their IGF to more productive use by making these types of investments,” he said.

The Minister also disclosed that the government was working with development partners to construct additional landfill sites, while investing in transfer stations and vehicles to improve waste collection and evacuation.

AMA deploys tricycles across electoral areas

The Mayor of Accra, Michael Kpakpo Allotey, said the tricycles were procured with the Assembly’s internally generated funds following requests from assembly members for equipment to support sanitation activities in their respective electoral areas.

He said the assembly members had asked him to provide the equipment within one or two months, adding that the Assembly fulfilled the request last week.

“Any time I have an opportunity to talk, I say it’s not about talking, it’s about action,” he said.

The Presiding Member of the AMA and Assembly Member for the Amamomo Electoral Area, Musa Ziyad, said the tricycles formed part of efforts to advance President John Dramani Mahama’s vision of making Accra a cleaner and greener city.

He said the equipment would be distributed across the 20 electoral areas to help assembly members respond to sanitation complaints, evacuate accumulated refuse and address problems such as gutters requiring desilting.

Mr Ziyad explained that having the tricycles available in the electoral areas would allow assembly members to respond more quickly when residents reported sanitation problems.

The initiative forms part of the AMA’s efforts to strengthen community-level sanitation and improve waste management across the capital.

Ghana News.title: Afua Kobi Ampem SHS wins Ashanti NHIS inter-school quiz
Ghana News.content:
Afua Kobi Ampem Senior High School has emerged as the winner of the Ashanti Regional edition of the National Health Insurance Authority’s (NHIA) inter-school quiz competition, beating Ibadur Rahman Academy SHS and Opoku Ware School.

The competition forms part of a nationwide public education initiative aimed at improving students’ understanding of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), including its benefits, entitlements and operations.

Organised under the auspices of NHIA Chief Executive, Dr Victor Asare Bampoe, the initiative involves 48 schools across the country.

Participating schools were provided with study materials and sensitisation to strengthen their knowledge of the scheme ahead of the regional contests.

Speaking on behalf of the NHIA head office in Accra, Acting Head of Corporate Affairs, Oswald Essuah-Mensah, said the initiative was intended to equip young people with the knowledge to understand and effectively use the scheme.

He explained that the sustainability of the NHIS depended on three key stakeholders: the scheme itself, healthcare providers and its members.

“The scheme survives on three legs. Basically, we have the scheme itself, we have our providers, and we have you as members,” he said.

Mr Essuah-Mensah encouraged the students to become ambassadors of the scheme by sharing information about its benefits with people in their communities.

Students highlight learning experience

Speaking on behalf of her teammates, Jacqueline Aygabeng of Afua Kobi Ampem SHS expressed excitement over their victory, describing the competition as challenging but rewarding.

“We don't know how to express the joy, but it wasn't an easy competition. At the end of the day, we give thanks to the Almighty God for being so good to us,” she said.

She said preparing for the contest had been challenging because the subject was relatively new to the team, but support from their patrons and fellow students helped them succeed.

“The moment of learning it and putting the points in our heads was quite tough because it came our way and we didn't really have much knowledge about it,” she added.

Jacqueline said the competition had broadened her understanding of the NHIS and the benefits available to its members.

“I didn't really know how much NHIS was putting into our healthcare until I joined this competition,” she said.

Sixteen winning schools are expected to progress to the zonal competitions, with successful contestants advancing to the grand finale in Accra.

Organisers say the initiative is expected to strengthen awareness of the NHIS among students and encourage them to share their knowledge with their families and communities.

Ghana News.title: GH¢31bn informal cross-border trade faces hurdles despite AfCFTA commitments
Ghana News.content:
Informal cross-border trade in Ghana, estimated at GH¢31 billion in the first three quarters of 2025, continues to face significant operational challenges, raising concerns about the country's ability to fully harness the benefits of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

Despite its contribution to the economy, small-scale traders, particularly women, are confronted with complex border procedures, undocumented levies, prolonged transit delays, inadequate infrastructure and limited access to trade information.

The figures, cited from the Ghana Statistical Service at a stakeholder dialogue in Aflao in the Volta Region, indicate that informal cross-border trade was approximately 54 per cent higher than trade recorded through formal land channels during the period.

It also represented about six per cent of Ghana's total trade, highlighting the economic importance of trading activities that largely operate outside formal channels.

However, representatives of cross-border women traders from Elubo, Hamile, Paga, Aflao and Akanu say the challenges confronting them continue to undermine their ability to expand their businesses and participate fully in formal trade networks.

At the dialogue, the traders reported experiences of arbitrary charges, harassment, confiscation of goods and lengthy delays at border crossings.

They also identified inadequate information on approved trading procedures and the absence of effective complaint mechanisms as factors discouraging their participation in formal trade.

The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) Customs Division says it is taking steps to simplify border procedures through the introduction of the Simplified Goods Declaration (SGD) system, which allows traders to declare their goods and pay the required duties through simplified processes.

A representative of the Customs Division, Joseph Mills, said the authority was working to streamline border operations to facilitate trade.

However, stakeholders noted that existing AfCFTA and ECOWAS simplified trade arrangements are yet to provide specific protections for small-scale traders.

National Coordinator of the AfCFTA National Coordination Office, Dode Seidu, said there was a significant gap between the commitments under the continental trade agreement and the everyday experiences of traders at Ghana's borders.

He called for simplified, gender-responsive trade procedures, improved border infrastructure, accessible trade information and stronger coordination among border agencies.

The stakeholder dialogue, organised by the Africa Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF) in collaboration with the Ghana National AfCFTA Champions, also identified the need to formalise informal trading activities without creating additional barriers for small-scale operators.

A Joint Stakeholder Action Plan developed at the meeting proposes the digitalisation of border processes, including digital travel itineraries and the publication of approved fees.

The Ghana Immigration Service and GRA Customs have been assigned responsibility for advancing these measures, while the Ministries of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, and Gender, Children and Social Protection are expected to support infrastructure improvements, gender-responsive training and trader empowerment.

The Paramount Chief of Aflao, Torgbui Adzonugaga Amenya Fiti V, also called for the development of Aflao into a modern logistics and commercial hub to create more opportunities for women, young people and businesses in border communities.

The dialogue was convened under the African Development Bank-funded CADAST programme, implemented with ESAMI-TRAPCA, to align Ghana's trade and border governance commitments with the realities confronting traders.

Stakeholders say addressing the challenges through transparent fees, simplified procedures, improved infrastructure and accessible grievance mechanisms will be critical to ensuring that small-scale traders benefit from the opportunities offered by AfCFTA.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: AI stocks plunge after US election, driving down markets
World.content:
Tech stocks lead US market slide as investors weigh impact of midterm election results on AI industry.

Share AI stocks plunge after US election, driving down markets on social media

United States markets slid on Thursday, with losses in US chip and data centre-related stocks fuelling pressure on the technology sector following Democrats’ sweeping midterm election wins.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq was down 4.8 percent in midday trading, while the S&P 500 fell 3.6 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 2.8 percent.

US markets jumped on Wednesday following the midterm election, with Democrats’ sweeping wins signalling limits on policy shocks from a Congress at odds with the White House. Markets were also reassured by US President Donald Trump’s remarks that he would accept the election results.

Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks – which have driven much of the market’s growth – led the plunge in the tech sector that drove down markets on Thursday.

Of the 45 data centre ballot initiatives around the country, voters backed restrictions on most of them. According to Data Centers on the Ballot, 39 ballot measures to restrict AI were successful, while only one — in North Dakota — voted against restrictions.

UBS analysts estimated that potential construction pauses could put roughly 30 percent of planned US data centre capacity additions in 2028 at risk, according to the Reuters news agency.

“Yesterday, markets rallied on certainty as election results removed a layer of uncertainty. Today, portfolio managers and analysts are digging into the implications and adjusting expectations for potential political resistance to AI infrastructure, particularly at the state and local levels,” Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager of Founders 100 ETF, told Al Jazeera.



“We’re seeing that concern reflected in the selloff across semiconductors and hyperscalers.”

Data centre operators and neocloud companies were slumping, with CoreWeave down over 12 percent and Nebius Group down nearly 17 percent. Semiconductor stocks such as AI market leader Nvidia fell by 8.2 percent, Micron by nearly 14 percent and Intel by 6.8 percent in midday trading.

AI server manufacturer Dell dropped nearly 13 percent.

Other tech giants were also in negative territory, with Amazon falling 2 percent and Facebook and Instagram’s parent company, Meta, down 3.8 percent.

SpaceX also took a big hit, with shares down 9.5 percent, while Tesla, also owned by billionaire Elon Musk, fell over 11 percent, following Musk’s nearly half-billion-dollar midterm election spending spree.

In Texas, where both companies are headquartered, Musk bet against Democratic candidates who ended up winning their races. Musk shelled out $230m to defeat US Senate candidate James Talarico, $5m to back Gina Hinojosa’s opponent in the governor’s race and $500,000 in the lieutenant governor’s race, which Democrat Vikki Goodwin won.

“We will believe a SpaceX/Tesla merger happens but now faces a much tougher regulatory roadmap to get this deal done in 2027 given this new political blue roadmap in DC/Texas,” Dan Ives, managing partner of Yorkville Ives, said in a note on Thursday.

Gold prices hit a two-week high on Thursday. Spot gold, which is usually considered a safe investment in times of economic uncertainty, jumped just over one percent to $4,115 per ounce.

Technology stocks also pulled the European benchmark stock index lower on Thursday as investors ⁠assessed the outlook for the sector following a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections, Reuters reported.

“It’s really a story of a rotation happening from technology to non-technology and from the US to non-US markets as a result of the midterm elections and the very aggressive Democratic sweep,” said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote Bank.

World.title: Paraguay President Pena resigns in wake of bank collapse
World.content:
President Pena, a Trump ally, had faced an impeachment motion and protests after the collapse of digital lender ueno.

Paraguayan President Santiago Pena resigned on Thursday after calls for his removal swelled following the collapse of digital lender ueno that left millions of customers unable ‌to access their accounts.

“I do so with the stability of our country, social peace and the need to preserve our democratic institutions in mind,” he said in a video recorded address on Thursday.

Pena, an ally of US President Donald Trump, is stepping down after the ⁠opposition called an extraordinary session to begin the process of filing an impeachment motion in Congress, and as protesters demanded his resignation.

Earlier on Thursday Pena lost backing from members of his own conservative party. Vice President Pedro Alliana is set to take office as his replacement.

Lawmakers had accused Pena of conflicts of interest, misuse of pension funds and institutional cover-ups linked to the collapse of ueno, which had grown ‌quickly ⁠from a niche fintech player into a mid-tier bank administering close to $850 million in public funds.

“He is accused of negligence at the very least and complicity in covering up the fact that the bank was insolvent,” said Al Jazeera’s Latin America editor Lucia Newman.

“The congress right now is tying to impeach the president and the vice president, this session is underway,” she added. “As a I speak, there are people outside urging congress not to accept the resignation of the president because they say that they want him tried and impeached.”

Paraguay’s central bank intervened in ueno after determining ⁠that it had breached minimum solvency requirements, setting off a crisis that has left the company’s roughly 3 million customers, in a ⁠country of 6.5 million people, unable to access accounts.



“My greatest wish is that the return of those funds be guaranteed, that the deposit guarantee fund fulfill its purpose, and that ⁠public funds – as well as the resources that belong to all Paraguayans – be protected,” Pena added in his address.

Ueno has made no public statement on the issue.
