World.title: Photos: Spain mourns Jesus de Miguel, who died after on-pitch collision
World.content:
Spain’s national football team coach and the president of Real Madrid joined family, friends and teammates on Thursday at the funeral of Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife player who died after an on‑field collision earlier this week.

The service was held in Navahermosa, a town of about 3,000 people in central Spain, where De Miguel’s parents were reportedly born.

A hearse covered in flowers moved slowly towards the church as dozens of mourners, some carrying candles, walked behind. The town hall declared three days of mourning, with flags at half-staff.

De Miguel, 30, suffered cardiac arrest after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono while challenging for a high ball during a second‑division match on Monday. He died in hospital the following day.

Spain coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid President Florentino Perez attended the funeral, with De la Fuente saying the game’s community “stands united” in grief.

Police have opened a routine investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter to assess whether the challenge went beyond normal play.

Tributes have poured in from clubs across Europe, with De Miguel’s death described as a rare and shocking tragedy in professional football.

World.title: Hoax bomb threats target European airlines and airports for second time in a week
World.content:
At least 21 aircraft and several airports across Europe have been targeted by bomb threats in the second such incident this week, with the UK calling it a "malicious hoax".

Flights to Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, France, Italy, Poland and Romania were affected. An Aer Lingus plane from Dublin to Rome was diverted to an air base in France and Italian fighter jets escorted Finnair's Helsinki-Rome flight.

EasyJet said its flights from Newcastle and Glasgow were met by police in Prague as a precaution. London Heathrow and Birmingham airports received threats that were assessed as not credible.

No explosives have been found during searches, and it is not clear if the incidents, some claimed by a little known group, are related.

World.title: Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war
World.content:
Vice-President JD Vance sent shockwaves through Washington on Wednesday by blaming his party's midterm defeat squarely on the Iran war, in what was widely interpreted as an effort to distance himself from President Donald Trump ahead of a potential 2028 White House run.

In a carefully calibrated, 600-word statement on X, the vice-president acknowledged that Trump's 2024 voters had deserted Republicans in the midterm election.

"The reason we lost is the war," he wrote. "The president himself said so last night."

In interviews late Tuesday night and Wednesday, Trump had defended the war but acknowledged that it played a factor in Democrats flipping control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate.

Vance's view on the war in Iran is an open secret in Washington. While he has repeatedly backed the conflict since the US and Israel attacked Tehran in February, he has reportedly expressed opposition in private meetings with administration officials.

But those disagreements had been kept out of the public eye - until now.

World.title: French protests see numbers surge as unions join strikes over high cost of living
World.content:
More than 600,000 protesters have taken part in rallies and marches across France, according to France's interior ministry, with five unions joining a day of action demanding more money for wages and public services.

The left-wing CGT union put the number of people taking part in Thursday's mobilisation at 1.57 million and hailed the figure as "a level unmatched" since 2023, citing big protests in Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux and Lille.

As darkness fell in Paris, Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu said he would convene a "social conference" with unions and employers next Monday.

The wave of protests began in September over poor conditions and resources at lycÃ©es (high schools), before spreading to universities, workers and a revived "yellow-vest" movement against high prices.

The unions had vowed to take the co-ordinated move against the government "to the next level", and CGT chief Sophie Binet had said their message was that "the only thing that will bring this mobilisation to a halt is responding to our demands".

Interior Minister Laurent NuÃ±ez had earlier deployed 70,000 police, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence.

Some unrest was reported in several cities.

A car was set alight near the Gallieni bridge over the RhÃ´ne river in Lyon, as hundreds of activists from the radical left-wing "black bloc" clashed with police.

Clashes were also reported in the north-western city of Rennes, where the local prefect said a "hostile group of masked individuals" had gathered in front of the main union march. Tear gas was used to clear a square in the south-western city of Bordeaux and a teenager was hurt in a stabbing involving a student at a high-school blockade in the Seine-Saint-Denis suburb of northern Paris.

But the trouble was not on the scale seen during the last big day of protests, on Saturday 17 October, when more than 2,000 stores were looted and historic buildings set on fire.

The provisional numbers reported on Thursday were higher than on 17 October, considered the biggest day of rallies until now when the interior ministry said 550,000 people had turned out and the unions counted 800,000.

Earlier on Thursday the leader of the CFDT union, Marylise LÃ©on, said she would be happy if the protests matched that earlier level.

World.title: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
World.content:
Paraguay's President Santiago PeÃ±a has announced his resignation following a political crisis sparked by the collapse of a bank linked to him.

"I want to apologise to the people if at any point I failed," he said in a video message on social media. "It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me."

The crisis erupted after Ueno Bank entered an insolvency process, which froze all operations. Lawmakers accused PeÃ±a, who was a shareholder until last year in the company that owned the bank, of conflicts of interest and misconduct.

PeÃ±a has rejected suggestions of impropriety. His resignation comes after Paraguay's lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial.

In his video message posted on X, PeÃ±a said his resignation was to protect stability, social peace and democratic institutions.

Ueno Bank has said it has about three million customers, equivalent to about 60% of Paraguay's adult population.

It held pensions and some other public funds and, after its collapse earlier this week, millions could not access their accounts.

The central bank seized the digital lender, and people took to the streets protesting and demanding PeÃ±a's resignation.

A new president of the Central Bank of Paraguay has been appointed and Congress has approved a process to pay depositors.

PeÃ±a won election in 2023 representing Paraguay's ruling conservative Colorado Party, beating a centre-left challenger.

World.title: Manhunt in western Turkey after eight killed in series of shootings
World.content:
A manhunt is under way for a suspect in western Turkey after eight people were killed and one seriously injured in a series of shootings.

The attacks took place in the Afyonkarahisar province on Thursday, with victims found in several locations in three separate vehicles, according to local reports.

CCTV footage published in Turkish media showed a man in a black jacket, white trousers and glasses clutching a long weapon as he stood by a red minivan.

Turkey's state-run Anadolu Agency reported that three people were killed near Ayazini village and three others near Kiyir village. In Yukaritandir, two women were found injured and later died in hospital.

Two teachers were reportedly among the dead.

Local media said roads leading to the affected villages were closed by police, while officers launched a large-scale operation to find the suspect, who fled the scene.

The newspaper Milliyet reports that a vehicle allegedly taken by the attacker was later found stuck in mud, and that the suspect had abandoned it before fleeing on foot.

In a statement posted on social media, the Afyonkarahisar Governorate said "all relevant institutions of our state have been working in coordination since the very first moment and are meticulously carrying out the necessary work."

It added: "We pray to God for mercy on the deceased citizens and offer our condolences and patience to their grieving families and loved ones."

World.title: The Pitt and ER are similar enough for lawsuit to proceed, judge rules
World.content:
US drama The Pitt is similar enough to medical series ER for a lawsuit against its producers to progress, a court in the US has ruled.

The widow of Michael Crichton, who created ER, argues The Pitt is effectively a reboot of the series, which has been made without proper permission or credit.

Sherri Crichton says her husband's contract included a "frozen rights" provision that prohibited any spin-offs, sequels or reboots of ER being made without his express consent.

A three-judge panel said there are "clear and numerous similarities between The Pitt and ER," which means the case can go ahead. Warner Bros previously described the lawsuit as "baseless" and sought to have it dismissed.

Listing the similarities between the two shows, the court cited the emergency room setting, the fast pace, use of medical jargon, graphic depictions of injuries, and younger doctors fresh from medical school being trained.

"We find the details here suffice for a prima facie case," the judges said.

It means the case will now go to a jury trial in Los Angeles Superior Court.

But the judges dismissed separate claims against actor-producer Noah Wyle, executive producer John Wells and showrunner R Scott Gemmill.

The justices said there was insufficient evidence to show the three producers were aware they could be violating Crichton's contractual rights.

World.title: Russell Brand is being investigated over two new rape complaints, police say
World.content:
Warning: Details of rape and sexual assault

Russell Brand is being investigated over rape allegations made by two more women, it can now be reported.

The disgraced comedian has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault by a jury of eight men and four women at Southwark Crown Court, following a three-week trial.

More victims are likely to come forward following his conviction, the detective who led the police investigation has said.

Det Supt Andy Furphy, from the Metropolitan Police, said he hoped other women would gain "courage" and "confidence" from the guilty verdicts.

Brand was found not guilty of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault.

World.title: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years
World.content:
Wong, who turned 30 last month, has already been imprisoned multiple times for his activism which started when he was in his early teens.

On Thursday, he arrived in court wearing a dark blue long-sleeved shirt, khaki trousers and black-rimmed glasses. He looked slimmer compared to his previous public appearances.

He nodded in greeting towards members of the packed public gallery, and took notes intermittently as the judge read out the reasons for his sentencing.

A crowd had gathered outside the court, with dozens of Hongkongers having queued for hours hoping to get a seat in the public gallery. There was also a heavy police presence.

Wong is already serving time for subversion and was due to be freed early next year when he was handed the latest charges, to which he pleaded guilty in September.

Two months and two days of the 10-year term will be served concurrently with his ongoing sentence, the judge said on Thursday.

Prosecutors said Wong had conspired with other campaigners, including self-exiled activist Nathan Law, to lobby for foreign sanctions and blockades against Beijing.

These activities took place between July and late November 2020, the court heard.

Wong and Law had been co-founders of Demosisto, a now defunct pro-democracy political party.

On Thursday, Hong Kong's chief executive John Lee said Wong and Law were "among the primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong's prosperity and stability".

Their actions "not only severely undermined national sovereignty, security, and development interests, but also directly prejudiced the well-being of the general public and the stability of society," Lee said in a statement issued after the ruling.

Beijing's foreign ministry said China "firmly supports [Hong Kong] in safeguarding national security in accordance with the law". It also called on "relevant parties" to "earnestly respect China's sovereignty and Hong Kong's legal system".

World.title: MultiChoice introduces new DStv, GOtv packages
World.content:
MultiChoice Nigeria, a CANAL+ company, has introduced new subscription packages for its DStv and GOtv platforms to broaden its offerings and improve subscribers’ viewing experience.

The company unveiled the packages at an event held on Wednesday at The Royal Box, Victoria Island, Lagos. Media professionals, industry stakeholders, partners and other guests attended the event to witness the unveiling and learn about the updated subscription options.

The new arrangement, which takes effect on 5 November, brings SuperSport KICKOFF and Africa Magic+ to the lower subscription tiers. According to MultiChoice, the additions will give more households across the country access to football and Nigerian drama.

Under the revised arrangement, DStv subscribers can choose from four packages: Starter, Select, Sports and Premium. GOtv customers, meanwhile, will have access to Easy, Starter, Select and Sports.

Subscribers on DStv’s ₦6,000 Starter package will enjoy SuperSport KICKOFF and Africa Magic+. In contrast, the ₦21,000 Sports package will cover every Premier League and Champions League fixture, alongside WWE and UFC content.

Feedback

MultiChoice Nigeria CEO Kemi Omotosho said the company incorporated subscribers’ feedback into developing its new packages.

She said the changes reflect Nigerians’ calls for improved value, greater choice and content that caters to their preferences.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Folu Storms and Deji Osikoya co-hosted the event, which featured performances by spoken-word artist Ibquake and The Loud Choir. The two acts entertained attendees with a medley of popular Nigerian songs.

Several personalities attended the event, including media executives Darey Art Alade and Deola Art Alade, filmmaker Tola Odunsi, actress Enado Odigie, costume designer Yolanda Okereke, BBNaija stars Temi Nkem, Kola Omotosho and Imisi Ayanwale, and media personalities Uti Nwachukwu, Chuey Chu and Hero Daniels.

World.title: Civil society groups demand methane crackdown ahead of 2027 elections
World.content:
Civil society organisations working on environmental accountability and extractive industry governance have called on the Nigerian government to strengthen enforcement of methane regulations, improve access to emissions data and address environmental damage in oil-producing communities ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The organisations, under the methane emissions cohort of the Civil Society Expert Group on Gas (CSEGonG), said Nigeria’s methane governance framework had recorded progress but remained crippled by weak implementation, inadequate regulatory oversight and limited public access to credible emissions information.

They also raised concerns about the transparency and accessibility of environmental remediation funding following the introduction of Executive Order 9 of 2026, warning that changes to existing funding arrangements could weaken efforts to address longstanding environmental problems in oil-producing communities.

The concerns were in a communiqué issued after a stakeholder engagement convened in Abuja on 26 October by the Natural Resource Governance Institute (NRGI) and Africa Practice, in consultation with the Environmental Defense Fund.

The meeting brought together civil society organisations and researchers working on methane emissions, environmental accountability and energy transition to assess progress, identify gaps and develop a coordinated advocacy agenda.

The groups said the 2027 elections presented an opportunity to make methane governance a major issue in public policy debates, calling on civil society organisations to engage political candidates and institutions through nonpartisan, evidence-based advocacy.

The call coincides with a series of PREMIUM TIMES investigations documenting constant gas flaring, weak enforcement of anti-flaring regulations and the consequences of methane emissions for oil-producing communities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In September, PREMIUM TIMES reported that oil companies continued to flare gas and emit methane despite Nigeria’s strengthened anti-flaring and methane reduction laws, with regulatory failures allowing violations to continue. A subsequent investigation published in October documented weaknesses in the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission’s enforcement of methane regulations and notable gaps in emissions measurement and disclosure.

Bille gas leaks raise accountability concerns

The organisations specifically highlighted the ongoing gas seepage in Bille, a riverine community in Degema Local Government Area of Rivers State, as an example of the need to strengthen community-level environmental monitoring and regulatory accountability.

PREMIUM TIMES reported in June that gas had continued escaping from abandoned oil and gas infrastructure in the community, threatening residents’ livelihoods and raising concerns about environmental contamination and public safety.

The situation subsequently took a tragic turn when Joy Amos, a 29-year-old woman who suffered severe burns in a gas explosion in Bille, died in September.

The civil society organisations called for improved community-led documentation of gas leaks, flaring incidents and emissions from abandoned or improperly decommissioned oil infrastructure.

They also asked authorities to provide clearer mechanisms through which affected communities could report environmental incidents, obtain investigations and secure remediation.

The groups called for an assessment of the implications of Executive Order 9 of 2026 for environmental remediation funding, arguing that the revised arrangements could weaken transparency, accessibility and accountability in the management of resources meant to address environmental damage.

The Petroleum Industry Act provides for an Environmental Remediation Fund to finance the rehabilitation or management of negative environmental impacts arising from petroleum operations. Its provisions allow regulators to apply the fund where operators fail or are unable to undertake the required remediation.

EU methane rules could affect Nigerian gas exports

The organisations also warned that Nigeria’s failure to improve methane measurement, reporting and verification could expose its oil and gas industry to commercial risks as international markets tighten environmental requirements.

They particularly cited the European Union’s methane regulations, which introduce monitoring, reporting and verification requirements for imported oil and gas from 2027.

According to the communiqué, Nigerian exporters seeking to maintain access to European markets would increasingly need to show credible emissions reporting and compliance with emerging requirements.

The groups said that capturing methane that would otherwise escape into the atmosphere or be flared could also provide economic benefits by recovering gas for commercial use, improving energy supply and reducing emissions.

They urged government agencies, petroleum operators and development partners to prioritise commercially viable methane capture and utilisation projects while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.

Groups seek coordinated advocacy

The organisations further recommended that the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority and other relevant institutions improve public access to emissions data, compliance records, enforcement actions and progress towards methane reduction commitments.

They called on civil society organisations to consolidate existing research and monitoring initiatives into a coordinated advocacy framework, with clear policy proposals on regulatory enforcement, environmental remediation, emissions disclosure, energy recovery and community protection.

The communiqué also identified the need to involve faith-based organisations, labour unions, professional associations and other influential groups in methane accountability campaigns.

It said existing expertise and monitoring initiatives were not being shared sufficiently among organisations, resulting in missed opportunities for collaboration and possible duplication of efforts.

The organisations recommended strengthening the use of independent emissions data and available monitoring technologies to help journalists, researchers and community groups scrutinise the activities of petroleum operators and regulators.

Members of the Methane Emissions Cohort of CSEGonG include: NRGI, Policy Alert, Paradigm Leadership Support Initiative, BudgIT Foundation, Stakeholder Democracy Network, We The People, Center for Environment, Human Rights and Development and Africa Practice.

World.title: GTCO launches directory for African textile makers, artisans
World.content:
Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc (GTCO) on Thursday unveiled an online directory for textile producers, indigenous artisans and fashion manufacturers.

The initiative was announced at a media briefing in Lagos ahead of the ninth GTCO Fashion Weekend, scheduled for Saturday and Sunday at the GTCentre, Plot 1, Water Corporation Drive, Oniru.

Speaking at the briefing, GTCO’s Group Head of Corporate Communications, Oyinade Adegite, said the directory formed part of the GTCO Fashion Collective, a platform intended to keep fashion professionals connected beyond the company’s annual two-day event.

According to her, the collective will accommodate designers, models, stylists, photographers, editors, buyers, content creators and other industry professionals.

Textile and manufacturing directory

The platform includes separate directories for textile makers and manufacturers, with information on their locations, specialities, and contact details.

The textile section features fabric suppliers, printmakers and producers, including artisans involved in Aso-oke weaving, Adire dyeing and other indigenous textile-making processes.

Its manufacturing catalogue focuses on Nigerian businesses working across different areas of fashion production.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ms Adegite said the directory was created to give greater visibility to producers whose contributions often received less attention than those of designers and fashion brands.

“These makers are the foundation on which African fashion stands, and they deserve a permanent, searchable home in our ecosystem,” she said.

Fashion manufacturers interested in being listed can submit their business information for consideration.

GTCO, however, said the directory was provided only for discovery and listing purposes. It said it neither endorsed nor guaranteed the manufacturers listed and advised users to conduct their own checks before entering into business agreements.

The platform also offers guidance on questions designers may need to ask prospective manufacturers, including minimum order quantities, production timelines, available materials, sampling procedures, pricing and payment terms.

Fashion Weekend begins Saturday

Meanwhile, the ninth GTCO Fashion Weekend will run from Saturday through Sunday.

The event, themed “Fashion Is Timeless,” will run from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. on both days, with free public admission.

Organisers said the programme would feature runway presentations, masterclasses, retail outlets, a craft and fabric market, industry conversations and a streetwear hub.

Designers scheduled to present collections on Saturday include Tongoro, FIA Factory, Ibrahim Fernandez, Washington Roberts, Maison Sara Chraibi and Imane Ayissi.

Sunday’s runway programme will feature Sukeina, House of Marvee, Selam Fessahaye, Kim Shui, Ohlanna by Zikora and LaQuan Smith.

Fashion and beauty professionals billed to lead masterclasses include Sherlina Nym, Rachel Ojuromi and Renee Morris, founder of natural hair brand Uncle Funky’s Daughter. A skincare session by Buttah Skin is also scheduled.

According to GTCO, about 140 fashion retailers will participate over the weekend.

The addition of a craft and fabric market will give textile makers and artisans a physical space to exhibit their products alongside the runway shows and retail activities.

The Fashion Collective will remain accessible online after the event, providing industry listings, professional profiles and information about subsequent programmes.

World.title: Group calls for withdrawal of charges against Kaduna journalist
World.content:
The Legal Defence and Assistance Project (LEDAP), a nonprofit organisation that promotes and protects human rights and the rule of law, has called for the withdrawal of criminal charges against Farida Isiak, a 23-year-old journalist with Nagarta Radio in Kaduna State, over a Facebook post criticising the police.

The rights organisation also demanded an independent investigation into alleged misconduct by the police officers involved in her arrest and the detention of her parents.

In a statement issued on Thursday, LEDAP said recent investigative reporting by the International Centre for Investigative Reporting (ICIR) had raised fresh concerns about the circumstances surrounding Ms Isiak’s arrest and prosecution.

PREMIUM TIMES had earlier reported that the incident began on 19 October following a disagreement between Ms Isiak’s mother and a neighbour over ₦100 change from a charcoal sale.

According to family sources, the journalist’s mother sold N400 worth of charcoal to a girl sent by their neighbour. The girl paid with a N500 note but was allowed to take the charcoal and return later with the money. When she eventually paid, the woman gave her N100 as change.

The following day, the neighbour returned to buy charcoal and disputed the earlier transaction, insisting that she had not received her change. The disagreement escalated, and the neighbour reportedly returned with another woman before police officers were called to the scene.

As PREMIUM TIMES reported, police officers arrested Ms Isiak’s mother. Her father was also detained after he went to the police station to secure his wife’s release.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Family sources alleged that the police used the detention of her parents to compel the journalist to report to the station.

Ms Isiak had earlier criticised the police on Facebook over the arrest of her parents. PREMIUM TIMES reported that officers accused her of defamation and demanded that she delete the post and apologise to Usman Adamu, the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) of Mararaban Jos.

She reportedly complied, hoping her parents would be released. However, the police subsequently detained her.

On 21 October, she was taken before a Sharia Court in Kawo, where she pleaded guilty to the defamation charge and was sentenced to four years’ imprisonment or a ₦1.75 million fine.

However, after her lawyer, Mukhtar Abubakar, intervened, the court set aside the initial proceedings and conviction, allowing her to enter a fresh plea. She pleaded not guilty and was granted bail, PREMIUM TIMES reported.

Allegations against the police

LEDAP’s statement drew on an ICIR investigation published on 2 November, titled “How Police Allegedly Discarded Due Process in Kaduna Journalist’s Arrest.”

The investigation detailed Ms Isiak’s allegations that police officers detained her parents to force her to report to the station over her Facebook post.

She also alleged that officers demanded that she delete the post and apologise to the DPO before her parents could be released.

LEDAP said the alleged detention of her parents raised concerns about the practice of “arrest by proxy”, which it said is prohibited under Section 36 of the Nigeria Police Act 2020.

The provision prohibits the police from arresting a person in place of a suspect.

“The reported facts therefore warrant an independent examination of the legal basis for the detention of her parents and the actions of the officers involved,” the statement said.

The organisation also questioned the impartiality of the police investigation, noting that the DPO was reportedly the subject of Ms Isiak’s criticism but was allegedly involved in the investigation.

It said the circumstances raised concerns about a possible conflict of interest, abuse of police authority, and officers’ obligation to act within the law.

Concerns over court proceedings

LEDAP also questioned the initial court proceedings that resulted in Ms Isiak’s conviction and sentence.

It said reports indicated that she was arraigned, convicted and sentenced without her lawyers present, raising concerns about whether she understood the proceedings, had access to legal representation and could exercise her right to a fair hearing.

The organisation said the circumstances surrounding the initial conviction required scrutiny, particularly the decision to proceed without her lawyer.

“The administration of justice must not only be fair but must also be seen to be fair,” the statement said.

Constitutional rights

LEDAP cited Sections 35, 36 and 39 of the 1999 Constitution, which guarantee personal liberty, the right to a fair hearing and freedom of expression.

It said these constitutional protections meant that criminal proceedings should not be used to intimidate people for expressing criticism or holding public officials accountable.

The organisation acknowledged that freedom of expression did not place anyone above the law but stressed that public criticism should not attract intimidation or retaliatory action.

“Criticism of public officials must not attract intimidation, retaliatory action or disproportionate criminal proceedings,” it said.

It added that defamation allegations should be addressed through lawful procedures rather than the misuse of police powers.

LEDAP said the case raised broader concerns about police accountability, access to justice and the integrity of judicial proceedings, particularly the treatment of journalists who report on public institutions.

What LEDAP wants

LEDAP called on the relevant authorities to withdraw the charges against Ms Isiak and take all lawful steps necessary to discontinue her prosecution.

It also demanded an independent, impartial and transparent investigation into the alleged detention of her parents, the circumstances of her arrest, the reported demand that she delete her Facebook post and apologise, and the conduct of the officers involved.

The organisation further called for an investigation into possible abuse of police authority and conflict of interest, with appropriate disciplinary or legal action against any officer found culpable.

It also sought an independent review of the initial court proceedings, including the conduct of the presiding judicial officer.

The group urged the authorities to guarantee Ms Isiak’s right to a fair hearing in any further proceedings, including access to legal representation, adequate time to prepare her defence and protection from intimidation.

It further called for appropriate remedies for any unlawful arrest or detention suffered by the journalist and her parents, as well as measures to protect journalists reporting on public institutions.

“No individual should be subjected to intimidation, unlawful detention or questionable criminal proceedings for exercising constitutionally protected rights,” the statement said.

LEDAP warned that public officials should not use their office’s authority to pursue personal grievances or suppress legitimate criticism.

It urged Nigerian authorities to demonstrate their commitment to the rule of law, due process, freedom of expression and the protection of citizens’ fundamental rights.

LEDAP is a non-governmental organisation that promotes human rights, the rule of law, accountability and access to justice in Nigeria through legal assistance, advocacy, public interest litigation and human rights education.

World.title: Afrinvest CEO recalls how Elumelu’s $1 million loan helped salvage firm from crisis
World.content:
Tony Elumelu played a supreme role in getting investment bank Afrinvest back on track in 2011 after the global financial meltdown pushed the investment bank to the brink, its chief executive recalled in a letter to the tycoon seen by PREMIUM TIMES.

The multisectoral magnate, who is the top shareholder of United Bank for Africa, the Transcorp Group, and Seplat Energy, granted a soft loan of $1 million to Ike Chioke, the CEO of the financial institution, as a mark of urgent support when the firm direly needed the cash to recapitalise, the latter said.

“Fifteen years ago, Afrinvest was navigating one of the most challenging periods in its history, as we struggled to rebuild and recapitalise the business in the aftermath of the global financial crisis,” Mr Chioke said.

“At that critical juncture, when the future was far from certain, you made the remarkable decision to lend me US$1 million of your personal funds. You placed your confidence not simply in the prospects of a business but in me as an individual, my integrity, my determination and my conviction that Afrinvest could emerge stronger from adversity.”

This June, Mr Chioke eventually completed the repayment of the credit, according to the letter, describing the gesture as an extraordinary act of friendship, generosity and trust.

Mr Elumelu, whose economic vision is anchored on what he calls “Africapitalism” – an investment philosophy that prioritises the private sector’s role in democratising the wealth Africa needs to power large-scale growth, has been involved in active philanthropic initiatives on the continent.

In March, his foremost charity project, the Tony Elumelu Foundation, turned sixteen, and he said the initiative had disbursed over $100 million in seed capital to 24,000 entrepreneurs in Africa and created more than 1.5 million jobs over the period.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The foundation expects to fund an additional 3,200 entrepreneurs this year, it said in September.

Mr Chioke applauded the profound impact Mr Elumelu’s financial assistance has had on Afrinvest, notably transforming it into a diversified regional financial services group with an expanding universe of clients and operations in asset management, investment banking, research & consulting, and securities trading.

World.title: ‘Nigeria is proud of you’ – Tinubu hails Flamingos’s historic World Cup feat
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, following their historic qualification for the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco.

The President also expressed confidence that the team can defeat Japan in Saturday’s final and win the country’s first title in the competition.

The Flamingos booked their place in the final after defeating Brazil 3-1 in Wednesday’s semi-final at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat.

Queen Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute before Awawu Bashiru struck twice in the 71st and 80th minutes to give Nigeria a commanding advantage. Brazil’s Greise Kelly scored a late consolation in the 89th minute.

In a statement issued on Thursday by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, Mr Tinubu described the qualification as a remarkable achievement that had brought pride and joy to Nigerians at home and abroad.

He also commended the team’s coaching crew and others whose contributions supported the Flamingos’ impressive campaign.

The President urged the players to maintain the determination and confidence that had taken them to the final, assuring them of the nation’s support.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I encourage you to approach the final with the same fighting spirit and belief that have brought you this far. I have confidence in your ability to make history by winning the coveted world title,” he said.

Mr Tinubu also called on Nigerians to rally behind the team, describing the players as young ambassadors whose achievements could inspire more girls to pursue their sporting ambitions.

“Once again, Nigeria is proud of you. Go for the trophy, Flamingos!” he added.

A historic campaign

The Flamingos’ qualification represents Nigeria’s first appearance in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup since the competition began in 2008.

Their previous best performance came at the 2022 edition in India, where they finished third after defeating Germany in the bronze-medal match. They also reached the semi-finals in that tournament.

The team’s journey in Morocco has been marked by an impressive recovery after a 2-1 opening-day defeat to Poland.

Under head coach Akeem Busari, Nigeria responded with victories over Puerto Rico and defending champions DPR Korea before eliminating Mexico and Venezuela in the knockout rounds.

Their 3-1 victory over Brazil was particularly emphatic, with the Flamingos registering 35 attempts on goal against the South Americans’ seven.

The result also ended Brazil’s hopes of reaching their first final in the competition.

Nigeria will now face Japan in Saturday’s title decider, with both teams seeking their maiden U-17 women’s world crown.

The Flamingos have already secured Nigeria’s best-ever finish in the competition. A victory over Japan would, however, take the achievement further by delivering the country’s first world title at this level.

World.title: Criticise government, but don’t incite violence, Akume tells writers
World.content:
The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, has urged Nigerian writers to continue scrutinising those in authority without using their influence to promote violence or deepen divisions.

Mr Akume was represented by the Permanent Secretary, Political and Economic Affairs in the Office of the SGF, Bekearedebo Augusta Warrens, who delivered his address at the opening of the 45th International Convention and Conference of the Association of Nigerian Authors (ANA).

The event was held on 30 October at the Mamman Jiya Vatsa Writers’ Village in Mpape, Abuja.

The convention, themed “Literature, National Security and the Place of Nigeria in the World,” brought writers, scholars and other stakeholders together to examine literature’s contribution to peace, security and Nigeria’s international image.

In the address delivered on his behalf, Mr Akume said literature went beyond entertainment because writers highlighted communities’ struggles and articulated experiences people might find hard to express.

He said poems could capture shared emotions, while plays and other literary works could demonstrate the consequences of injustice in ways that statistics alone could not.

The SGF maintained that writers had the right to examine difficult subjects, question public officials and criticise government policies. He warned, however, against using words to encourage hostility among Nigerians.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This does not mean that writers should avoid difficult subjects or that government criticism should be discouraged, far from it. Freedom of expression and the right to question those in authority are important features of democratic life,” Mrs Warrens said, quoting the SGF.

“What we should resist is the deliberate use of words to incite violence or cause Nigerians to hate one another.”

‘Nigeria needs honest voices’

Mr Akume encouraged ANA members to remain outspoken about the country’s problems while framing their interventions in ways that could improve public understanding and encourage practical responses.

“My appeal to members of the Association of Nigerian Authors is simple: Nigeria needs honest voices, not silence,” the address read.

“Continue to speak frankly about our national challenges. Help us to confront the issues that divide us, but do so in ways that deepen understanding and encourage solutions.”

He added that serious engagement between intellectuals and policymakers could help public conversations move beyond accusations towards workable solutions.

According to him, contributions from organisations such as ANA could enrich national debates and sharpen government policies.

‘Writers are prophets’

Senator Ekong Sampson, who also spoke at the convention, described writers as prophets whose works frequently anticipated the crises societies later confronted.

Citing Chinua Achebe’s A Man of the People and the writings of Cyprian Ekwensi, the senator said Nigerian authors had long warned about many of the political and social problems confronting the country.

“Writers have paid their dues. They have prophesied, and they must be listened to,” he said. “The more we listen to our writers, the safer we are as a country.”

Mr Sampson urged the government to protect the legacies of Nigerian writers, noting that authors remained alive through their works long after their deaths.

He recalled the deaths of poet Christopher Okigbo and soldier-poet Mamman Jiya Vatsa, after whom the ANA Writers’ Village is named, arguing that a democratic society might have offered them greater protection.

Although Mr Okigbo died during the Nigerian Civil War and Mr Vatsa was executed following his conviction over an alleged coup plot, the senator said their stories continued to be retold because of their literary contributions.

“Writers never die. Writers live on through the stories they have told,” he said.

Government, writers must collaborate

Mr Sampson said the government should not remain distant from citizens, just as writers should not treat public institutions as inaccessible.

He maintained that insecurity affects everyone and requires collective responsibility, rather than leaving the burden entirely to security agencies or the government.

“With insecurity, you are either infected or affected,” he said. “It is a great responsibility, so we must all join hands. More importantly, we must listen to writers.”

The senator argued that Nigeria already had several laws but struggled to implement them. He urged citizens and public officials to accept responsibility for obeying and enforcing existing laws.

He also challenged writers to examine contemporary problems in light of past experiences and offer society broader perspectives.

Mr Sampson cited the monthly Uyo Book Club as an example of how writers could build closer relationships with public institutions. The club brings officials, readers and writers together for book readings and conversations with featured authors.

“You get close to the government that way,” he said. “I look forward to ANA meeting me the same way. Let us see how we, as writers, can meet, talk to ourselves and determine how we can work with the states for facilities.”

Literature beyond propaganda

Delivering the keynote address, Professor Mahfouz Adedimeji said literature should not be reduced to propaganda or treated only as a commercial and entertainment product.

He examined the connection between literature, peacebuilding and the struggle to shape public imagination, arguing that national security could not be achieved through military force alone.

Mr Adedimeji recommended that literature be incorporated into Nigeria’s security and peacebuilding strategies. He said films, plays and other creative productions should contribute to building a peaceful society rather than focusing exclusively on awards and profits.

He also called for literature and the humanities to be strengthened within the education system, with greater emphasis on reading, writing, critical thinking, ethical reasoning, civic consciousness and cultural understanding.

“The world is in turmoil today because guided weapons are in the hands of misguided people,” he said.

According to him, society’s emphasis on economic figures and other quantitative measures often came at the expense of values and the quality of human relationships.

Publishing, education and cultural diplomacy

The professor urged the government and private sector to strengthen Nigeria’s publishing industry, provide more awards and incentives for authors, and improve institutional protection for intellectual property.

He said books should occupy an important place in any country seeking meaningful development, particularly at a time when some young Nigerians described education as a scam.

Mr Adedimeji also proposed using literature to promote national integration. He encouraged tertiary institutions to expose students to works from different Nigerian communities and African societies.

Literary festivals, school debates, drama competitions and cultural programmes, he said, could serve as instruments of social cohesion.

He further recommended incorporating international literary exchanges, publishing partnerships, the translation of Nigerian works, and cultural diplomacy into the country’s foreign policy.

Universities, he added, should conduct practical research into subjects such as literature’s role in reconciliation and the ways language could shape conflict.

Good governance and security

Mr Adedimeji said literary interventions could not compensate for poor governance, injustice and institutional failure.

He urged political leaders to show through their actions that every Nigerian has dignity, value, and a stake in the country.

The professor argued that insecurity extended beyond physical violence to include political, food, economic, personal and environmental insecurity.

He said many security problems originated in damaged human relationships and crises of trust, citizenship, justice, memory and identity.

Literature, according to him, could expose injustice before it became normalised, transform citizens’ thinking and give Nigeria a voice that travelled beyond conventional diplomatic and political relations.

ANA seeks improved security

ANA National President Usman Oladipo Akanbi commended the federal government for supporting Nigerian writers, including by providing the land on which the writers’ village was developed.

Mr Akanbi also acknowledged the administration’s support for measures enabling authors to benefit from the reproduction of their works through the Reproduction Rights Society of Nigeria.

He urged the government, however, to intensify efforts to address insecurity and create conditions that would restore Nigerians’ confidence in the country’s future.

READ ALSO: Akume seeks unity in Benue APC ahead of presidential primary

“No nation can grow when its young people have lost hope. And without hope, no reform can succeed,” he said.

“Reforms, however well-intentioned, must not be perceived as punishment.”

Warning ahead of 2027 elections

Mr Akanbi cautioned political parties, candidates and their supporters against inflammatory conduct as preparations intensify for the 2027 general elections.

He said political competition should not become a source of violence or hostility.

“We must ensure that the 2027 elections are conducted in an environment devoid of rancour, bitterness and ill will,” the ANA president said. “Our politics must not become a war.”

He added that building a stable country required cooperation between citizens and those entrusted with public office.

“Nation-building is a collective task. Government cannot do it alone, and citizens cannot thrive without responsible government,” he said.

World.title: Governor Lawal distributes 300 vehicles, 2,000 bikes to Zamfara groups, individuals
World.content:
Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal has distributed 300 vehicles and 2,000 motorcycles to various Zamfara groups and individuals saying that the empowerment means giving people and grassroots organisations practical tools to become self-reliant, restore dignity, and deliver democracy’s dividends, not rhetoric.

The governor on Thursday distributed the vehicles and motorcycles to groups and individuals at a ceremony held at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau.

The empowerment programme recognises the immense contributions of groups and individuals to the State’s overall development.

The distribution of 300 vehicles and 2,000 motorcycles is part of a state government empowerment programme aimed at engaging people and groups in productive activities and boosting the local economy.

In his remarks, Governor Lawal said the event marks another milestone in his rescue agenda to reward dedicated people and groups contributing to Zamfara State’s socio-economic and political development.

He said, “It gives me great pleasure to be here for the official distribution of vehicles to various carefully selected individuals and political groups across Zamfara State. This gathering is particularly important because it offers me a unique opportunity to distribute these vehicles formally.

“Let me emphasise here that empowerment goes beyond rhetoric – it requires providing our people and grassroots organisations with the practical tools needed to be self-reliant, restore dignity, and deliver the real dividends of democracy. We remain fully committed to supporting our people in rebuilding and revitalising Zamfara to make it a more prosperous State.

“I therefore call on you as beneficiaries of the gesture to remain firm and committed to championing our drive to rescue the good people of Zamfara State. Your strategic role in partnering with the current administration remains vital.

“As you are officially presented with your vehicles, which will be performed shortly, I urge you to utilise them efficiently. This gesture is designed to facilitate mobility across the State and improve the local economy.

World.title: 2027: Obi’s wave doesn’t exist again, he has nothing to offer — Wike
World.content:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has dismissed the political support behind Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying the wave that propelled him in the 2023 election no longer exists.

Wike also described Obi as a dramatist, insisting that the former Anambra State governor had nothing to offer Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election.

The minister spoke on Thursday during his monthly media chat in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, where he questioned the prospects of the NDC presidential ticket featuring Obi and former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.

“All this so-called Obi kererenke doesn’t exist again. I have killed it,” Wike said.

He argued that the political circumstances that helped Obi secure significant support in the 2023 presidential election had changed.

“Nigerians know that Obi has nothing to offer, he is a dramatist. You were there when Soludo exposed him,” the minister said.

Wike also criticised the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, saying Nigerians had already given him and other politicians opportunities to govern.

“Nigerians know that Atiku and co have been given the opportunity, but they did not do anything. Nigerians know that the former governor of Rivers State looted our state,” he said.

The FCT minister acknowledged Kwankwaso’s popularity but questioned whether his political influence extended beyond Kano State, where he won the 2023 presidential election.

“I agree that Kwankwaso is very popular, but he ran in 2023 and won in Kano, fine, but what about the other northern states? What about the North-Central, what will happen there?” he asked.

Wike further questioned whether Obi still enjoyed the level of financial and popular support associated with his 2023 presidential campaign.

“The Obi wave is dead and buried. How many people are contributing money for Obi today?” he said.

World.title: Bwala to David Mark-led exco: You took over ADC leadership undemocratically and hoped all is well
World.content:
Special Adviser to President Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala

Presidential aide Daniel Bwala has criticised the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), accusing it of taking over the party’s leadership without due process.

Bwala made the remarks in a post on his X platform on Thursday, following the controversy surrounding the leadership of the opposition party.

He said a political party seeking to govern Nigeria must uphold the principles of due process, equity and justice, accusing the Mark-led executive of disregarding those principles in its emergence.

“A political party that wants to govern Nigeria must be a party of due process, equity and justice.

“You descended on ADC like a thief in the night, took over its leadership undemocratically and hoped that all is well,” he wrote.

Bwala further accused the leadership of violating the party’s constitution and guidelines, as well as the Nigerian Constitution and the provisions of the Electoral Act and guidelines of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

He said the alleged violations amounted to a disregard for Nigerians, accusing the party leadership of assuming that the public could be misled over the circumstances surrounding its emergence.

Bwala also took a swipe at individuals lobbying on behalf of the party leadership, suggesting that they were expecting financial rewards.

The comments came amid the dispute over the ADC leadership and a court ruling affecting the Mark-led executive committee.

World.title: 2027 Polls: Tinubu storms Akwa Ibom, Rivers for presidential campaign
World.content:
—To commission projects in Uyo

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA –PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu will depart Abuja on Friday, November 6, for a two-state visit to Akwa Ibom and Rivers.

The President will first visit Uyo, the Akwa Ibom State capital, to commission landmark projects completed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration and attend a political rally.

Governor Eno, the host, has declared Friday a work-free day in the state to give the President a rousing reception.

Among the projects President Tinubu scheduled for commissioning in Uyo are the new International Terminal Building, the International Airport Hospital, and the Ibom Aviation Village, all located at the Victor Attah International Airport.

President Tinubu will also commission the Airport-Okopedi Road in Nsit Atai and Okobo Local Government Areas and Ring Road 3, linking Idoro Road to Ikot Ekpene Road through Uyo and Ibiono Ibom.

Other projects include the AKWA-GIS Office Complex, the Command and Control Centre and the ARISE Palm Resort.

On Saturday, President Tinubu will leave for Port Harcourt, Rivers State, to take part in the All Progressives Congress rally.

The rally will be his third, since he flagged off the re-election campaign in Kaduna last month.

The visits will also give President Tinubu opportunities to engage with political stakeholders, party members, and supporters while emphasising unity, political stability, and a shared commitment to national progress.

World.title: Atiku, Obi, SDP, CUPP, ADC kick as court sacks Mark-led ADC exco
World.content:
By Nwafor Sunday, Henry Umoru, Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Luminous Jannamike, & John Alechelu

The Federal High Court in Abuja’s decision to sack the Senator David Mark-led executive committee of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and nullify all actions taken by it has drawn criticism from former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, presidential candidate Peter Obi; the Social Democratic Party, SDP, and the Coalition of United Political Parties, CUPP.

While Atiku accused the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, of using the judgment to frustrate his presidential ambition and weaken his support base in the North, Obi urged Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive.

The court, in a judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu, declared the Mark-led ADC caretaker committee illegal and invalidated all actions taken by it, including the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate for the 2027 general election.

The judgment followed a suit instituted by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the ADC (North-East), who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the party.

Gombe had argued that following the resignation of the party’s former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, he was entitled to assume the leadership of the party.

The court upheld his claims and granted the reliefs sought.

The ruling has raised questions about the status of Atiku’s candidacy, coming barely 24 hours after he held a campaign rally in Sokoto State.

Atiku alleges plot to weaken Northern support

Reacting to the judgment, Atiku accused the APC of using the court ruling to frustrate his presidential ambition and contain the ADC’s growing political influence ahead of the 2027 elections.

Atiku said the ruling came barely 24 hours after thousands of supporters welcomed him to Sokoto for the launch of the ADC campaign, alleging that the development was part of a strategy to weaken his Northern support base and halt the spread of his campaign beyond the region.

In a statement issued on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the former Vice-President insisted that the judgment would neither derail the party’s campaign nor diminish its appeal across the country.

He said the reception in Sokoto reflected Nigerians’ growing frustration with economic hardship and their desire for a change of government.

“The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning. The people of Kebbi will have their say, and so will Nigerians across the country as our campaign moves forward,” he said.

Rejecting attempts to portray his candidacy as a Northern project, Atiku said the economic crisis confronting Nigerians had made his political message relevant across regional boundaries.

“My roots are in Northern Nigeria, but my candidacy belongs to all Nigerians. There is a difference between being from the North and being a candidate only for the North. Hunger and hardship do not respect regional boundaries. Nigerians across the country are suffering under this government, and they deserve a leader with a credible plan to make life affordable again,” he said.

Atiku alleged that the judgment was intended to disrupt the momentum of his campaign and weaken the opposition’s growing political reach.

“The timing of this judgment is no coincidence. It is part of a strategy to weaken my support in the North and frustrate a campaign whose message is resonating across the country. But the ruling party’s greatest miscalculation is to assume that my support ends in the North. What we saw in Sokoto, what we will see in Kebbi and across the country, is the strength of a national movement,” he said.

On the legal implications, Atiku questioned why the leadership dispute was reopened despite an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the Federal High Court, Abuja, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025.

He said the court had dismissed the challenge to the David Mark-led leadership after upholding objections bordering on jurisdiction, standing and failure to exhaust internal party remedies, adding that the substantive issues were also resolved in favour of the defendants.

“Why, after that judgment, was another case filed to reopen the same dispute? This is a calculated attempt to circumvent a subsisting judgment. We will challenge this judicial manoeuvre at the Court of Appeal,” he said.

The former Vice-President urged ADC supporters to remain peaceful and law-abiding, insisting that the ruling would not interrupt the party’s mobilisation.

“Our journey to rescue Nigeria from the hardship imposed by the APC government is a long one. Our Affordable Life campaign will continue because Nigerians deserve relief from this crushing cost-of-living crisis,” he said.

With the campaign train already in Kebbi, Atiku urged supporters to take the party’s message from house to house and door to door, declaring, “There is no shaking.”

Obi warns against undermining democracy

Also reacting to the development, Obi urged Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive.

Obi, who expressed shock over the judgment, said the development had created uncertainty in the country’s political landscape, particularly with the 2027 general election approaching.

He disclosed this in a statement posted on his X platform on Thursday.

The former Anambra State governor said although he respected the court’s authority to determine disputes in accordance with the law, the timing of the judgment raised concerns about electoral certainty.

“I do not challenge the ruling of the court. The court of law is constituted to determine disputes according to the law. My concern is that three months before a general election, it is in the public interest to have certainty,” he said.

Obi argued that uncertainty over political parties and their candidates close to an election could undermine the electoral process and restrict the space for opposition campaigns.

He alleged that the ruling party was engineering instability within opposition parties, claiming that similar developments had affected him in the Labour Party.

He also alleged that opposition campaigns had been subjected to violence, describing the developments as part of what he called efforts to shrink the civic space and weaken opposition politics.

Emphasising the importance of voters in a democracy, Obi said the choice of political leaders should ultimately rest with the electorate.

“One mark of democracy is that at all times, it is voters and not courts that choose leaders. I trust in the judiciary. As a public officer, I have shown deep respect for the judiciary,” he said.

He appealed to the judiciary and other stakeholders to protect democratic institutions and ensure that candidates were allowed to participate freely in electoral contests.

Obi further warned against weakening opposition politics, citing the spread of military rule in parts of West Africa as a reason Nigeria should strengthen its democratic institutions.

According to him, the survival of democracy requires a political environment in which opposition parties are allowed to operate, organise and compete without persecution.

He said he had consistently maintained that, if elected president, he would give special attention to ensuring that opposition parties remained stable and viable.

Obi added that his administration would protect opposition candidates from being pushed out of electoral contests.

“This is a time to strengthen our democracy by allowing the opposition to thrive,” he said.

CUPP accuses APC of pursuing one-party state

Similarly, the Coalition of United Political Parties (CUPP) criticised the judgment, alleging that it could weaken opposition parties and undermine political competition in the country.

In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday through its Office of the Spokesperson, the coalition accused the ruling APC of benefiting from what it described as a systematic effort to weaken opposition parties.

CUPP alleged that the judgment was part of a broader attempt to undermine opposition political structures and create conditions for a one-party state.

The coalition also expressed concern over the role of the judiciary, arguing that the ruling raised questions about the courts’ responsibility to protect democratic rights and political participation.

“CUPP views this controversial judgment not as an isolated legal dispute, but as part of a well-choreographed, state-sponsored onslaught aimed at wiping out viable opposition parties and turning Nigeria into a one-party state,” the statement read.

It further alleged that sections of the judiciary had failed to adequately protect the interests of citizens and the electoral process.

CUPP also accused the APC-led government of relying on legal technicalities to challenge opposition candidates and party leadership structures, saying such developments could restrict political competition and undermine public confidence in the electoral system.

“The judiciary must remember that its allegiance belongs to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, not to the political actors of the day. When the courts become a tool for political liquidation, the very survival of our democracy is at stake,” the statement added.

The coalition declared solidarity with the ADC and other opposition groups, saying it would continue to defend democratic participation and political pluralism.

SDP condemns alleged move to disqualify Atiku

Meanwhile, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) condemned alleged attempts to disqualify Atiku from the 2027 presidential election, insisting that political parties should be allowed to freely present candidates.

The SDP National Chairman, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, stated this on Thursday in Abuja while addressing journalists after a meeting with the party’s nine governorship candidates from different states.

Gombe called on the judiciary, security agencies and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remain impartial and protect the country’s democratic process.

He also accused the APC of allegedly plotting to infiltrate opposition parties and weaken their ranks ahead of the elections.

The SDP chairman alleged that the ruling party, having lost the confidence of Nigerians over its governance record, was using the proposed Rainbow Coalition to woo opposition members and undermine their unity.

He, however, said the SDP was working with other opposition parties towards building a coalition of Nigerians committed to credible elections, including joint training of party agents and the establishment of common situation rooms to protect votes at polling units.

Gombe reaffirmed the party’s commitment to presenting what he described as credible alternatives to Nigerians, naming its presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and vice-presidential candidate, Prof. Usman Bugaje.

“I want to assure you that SDP, as a political party, has nothing to do with anything called Rainbow Coalition.

“We are with other political parties in the opposition, doing everything possible to rescue our dear country through a coalition of the Nigerian people.

“We are not into any Rainbow Coalition where we will have candidates here and profess support for the APC presidency. We are SDP and we are for SDP candidates,” he said.

He said the party had resolved to discipline any member who participated in the proposed arrangement without its authorisation.

The SDP chairman also expressed concern over the alleged failure of INEC to publish the names of some of the party’s candidates, saying the matter was already before the court.

He accused the commission of failing to recognise the candidates despite what he described as the party’s compliance with the Electoral Act, the Constitution and its internal nomination procedures.

Gombe further raised concerns about the voters’ register and the creation of polling units, warning against actions capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process.

Earlier, the Chairman of the SDP Governors’ Forum and Nasarawa governorship candidate, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, said the meeting was aimed at developing strategies to secure victory in the presidential, governorship and legislative elections.

Adamu said the candidates shared experiences from their respective states and discussed ways to address organisational gaps ahead of the polls.

The meeting brought together the party’s nine governorship candidates and members of its National Working Committee as part of efforts to strengthen its structures ahead of the 2027 general elections.

ADC vows to appeal judgment

The ADC has vowed to appeal the judgment. Its National Welfare Secretary, Nkemakolam Ukandu, who was joined as an interested party in the case, said the party would challenge the verdict at the appellate court.
