World.title: No child is useless, every child is ordained for greatness — Foluke Adeboye
World.content:
By Olayinka Latona

The wife of the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Foluke Adeboye, has called on parents, churches, governments and other stakeholders to take greater responsibility for raising children with godly character and values, saying Nigeria’s future depends on how its young people are nurtured.

Adeboye made the call in her welcome address, titled “The Mandate of Kingdom Education in National Transformation,” at the annual summit of Christ The Redeemer’s School Management (CRSM), a multidimensional ministry of the RCCG, held at Redemption City of God along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

The summit was themed “Revisiting Kingdom Education: The Role of Stakeholders.”

She said the responsibility for effective Christian education begins at home, urging parents to train their children properly and cooperate with teachers in shaping their character.

Adeboye cautioned parents against over-pampering their children during school holidays, urging them to allow the young ones to grow in accordance with godly values.

“Every child must fear God because the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom. We see many of these children that look down on their teachers. If parents discharge their duties effectively, it will make the teacher’s work easier. Meditate on God’s word day and night,” she said.

She also urged parents not to shy away from correcting their children, stressing that discipline and proper upbringing were essential to national development.

“If only everyone of us can come together, do the right things, raise our children rightly, the success of Nigeria is in our hands,” she added.

Adeboye further charged children to obey their parents and called on churches to teach sound biblical doctrines.

She urged leaders to discharge their responsibilities diligently and exercise sound judgment, warning that failure to provide responsible leadership could create room for corruption, criminality and other social vices.

On the role of government, she called for the provision of adequate structures and learning facilities in schools, particularly in rural communities where, she said, some pupils still sit on the floor because of a lack of chairs.

She noted that such schools were often upgraded through evangelism and missionary activities because of the need to address the challenges confronting rural education.

“So many things are wrong and these children from the village have great destiny to fulfil. God is counting on them. They brought David from the bush to be a king of Israel. No child is a useless child; God ordained every child to be great. I believe by the time I leave, I must have made substantial impact over the education in this nation,” she said.

In her keynote address on the same topic, former Minister of Education, Dr Oby Ezekwesili, said professionals who remained indifferent to the challenges facing society could not contribute meaningfully to its transformation.

Ezekwesili expressed concern over Nigeria’s education challenges, particularly the high number of out-of-school children, and urged Christians to demonstrate the values they profess, noting that they were called to be the light of the world.

She said nation-building required children equipped with character, competence and capacity, describing the three qualities as essential to preparing young people for responsible citizenship.

According to her, Christian schools must promote diligence, courage, compassion and stewardship as core values, describing the approach as character-based education.

The panelists also stressed that Kingdom Education should produce ethical citizens who actively contribute to society rather than remain passive spectators.

They said school activities, including curriculum delivery, should be anchored on a biblical worldview, adding that Kingdom schools must prepare students to understand their identity, defend their faith and withstand social pressure.

World.title: Tinubu saved Nigeria from turning to Venezuela — Emerhor
World.content:
A founding leader of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Delta State, Olorogun O’tega Emerhor, has declared that Nigeria would have suffered an economic collapse similar to Venezuela’s if President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had not demonstrated the courage and foresight to introduce far-reaching economic reforms upon assuming office in 2023.

Olorogun Emerhor, who stated this on Thursday during the Delta State APC campaign flag-off in Oleh, Isoko South Local Government Area, said Tinubu inherited an economy weakened by years of poor management and unsustainable policies, insisting that the President’s difficult but necessary decisions had rescued the country from the brink of economic disaster.

The APC chieftain also called for the re-election of President Tinubu and Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, in 2027, arguing that both leaders had demonstrated the capacity to reposition the country and state for sustainable economic growth and infrastructural transformation.

According to Emerhor, Nigeria was heading towards an economic crisis comparable to that of Venezuela, an oil-rich South American country that experienced severe economic difficulties despite possessing some of the world’s largest crude oil reserves.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has rescued Nigeria. If our President had not taken those bold decisions, Nigeria would have gone the way of Venezuela. Do you want Nigeria to become another Venezuela?

“Venezuela has more oil than Nigeria, but bad leadership and years of economic mismanagement destroyed its economy. For many years, that was the kind of governance we experienced in Nigeria,” he stated.

Emerhor criticised some opposition political figures seeking to challenge Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, alleging that several of them were part of the political establishment responsible for the country’s longstanding economic difficulties.

He maintained that it took Tinubu’s political courage and determination to confront the structural challenges that previous administrations had failed to address.

“All those who are today running to become President were part of the system that contributed to the destruction of Nigeria. It was Bola Ahmed Tinubu who had the courage to take those difficult decisions.

“Today, we are beginning to have a stable economy. The President has laid a strong foundation for economic prosperity. We have a prudent President, and our foreign reserves are growing. Tinubu is doing well,” Emerhor declared.

The APC leader argued that removing Tinubu after his first term would amount to abandoning the economic recovery process midway, stressing that the President deserved another four years to consolidate his reforms and deliver their anticipated benefits to Nigerians.

Using the analogy of constructing a building, Emerhor said the President had successfully laid the foundation for Nigeria’s economic recovery and should be allowed to complete the structure.

“Do you want to invite those who destroyed the house to come back and rebuild it? We have to give President Tinubu another four years to build the skyscraper on top of the foundation he has laid.

“We need to give him those four years, and you will see what Nigeria will become. We must give him our full support,” he said.

Turning to Delta State, Emerhor showered praises on Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, describing his performance under the MORE Agenda as remarkable and deserving of another term in office.

He said the governor had recorded significant achievements in infrastructure and other critical sectors within barely three and a half years, expressing confidence that another four years would position Delta State among Nigeria’s most developed states.

Emerhor, who referred to Oborevwori by his popular nickname, Ukodo, said the governor’s achievements were so numerous that recounting them would be like singing the popular Christian hymn, Count Your Blessings.

“Now, let me talk about our Ukodo. Many people have already counted so many things that he has done. I would have loved us to sing, ‘Count your blessings, name them one by one.’

“Look at what he has done in just three years. Give him another four years, and we will beat Lagos. Don’t you want that?” he asked, drawing cheers from party supporters.

The APC founding leader further declared that the massive gathering of political leaders and supporters at the Oleh campaign flag-off demonstrated the growing strength and dominance of the ruling party in Delta State.

He described the occasion as a gathering of the state’s political heavyweights, insisting that the APC had emerged as the dominant political force ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“I have come here today as the happiest man. I can see the cream of the political class, all the political juggernauts, gathered here today.

“There is no other party in Delta State than APC! Anybody pretending that there is another party in this state is deceiving himself. Can you see what is happening here today?” he declared.

Emerhor maintained that the unity of political leaders and the massive turnout of supporters at the campaign flag-off were indications of the party’s strength and electoral prospects.

He urged party members not to become complacent but to translate the enthusiasm witnessed at the rally into effective grassroots mobilisation and votes during the elections.

Addressing the crowd, which he estimated at more than 20,000 people, Emerhor challenged every supporter to mobilise at least ten additional voters for President Tinubu and other APC candidates.

“The people in this stadium are more than 20,000. Every one of you should go back and make sure you get a minimum of ten people to vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

“If everybody here brings ten additional voters, imagine the number of votes we will deliver. We have already won the election,” he declared.

Emerhor expressed confidence that the combination of Tinubu’s economic reforms, Oborevwori’s infrastructural achievements and the unity of APC stakeholders would strengthen the party’s chances of securing overwhelming electoral victories in Delta State.

He urged party faithful to sustain their commitment to grassroots mobilisation, stressing that the 2027 elections would provide an opportunity for Nigerians and Deltans to consolidate what he described as the gains of purposeful leadership at the federal and state levels.

World.title: ADC Judgment: CUPP accuses APC of seeking one-party state
World.content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA — The Coalition of United Political Parties (CUPP) has criticised the court ruling nullifying the African Democratic Congress (ADC) executive committee and its candidates, alleging that the development could weaken opposition parties and undermine political competition in Nigeria.

In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday through its Office of the Spokesperson, the coalition accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of benefiting from what it described as a systematic effort to weaken opposition parties.

CUPP alleged that the judgment was part of a broader attempt to undermine opposition political structures and create conditions for a one-party state.

The coalition also expressed concern over the role of the judiciary, arguing that the ruling raised questions about the courts’ responsibility to protect democratic rights and political participation.

The statement read in part: “CUPP views this controversial judgment not as an isolated legal dispute, but as part of a well-choreographed, state-sponsored onslaught aimed at wiping out viable opposition parties and turning Nigeria into a one-party state.”

It further alleged that sections of the judiciary had failed to adequately protect the interests of citizens and the electoral process.

CUPP also accused the APC-led government of relying on legal technicalities to challenge opposition candidates and party leadership structures, saying such developments could restrict political competition and undermine public confidence in the electoral system.

The coalition warned that the judiciary must remain guided by the Constitution and the interests of Nigerians rather than political considerations.

“The judiciary must remember that its allegiance belongs to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, not to the political actors of the day. When the courts become a tool for political liquidation, the very survival of our democracy is at stake,” the statement said.

CUPP declared solidarity with the ADC and other opposition groups, saying it would continue to defend democratic participation and political pluralism.

The coalition added: “CUPP stands in solidarity with the ADC and all progressive forces in Nigeria. We will not sit idly by while the hard-earned democratic gains of our nation are plundered by an authoritarian regime.”

World.title: City Boy Movement Plans 100,000-man Solidarity Walk For Tinubu, Others In Borno
World.content:
The City Boy Movement, Borno State chapter, has announced a 100,000-man solidarity walk scheduled to take place in Maiduguri on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, to express the organisation’s full support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima.

Ahead of the 2027 general election, the organisation said the 100,000-man Solidarity Walk is in solidarity with the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in the state, Alhaji Mustapha Gubio, and other candidates of the party.

Director of the state chapter of the City Boy Movement, Comrade Mahmud Muhammad, explained that the solidarity walk is aimed at bringing together youths, women, political stakeholders, community mobilisers and supporters from across the 27 local government areas of Borno State to demonstrate their support for the Tinubu-Shettima administration, the Renewed Hope Agenda and the APC.

In a statement issued on Thursday, Mahmud, who is also the Personal Assistant to the President on Domestic Affairs (North-east) (Office of the Vice-President), said the event will also provide an opportunity for participants to demonstrate their commitment to peaceful political participation, democratic engagement and collective civic expression.

He noted that the march will commence at 8:00am from the Shehu’s Palace, Maiduguri and proceed to the Borno State Government House, where the organisers intend to present a solidarity message.

The statement read in part: “The City Boy Movement invites youths, women, APC stakeholders, community leaders and supporters from across Borno State to participate in the event and be part of this public expression of solidarity.

“The movement calls on all participants to maintain peace, demonstrate discipline and conduct themselves responsibly throughout the exercise. Participants are expected to respect public order, cooperate with relevant security personnel and avoid any actions capable of disrupting the peace.”

Mahmud further said that The City Boy Movement, Borno State Chapter, was looking forward to “a peaceful and orderly event that reflects the spirit of responsible civic participation”.

World.title: 2027 Campaigns: Presidency Seeks Caution In Use Of AI By Parties
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Presidency on Thursday called on politicians to seek caution in the deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as the 2027 electioneering gathers momentum.

Presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, canvassed for responsible and cautious deployment of AI in the course of political activities and campaigns ahead of the 2027 polls.

He warned that while the scientific breakthrough has had positive effects, it is now imperative to put guardrails in place to protect the sanctity of democratic institutions and public trust.

Onanuga made the call in Beijing, China, while delivering a paper, ‘AI and the Future of Global Communication,’ at the 7th World Media Summit organised by Xinhua News Agency and the People’s Government of Beijing Municipality.

According to him, social media, including X, Facebook and TikTok, are inundated with AI-generated videos and images to promote political interests and entertain.

His words: “We are in the thick of the political season and campaigns ahead of the 2027 general election, where new political leaders at the national and sub-national levels will be elected. AI, for good and bad, has become a powerful tool for electoral contests for politicians and their supporters.

“Some political actors use AI to spread falsehoods, some use it satirically for entertainment, and some highlight candidates’ achievements.”

The presidential aide said the growing influence of AI in political communication makes it imperative for stakeholders- political actors, media organisations, and the general public to exercise greater responsibility in content creation and sharing.

Onanuga acknowledged that AI’s growing contributions, including innovations in medicine and major feats in mathematics, make it an indispensable tool for improving the lot of humanity.

“Today, AI governs our existence, and we encounter it all the time. In the car, it warns you about your immediate surroundings. It maps your fastest route to your destination. We can go on, citing AI’s Leviathan impact on our lives.

“I believe we can no longer ignore AI’s penetrating impact, most of it beneficial, unless we want to return to the Stone Age,” he added.

Onanuga expressed optimism that stakeholders, including individuals, scientists and governments such as the United Nations, are equally concerned about AI’s direction and are pushing for necessary controls.

“The world must act before it becomes too late. Build guardrails quickly to save humanity,” he further stated.

World.title: Omotola Predicts Tight 2027 Race, Gives Tinubu Slim Lead Over Obi, Atiku
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

The Publisher of Politico.ng, under the Political Intelligence Group, Lai Omotola, Thursday, projected President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as maintaining a slim lead over former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar ahead of the 2027 general election.

Omotola, who disclosed this while presenting the third edition of his November 2026 electoral map, in Lagos, explained that the presidential contest was becoming increasingly competitive, with changing voter preferences and the growing influence of young Nigerians expected to shape the outcome.

He projected that Obi would come second, while Atiku would occupy the third position, although the margin separating the three leading contenders remained narrow.

According to him, the political landscape has changed significantly, making it difficult for political parties to rely on previous electoral strategies and voting patterns.

He warned that politicians who approached the 2027 election with a business-as-usual mentality risked defeat.

“There are about 68 million new voters that will be voting for the first time in the 2027 elections, and the majority of these voters are youths. Unlike before, young people between the ages of 18 and 49 will dominate the election,” he stated.

Omotola also predicted that the 2027 general election could record the highest voter turnout in Nigeria’s electoral history, projecting participation of about 40 per cent, compared with the 29 per cent recorded in the last election.

In his state-by-state projection, he predicted that the All Progressives Congress (APC) would win 13 states, the New Democratic Congress (NDC) 13 states and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) 11 states.

He projected that the APC would dominate the South-west and North-central regions, while the NDC would win all states in the South-east and South-south, as well as Kano State and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The ADC, according to him, would win states in the North-east and North-west, except Kano and Zamfara States.

He, however, stressed that the projections were based on the assumption that the 2027 elections would be free and fair.

Reviewing political developments in October, Omotola identified the commencement of campaigns by the three leading parties, the controversy surrounding the preliminary voters’ register released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), and renewed debate over fuel subsidy as developments that could influence the electoral landscape.

He also cited the APC’s inaugural campaign in Kaduna, led by Tinubu, and Atiku’s proposal for the restoration of fuel subsidy as significant political and economic developments during the period.

Omotola expressed concern over the controversy surrounding the preliminary voters’ register, which he said had been affected by the inclusion of AI-generated names.

He further observed that opposition parties were encountering stiff resistance in their campaign activities, while internal disagreements within the APC could affect its electoral fortunes.

According to him, these developments could influence the three parties differently as political activities intensify ahead of the 2027 polls.

Omotola also identified political developments within opposition parties and the legal challenges confronting them as factors capable of changing the electoral projections before the election.

On the influence of religion in the 2027 election, the publisher said it remained a significant factor, particularly in northern Nigeria, where religious considerations continued to influence voter behaviour.

He interpreted Tinubu’s decision to retain his Muslim-Muslim ticket and his recent visit to Saudi Arabia as part of efforts to reinforce his religious credentials and appeal to northern voters.

He added that the north would play a decisive role in determining the outcome of the presidential election, noting that the contest would also test whether the region could maintain a united political position or become increasingly divided.

Omotola, however, cautioned that the electoral projections could change as political alignments, legal developments and campaign activities unfold.

He urged political parties, INEC and other stakeholders to prioritise peaceful, free and credible elections, describing the forthcoming poll as a defining moment for Nigeria’s democracy.

“This will be a turning point for Nigeria’s democracy, and the country will be a better place for it,” he said.

World.title: NYSC Members’ Kidnap: Two Defendants Admit DSS Confessional Statements, Beg Court for Forgiveness
World.content:
Two men standing trial over the Independence Day abduction of 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in Imo State on Thursday admitted making the confessional statements tendered before the court by the Department of State Services (DSS).

The defendants, Usman Aliyu and Babangida Aliyu, who are the first and second defendants respectively, however, pleaded with the court to forgive them and set them free.

At the resumed hearing on Thursday, the two defendants opened their defence by testifying for themselves before the court.

During cross-examination, they admitted voluntarily making the audio-visual confessional statements and thumb-printing the written statements in the presence of their counsel.

The statements and audio-visual recordings were subsequently tendered by the DSS and admitted in evidence by the court.

Earlier, while giving their evidence-in-chief, the defendants had appealed for forgiveness and urged the court to discharge and release them in the case involving charges of conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms.

In a related development, the trial of two other defendants accused of conspiracy, kidnapping and unlawful possession of firearms continued on Thursday.

A prosecution witness identified the two defendants as the persons who allegedly abducted him for ransom in the state on October 4, 2026.

At the conclusion of proceedings, the trial judge, Justice Emeka Orafu, adjourned both cases until November 6 for continuation of hearing.

World.title: 2027: Lawyers Seek Timely, Transparent Display of Voters’ Register
World.content:
* Urge amendment of law requiring AG’s consent to enforce monetary judgment against government

Alex Enumah

As activities continue to gear up towards the conduct of the 2027 general election, legal practitioners in the country have called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to ensure the timely and transparent display of the voters’ register, so as to ensure the credibility of the polls.

The lawyers, who noted that electoral credibility begins before the polling day, stressed that accurate records, lawful procedures and meaningful public scrutiny are essential to public confidence.

This is just as they have called on the National Assembly to abolish the law requiring the consent of the Attorney-General to enforce monetary judgment against government.

The lawyers made the call on Thursday in Abuja, at an event marking the Law Corridor Founders’ Day, as well as the introduction of a Professor of Public and International Law, Prof. Olarenwaju A. Aladeitan, as a Partner of the Law Corridor.

Speaking at the occasion, the Managing Partner of Law Corridor, Henry Kelechi Eniotu, explained that under the Electoral Act 2026, while Section 19 addresses the display or publication of the voters’ register, Section 77 addresses political-party membership registers and their submission to INEC before primaries, congresses and conventions.

“INEC must clearly communicate the applicable timelines, provide accessible opportunities for voters to inspect their records and ensure effective procedures for claims, objections and corrections. It should also explain how compliance with party membership register requirements will be verified and enforced, subject to lawful safeguards for personal information.

“Publicly announced voter statistics must be clear and verifiable. The Commission should distinguish between applications received, completed registrations and the final number of eligible registered voters. Where figures change or credible discrepancies arise, it should provide timely explanations,” Eniotu said.

The lawyer further stated that political parties must equally maintain accurate records and comply with their statutory obligations, adding that the same standards must apply consistently to every party and candidate.

He stressed that public confidence grows when electoral procedures and information can withstand scrutiny.

Speaking on enforcement of monetary judgment against the government, the lawyers who argued that a judgment must provide an effective remedy, submitted that citizens who successfully establish their claims against public institutions should be able to obtain the benefits of those judgments without avoidable obstruction.

They observed that while Section 84 of the Sheriffs and Civil Process Act requires the consent of the appropriate Attorney-General before a garnishee order nisi may be made where the money sought to be attached is held by a public officer in an official capacity, the said requirement is subject to judicial interpretation.

According to them, “The continued existence of the consent requirement creates opportunities for delay in cases to which it applies.”

They alleged that successful litigants may spend years pursuing payment while their businesses suffer and inflation erodes the value of their judgments.

“Government has access to appeals and applications for a stay of execution. An executive officer should not possess an additional, indefinite power to obstruct enforcement against the government that officer represents.

“We therefore call on the National Assembly to abolish the Attorney-General’s consent requirement and establish clear enforcement procedures supported by definite timelines, responsible budgeting and judicial oversight.

“Government must respect the judicial authority it expects citizens to obey”, they said. Eniotu assured that the Law Corridor will continue to contribute its quota towards development of the country, through legal analysis, public-interest advocacy and constructive engagement with institutions responsible for reform.

“As we mark our Founders’ Week and welcome Professor Aladeitan into the partnership, we renew our commitment to professional excellence and meaningful service to society.

“We thank our clients for their trust, our colleagues for their dedication and the media for their contribution to public accountability,” Eniotu said.

World.title: Tinubu To Flamingos: Go For The U-17 Women’s World Cup
World.content:
* Congratulates team for historic qualification for cup final in Morocco

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has charged Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, to go for the gold as they meet Japan in the final of the 2026 Women’s World Cup in Morocco.

The president, in a release issued on Thursday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, told the young female footballers: “Nigeria is proud of you. Go for the trophy, Flamingos.”

As the Flamingos prepare to face Japan in the final, Tinubu urged the players to remain focused, confident and determined, assuring them of the prayers, goodwill and unflinching support of the Nigerian nation.

“I encourage you to approach the final with the same fighting spirit and belief that have brought you this far. I have confidence in your ability to make history by winning the coveted world title.

“I call on all Nigerians to rally behind the young ambassadors of the nation, whose achievements continue to showcase Nigeria’s sporting excellence and inspire a new generation of girls to pursue their dreams uninhibited.”

The president congratulated the Flamingos on their impressive victory over Brazil in Wednesday’s semi-final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

He described the team’s qualification for the final as a remarkable achievement that has brought immense pride and joy to millions of Nigerians at home and abroad.

Tinubu also applauded the coaching crew and all those whose hard work and support contributed to the team’s successful campaign.

World.title: Champion Brands Showcase Expanded Beverage Portfolio at ART X Lagos 2026
World.content:
Champion Breweries Plc is showcasing its expanded portfolio at ART X Lagos 2026, bringing together a diverse range of beverage brands as part of its continued commitment to celebrating African creativity, culture and shared experiences.

The 11th edition of ART X Lagos runs from November 5 to 8, 2026 at the Federal Palace, Lagos, under the theme ‘A New Chapter, A New Decade,’ exploring how Africa’s cultural traditions continue to inspire new artistic expressions.

The theme also resonates with Champion, which is building on its established brewing heritage as it expands into new beverage categories and markets.

This marks the second consecutive year that Champion has supported ART X Lagos, reflecting a longstanding commitment to platforms that champion African cultural expression.

This year, Champion Brands is bringing its diverse beverage portfolio into one of the continent’s foremost celebrations of contemporary art and culture.

“Culture is one of the most powerful ways we express who we are, where we come from and what we aspire to become,” said Eric Idiahi, Group CEO, Evercorp Industries, and Director, Champion Breweries.

“It lives in our art and music, but also in the everyday experiences we share. We believe businesses have a role to play in supporting the creative people and platforms that keep those expressions alive, while helping create opportunities for new audiences to discover and participate in them.

”That commitment will come to life at the Champion Brands Lounge, a welcoming space where visitors can unwind between exhibitions and discover the breadth of the group’s beverage portfolio. The offering brings together brands from across Champion Brands’ businesses, including Champion Lager and Champ Malt from Champion Breweries, Bullet Black ready-to-drink alcoholic beverage, Bullet Blue energy drink, Harmattan Vodka Soda, Éclat No Sugar Co. and Bitter botanical sparkling drinks.

The expanded portfolio reflects Champion Brands’ strategy to build a diversified, global beverage business. A significant milestone in this journey was the acquisition of the Bullet brand portfolio, which strengthened the group’s presence in ready-to-drink alcoholic beverages and energy drinks and expanded its commercial footprint across 14 African markets.

Through its businesses, Champion Brands is building a broader consumer offering, stronger distribution capabilities and a platform for sustainable growth. Champion’s partnership also extends into music through ART X Live!, the fair’s flagship music and visual art experience, taking place on Saturday, 7 November.

Bullet will be the featured partner brand for the evening, which will showcase a new generation of African musical voices, including Kunmie, Lulu and Taves. Curated by Lanre Masha, the programme celebrates artists drawing on the continent’s musical traditions while developing new sounds and forms of expression.

Visitors can experience the Champion Brands Lounge during the fair’s programme on 6, 7 and 8 November, with ART X Live! beginning at 10.30 pm on Saturday.

World.title: Chartered Institute of Directors to Hold 2026 Walk for Life Saturday
World.content:
Oghenevwede Ohwovoriole in Abuja

The Chartered Institute of Directors (CIoD) Nigeria, Abuja Zone, will hold its 2026 Walk for Life on Saturday at Millennium Park, Abuja, as part of efforts to promote executive wellness, strengthen professional connections and inspire healthier leadership.

The Media Officer of CIoD, Rex Abitogin disclosed this in a press statement that was made available to the media on Thursday.

He said the event, themed “Advancing Executive Wellness, Building Connections, and Inspiring Healthier Leadership,” will be led by the National President and Chairman of the Governing Council of CIoD Nigeria, Otunba Adetunji Oyebanji, F.CIoD, and hosted by the Abuja Zonal Chairperson, Mrs Rose N. Eshiett, M.CIoD.

He noted that, “The annual walk reflects the Institute’s recognition that effective and sustainable leadership extends beyond professional competence and boardroom responsibilities to include personal health and wellbeing. Directors and senior executives operate in demanding environments that require sound judgement, sustained attention and the capacity to navigate complex organisational challenges. These responsibilities make personal wellness an important consideration in the pursuit of leadership effectiveness.

“Through the Walk for Life, CIoD Abuja Zone seeks to encourage directors, senior executives, professionals and members of the wider community to embrace healthier lifestyles and incorporate physical activity into their daily routines. Walking provides a simple and accessible way to promote fitness while creating opportunities for participants to interact beyond formal professional settings.’

According to him, “The initiative also highlights the connection between executive wellness and organisational culture. As leaders influence workplace values through their decisions and personal example, their commitment to healthy living can encourage organisations to give greater attention to employee wellbeing and the creation of healthier, more sustainable working environments.”

In addition he said, “Beyond its wellness objectives, the event will provide an opportunity for fellowship, networking and relationship-building among members of the Institute and other participants. By bringing people together in an informal and engaging setting, the walk aims to strengthen professional connections and reinforce the importance of collaboration in leadership and business.

He also stated that, “The Abuja Zone of CIoD Nigeria invites directors, senior executives, professionals, members of the business community and the general public to participate in the event at Millennium Park on Saturday, November 7, 2026.

“The Institute also calls on media organisations to support the initiative by amplifying its message and encouraging wider public participation. It hopes that the event will inspire participants to carry its message beyond the park by making personal wellness a more deliberate part of their everyday lives and leadership practices.” he said

In his explanations, he said, “The 2026 Walk for Life underscores CIoD Nigeria’s commitment to promoting leadership that combines professional excellence with personal wellbeing, recognising that healthy leaders are an important part of building resilient organisations and a more sustainable business environment.”

World.title: South African restaurant climbs 20 places in world’s best rankings
World.content:
A South African restaurant has secured a place among the world’s 35 best, giving the country’s fine-dining scene another major international achievement.

Cape Town’s La Colombe has been ranked 35th in The 50 Best Restaurants 2026, as well as earning the title of Best Restaurant in Africa.

The announcement was made at the awards ceremony in Lima, Peru, on Wednesday evening, 4 November.



Executive Chef James Gaag accepted the accolade on behalf of the restaurant’s team.

“We are incredibly honoured to be recognised among the world’s best restaurants. It is a very special moment for the entire team, whose dedication and passion make La Colombe what it is,” said Gaag.

He added that representing Cape Town and South Africa on an international stage was something the team never took for granted.

La Colombe climbs 20 places

The latest ranking marks a significant improvement for the Constantia restaurant, which placed 55th in 2025.

It also represents a return to the top 50 after dropping out of the main ranking last year.

La Colombe previously ranked 49th in 2024, when it was also named Best Restaurant in Africa.



South African restaurants on the world stage

La Colombe was not the only Cape Town restaurant to feature in the 2026 rankings.

FYN secured 65th place, while Salsify at the Roundhouse came in at 71st in the extended list of the world’s top 100 restaurants.

The global ranking brings together leading dining destinations from around the world and recognises the talent and creativity shaping the international restaurant industry.

This year’s top spot went to Spain’s Asador Etxebarri, followed by Gaggan in Bangkok and Alchemist in Copenhagen.

World.title: EFF treasurer stabbed to death near voting station
World.content:
Police have arrested a 35-year-old suspect after an EFF branch treasurer was stabbed to death near a voting station in Polokwane, Limpopo. Image: Pexels

Police have arrested a 35-year-old man following the murder of an Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) branch treasurer near a voting station in Polokwane, Limpopo.

The 31-year-old victim died after a man allegedly stabbed him in the neck at a park opposite Flora Park Comprehensive School at about 05:00 on Thursday, 5 November.

EFF Limpopo provincial chairperson Lawrence Mapoulo confirmed that the deceased was the party’s Flora Park branch treasurer.



Argument turns deadly

Limpopo police spokesperson Brigadier Hlulani Mashaba said an argument broke out between two men who were among a group gathered at the park.

Police believe both men belonged to the same political party.

The argument initially subsided, but the suspect allegedly returned and stabbed the victim in the neck before fleeing.



Emergency services declared the man dead at the scene.

Officers recovered a knife believed to have been used in the attack and later tracked down the suspect.

Suspect to appear in court

The suspect is expected to appear in the Polokwane Magistrate’s Court on Friday, 6 November, on a murder charge.



Mashaba said investigators had yet to establish a motive.

Police continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the murder.

World.title: South African business confidence hits lowest level since 2020
World.content:
South African business confidence has fallen to its lowest level since August 2020, according to a private-sector survey released on Thursday.

The S&P Global South Africa Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) remained at 49.0 in October, unchanged from September.

A reading below 50 indicates deteriorating private-sector business conditions, rather than a contraction across the entire South African economy.



Why is South African business confidence falling?

According to Reuters’ report on the survey, David Owen, principal economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence, identified the sharp decline in business confidence as a particularly concerning finding.

Businesses’ expectations for activity over the next 12 months fell to their lowest level in more than six years, with confidence weakening across every sector surveyed.

That does not mean companies expect business activity to decline throughout 2027. Firms still anticipate growth on average, but their expectations are considerably weaker than before.



Fuel prices and port delays push up costs

Higher fuel prices placed further pressure on businesses, pushing purchase-price inflation to its highest rate since June.

Companies also passed some of these costs on to customers, with the rate of increase in selling prices reaching a four-month high.

Supply-chain disruptions added to the pressure. Businesses reported continued delivery delays, including hold-ups at the Port of Durban.



Output declined for a second consecutive month, recording its sharpest fall since December 2025.

The October survey predates the government’s temporary fuel-levy reductions introduced on 4 November. Whether that relief will improve business sentiment remains uncertain.

Orders fall at home and abroad

New orders declined again in October, although the fall was less pronounced than in September. Export demand also weakened for the first time since May.



For workers and consumers, the findings raise concerns about employment opportunities and household costs.

Businesses facing weaker demand may become more cautious about hiring, while rising operating costs can place additional pressure on prices. However, the survey does not establish how many jobs could be affected or predict future retail price increases.

World.title: ELECTIONS 2026 | DA tops 800 000 votes in Gauteng
World.content:
The DA remains ahead in Gauteng with 36.4% of votes counted, followed by the ANC on 20% and ActionSA on 16.35%. Image: IEC Election Dashboard

The Democratic Alliance (DA) remains Gauteng’s leading party in the 2026 municipal elections, despite its share of the counted vote dropping by more than four percentage points since Thursday morning.

According to the Electoral Commission’s (IEC) results dashboard, the DA had secured 809 787 votes (36.4%) by 18:24 on Thursday, 5 November.

The African National Congress (ANC) followed with 444 842 votes (20%), while ActionSA occupied third place with 363 677 votes (16.35%).



The DA held a lead of 364 945 votes over the ANC, with 37% of Gauteng’s votes counted.

How Gauteng’s election results have changed

The DA’s lead in Gauteng has narrowed since Thursday morning, when it held 40.55% of votes counted, compared with the ANC’s 18.87%.

By 18:24, the DA had dropped to 36.4%, while the ANC climbed to 20%, cutting the gap between the parties from 21.68 to 16.4 percentage points.

Only 6% of Gauteng’s votes had been counted during the morning update, compared with 37% by Thursday evening.

ActionSA maintains third place

ActionSA has also increased its share of the counted vote, rising from 15.14% in the morning to 16.35%.

The party now trails the ANC by 81 165 votes in Gauteng.



Further down the standings, the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) had secured 6.37%, narrowly ahead of the Freedom Front Plus (FF Plus) on 6.18%.

The uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MK Party) followed with 4.5%, while the Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) stood at 1.13%.

The Patriotic Alliance (PA) had received 1.07% of votes counted.

What happens next in Gauteng?

With 63% of Gauteng’s votes still outstanding, results from Johannesburg, Tshwane, Ekurhuleni and other municipalities could change the current standings.

IEC Chief Electoral Officer Sy Mamabolo said on Thursday that officials capture results twice and conduct independent audits before confirming them.

The commission urged political parties and the public to refrain from spreading unverified information while counting continues.

The latest election results are available on the IEC’s official dashboard.

World.title: Report: Jessica Motaung steps down from key Kaizer Chiefs role
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs Marketing Director Jessica Motaung has reportedly stepped down from her position at the club.

After decades of service to the Soweto giants, it was reported on Thursday that Motaung had vacated her role as Marketing and Commercial Director but would remain a member of the club’s board.

“Jessica Motaung has confirmed to SABC Sport that she has stepped down from her role as Kaizer Chiefs Marketing Director but will stay on as a board member,” SABC Sport journalist Mazola Molefe reported.



Motaung has been part of Kaizer Chiefs since 1998 and was appointed Marketing Manager in 2003. Four years later, she became the club’s Marketing and Commercial Director, a position she has held ever since.

Her influence in football has also extended beyond Kaizer Chiefs. In 2022, she joined the CAF Organising Committee for Women’s Football.

Jessica Motaung has been with Chiefs for 28 years

A year later, Motaung was elected Deputy Chairperson of the African Clubs Association.

Despite SABC Sport reporting her departure from the position, Kaizer Chiefs are yet to release an official statement confirming the development.

With Jessica stepping down as Chiefs Marketing Director, it remains to be seen if Bobby Motaung or Kaizer Jr will take over her role. Both her brothers are part of the Chiefs board and occupy specific roles at the club.

Amakhosi are in action this weekend against Siwelele in the quarter-finals of the Carling Knockout Cup.



Do you think Jessica’s role should be filled by one of the Motaungs or externally?

World.title: Transfer report: Second German club targets Relebohile Mofokeng
World.content:
Relebohile Mofokeng celebrates scoring for Royale Union Saint-Gilliose in the Belgian Pro League. Image: RUSG

Following Beyer Leverkusen’s reported interest in Mofokeng in recent weeks, the German publication Fussbal News has revealed that fellow Bundesliga club SC Freiburg have joined the fray.

The outlet further revealed that Dutch club AZ Alkmaar are in the mix.

SC FREIBURG INTEREST IN RELEBOHILE MOFOKENG

“German Bundesliga sides Bayer Leverkusen and SC Freiburg are reportedly monitoring the 22-year-old South African international, who currently plays for Royale Union Saint-Gilloise,” the report said.



The Sharpeville-born star Mofokeng has enjoyed a dream start in Europe since leaving the Betway Premiership as the Player of the Season.

The 22-year-old winger completed a €3.5 million move to Belgian Pro League champions Royale Union Saint-Gilloise in July 2026 after an outstanding final season with league champions Orlando Pirates.

He first announced himself in Belgium with a decisive penalty on his debut against Club Brugge to help Union SG win the Belgian Super Cup. He has since continued to impress under coach David Hubert, showing his versatility in attacking positions.



PRESIDENT YAMA 2K MAKING HIS MARK IN EUROPE

Mofokeng has delivered five goals and four assists in his first 15 appearances for the Belgian outfit.

His impressive start has also extended to the continent, where he scored on his UEFA Europa League debut against Viktoria Plzeň.

To cap it all, Mofokeng earned a nomination for the Jupiler Pro League Player of the Month award for October.



RELEBOHILE MOFOKENG SHINES FOR BAFANA BAFANA

Mofokeng has also carried his impressive club form into international football, playing a leading role in South Africa’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign.

One of his standout performances came in an important away qualifier against Eritrea, where he scored twice to help Bafana Bafana secure a crucial victory.

The brace further underlined his growing importance to the national team, with the 22-year-old becoming an influential figure in South Africa’s attack.



His performances for both club and country have strengthened his reputation as one of the country’s most exciting attacking talents.

These municipalities tracked exclude 44 district councils.

Moepya said the counting and tallying of results are advancing steadily.

World.title: Number of the Day | 5% JSE Surge: Why US Midterms Sent SA Markets Soaring | 5 November 2026
World.content:
The Global Economy Has No Borders. South Africa's Stock Market Proves It.

When American politics changes, the consequences can travel through currencies, commodity markets and investment portfolios long before they reach South African households. The challenge is understanding whether those movements represent lasting economic opportunity or temporary optimism.

A 5% surge on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange is the kind of market movement that attracts attention well beyond trading floors. It creates an impression of renewed

confidence, improved expectations and possibly better economic conditions. Yet the forces driving such a rally are not always rooted in South Africa's domestic economy. Sometimes, the catalyst is a political development thousands of kilometres away.

The market reaction discussed on eNCA's Number of the Day on 5 November illustrates this connection. As investors responded to the US midterm elections, attention shifted towards potential changes in American economic and foreign policy. Oil prices, the dollar and precious metals became part of a much larger story about the relationship between political power and economic expectations.

Why political expectations move financial markets

Financial markets are forward-looking. Investors do not simply evaluate what a company earns today; they consider what it might earn tomorrow, what could threaten those earnings and which developments might improve its prospects. Political elections become important because they can change expectations about taxation, international trade, government spending, regulation and geopolitical stability.

This helps explain why markets sometimes rally before any substantial economic policy changes. A shift in the balance of political power can encourage investors to anticipate a different approach to governance. Those expectations may influence investment decisions even while existing laws, tariffs and international agreements remain unchanged.

The distinction is important because anticipation is not evidence of a guaranteed outcome. A political party's electoral setback does not automatically reverse government policy, just as investor optimism does not guarantee stronger economic growth. Markets can respond favourably to uncertainty that appears to be easing, only to retreat when political negotiations prove more complicated than expected.

Why the dollar matters to South African businesses

South Africa's position in the global economy makes its financial markets particularly sensitive to international currency and commodity movements. Gold and platinum are traded internationally in US dollars, meaning changes in exchange rates can influence prices, demand and the earnings expectations of companies producing these metals.

A weaker dollar can make dollar-denominated commodities more affordable to buyers using other currencies, potentially supporting demand and prices. For South African mining companies, favourable commodity prices can improve anticipated revenue, although exchange rates, production costs and operational conditions ultimately determine how much of that benefit reaches their financial results.

This relationship explains why mining shares can rise sharply even when domestic economic challenges remain unresolved. The companies listed on the JSE operate within global markets, and many derive substantial value from international customers, currencies and commodity prices.

However, the benefits of stronger mining shares do not immediately translate into relief for households. An increase in a company's market valuation is different from an increase in employment, wages or investment in local communities. The wider economic benefit depends on whether improved market conditions lead businesses to expand production, invest in infrastructure and create sustainable opportunities.

The trade relationship South Africa cannot ignore

South Africa's commercial relationship with the United States introduces another dimension to this global dependence. American tariffs and preferential market-access arrangements, including the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), can affect the competitiveness of South African exporters.

For manufacturers, agricultural producers and other export-oriented businesses, access to a major international market influences decisions about pricing, investment, production and employment. Uncertainty over trade arrangements can make those decisions more difficult, particularly when businesses must commit resources long before the policy environment becomes clear.

Changes in America's political balance may influence expectations about future trade policy, but they do not automatically guarantee favourable outcomes for South Africa. Trade negotiations remain complex, and preferential access can depend on legislation, eligibility requirements and diplomatic relationships.

The more significant economic lesson is that South Africa must remain competitive regardless of political changes abroad. Reliable infrastructure, efficient logistics, regulatory certainty and strong domestic institutions can help businesses withstand international disruptions while positioning them to take advantage of new opportunities.

A market rally is not an economic recovery

There is a temptation to treat a rising stock exchange as proof that an economy is getting stronger. Yet stock-market performance and everyday economic conditions are related without being identical. Shares can rise because investors anticipate higher corporate earnings, even while households continue struggling with living costs and businesses face difficult operating conditions.

The more meaningful test is whether improved financial sentiment produces sustained investment, productive economic activity and greater resilience. That requires both favourable international conditions and a domestic environment capable of converting opportunity into measurable progress.

South Africa cannot determine the outcome of American elections or control movements in international commodity markets. It can, however, strengthen the foundations that allow its economy to benefit when global opportunities arise and better withstand periods of uncertainty.

The JSE's 5% rally demonstrates the speed at which international political developments can influence South African financial markets. Whether those gains become part of a more durable economic improvement is a question that can only be answered beyond the trading day.

· Editorial analysis of the market mechanisms and trade-policy implications discussed in the programme.

World.title: Goon financiers should be cursed and sent to hell, Chief Justice Koome says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Chief Justice Martha Koome said goonism falls under serious organised crimes that goes against the Rome Statute and humanity. [Phares Mutembei, Standard]

Chief Justice Martha Koome now says those mobilising and financing goons should be cursed and thrown to hell.

Koome on Thursday said goonism falls under organised serious crimes that go against the Rome Statute and humanity.

She spoke at Kieganguru, Maara constituency, where she presided over the opening of the Maara law courts.

While calling on police to focus more on arresting the mobilisers and financiers, Koome said a time has come for the country to plead with God to protect the country and rescue the youth who are being misused and misled into organised gangs and goonism.

“Nobody gives birth to a child to be called a goon. Those organisers will go to hell, we curse them,” Koome said, adding, “If they will not go to hell they will meet God's justice. These are our children, and we reclaim them in the name of our Lord Jesus.”

According to her, the last time she checked, people are charged at the International Criminal Court with Organised crime.

She maintained that the best solution to the current goonism that wreaked havoc, especially in political meetings, is to arrest the organisers.

Koome said the courts cannot hold arrested goons without bail, yet the constitution grants them the right to bail or bond.

“When we arrest small people with petty crimes of causing disorder, the law allows us to release them on bail and bond, but when you bring the organisers, we will charge them under the Serious Crimes Act,” she said.

Koome said currently, the judiciary has gazetted a serious crimes division at the High Court to support Magistrates handling the cases.

“Let us look at the root cause of goonism across the country and rehabilitate those involved by getting them gainful employment,” she said.

Her sentiments, however, differ from those of Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen, who on Wednesday told the National Assembly that the judiciary was the weakest link in the fight against the menace.

Tharaka Nithi Governor Muthomi Njuki, in his remarks, supported Koome’s view of arresting the planners.

Njuki, who doubles up as the Council of Governors Chairperson, said politicians have had their time and organising goons against their opponents should not be condoned.

Using the analogy of a dog, Njuki said ‘every barking dog has an owner ’, and it is time serious action was taken against such characters at whatever level they are.

The county boss said CoG will work closely with county security teams to arrest the fast-rising menace and report all cases.

Security agencies have been under scrutiny regarding goons, with calls for their arrest and prosecution.

Earlier on, Koome and DCI boss Mohammed Amin differed on how to handle the goons during a National Council for Administrative Justice meeting as with the DCI boss also accusing the Judiciary of laxity and granting minor bail to arrested goons.

But Koome maintained the issue must be addressed lest it becomes a thorn in the flesh ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: IEBC warns UDA SG Hassan Omar over remarks on deceased voters
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

UDA Secretary General Hassan Omar meets Village Elders and Mabalozi wa Nyumba Kumi from Jomvu Sub-County’ on September 10, 2026. [Nehemiah Okwemba, Standard]

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has issued a stern warning to Senator Hassan Omar after finding him in breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct over remarks he made at a political rally in Mombasa, cautioning that any repeat offence could attract tougher sanctions.

In a determination released on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee (ECCEC) found Omar guilty of breaching paragraphs 6(k)(i) and 6(l) of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

The committee consequently issued the senator with a formal and strict warning and severe caution, directing him to comply with the electoral regulations for the remainder of the applicable election period.

Omar was further instructed to refrain from language or conduct that could reasonably be understood as encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice or undermining public confidence in the integrity of the ballot.

The decision follows investigations into remarks the senator allegedly made during a public rally in Mombasa on September 11, 2026, which raised concerns over the possibility of encouraging electoral malpractice.

According to the commission, Omar was summoned to appear before the committee on October 21, 2026, to respond to the allegations. He honoured the summons and appeared in person, accompanied by his lawyer, where he was given an opportunity to explain his remarks and present his defence.

In reaching its determination, the committee considered the context in which the statements were made, Omar's explanation that his words were intended figuratively to encourage voter registration and participation, his subsequent clarification and the absence of evidence linking the remarks to an actual electoral incident.

However, the committee maintained that the language used could not be excused by the explanation offered.

It observed that the impugned words, considered in their original Kiswahili form and ordinary meaning, invoked the use of biometric identification details belonging to a deceased person to facilitate voting in that individual's name.

The committee consequently found the remarks inconsistent with the obligation under paragraph 6(l) of the Electoral Code to reassure voters about the integrity of the ballot.

The warning places Omar on clear notice that any recurrence of similar conduct could attract more severe sanctions under the Electoral Code of Conduct and applicable laws.

“The determination places Hon. Hassan Omar on clear and unequivocal notice that the warning issued by the Committee is intended to mark a firm boundary against any recurrence of similar conduct,” IEBC stated.

The commission further emphasised that political leaders and other electoral stakeholders have a constitutional right to campaign, criticise, debate, persuade and participate in political discourse.

However, it cautioned that political expression must be exercised responsibly, warning that statements perceived as advocating, encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

“As Kenya prepares for the 2027 General Election, the Commission calls upon all political leaders, candidates, political parties, supporters and other electoral stakeholders to exercise responsibility, restraint and vigilance in their public utterances and conduct,” the commission said.

The determination comes as political activities gradually intensify ahead of the 2027 General Election, with the electoral body seeking to strengthen compliance with regulations governing political campaigns and public conduct.

IEBC maintained that enforcement of the Electoral Code should not be interpreted as an attempt to suppress legitimate political competition or freedom of expression.

Instead, it said the measures were intended to safeguard democratic participation and ensure that every Kenyan could exercise their right to vote without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

The commission reiterated its commitment to protecting the sanctity of the ballot, assuring Kenyans that every vote must be protected and counted in accordance with the law.

It warned that it would continue enforcing electoral regulations firmly, fairly and without fear or favour, as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

World.title: Death rumours made me stronger, says ODM leader Oburu
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi when they paid a visit to ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi residence on November 4, 2026. [Speaker’s Press Unit]

ODM leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga has said rumours about his death while he was admitted to hospital only strengthened his determination to overcome his illness.

Dr Oburu who is recovering after being discharged from hospital, assured his supporters that he was making remarkable improvement and would return to active politics soon.

Speaking at his Nairobi residence on Wednesday when Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi paid him a visit, the ODM leader said the rumours only strengthened his resolve to come out of the hospital bed.

“Those who wrote me off while I was in hospital by declaring me dead only made me stronger and more determined to fight my sickness. Here I am, recovering and growing stronger by the day,” he said.

He said that his recovery was a testimony to God's protection, saying those who had spread the false reports had been put to shame.

Oburu admitted that the illness had slowed down him down but he was looking forward to returning to the political arena.

“The sickness slowed my political activities. Very soon, I will be back roaring in the best way I know how,” he said.

The senator thanked the National Assembly Speaker Wetang’ula, his Senate counterpart Kingi and other legislators for taking time to visit him following his discharge from hospital.

He said the visit had lifted his spirit and revealed that he missed participating in parliamentary debates and engaging in national political affairs.

“I have no words to explain my feelings after the Speakers of both Houses and fellow legislators created time to come and check on me,” he said.

“I miss being on the floor of the House debating and roaring in the political arena. I urge my supporters to pray for me and be patient because soon I will be back,” he added.

Despite his recent health challenges, Oburu kept his visitors entertained with his trademark humour while expressing confidence that he would soon resume his political duties.

The two Speakers condemned the spread of false information on social media, particularly rumours that the senator had died while undergoing treatment.

Wetang’ula said they were encouraged by the senator's recovery and wished him a full and speedy return to good health.

He, however, cautioned Oburu against rushing back into politics before fully recovering, urging him to give his health priority.

“Prioritise your health and avoid rushing back into political engagements before making a full recovery,” he said.

The National Assembly Speaker also praised the senator for his courage and determination in facing his health challenges.

Kingi said the Senate missed Dr Oburu's contribution to debates, parliamentary proceedings and national politics.

“As the Senate, we miss your contributions to proceedings and debates as well as your guidance in national politics. We pray that you get better and resume your political duties as soon as possible,” he said.

Those who accompanied the two Speakers included Senate Chief Whip David Wakoli, Senate Minority Leader Stewart Madzayo, Senators William Kisang and Daniel Maanzo.

Others were National Assembly Minority Whip Millie Odhiambo, Parliamentary Commissioner Mishi Mboko and MP Eve Obara.

World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).
