World.title: Kenya: Four Acquitted in Murder of U.S.-Based Couple Killed During Kenya Vacation in Nyamira
World.content:
Kisii — Four suspects charged with the murder of a Kenyan-American couple who were brutally killed at their home in Gesima, Nyamira County, have been acquitted after the court found insufficient evidence linking them to the killings.

The four were accused of murdering Edward Nyagechi and his wife, Grace Mong'ina Morema, in March 2023 while they were visiting Kenya from the United States.

The victims, who were based in Minneapolis, Minnesota, were found dead at their Nyamakoroto home on March 21, 2023, after neighbours raised concern over their failure to appear for their usual morning routine.

The murder triggered investigations that led to the arrest and prosecution of four suspects: Ezekiel Mogeni Migiro, Peris Ondara, Dennis Ondara Clement and Peter Njoroge Kirika.



The prosecution had accused the four of participating in the killings, which occurred between the night of March 20 and the early hours of March 21, 2023.

However, in its determination, the court found that the evidence presented was insufficient to establish a connection between the accused persons and the murders, resulting in their acquittal.

The ruling brings to a close the prosecution of the four suspects in the case, although the court's findings do not in themselves establish who was responsible for the killings.

The deaths of Morema and his wife sent shockwaves through Nyamira County, particularly because the couple had travelled from the United States for a holiday when they were killed.

Postmortem examinations established that Edward had sustained injuries to his head and stab wounds, while Grace died from strangulation.

Investigations also uncovered suspicious financial transactions involving mobile phones belonging to the deceased on the night of the killings.

During the trial, witnesses testified about money transfers made from the couple's phones, including transactions involving Sh62,000.

The case attracted considerable public attention, with the family repeatedly seeking answers over the circumstances surrounding the couple's deaths.

World.title: Sudan: Sanctions Against Commanders Implicated in Sudan Rapes 'Seek Accountability', Says UK Minister
World.content:
Geneva — UK Development Minister Kirsty McNeill says that sanctions her government has announced against military commanders suspected of atrocities, including conflict-related sexual violence, during the fall of El Fasher in western Sudan are aimed at seeking accountability.

McNeill spoke to journalists at a Nov. 4 press conference in Geneva, where she said that one year after the fall of El Fasher, the capital of North Darfur State, the UK had last week brought forward a new package of action for Sudan.

“I've also today been sitting with the fact-finding mission on Sudan and reflecting on what more we can do as the founder of the Coalition for Atrocity Prevention and Justice in Sudan,” said McNeill during a visit to Geneva.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

“We were a big supporter and initiator of the fact-finding mission. We are the initiator of the international coalition on atrocity prevention.”

She said, “Sudan is very close to the top of our priority list,” and the UK is working, and the UK approach is “focused on partnership, not paternalism, brisk business-like relationships of equals, where we work with partner countries to strengthen their systems.

“We do it bilaterally with government counterparts, we do it through the multilateral system, but we are also trying to give space to Sudanese civil society and human rights defenders, and journalists and researchers, give them platforms from which to make their case directly,” said McNeill.

- HUMANITARIAN RESPONSE NEEDED

McNeill said that there is a need for a humanitarian response “in what remains the world's biggest humanitarian crisis today” and the UK is working bilaterally

Action has come as UK-backed investigations expose campaigns of deliberate starvation and sexual violence by all sides in the conflict.

The continuing armed conflict began on April 15, 2023, between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the group calling itself the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), with other warring parties involved, according to the United Nations.

McNeil noted that the humanitarian response does not just take money.

“It takes access. It takes upholding international humanitarian law. It takes a commitment to people's rights being respected and lives saved in really unspeakable humanitarian conditions,” said McNeill.

The British government said last week that action came as UK-backed investigations exposed campaigns of deliberate starvation and sexual violence by all sides in the conflict.

Under the UK action, 15 senior commanders from both the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have been sanctioned for suspected atrocities, including conflict-related sexual violence.

“This includes Hussein Abu Jalak, an RSF colonel linked to atrocities during the siege of El Fasher, and Al-Nour Ahmed Adam (‘Al-Qubba’), identified as present and playing a prominent role in besieging and attacking the city.#

McNeill said that the UK action “is designed to shine a spotlight on the horrific violence seen during the siege of the city - and help survivors rebuild their lives.”

The sanctions impose a travel ban and asset freeze on those designated, while further ensuring the horrors that took place at El Fasher will be known to the world.

- HUMAN CATASTROPHE IN SUDAN

The UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: "The war in Sudan has created a humanitarian catastrophe.

“A year on from the atrocities in El Fasher, UK-funded investigations have shown that rape and starvation are still being weaponised against the people of Sudan.”

He said that those are crimes against humanity and the perpetrators must be held accountable, while support from all external backers to the warring parties must end.

Close 

One year ago, after an eighteen-month siege that starved hundreds of thousands of civilians, El Fasher fell to the Rapid Support Forces.

In the days that followed, civilians were massacred, women and girls were subjected to horrific sexual violence, and entire communities were devastated.

The action comes as UK-backed investigations expose campaigns of deliberate starvation and sexual violence by all sides in the conflict.

The UK said it is allocating a total of 15 million British pounds (20.2 million dollars) to support the survivors of conflict-related sexual violence in Sudan and to back the ongoing response to the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Sudan.

Sudan occupies 1,886,068 square kilometres (728,215 square miles), making it Africa's third-largest country by area, and has a population of around 53 million, according to Worldometer.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 5, 2026
World.content:
Ghanaian Mother Travels to US After Son's Fatal Shooting

The mother of 15-year-old Ghanaian boy Javits Frimpong, who was fatally shot while walking to school in New York's Bronx, has travelled to the United States. She was granted an emergency visa by President Donald Trump. Doris Adu Gyamfi said that she wants justice for her son at the airport before her departure. Police are still searching for three teenage suspects in connection with the shooting. No arrests have been made. The killing has sparked outrage in Ghana and the US. New York mayor Zohran Mamdani said the murder of a child was a pain no parent should endure, "let alone from thousands of miles away." Ghana's government is calling for a thorough investigation and pledging legal and consular support to the family.

Africa Emerges as Growing Hub for Synthetic Drug Production



Discoveries of clandestine drug laboratories across Africa are raising concerns that the continent is becoming an increasingly important centre for the production of synthetic drugs, rather than simply serving as a transit route for international trafficking networks. In Nigeria, authorities recently dismantled what they described as the country's largest methamphetamine laboratory, seizing more than 2.4 tonnes of the drug and precursor chemicals, with an estimated international value of 363 million dollars. Similar laboratories have been uncovered in South Africa, Kenya and Mozambique. The increasing production and use of synthetic drugs is causing addiction, school dropouts, family breakdown and other social problems, experts said. They are calling for stronger regional cooperation, rehabilitation services and prevention programmes alongside law enforcement.

Tinubu Seeks Senate Approval for $7.7bn External Loan

Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked the Senate to approve $7.7 billion in external borrowing to help finance the Federal Government's 2026 budget deficit. Senate President Godswill Akpabio said that the latest request supersedes an earlier proposal for 20.3 billion dollars in external loans. Tinubu said that the funds will be sourced through a combination of multilateral and bilateral loans, international financial institutions and Eurobond issuance. Priority will be given to financing defence, security, infrastructure, agriculture, education and healthcare. He also said that the borrowing will help strengthen Nigeria's foreign reserves and support the naira. He said that the funds would be received by the Central Bank of Nigeria on behalf of the Federal Government, thereby increasing the country's foreign reserves. The request has been referred to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debt for consideration.

DR Congo Rebels Threaten Radio Station, Demand Broadcast Approval

The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) has called on rebel leaders in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo to stop threatening journalist Guillaume Munguakonkwa and interfering with the operations of community radio station Kamole FM. Munguakonkwa went into hiding for five days after armed members of the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) reportedly searched for him over broadcasts relating to their activities. The station's director was also summoned and ordered to submit all news reports for approval before they could be aired, with threats of imprisonment for non-compliance. CPJ said that the threats highlight the growing dangers facing journalists covering the conflict in eastern DR Congo and has urged all armed groups to respect press freedom and allow independent reporting.

Somalia Rejects Israel's Diplomatic Moves in Somaliland

Somalia has rejected Israel's appointment of an ambassador to Somaliland and plans to establish an embassy in the region, describing the moves as a violation of its sovereignty and territorial integrity. Israel's ambassador, Michael Lotem, recently presented his credentials to Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi Irro, followed by a ceremony marking the planned embassy site in Hargeisa. Somalia maintains that Somaliland remains part of its territory and has no authority to establish independent diplomatic relations. It has called on Israel to reverse the decisions and urged the international community not to recognise them, warning that the developments could increase tensions in the strategically important Red Sea and Gulf of Aden region.

Close 

Mugabe's Youngest Son Arrested in Zimbabwe Over Assault and Vehicle Smuggling

Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe, the youngest son of Zimbabwe's late former president Robert Mugabe, has been arrested alongside four other men in connection with an assault case in Harare. The arrests follow an investigation into the alleged smuggling of two luxury vehicles into the country, which the Zimbabwe Anti-Corruption Commission has reportedly seized. The suspects face charges of contravening Section 136 of the Criminal Law (Codification and Reform) Act, alternatively Section 182 of the Customs and Excise Act. Police said that the alleged assault took place at Brompton Guest Lodge. Bellarmine previously made headlines in South Africa following his arrest in February 2026 after a shooting incident at his Hyde Park residence in Johannesburg, in which a gardener was wounded.

World.title: Charles Barkley rips bold trick-or-treaters or ask him to sign their basketball cards
World.content:
Halloween is in the books, which means that if your household is anything like mine, you will soon be tasked with hanging Christmas lights on the front porch. However, NBA great Charles Barkley still has one Halloween-related gripe he needs to get off his chest.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

He's got some bold kids in his neighborhood who aren't content with just a fun-sized Snickers bar or a pack of Skittles Gummies (which are actually very good, by the way); they want the Round Mound of Rebound to grab a Sharpie and sign their basketball cards.

On a recent edition of "Inside the NBA," Barkley took a moment to address the youngsters — I think we need to assume they're youngsters, but who knows? — who were looking to add something with some resale value to their jack-o'-lantern candy buckets.

CHARLES BARKLEY CALLS OUT LEBRON JAMES FOR DISRESPECTING THE NATIONAL ANTHEM WITH PRACTICE GOLF SWING

COOPER FLAGG ROOKIE CARD MAKES EYE-POPPING RECORD SALE, BUT IS IT ACTUALLY A GOOD INVESTMENT?

I can understand the frustration. This is premeditated. I don't think many kids are keeping Barkley cards in their wallets at all times on the off chance they run into him while dressed as a pirate, football player, or inflatable Minion.

However, weirdly, I respect the boldness. Those kids are go-getters.

That said, they may want to leave their binders at home next year.

"I love being home and giving the kids candy," Barkley continued. "But now they're bringing cards. You can't be mean to kids. I wanted to punch them in the face, but I couldn't do it."

CHARLES BARKLEY JOKINGLY WARNS 'INSIDE THE NBA' CREW ABOUT SHAQUILLE O'NEAL'S FBI CONNECTION

World.title: Schumer faces mutiny from newly elected Senate Dems as party prepares to seize power
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Senate Democrats will soon decide who will lead them with their newly acquired grip on power in the upper chamber, and while Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., appears to be the favorite, some in the caucus aren’t eager to back him.

Schumer has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade, helming the caucus as both majority and minority leader since 2017. But many of the fresh crop of Democratic senators-elect, which span the ideological gamut from moderate to progressive, are tepid, at best, in backing him for another term.

And some said throughout their campaigns that they wouldn’t support him at all.

DEM SENATE HOPEFUL REJECTS SCHUMER BUT BENEFITS FROM MILLIONS IN SPENDING BY HIS ALLIES

"I mean no disrespect for Chuck Schumer, but we need new leadership," Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton told CNN in September. "We need new younger leadership, young blood."

Hamilton is the moderate megachurch pastor who toppled Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., on Election Night, flipping the Sunflower State for the first time in nearly a century. He, like others this cycle, argued that Democrats needed "fresh ideas and fresh leadership."

"In Kansas, Chuck Schumer is a liability for Democrats, and we've got to have leaders that can unite us, bring us together, not just Democrats, but bring together Democrats and Republicans to solve real problems," he said. "And I think people are frustrated with the gridlock in the sense that people are not working together to solve problems."

Democrats are expected to hold their leadership elections later this year, and Schumer will have to shore up support within his newly expanded caucus to stay at the top. But he will only need a majority of Senate Democrats to back him.

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS BRACES FOR POST-ELECTION GAME OF MUSICAL CHAIRS AS LEADERSHIP BATTLES LOOM

So far, Democrats’ majority in the upper chamber is at 54 seats and could further expand depending on the results in Mississippi and Alaska, which as of Thursday were leaning in their favor.

Schumer believed that he would still be the one to lead Democrats and contended to reporters on Wednesday that issues that incoming senators and their voters may have had with the direction of the Democratic Party in recent years were not about him.

"The issue is not me," Schumer said. "I'll be re-elected as majority leader, but the issue is focusing on the American people and what they want."

Still, there is a faction of newcomers, including senators-elect Troy Jackson in Maine, Julianna Stratton in Illinois, Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota, who aren’t all in for Schumer.

THUNE GOES ALL-IN ON CAMPAIGN TRAIL AS SCHUMER STAYS ON BENCH, FACES REJECTION FROM FELLOW DEMS

Jackson, speaking to reporters just before Election Day, said his position hadn’t changed on Schumer.

"I told Schumer that I’m going to, you know, support somebody else," Jackson said. "So it’s no different now."

That somebody else could be Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., who has been proposed as an alternative by progressives, like El-Sayed, to lead Senate Democrats instead of Schumer. Van Hollen may have his eyes elsewhere — he has said that he’s "kicking the tires" on a 2028 run.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

A Democratic aide familiar with Van Hollen’s thinking told Fox News Digital that before selecting a new leader, the lawmaker believed "the caucus needs to have an honest and open conversation about how we move an agenda forward that reflects the will of the American people."

"He’s made it clear that the new Democratic majorities need to use their power to push a proactive, economic agenda," they said.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

I'm, of course, talking about the breakup of Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson. I thought these two were going to make it. Unfortunately, they called it quits last year, but remain close friends and business partners.

So, who knows what the future holds for these two and their nearly 50-year age gap? The reason for the split, according to the Daily Mail, was that the relationship became a distraction. Neither of them wanted that.

"Looking back, that was a big part of what pulled his focus away from football last season," the Daily Mail reported.

"He was thinking about taking the next steps with her, getting engaged, getting married, and building a future together, while also dealing with the constant attention and outside scrutiny that came with being in such a high-profile relationship. It became overwhelming for both of them."

Enough about these two. Let's get to the reality of dating a professional athlete. If you're only invited to attend road games, there's a decent chance you're the side chick. An adult film star says she found this out the hard way.

Plus, Lindsey Vonn has a relationship update that she felt the need to share. But don't expect these updates to take place on a regular basis going forward.

Go follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook and keep sending your emails here: sean.joseph@outkick.com (anonymously if you prefer).

Adult film star Silvia Saige had no idea she was Royals pitcher Bruce Chen's other woman until he got engaged

Who among us doesn’t love a good story about baseball and romance? We all remember "Bull Durham," don't we?

Adult film actress Silvia Saige claimed on the "Holly Randall Unfiltered" podcast that she once dated former MLB pitcher Bruce Chen while he was a member of the Kansas City Royals.

Chen was close to the end of his career at the time, she said. The two met, according to Saige, thanks to Eric Hosmer while she was doing promotional modeling in Kansas City before she got into porn.

"I had gone to an event and I had actually gone home, and I'll say this guy's name too, cause f--- him, I truly hate this man, Eric Hosmer, was our first baseman at the time and he and I had kind of hit it off at the event," Saige said. "So I went home with him."

She alleged that he kicked her out of his place after she refused to sleep with him. She assumes Chen got her phone number from Hosmer after he bragged about it in the locker room the next day.

'CHARLIE'S ANGELS' ACTRESS CLAIMS COSTAR INVITED HER TO THREESOME, A CONTRABAND BRA FOR LOVE & NO HARM NO FOUL

Saige continued, "He (Chen) had hit me up, and he said, you know, 'I would like to take you out, and I would like to show you how a woman should be treated, because what Eric did to you was completely wrong, and I'm so sorry, let me make that up to you.'"

She said that Chen did make it up to her. He flew her out to an away game first class like a gentleman for their first date and pulled out all the stops once she arrived.

"When I got there, the doorman knew my name and what I was wearing and escorted me up," Saige claimed. "I had a massage table waiting and money to go shopping."

None of that was a red flag to her. She thought going all out with the red carpet treatment was how it was supposed to be. They ended up dating for several months, and he even met her family, according to Saige.

The entire time, it was first-class flights to away games and "service, service, service." Around eight months into the relationship is when she found out that she was the side chick.

That news was delivered by a phone call from her aunt. Saige said that her uncle had seen on the news that Chen was engaged.

She called Chen up, and he confirmed that he was going to marry someone else, but that he would still like to see her too. According to her, he offered her money.

"It was like, you know like, 'I'll pay your bills and keep you happy,'" she told host Holly Randall.

That wasn’t an arrangement she was willing to knowingly enter into at the time. She genuinely thought she was in a real relationship and turned it down. The invites to only away games didn’t give it away that there was someone else.

Ladies, if you're romantically involved with an athlete, and you're only being invited to away games, take it as a sign. There's a good chance you're not the starter on their roster.

Follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook .

Lindsey Vonn has a relationship update

No, Lindsey Vonn isn't engaged to her boyfriend, fellow alpine skier Matthieu Bailet. She just wants you to know that she's "really happy" about her "amazing boyfriend," she told People.

Now to be fair to her, she told People that at a fashion awards show where the outlet likely asked her about her relationship. But don't expect too many of these kinds of updates. She's not trying to put it in everyone’s face.

"I think in my past it’s kind of been mixed of keeping things private and maybe oversharing. I’m trying to strike a nice balance," Vonn said.

"He’s awesome and I wanted to share that. People know now I’m dating someone, and I’m happy, but I’m not going to share too much moving forward."

Good for her. It's the right call. Finding the perfect balance and picking your spots to show off your boyfriend shirtless while in a bikini isn't done enough.

It's a "look at me" society we live in. I like those who are able to show restraint.

You know Lindsey Vonn is dating someone. Boom, they're hot together in swimwear, and happy, then they keep it to themselves again for a while.

That's a couple you can root for. They're not proposing in your face on the jumbotron trying to make everything all about them.

It's an occasional behind the scenes, don't we look good in our underwear? The answer is yes. Yes, you do. We'll all be here for your next partially clothed relationship update. Until then, we wish you nothing but the best.

Girls who married the bad boys, how is your marriage?

As you might have guessed, there are a lot of not-so-great outcomes from marrying a bad boy. But what about those who beat the odds?

The ones who have made it work for 40 years even after being stood up on their first date because the bad boy was helping his girlfriend move out.

That's what we're all chasing. Isn't it? A little bit of magic in places nobody else is willing to look. There will be failure, but what about the ones that succeed?

Here's some of the good, the bad, and the sometimes ugly:

A girl I went to school with who became a criminal lawyer, fell into love with a criminal that she was defending. Ended up participating in his crimes, got caught by the police, ended up in gaol and is now released but is banned from ever being a lawyer.

Preparing to divorce him! I will say that what’s attractive at 22 is very much not attractive at 32.

Over. He was the biggest mistake I ever made. What I loved about him the most (that he was a free spirit, and wild) was what I ended up hating about him. Turned out that love didn’t pay the bills. I did.

Thankfully didn't marry him, but did spend 10 years with him. Almost ruined me and my kids. We survived and recovered, he is not doing well these days last I heard.

Happily Divorced from that one

I decided not to marry him. He's been divorced 3 times and has 4 kids from 3 different women. Definitely dodged a bullet

I did! My husband had some wild-ass 32 years before I met him. He loved the bars and drinking whiskey. He did some drugs casually and made a few law-related mistakes. He was on his way out of the hard living when I met him, but still had a wild streak. This is the same man who goes to bed before 9 now and is currently piled up in my pink quilt baby-talking our Yorkie.

My mom married the bad boy. Their first date, he stood her up to help his other girlfriend move out. They've been married for almost 40 years now. I love hearing my mom react in horror when my dad tells her stories of his younger days.

Married a druggie bartender after knowing him 6 months! He’s now a CEO and the best husband and dad in the world. I still swoon when he smiles. It’s been 26 amazing years.

World.title: LIV Golf is officially over after announcing plans to 'wind-down' operations after failed rescue deal
World.content:
LIV Golf is dead.

The remaining powers that be were working to manufacture some form of a second edition of the circuit despite having no funding and an entirely unknown roster of players, but the white flag has officially been waved after five seasons.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

During a bankruptcy court hearing held on Thursday, LIV Golf's lawyers shared plans for the circuit to begin liquidating its assets, with the process expected to begin on Nov. 9. LIV Golf released a statement following the hearing, announcing that it "intends to transition to an orderly wind-down of its operations."

RORY MCILROY MAKES SERIOUS ACCUSATION ABOUT LIV GOLF WANTING TO 'DESTROY' THE EUROPEAN TOUR

Nothing about LIV officially closing up shop is a surprise given recent developments.

In April, the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced that it would cease funding the circuit at the end of the 2026 season. The Saudi PIF was the sole funder of LIV, and following a reported $266 million injection into the league for 2026, was set to reach $6 billion invested dating back to 2021.

With the never-ending spigot of cash shut off by the Saudis, LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September, but was quickly tossed a lifeline by BC Partners in the form of a $300 million pledged investment to navigate through the proceedings and, in theory, be suited to launch 'LIV 2.0' when all the dust had settled.

On Wednesday, LIV's lifeline disappeared. BC Partners scrapped the planned rescue deal after the circuit failed to get any firm commitments from the few high-profile players who had yet to officially announce their departure from the circuit.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

According to The Athletic, BC Partners had secured signatures from more than 30 players willing to compete on 'LIV 2.0,' but 10 additional players of higher-profile status failed to commit before the Oct. 25 deadline that was given.

"We thank our partners at the PIF for their collaboration and support, and BC Partners Credit for its engagement throughout this process," LIV CEO Scott O'Neil said in a statement. "We are also deeply grateful to our employees, Board, advisors, and fans around the world, whose dedication, resilience, and belief made this remarkable journey possible. Golf has given so much to so many, and my hope is that those entrusted with its future will lead with the generosity, perspective, and shared purpose this extraordinary game deserves."

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

LIV Golf was originally formed in October 2021 before the league hosted its inaugural tournament in England in June 2022. Its initial events were contested over three days, consisting of no-cut, 54-hole tournaments with guaranteed paydays for every player in the field.

The circuit was able to poach many stars away from the PGA Tour, including Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm, Brooks Koepka, Dustin Johnson, and Phil Mickelson, with the incentives of a limited schedule and nine-figure signing bonuses in some cases.

Koepka (2023 PGA Championship) and DeChambeau (2024 U.S. Open) were the two lone players to win a major championship while competing on LIV.

PGA TOUR CEO BRIAN ROLAPP REITERATES IT IS NOT CONSIDERING A RETURNING MEMBER PROGRAM FOR LIV GOLFERS

The playing fate of former LIV golfers looking to return to the PGA Tour is unknown at this moment. Koepka returned to the Tour at the beginning of 2026 after taking advantage of a now non-existent Returning Members Program that included many penalties and financial requirements.

With LIV no longer in operation, players who stood alongside the circuit until the final minutes – which includes DeChambeau – do not hold any leverage with the PGA Tour and DP World Tour, which now hold the only cards in the game.

Schumer was pressed on whether he plans to abolish the filibuster as speculation grows that Democrats could eliminate the filibuster after President Donald Trump urged Senate Republicans to terminate it numerous times to pass the SAVE America Act. Trump previously warned that if Republicans didn’t act on it, the Democrats would if given the opportunity — which they now have.

Schumer ignored the question after being asked twice by Fox News Digital if he plans to eliminate it.

FETTERMAN STRONGLY SUPPORTS THE FILIBUSTER AS TRUMP URGES SENATE REPUBLICANS TO SCRAP IT

The question comes as some Democrats have previously signaled openness to eliminating the filibuster if they regained the Senate.

During a press conference Wednesday morning, Schumer also refused to answer questions about some of his plans for the Senate as they take back the majority — including eliminating the filibuster. He also said that he will be "re-elected as majority leader" by the Senate Democratic caucus, despite opposition from newly elected Democrats. He quickly redirected the conversation to focus on the blue wave in the midterm elections and what the party plans to do with the "generational remake of the Senate map."

SCHUMER SAYS HE'S NOT GOING ANYWHERE, BUT HIS OWN CANDIDATES AREN'T READY TO BACK HIM

Jeffries was also asked by Fox News Digital about the looming question over whether Democrats will probe Elon Musk after the party has begun eyeing targets in their discussed efforts to investigate alleged corruption in the Trump administration.

Jeffries gave Fox News Digital a thumbs-up when approached but did not respond when asked whether House Democrats would investigate Musk.

Musk has emerged as a potential target of Democratic oversight, with some lawmakers calling for scrutiny of his time as head of the Department of Government Efficiency. Democratic lawmakers have also suggested looking into this companies' multibillion-dollar contracts with the federal government, and more recently, his role in cutting internet access to the Ukrainian military.

‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

The House Minority Leader’s refusal to comment comes as Democrats are divided over whether they would select Jeffries as Speaker of the House. There was a petition started that has received over 550,000 to oust Jeffries from leading the House, arguing the party needs a Speaker that represents "the Democratic voters, not just the Democratic establishment."

World.title: Melania Trump: Oleshky ceasefire is a ‘spark’ for 'more enduring' peace between Ukraine, Russia
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

First lady Melania Trump and envoys from both Russia and Ukraine spoke from the White House on Thursday, hailing the ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Oleshky region as a potential "spark" for peace that lasts beyond a temporary regional ceasefire.

"We have chosen humanity over war," the first lady said in a White House trilateral news conference with the two warring countries. "Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace. Every significant transformation begins with a small spark."

"Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire," she added, calling Oleshky "a spark in a world of darkness capable of illuminating the best in humanity."

INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL

Trump said she became aware of a humanitarian crisis in the region in September and directed her representative, Marc Beckman, to engage with Russia and Ukraine on her behalf. She said both countries agreed to work with her as an "exclusive intermediary" to establish a ceasefire in Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region, deliver humanitarian aid and create a safe evacuation route for civilians.

Her remarks were followed by comments from Russian special envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who said Russian President Vladimir Putin appreciated President Donald Trump’s efforts to stop the fighting.

US WILL MEDIATE UPCOMING UKRAINE-RUSSIA TALKS IN ABU DHABI, WITKOFF SAYS

"President Putin also appreciates President Trump's peacemaking effort and his team working on a peace plan to resolve Ukrainian crisis," Dmitriev said in a rare moment of a Russian diplomat speaking at the White House. "President Trump has asked President Putin to support a number of initiatives on exchanging of prisoners, on releasing U.S. prisoners on humanitarian efforts. And President Putin supported those ideas and those initiatives."

"And it's very important that cooperation between Russia and Ukraine and Russia in the United States matters not only for our two nations, but for the entire world," he continued. "Let us continue making great humanitarian contributions. We can together, let us build a future of peace, partnership and prosperity for the benefit of our families, our children and future generations."

RUSSIA RELEASES AMERICAN TEACHER IMPRISONED ON UKRAINE MERCENARY CHARGES AFTER TRUMP PRESSED PUTIN

"Dear Melania, you saved and touched so many lives," he concluded.

David Arakhamia, the leader of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's political party, called Melania Trump's ceasefire the 'biggest de-escalation since 2022," when the war began.

UKRAINE'S ZELENSKYY OPEN TO FREEZING FRONT LINES IN CEASEFIRE WITH RUSSIA

"Madam first lady, I would like to thank you: You did an amazing job," he said. "I think when everything started with you and your team, we had about 5% of people who believed in success, and 95% of skeptics who said it wasn’t going to work. Now, after it happened, it’s switched completely: 95% of the people believe that we can do things like that, and 5% are still skeptical."

Peace is now a matter of when, not if, he added.

KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE

Getting fearful Ukrainians out of the Russian-controlled city is an important step toward deciding how peace will be made and determining the long-term fate of the occupied territory of southern Ukraine.

"On the first day, people in the area did not believe it was happening," Arakhamia said. "They stayed in their homes, waiting to see if the clock was ticking backward. The next day, they started walking around their homes. The day after that, they came to see their broken homes and find their belongings.

"This is really emotional to watch and supervise, to understand what we are doing," he added. "I think we are creating momentum where both sides are learning the little mechanics of how to keep the peace when the peace comes.

"I would also like to sincerely thank you, from my heart, for doing this."

Dmitriev attended the event and met with U.S. officials, sources told Reuters. Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, also attended the event.

World.title: DAVID ASMAN: Democrats exploit gas-price pain while ignoring their own record
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The incredible irony of this election is that Democrats won largely on the issue of higher gas prices…when those same Democrats have done everything they can to raise gas prices when they’ve been in power.

The very first executive order that President Biden signed on his first day in office was cancelling the 1,200-mile-long Keystone XL pipeline, which would have brought 830,000 barrels of Canadian oil a day into U.S. refineries. The U.S. Gulf Coast refineries that the Keystone pipeline would have served are built and optimized to process Canada’s heavy, sour crude oils — like Alberta tar sands/bitumen — into high volumes of diesel and jet fuel. That is exactly the kind of fuel we’re in most need of right now.

And it wasn’t just President Biden. On February 24, 2015, President Barack Obama vetoed the Keystone XL Pipeline Approval Act passed by Congress. An attempt in the Senate to override Obama’s veto failed on March 4, 2015.

DUFFY UNLEASHES ON BUTTIGIEG WITH SWIPE OVER WHICH ADMIN HAS ACCOMPLISHED MORE: 'MOVED LIKE A SLOTH'

Other Democrat presidential contenders are on record favoring a carbon tax, which would have an immediate effect on raising gas prices. On Sept 4, 2019, Kamala Harris said, "Under my plan there will be a carbon fee." Likewise, Pete Buttigieg campaigned on the idea of an expensive carbon tax, saying, "I propose that we assess a carbon tax. I know you’re not supposed to use the "T" word when you’re in politics, but you might as well call this what it is."

When Buttigieg became secretary of Transportation under President Biden, he worked hard trying to get auto companies to switch from gas-powered cars to EVs, even though consumers weren’t buying and car companies and dealers were left warehousing thousands of unsold vehicles. GM absorbed $11.2 billion in losses and cancellation of its EV infrastructure plans. Ford eliminated entire models, such as its electric F-150 truck, which Buttigieg promoted and President Biden test drove in Dearborn, Michigan, in May 2021. Eventually, Ford took a $19.5 billion EV write-down. But through it all, Buttigieg insisted that EV buyers would never go back to gas-powered cars…even after a brutal winter when EV owners in Chicago and elsewhere swore they’d never buy another EV, as batteries failed to function in the cold weather.

Of course, the younger generation of Democrat presidential contenders are just as eager to raise your gas prices. Rep Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s "Green New Deal" was shoehorned, in part, into President Biden’s infamously named "Inflation Reduction Act." The Act's multi-trillion-dollar green energy spending boondoggle became a major factor in the Biden administration’s 21.5% cumulative inflation, which is still part of the unaffordability crisis that Democrats blame on President Trump.

All these lame-brain ideas and unworkable investments ended up creating big increases at the pump that dwarf today’s prices. The gas prices under President Obama peaked at $4.55 a gallon, in some areas, in May 2011. Inflation adjusted, that would be $6.78 today. Gas peaked under President Biden at $5.03 in June 2022. That would be $5.79 today. And the highest spike hike under President Trump was $4.55 a gallon in mid-May of this year.

JEFFRIES CALLS OUT TRUMP-ERA GAS PRICES AFTER TELLING REPUBLICANS NOT TO POLITICIZE PUMP PAIN UNDER BIDEN

President Trump claims that once the Iranian war is over, gas prices will come back to the $3 level we saw just before the war began. But voters became understandably frustrated with the president’s failed estimates of when the war will end. We did see oil prices drop dramatically when it looked like we had an Iranian deal in April. But exactly when the war is over, we don’t know.

World.title: LeBron James sends cease and desist to 'Bron AI' sports betting app over unauthorized likeness
World.content:
LeBron James has issued a cease-and-desist letter to an AI-powered sports betting tool that the NBA star says uses his likeness, a spokesperson for James confirmed.

Anish Gupta, the CEO of the app "Bron AI," released a video that features a person resembling James wearing a jersey with his nickname, "Bron," and the number 23.

The character appears to be scrolling through players before stopping on Dillon Brooks, a longtime rival of James.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Dillon Brooks? On Kalshi? Hell nah," the character says.

According to Apple's App Store, Bron is "a sports analytics and betting research app with live odds comparisons, data-backed picks, player and team brands, a multi-leg Slip, and bet tracking."

But the striking resemblance to the NBA's all-time leading scorer was enough for James himself to act.

"LeBron is in no way affiliated with this unauthorized use of his likeness," a spokesperson for James said to Front Office Sports.

The letter said the "unauthorized use and illicit exploitation of" James' "name, nickname, likeness, image, persona, and other identifying attributes, materials and related information" were used in the ad. The letter also says that it implies James is "involved with betting on basketball, which is a very serious violation of NBA rules and regulations."

VICTOR WEMBANYAMA DOES BEST WILT CHAMBERLAIN IMPRESSION WITH 50-20 NIGHT, SAYS HE CAN 'STILL DO MORE'

James has a brand deal with the prediction market Polymarket.

The letter is asking Bron AI to permanently stop using James' likeness and tell everyone who uses the app that the Philadelphia 76ers star is not affiliated with the app.

"I’m sure the intent here was for us to send a cease and desist in order to make it a story," James' longtime media adviser Adam Mendelsohn told Front Office Sports. "You would prefer not to respond but you don’t have a choice in a situation like this. It’s not the first time and it won’t be the last. For what it’s worth, these gimmicks never work because people see through it."



The app is free to download but costs $249.99 annually, or $29.99 monthly, to use its pro version.

World.title: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman defeats Karen Bass in the L.A. mayor’s race
World.content:
City Council member Nithya Raman has defeated incumbent Karen Bass in the Los Angeles mayoral race, NBC News projects, capping off a rapid political ascent for a progressive challenger who railed against the “broken status quo” in the country’s second-largest metropolis.

Raman, 45, who is part of the Democratic Socialists of America, unseated Bass, a former six-term congresswoman and a fixture of California’s political scene for decades. The result means three major cities will be led by democratic socialists, with Raman joining New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Janeese Lewis George, who won the mayor’s race in Washington, D.C., this week.

Bass faced intense scrutiny over her response to a January 2025 wildfire in the Pacific Palisades neighborhood, the most destructive in Los Angeles history. The blaze erupted while she was in the West African nation of Ghana attending a presidential inauguration. It went on to destroy thousands of homes and kill 12 people.

Follow live updates on the midterm elections.

Raman, a former urban planner and activist, accused Bass of mismanaging the city’s homelessness problem and rising housing prices. She blasted City Hall for what she characterized as “a reluctance to move forward with the transformative policy change that this city needs right now.”

Bass, for her part, argued Raman was “not ready for primetime” after six years on the City Council.

Karen Bass in Elysian Park in Los Angeles. Jason Armond / Los Angeles Times via Getty

The two Democrats also differed sharply on Israel’s war in Gaza, highlighting a generational split in the party. Speaking at a September forum co-hosted by the Jewish Federation Los Angeles, Raman said she agreed with left-wing influencer Hasan Piker that Israel had committed genocide against Palestinians; Bass rejected that label.

Raman’s candidacy drew comparisons to that of Mamdani, whose campaign rallied New York City voters dissatisfied with the political old guard. Raman touted her progressive bona fides while stressing her “independence” from the Democratic Socialists of America.

The incoming mayor’s agenda will be defined in part by the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles, a complex undertaking that will test the city’s physical infrastructure, public transportation services and security systems.

Raman endorsed Bass at the beginning of the year before she launched a last-minute bid of her own. Bass and Raman took the top two spots in a June 2 primary contest, advancing to a runoff over populist insurgent Spencer Pratt, a former reality television star who blasted the city’s political establishment with provocative social media videos.

On the City Council, Raman represents a district that ranges from the San Fernando Valley to the Santa Monica Mountains. She was born in India and moved to the U.S. with her family as a child, later attending Harvard University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

World.title: Head of DOJ Civil Rights Division resigns after GOP midterms loss
World.content:
WASHINGTON — Harmeet Dhillon, the Republican attorney who oversaw a massive overhaul of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, submitted her resignation on Thursday.

Attorney General Todd Blanche posted on X that he has accepted Dhillon’s resignation. He wrote that she “defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favor” and that the DOJ “is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavors.”

The departure of Dhillon, who had a long history of working as an election lawyer for the GOP, comes just two days after Democrats won control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections.

Under Dhillon’s leadership, the Civil Rights Division led some of the Trump administration’s most controversial legal maneuvers, including lawsuits that cited claims of discrimination at elite universities. The division declined to open a use-of-force investigation into the ICE officer who shot and killed Renee Nicole Good in Minnesota earlier this year.

Her office also filed lawsuits against 30 states and Washington, D.C., in an effort to obtain voter registration lists from the states in the months before the election, with federal judges dismissing 27 of those cases. Dhillon was a regular presence on conservative media in the run-up to Tuesday’s elections, promoting the work of the Civil Rights Division.

Dhillon is set to speak at the Donald Trump Ballroom at the Mar-a-Lago Club during the Conservative Political Action Committee’s Circle Retreat and Gala on Thursday.

Bloomberg Law first reported her resignation plans.

Dhillon’s office recently attempted to indict Cassidy Hutchinson, the former Trump administration official who testified before the House Jan. 6 committee about Trump’s actions during the Capitol siege.

Her office also brought a criminal case against former CNN journalist Don Lemon and protesters over a demonstration at a church in Minnesota under a statute historically used to protect reproductive rights facilities.

Stacey Young, the executive director of the group Justice Connection, called Dhillon “the most destructive, lawless, and hateful head of the Civil Rights Division in DOJ history,” and said in a statement that she “wielded the enormous power of the Justice Department to threaten universities, state and local officials, and election workers in spurious cases that rarely won in court.”

Dhillon “decimated” the Civil Rights Division, Young said, and called on the incoming Senate “to exercise its full advice and consent powers to ensure the next Assistant Attorney General fulfills the division’s congressional mandate to enforce all Americans’ civil rights diligently and fairly.”

Kristen Clarke, the NAACP’s general counsel and the former chief of the Civil Rights Division during the Biden administration, said Dhillon “abdicated her responsibility to enforce our nation’s federal civil rights laws and destroyed the crown jewel of the Justice Department.”

Clarke said Dhillon “abandoned cases, purged the work force and weaponized the Division to target institutions to achieve illegitimate, partisan goals,” and that the NAACP would demand that Dhillon’s replacement “respect the agency’s sacred mission, enforce the law fairly, and protect our civil rights.”

World.title: LIV Golf plans to shut down
World.content:
LIV Golf, the breakaway golf tour backed by Saudi royalty and some of the biggest names in the game, said Thursday it planned to wind down — a stunning conclusion to an effort that had received billions of dollars in backing.

In a statement, LIV said discussions with financial backer BC Partners had failed to produce an agreement to keep the league going.

“In light of the current circumstances, we believe shifting toward an orderly wind-down is the most responsible path forward for the League at this time,” LIV said in the statement.

Formed in 2021 by a group of golfers led by Phil Mickleson and Greg Norman who expressed dissatisfaction with the long-running PGA Tour, LIV attracted numerous bold-faced names including Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson with millions in guaranteed payouts.

Since 2022, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, the league’s primary backer, has invested more than $5 billion.

Greg Norman talks to Dustin Johnson during the LIV London Draft in 2022. Tristan Fewings / LIV Golf via Getty

Its creation set off a civil war of sorts in the game between LIV players and others committed to sticking with the PGA Tour, whose tournaments were seen as more competitive. By contrast, LIV’s events were accused of lacking drama because players’ payouts were guaranteed.

While LIV tournaments attracted healthy audiences overseas, they failed to land a long-term TV partner in the U.S., hampering their visibility and revenue streams.

An earlier hearing in New Jersey bankruptcy court indicated LIV planned to shut down operations as it sought relief from creditors. It was not immediately clear how much it owed.

The Financial Times reported earlier this week that LIV had sought a last-minute investment with a large private equity group, only to see the deal fall apart. Sports media outlet The Athletic reported the group, BC Partners, did not receive enough commitments from golfers interested in reviving the tour, which had seen multiple events canceled this year, including a team championship.
