World.title: Rando Kuustik: The perpetual saving of Estonian education
World.content:
Estonian education is a remarkably resilient phenomenon. No matter how many times it is reformed, it always manages to find itself in such poor shape ahead of the next election that it needs rescuing once again. And then along come the politicians with their solutions.

Some suggest reorganizing the school network, others promise to give teachers the recognition they deserve, while still others argue that money is being spent in the wrong places. Meetings with school principals are also essential because how else could politicians later claim to have listened to them? It all sounds promising. About as promising as it did during the last election.

I have worked in education for nearly 30 years, more than a dozen of them as a school principal. I have seen wise decisions and dedicated people, but also reforms that simply gave old problems new names. The trouble is that the power to make decisions and the obligation to take responsibility do not reside at the same address.

A politician can make a decision, an official can approve it and the next government can reverse it. But come Monday morning, the school principal still has to make sure there is a teacher in front of every class, every child has a place to learn and the school is running. You cannot hang a sign on the school door saying, "Classes are suspended until political accountability has been established."

Historic schools had courageous leaders

The history of Estonian education is also a story of people who dared to think beyond the immediate future. Jakob Westholm and Hugo Treffner, for example, had a vision of the kind of person a young student could grow into and the kind of school they would need.

We tend to label historic schools as elite schools and expect them to deliver excellent results, uphold traditions and offer innovative teaching. Preferably without spending too much money.

Jakob Westholm High School waited nearly 30 years for an extension. Governments and promises came and went, children grew up, but the need for more space remained. The school, operating across multiple locations, was expected to deliver ever-better results. In December 2025, construction finally got underway. That deserves recognition, but it does not erase the preceding decades.

Now we are once again hearing representatives of several political parties argue that too much education funding is being spent on concrete. Of course, every investment must be justified and an impressive building is no substitute for a good teacher. But nobody expects a surgeon to perform a world-class operation while insisting that what matters is the doctor, not the operating room.

"Some discussions have been substantive, while others have been half-hour meetings with everyone's eyes fixed on their phones and calendars."

Yet in education, we somehow manage to have an entirely serious debate about whether the environment needed for teaching is part of educational quality or merely an unnecessary luxury. The cost of construction is clearly visible in the budget, but the cost of failing to build, particularly over 30 years, is far harder to calculate.

Half an hour of listening followed by four years of silence

Through school leadership organizations, I have met with representatives of political parties. We have discussed teachers, the responsibilities of school principals and unnecessary restrictions. Some discussions have been substantive, while others have been half-hour meetings with everyone's eyes fixed on their phones and calendars. Then come the thanks, assurances that it was all very interesting and everyone goes their separate ways. The meeting took place and the box has been checked.

But what changed? Which proposal made it into a party platform or legislation? Which unnecessary obligation was eliminated? When were school principals told, "Your reasoning was better than ours, so we're changing our plan"? I have received fewer answers than invitations to further meetings.

Politicians do not always have to agree with us because school principals make mistakes too. But listening that has no potential to change anything is more of a courtesy ritual than genuine engagement. It is easy to prove that a meeting took place, but harder to show what was learned from it.

A school principal must be a strategist, a human resources manager, a crisis manager, sometimes a lawyer and a psychologist and solve by morning a problem that has been under review elsewhere for years. Responsibility is at the heart of leadership, but it only makes sense when you have the power to influence the outcome.

The public sector needs rules and oversight, but oversight must not become an end in itself. Sometimes it seems that the more we document something, the more convinced we become that it actually exists. Meanwhile, the problem at school may quietly persist.

We call teachers professionals and expect them to be creative, then ask them to demonstrate in ever-greater detail exactly how they exercise that creativity. No reporting form has ever sparked a child's curiosity. That takes a teacher who has the time and freedom to put their knowledge to use.

Who should manage education?

The school network needs to be reorganized because student numbers are declining in some areas, while others face a shortage of school places. Politicians should set the goals and provide the funding, while professionals must be allowed to develop the solutions. A wise politician must know how to consult those who understand the work and then do something with their answers.

"No reporting form has ever sparked a child's curiosity. That takes a teacher who has the time and freedom to put their knowledge to use."

The state, local governments and education professionals should agree on goals for the school network, teachers and learning environments that span an entire student's school years. Publicly established deadlines and clearly assigned responsibilities would prevent each new administration from starting from scratch.

School principals must be able to make decisions about staffing, work organization and budgets within agreed limits. In return, they should be evaluated on results, not the number of approvals they obtain. Every reform needs an impact assessment establishing who will do the work, with what funding and within what timeframe and which existing task will be eliminated. Finally, the results of stakeholder consultations should be made public, showing which proposals were accepted and why others were rejected.

Ahead of the 2027 Riigikogu elections, I would like political parties to answer a rather uncomfortable question, in addition to making their usual promises: What decision-making powers are you prepared to give up so that teachers can teach and school principals can lead?

Jakob Westholm and Hugo Treffner are not remembered for how obediently they followed regulations. They are remembered for the schools and opportunities they managed to create. They dared to make decisions and take responsibility for them. Why do we regard such courage as exemplary in historical school leaders, yet tend to restrict it today?

Politicians come and go. School principals remain. To shoulder the responsibility. But perhaps it is finally time to entrust them with the authority to lead as well.

World.title: Gallery: Holger Marjamaa performs with Take 6 in Tallinn
World.content:
Jazz pianist Holger Marjamaa's trio and acclaimed American vocal group Take 6 performed at Alexela Concert Hall on Wednesday, with saxophonists Aleksander Paal and Mairo Marjamaa joining as surprise guests.

Marjamaa and the 10-time Grammy-winning Take 6 have collaborated extensively in the United States in recent years, but the Tallinn concert marked their first joint performance in Europe.

The 33-year-old Marjamaa has spent years dividing his career between Europe and the United States. In 2023, he performed at Alexela Concert Hall with his trio and special guest Chad Lefkowitz-Brown.

Founded in 1980, Take 6 blends gospel, jazz, soul, R&B, and pop music. Over the years, the ensemble has released more than 10 studio albums and collaborated with artists including Whitney Houston, Stevie Wonder, and Ray Charles.

Marjamaa has performed in the United States and across Europe and Asia at venues and festivals including the Seoul Jazz Festival, Monterey Jazz Festival, Dallas Symphony, Atlanta Symphony Hall, Sony Hall, Lincoln Center's Dizzy's Club, Mezzrow Jazz Club, Smalls Jazz Club, Blue Note Tokyo, Blue Note New York (2019–2023), Blue Note Beijing, Blue Note Jazz Cruise, and Blue Note Shanghai.

He has released two solo albums and appeared as a guest musician on more than 30 recordings.

World.title: KBR to design gas capture project for Iraq’s West Qurna-1 oilfield
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – AKT Oil Services Company has given KBR a comprehensive engineering design contract for the West Qurna-1 Low-Pressure Gas Capture Project in Iraq.

KBR will deliver comprehensive multidisciplinary engineering design services for the Gas Compressor Station 6 located at the West Qurna-1 oilfield.

The contract was awarded by AKT Oil Services Company, which is managing the EPC project for Basrah Gas Company (BGC).

To reduce emissions and lessen reliance on energy imports, the project aims to capture low-pressure associated gas that is currently flared during production at the West Qurna-1 oilfield.

The gas captured from the oilfield, which has over 20 billion barrels of recoverable reserves, will be routed into the domestic energy chain.

By lowering dependency on gas and power imports, the project helps Iraq achieve energy self-sufficiency. Additionally, it fortifies KBR’s four-decade foothold in the infrastructure and energy sector of Iraq.

The development took place after Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister for Energy Affairs Mohsen al-Mandalawi and a delegation from US-based KBR discussed in late October the development of the country’s oil and gas sectors.

According to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), the meeting addressed prospects for joint cooperation in the oil, gas, and energy sectors, as well as leveraging the firm’s expertise to develop infrastructure and enhance the efficiency of strategic projects.

According to al-Mandalawi, the government aims to implement actionable programs for the Majnoon oilfield and the recovery of associated gas at the West Qurna-1 field, as well as initiatives for ammonia production and efforts to minimize gas flaring at oil fields.

World.title: Race for 2028 heats up after US midterms firestorm
World.content:
Washington – President Donald Trump’s stunning midterms defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election — the race to replace him in the White House in 2028.

The crushing defeat for the Republicans is particularly stinging for Vice President JD Vance, who had been the frontrunner but now risks being seen as tied to his lame-duck boss.

But the midterms are a potential launchpad for rising Democratic stars like Georgia senator Jon Ossoff, whose youthful vibe has already drawn comparisons to former president Barack Obama.

– Republicans in turmoil –

The MAGA coalition that shot Trump to power in 2016 and 2024 effectively collapsed in Tuesday’s midterms, leaving any presumptive Republican heir with a mountain to climb.

Long seen as the odds-on favorite for the Republican nomination in 2028, Vance is the most obvious victim after hitching his wagon to Trump throughout the midterms campaigns with rallies in swing states.

The ambitious 42-year-old quickly tried to distance himself from the electoral disaster, blaming it on Trump’s unpopular war on Iran in a long thesis posted on X on Wednesday.

But voters are likely to reject his attempts to disown Trump.

It’s a familiar problem for US vice presidents. Former Democratic candidate and vice president Kamala Harris suffered from a similar problem in 2024 when she said that “there’s not a thing that comes to mind” when asked how she’d differentiate herself from Joe Biden.

“The bad news for Vance is that sitting vice presidents seldom win the presidency,” James Lindsay of the Council for Foreign Relations, said.

Trump’s Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s name has also been bandied about.

Rubio, 55, has kept a far lower profile during the midterms but any top official in Trump’s administration will struggle to wash their hands of the Iran war.

The Republicans’ midterm disaster could, however, be a boost for other possible candidates.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, 48, who ran against Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024, has suddenly become very vocal.

He described the Democratic sweep as “the political equivalent of a meteor strike” — and pointed out that it was only in his own state that Republicans held them off.

Texas Senator Ted Cruz, 55, has also left the door open, having run against Trump in 2016 — although his chances may have been harmed by the Democrats’ stunning senate and governor wins in the midterms in his state.

– Democrats on a high –

The Democratic field is crowded but the midterms have given some likely candidates a boost.

Ossoff’s reelection as Georgia Senator has fueled speculation about a 2028 run by a telegenic politician who has already gained attention for mocking Trump’s relationship with a young staffer.

The 39-year-old has said that he has “zero interest in running for president” but his swiftly-declared win in Georgia — and his victory speech — have bolstered his status in the party.

Before the midterms Kamala Harris, 62, had been the favorite for the nomination, but there are many in the party who would prefer to have someone without a losing track record.

Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, 53, who was interviewed by Harris to be her running mate in 2024, had a good night on Tuesday as he stormed back to reelection in the key battleground state.

Outgoing California Governor Gavin Newsom, 59, is another big name who has repeatedly taken on Trump. He predicted in an interview with AFP in September Trump’s presidency “as we know it would be over after the midterms.

But Newsom, like Harris, may be seen as more of an old guard figure in a party that is looking to its rising stars.

A prominent but potentially divisive choice would be left-wing New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who said in September that she was weighing a run, musing about whether a Latina could win in a country that rejected female nominees in 2016 and 2024.

Other possible contenders include former Chicago mayor Rahm Emmanuel, JB Pritzker, the billionaire Illinois governor who set out a lengthy national agenda after winning a third term on Tuesday, Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear, and Arizona senator and former astronaut Mark Kelly.

World.title: Sixers roll on to down Pistons, Knicks gore Bulls
World.content:
Los Angeles – Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid combined for 56 points as the Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Detroit Pistons 112-106 in their heavyweight top-of-the-table NBA Eastern Conference clash on Wednesday.

Brown finished with 30 points and Embiid added 26 to give the Sixers another impressive road win that moved them to 8-1 at the top of the standings, with Detroit (6-2) in second.

Brown and Embiid led another balanced offensive performance from Philadelphia, who saw all five starters reach double figures.

LeBron James added a double-double with 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists while Tyrese Maxey drained three three-pointers on his way to a 19-point haul.

Brown, who arrived from the Boston Celtics in the offseason, said he was “still adjusting” to his new team-mates.

“I’m still figuring it out,” Brown said, before paying tribute to the performance of 41-year-old team-mate James.

“LeBron has been great,” Brown said. “To see what he’s doing at his age makes sense for LeBron James, but for nobody else would it make sense.”

The Sixers moved into the lead towards the end of the first quarter and kept their noses in front for the remainder of the game, stretching the lead to 18 points before a late rally from Detroit.

Duncan Robinson led the Pistons with 27 points while Cade Cunningham added 26.

The reigning champion New York Knicks scored their biggest win of the season with a 135-105 blowout over the Chicago Bulls at Madison Square Garden.

The Knicks, who have made a slow start to the new campaign, improved to 4-4 after a dazzling 33-point performance from Jalen Brunson, who drained five three-pointers while making 10-of-17 from the field.

O.G. Anunoby scored 18 points while Karl-Anthony Towns added 17 for a Knicks team who led by as many as 44 points midway through the third quarter.

In Boston, the Milwaukee Bucks threatened to pull off a huge comeback before finally succumbing 109-102 to the Celtics.

Paul George (25 points) and Derrick White (24) led the scoring for Boston, who appeared to be cruising after leading by 20 early in the third quarter.

But a 38-point third quarter from Milwaukee flipped the script and the Bucks edged into a 96-95 lead with five minutes remaining.

Boston regained control down the stretch with George and White closing out the win.

World.title: Gaza turns rubble into power with homemade wind turbines
World.content:
Khan Yunis – Above a maze of tents in a crowded displacement camp in Gaza, homemade wind turbines made from scrap metal and salvaged debris spin in the sea breeze, bringing electricity to struggling Palestinians.

In the southern Khan Yunis camp, Kamal Al-Dabary, a former engineering student, has put his skills to work for families who, like most Gazans, live in displacement with no direct access to the tiny territory’s shattered power grid.

According to the World Bank, more than 90 percent of Gaza’s power generation and distribution capacity was destroyed in April 2026, much of it in Israeli strikes that devastated homes and infrastructure.

Sitting on the ground, Dabary tinkered with electrical wires, metal parts and basic tools on a plastic table.

After carefully twisting cables together and testing them with a multimeter, a small bulb flickered on, then another, signalling that the current was flowing.

“When solar panels were still relatively affordable, we bought one and kept moving it around to follow the sun,” the 60-year-old, displaced by the fighting between Israel and Hamas, told AFP.

The war was triggered by the Palestinian Islamist movement’s deadly October 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

But after three years of war, prices have soared as aid and commercial supplies trickled into Gaza through crossings tightly controlled by Israel.

A single solar panel now costs at least 15,000 shekels (nearly $5,000), putting it out of reach for most Gazans, Dabary said.

– ‘Changed everything’ –

“We haven’t had work or income for three years,” he added.

“That’s when the idea of a wind turbine came to mind. Why not harness the wind? So we salvaged parts from the rubble.”

The turbines are built from scooter motors and old water tanks cut into blades.

As the wind turns the blades, they drive a motor that generates electricity. The power then passes through circuits assembled from parts recovered from destroyed homes before being stored in batteries.

This provides enough electricity to charge phones and run lights, fans and even electric razors, small comforts that have become a luxury for families still living in tents and shelters.

Nearly all of Gaza’s residents were displaced at least once during the war, and most now live in a small area still under Hamas rule, while Israel controls more than 60 percent of the territory along its perimeter.

“They help us hold on… until God delivers us from this ordeal and we can return home,” said Dabary, known locally as Abu Ayman.

The output remains modest. But in a camp where shortages are constant, every watt counts.

The system “has changed everything,” said 50-year-old Saleh ben Hasan.

With healthcare and medication hard to access in Gaza, the power can also help keep medical equipment running.

“If a child needs a nebuliser (a device used to inhale medicine) in the middle of the night, who else can we turn to?” he said.

“Electricity is needed… So we turn to our brother Abu Ayman.”

World.title: Tech hit by new AI worries on positive day for most markets
World.content:
Hong Kong – Tech firms tumbled Thursday as investors contemplated the outlook for the AI boom after Democrats swept the US midterms, partly on the back of growing anger over the rapid building of data centres across the country.

However, broader markets mostly rallied and oil plunged after Donald Trump’s Republicans were dealt a historic defeat that was blamed on high prices, tariffs and the Iran war.

The result stoked hopes he will look to wind down the Middle East conflict, which would help temper inflation, and even soften his stance on trade.

But AI-linked firms came under the cosh amid fears for planned data centre construction projects as well as renewed scrutiny from newly installed Democrats on Capitol Hill.

The sector had already been in the crosshairs of investors owing to questions about the vast sums pumped into new facilities, R&D and chip development, and when any companies would see a profit.

Charu Chanana at Saxo Markets said the vote was accelerating a reassessment of AI that was already under way.

“A Democratic Congress introduces another layer of uncertainty: regulatory scrutiny,” she wrote, adding that the three main risks were more oversight, data centre restrictions and capital spending uncertainty.

“The congressional scrutiny could accelerate demands for AI safety standards, independent model evaluations and greater accountability for data centre developers,” she added.

However, she also said: “This is not the same as an outright anti-AI policy agenda. AI is strategically important for US competitiveness, particularly against China, and there remains considerable bipartisan interest in maintaining American leadership.”

Chip firms were hammered in Asia, with South Korea’s SK hynix off more than seven percent and Samsung 5.5 percent down.

Tokyo-listed Kioxia and Advantest shed nine percent, Tokyo Electron more than seven percent and SoftBank five percent.

US Nasdaq futures fell more than one percent.

Broader markets performed better as investors rotated into other sectors including finance and manufacturing names.

Seoul, the poster child of the AI-led surge in the first half of the year, shed around four percent, while Taipei lost almost two percent. Tokyo also fell.

But there were healthy gains in Hong Kong and Shanghai, helped by hopes for an easing of trade tensions between the US and China, with tech titans including Alibaba, JD.com and Tencent.

Sydney, Singapore, Wellington and Manila also advanced.

Oil continued to fall after diving more than eight percent Wednesday on the US result amid optimism Trump will seek a deal to end the Iran war, which has been a key driver of the inflation spike that has hammered US consumers.

Hopes were given a boost when Vice President JD Vance said in a social media post that the Republican defeat was due to the unpopularity of the eight-month-old conflict.

The drop in crude prices — both main contracts are now below $100 for the first time since the start of October — has also tempered inflation worries and in turn Treasury yields, which dipped again Thursday.

The lower cost of borrowing has also been helped by the prospect that gridlock on Capitol Hill would lead to less spending.

That also weighed on the dollar, which held losses against its peers in Asian trade.

World.title: What the US midterms mean for ties with China
World.content:
Beijing – A sweeping victory for Democrats in US midterm elections this week, giving them control of Congress, presents both an opportunity and challenge for top rival China, analysts say.

Here is how the outcome of the vote, which offers the Democratic Party the power to stymie President Donald Trump’s maverick foreign policy, could impact the thorny relationship between Washington and Beijing:

– Will tariffs be limited? –

Winning control of both houses in the US Congress puts Democrats in a position to limit Trump’s liberal use of tariffs on Chinese products in the two years he has left in office, analysts say.

That could be a potential blow to Trump, who has wielded duties throughout a frenzied US-China trade war before the two sides reached a truce, set to expire in January.

If Democrats limit Trump, that means he “will be less able to leverage a tariff card in negotiations with China”, said Wu Xinbo, dean at the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai.

However, Democrats will also have to weigh their actions against the popularity of Trump’s tariffs among US businesses.

Congress will “take every opportunity to thwart (Trump’s policies) over the next two years”, said Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies at Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.

But Democrats will still have to tread carefully on further restricting tariffs that “are popular with unions, blue-collar workers and small businesses… who have historically been a base constituency for the Democrats”, Thompson said.

Congress will be “less inclined to support measures that would sharply escalate pressure on China if doing so risks raising costs for American consumers and businesses or increasing the likelihood of conflict”, said Patricia Kim, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington.

– Taiwan a ‘game changer’? –

The issue of Taiwan, the US-backed democratic island claimed by Beijing, could be a “game changer”, said Neil Shearing, group chief economist at Capital Economics.

Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer and has sold billions of dollars’ worth of arms to Taiwan that the island would use to fend off a potential Chinese attack.

But Trump threw the US stance into question in May when he declared that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip in talks with China. His administration has since delayed for months a $14-billion batch of weapons.

China could use the remaining two years of Trump’s presidency to increase pressure on Taiwan, particularly if Beijing “judges that Washington is distracted or that Trump would be willing to agree terms to not intervene”, Shearing wrote in a note.

Trump, who recently hailed his “great friendship” with China’s President Xi Jinping, has so far resisted political pressure from Democrats — and some Republican lawmakers — to greenlight the arms package.

But a Democrat-controlled Congress “may force Trump to resume arms sales to Taiwan next year”, Wu said.

“If that happens, that will also undermine the stability of US-China relationship.”

Alternatively, for China, renewed support of Taipei from the US Congress may be “a stronger incentive for (Beijing) to play it safer with Taiwan”, said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute.

Nevertheless, Thompson pointed out, while Congress can pass bills requiring Trump to approve an arms sale, the president retains the power to veto it “or simply ignore it”.

– Will Beijing treat Trump as a lame duck? –

From China’s perspective, even though Trump has been politically weakened by the midterms, Beijing is unlikely to change its strategy towards working with him, analysts say.

“Beijing is likely to continue cultivating him through high-profile, leader-to-leader engagement with Xi Jinping, viewing this as the least costly way to manage relations with Washington,” said Kim.

“Neither Beijing nor Washington appears to expect or seek a fundamental improvement in bilateral relations,” she added.

Tsang of the SOAS China Institute said “Trump being relegated to lame-duck status will be used by the Chinese to put more pressure on him”.

But, he added, Beijing is “calculating” and “would not want to push too hard and trigger Trump behaving totally irresponsibly”.

World.title: Arsenal edge stubborn Slavia in Champions League
World.content:
Prague – Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres scored in the first half to hand Arsenal a 2-1 win at Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Arsenal got back to winning ways in Europe after a 2-2 draw at Bayern last month, reaching 10 points from four Champions League games so far, while Slavia have a single point in the standings.

“We have to value the fact that it’s very difficult to win away from home. We’ve done it against a really tough opponent, as we expected,” said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

“Two very different halves. The first one where we played at a really high level in terms of tempo, intensity, quality and clarity in what we had to do,” he added.

The Premier League champions were quick to take control of the game in chilly conditions in the Czech capital.

Madueke reaped the rewards on nine minutes.

Gyokeres controlled David Raya’s long clearance with his chest and passed the ball instinctively to Madueke sprinting behind him down the right flank.

Madueke left the Slavia back four behind him with ease and beat diving Ukrainian teenager Nazar Domchak in the Slavia goal with a low shot.

Gyokeres, one of six changes in Mikel Arteta’s starting line-up from Sunday’s 1-0 win at Liverpool, made it 2-0 on 38 minutes.

He beat Domchak with a neat shot off the far post after a one-two with Mikel Merino on the edge of the Slavia box.

– ‘Far from our standards’ –

Czech champions Slavia were sluggish throughout the first half, producing a single chance when skipper Tomas Holes fired wide from inside the box.

But they stepped up their pace considerably in the second half to stave off a repeat of a 3-0 home loss to the Gunners in the competition exactly a year ago.

Slavia’s Polish midfielder Oskar Kubiak forced a diving save from Raya seconds into the second half.

Gabriel Magalhaes and Raya cleared two headers off the goalline in quick succession with 15 minutes to go, while David Zima fired over the bar.

Raya then forced a Kubiak header onto the post.

Slavia scored a consolation goal in the 90th minute when David Jurasek’s cross bounced through the Arsenal defence and Wiktor Nowak blasted the ball into the net from close range.

“(We) scored two goals. It should have been three, four or five. We didn’t make that gap,” said Arteta.

“Right from the beginning, we were extremely far from our standards and everything that we have to do… in everything that we discussed to avoid the game that we played in the second half.”

It was the 23rd straight game without a win for the hosts in the Champions League, taking them within one of equalling AEK Athens’ all-time record from 1992-2006.

World.title: Haaland breaks City out of mini-rut at Leipzig
World.content:
Leipzig – Erling Haaland’s 78th-minute strike helped Manchester City shake off a mini-slump with a 3-2 Champions League win at RB Leipzig on Wednesday.

After an excellent start to the season, City had lost two Premier League games in a row either side of beating Brighton on penalties in the League Cup.

The visitors twice went ahead — through a Castello Lukeba own goal and an Enzo Fernandez header — only to be pegged back by goals from Ridle Baku and Antonio Nusa.

Despite having scored more against Leipzig than any other opponents in his career, Haaland had few chances but was right on the spot to turn in an Elliot Anderson cross for the winner.

“For me I think it’s easy. It’s around 100 minutes a game to just stay fully focused,” Haaland told reporters.

“In this period it was about trying to wait for the right moment and attack it in the right way and put it in the back of the net and that’s exactly what I did.”

Haaland has now scored 13 times in nine matches against Leipzig, including a memorable five-goal performance in a 7-0 rout in March 2023.

Despite the victory, City were well below their usual best against a Leipzig side in a rebuilding process under new coach Martin Demichelis.

City coach Enzo Maresca, who arrived in the summer, conceded his side were still a “work in progress” but praised Haaland.

“It’s important that he’s on his game. We know that at any moment he can help us, he can score goals,” Maresca said.

Maresca backed under-fire goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, who was out of position for Baku’s equaliser.

“It’s not a concern… We are talking about a mistake. A few minutes before he made a save that no keeper in the world could make.”

Nusa’s performance was a highlight for the hosts, with Haaland’s Norway teammate now on six goals and seven assists in 14 matches this season as Leipzig look to replace Yan Diomande, who left for Real Madrid in the summer.

“It’s a pity, to be honest,” Nusa told TNT Sports. “I feel like we deserved more today and you end up with zero points. It’s not a good feeling.”

– City’s mini-slide –

City travelled to Germany having lost two Premier League games in a row for the first time since August 2025.

Leipzig had won just one from three in the Champions League before Wednesday but had been excellent at home, winning five from five while scoring 19 goals without conceding once.

Haaland was handed the captain’s armband for the first time this season but it was another Norwegian, Leipzig’s Nusa, who impressed early.

Nusa forced Donnarumma to tip a shot over the crossbar with 14 minutes gone.

Leipzig looked more comfortable but then conceded in embarrassing fashion with 37 minutes gone when Lukeba bungled a Nico O’Reilly cut-back into his own goal.

Christoph Baumgartner forced an excellent save from Donnarumma just after the break but Leipzig were soon level when Baku threaded a low shot in from an acute angle with the Italian out of position off his line.

Haaland’s first dangerous moment came shortly after Baku’s equaliser, when he forced a close-range save from Maarten Vandevoordt.

Fernandez had City back in front just before the hour mark when he headed in a lovely Iliman Ndiaye cross, but Leipzig restored parity just three minutes later.

Christopher Nkunku linked up with Nusa just four minutes after coming off the bench, allowing the Norwegian to cut a low shot across the face of goal and in.

When Anderson broke down the right flank with 12 minutes left, Haaland immediately adjusted his run towards the far post, where he waited to tap in the England midfielder’s pinpoint cross.

World.title: Kashmir has 1 active local terrorist, says IG
World.content:
Valley recruitment stopped this year: Police chief

SRINAGAR: Kashmir has just one active local terrorist and recruitment in the valley completely stopped this year, while security forces were tracking a handful of foreign terrorists believed to be assisting him, J&K police IG Sujit Kumar said Thursday.

Police identified the lone local terrorist as Mohammad Lateef Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chader village in south Kashmirâs Kulgam district. A Rs 15 lakh reward was announced in Aug for information leading to his arrest. Bhat is accused of killing a head constable and two migrant workers in separate attacks in Anantnag and Kulgam in July. He is believed to have joined terrorist ranks last year.

âNo local has joined terrorist ranks this year. Local recruitment has completely dried up,â Kumar said.



He added that the number of foreign terrorists could not be established as they kept moving between locations. âGiving their figure would be an exaggeration,â he said.

Head constable Ashiq Hussainâs murder on July 22 was the first terrorist attack in Kashmir since the massacre of 25 tourists and a local pony operator in Pahalgam on April 22 last year.

On narcoterrorism, Kumar said police registered 1,651 NDPS cases this year, arrested 1,941 people, seized 1,711 kg of contraband and over Rs 1 crore in cash. Properties worth Rs 154 crore were attached and 567 bank accounts frozen.

World.title: Up to 10-fold statutory costs, month-long delays: Report flags hurdles in used vehicle transfers
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Vehicle ownership transfers can cost up to 10 times the statutory fees, with total expenses, including agent charges, in the range of Rs 13,000-14,000 in parts of Bihar, Rs 7,000-8,000 in Tamil Nadu and Rs 5,000-8,000 in Uttar Pradesh, according to the Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index 2026 released by a consumer rights advocacy organisation and a startup industry body.

The report, prepared by Consumer Voice and IndiaTech on the basis of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, transport policies of 15 states and interviews with automobile dealers, RTO agents and vehicle owners, has exposed the sharp gap between reforms initiated by the Centre and ground realities in states in terms of their actual implementation.

The report found that the all-inclusive cost of an RC transfer, including agent charges, is the lowest in Kerala (Rs 500-2,400), followed by Karnataka (Rs 2,000-2,500), Andhra Pradesh (Rs 3,000-3,500) and Delhi (Rs 3,000-3,600).



The time taken to complete a transfer also varies widely â as little as a week in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana but more than a month in Uttar Pradesh.

The study assessed ownership transfer procedures across 15 states accounting for more than 85% of Indiaâs organised pre-owned car market. It found Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Delhi to be top performers in ease of vehicle ownership while Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal were placed at the bottom of the list.





The report highlighted how unofficial expenses, procedural inefficiencies and dependence on intermediaries continue to inflate the cost of transferring vehicle ownership. Nearly 100% of respondents surveyed said they had relied on agents to complete the transfer process. âReducing these hidden transaction costs will be critical for improving accessibility, accelerating market formalisation and enhancing the overall ease of vehicle ownership,â it said.

None of the states figured in the âhigh easeâ or excellent category, with Andhra Pradesh, the top-ranked state, scoring only 5.9 on a scale of 0-10. Kerala scored 5.7, followed by Tamil Nadu and Delhi at 4.6 each. Rajasthan (4) and Haryana (3.9) were also in the lower half of the rankings, while West Bengal (2.6), Bihar (2.5) and Uttar Pradesh (2.5) brought up the rear.

The report comes at a time when Indiaâs pre-owned vehicle market is expanding rapidly and projected to grow from $36.4 billion in 2025 to over $73.5 billion by 2030.

The market has already overtaken new vehicle sales in volume. However, fragmented state-level rules, incomplete digitisation and cumbersome procedures continue to impede seamless vehicle ownership transfers.

It also found that 39% of respondents had reported delays in receiving their registration certificates after completing vehicle transfers, while 61.5% were unaware of the requirement of party peshi until they reached the RTO. As many as 63% could not accurately estimate the total cost of completing an ownership transfer, reflecting widespread opacity in transaction charges.

World.title: Temporary move: No slots next summer for 12 int’l carriers at CSMIA; can operate from Navi Mumbai
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) has allocated slots to 38 of the 50 international airlines for summer 2027 schedule to operate to and from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA).

Twelve airlines have not been given CSMIA slots next summer. These 12 collectively operate about 16 daily flights to 14 international destinations. Sources say they can operate the affected services from Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA).

This destination-based slot allocation is expected to leave about 91% of CSMIAâs existing traffic capacity unaffected, say sources, while adding that this is temporary arrangement to facilitate the redevelopment of Mumbai Airportâs old terminal 1.



âAirlinesâ historical slot allocations will be respected and left undisturbed during this temporary transition,â they add.

Indian carriers â IndiGo, Air India and Akasa â have already announced plans to shift flights serving 14 destinations to NMIA. âThe transition is expected to facilitate movement of about 50 lakh passengers annually from CSMIA to NMIA, creating the capacity required for the phased redevelopment of T1.





The new terminal will increase T1âs annual passenger handling capacity from the existing 1.5 crore passengers per annum (CPA) to 2 CPA.

Construction is scheduled to begin early next year, with the facility targeted to be operational by March 2029. The four-level extension will add four domestic bus boarding gates, along with expanded passenger processing, security screening and crew facilities,â sources say.

Its demolition is scheduled to begin in April 2027 and the terminal will be redeveloped in phases.

They called for upholding democratic values and protecting constitutional institutions, the ABVP said in a statement.Over 15,000 students and elected representatives participated in the gathering, held under the slogan "Stop Anarchy, Embrace Democracy", as a response to "disruptive and anarchic forces" allegedly trying to weaken constitutional institutions and undermine social harmony in the country, according to the ABVP.ABVP national general secretary Virendra Singh Solanki said governments in India are formed and changed through people's votes, not through street pressure or anarchy.He said criticism of the government and political dissent are integral to democracy, but alleged that attempts are being made to create distrust in electoral processes and constitutional institutions for political gain.Solanki questioned Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and the Opposition over their election-related allegations, saying such claims should be substantiated before the appropriate constitutional authorities.Referring to political developments in Bangladesh and Nepal, he said they could not serve as models for India's democratic future. He also raised questions over women's representation within the Congress, saying women's empowerment should translate into meaningful decision-making roles.ABVP Delhi state secretary Sarthak Sharma said the gathering reflected young people's faith in democracy and that student representatives had a responsibility to strengthen healthy political discourse and democratic traditions on university campuses.DUSU president Yash Dabas said elected student representatives had a responsibility to strengthen democratic dialogue and that disagreement and dissent should not lead to attempts to weaken constitutional institutions.The rally was part of ABVP's nationwide campaign against what it described as political anarchy and attempts to undermine democratic institutions. World.title: Cabinet approves Rs 14,500 crore VGF scheme for energy storage
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a Rs 14,500 crore viability gap funding (VGF) scheme to develop 92 gigawatt-hour (GWh) of grid-scale energy storage capacity by FY31 to facilitate integration of large-scale renewable energy generation.

Power ministry officials said the scheme will support the creation of additional storage capacity equivalent to 170% of the existing 54 GWh available in India. Govt has estimated the countryâs energy storage requirement at 411 GWh by 2031-32.

Under the proposed scheme, 60 GWh of pumped storage plants (PSP), 30 GWh of battery energy storage systems (BESS) and another 2 GWh of emerging storage technologies will be developed, involving a total estimated investment of Rs 97,600 crore.



The ministry said the scheme will strengthen Indiaâs power sector infrastructure by facilitating large-scale integration of renewable energy and ensuring reliable, affordable and round-the-clock power supply. âIt will also provide an impetus to domestic manufacturing of battery energy storage systems, reduce import dependence and enhance the countryâs long-term energy security,â the power ministry said in a statement.





The VGF support will improve the financial viability of projects and accelerate the deployment of large-scale storage infrastructure.

The capacity will be allocated through a tariff-based competitive bidding process, with both public and private sector electricity distribution companies eligible for VGF support.

The 40% domestic content requirement will help boost Indian manufacturing. A stable, clean grid powered by Made-in-India solutions is what we are working towards,â Kaushal said.

World.title: Oversight layer intact, says EC official after poll panel tweaks work order for IT chief Seema Khanna
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday said there is no change in the supervisory authority to which its director general of information technology Seema Khanna reports.

The clarification came a day after the panel issued a fresh work allocation placing Khanna under the charge of deputy election commissioner Prakash Raj Purohit instead of senior deputy EC Manish Garg.

A controversy had erupted after Garg issued an order on July 28 asking Khanna to report directly to the Election Commission, comprising Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Vivek Joshi and SS Sandhu.



Garg had issued the order after deputy EC Sanjay Kumar, to whom Khanna had been reporting, was transferred to the Delhi government. The change effectively removed an intermediary layer of oversight, allowing Khanna to report directly to the Election Commission.

ECs Sandhu and Joshi objected to the order and subsequently wrote separate letters to cabinet secretary TV Somanathan, raising concerns over the distribution of responsibilities.





The order was then put in abeyance. The EC also told the Supreme Court that the July 28 work allocation order was never implemented.

Asked whether Khanna had reported directly to the Commission between July 28 and November 4, without an added layer of a reporting boss in the form of a deputy EC, an election official on Thursday said: "Since the order was not implemented, Khanna was supervised by Garg after Sanjay Kumar moved out of the EC.

Now, she will report to Raj Purohit, who joined as deputy EC a few days ago."

Garg was the "link officer" for Kumar, which meant that Kumar's assigned tasks were transferred to Garg after he left the Election Commission.

Why was Seema Khanna's role under scrutiny?

Khanna's role had come under scrutiny amid concerns over the functioning of the electoral roll software and the exercise of powers by Electoral Registration Officers (EROs).

According to a report by The Indian Express, the two Election Commissioners were concerned that field-level officers, who are legally responsible for preparing electoral rolls, were unable to perform certain functions because the software did not permit them to do so.

The permissions required to carry out these functions were reportedly controlled by the EC's IT division, headed by Khanna.

The commissioners repeatedly raised concerns that powers legally vested in EROs were being increasingly centralised through the EC's IT system, potentially restricting the authority of officers responsible for preparing and revising electoral rolls.

World.title: Bodies of five fishermen from Tamil Nadu found near Kothapatnam beach in Andhra Pradesh
World.content:
The bodies of three fishermen from Tamil Nadu washed ashore at Kothapatnam coast in Ongole on Thursday while the bodies of two more fishermen were found later in the sea by the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) officials at Nizampatnam Port.

Using a Dornier aircraft, the ICG staff in coordination with the personnel of the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC), Chennai, launched a search and rescue (SAR) operation to find five more fishermen, who were sailing on the same boat that sank 2 km off the shore.

According to sources, three boats set out from Tamil Nadu for fishing On October 29, 2026. Owing to the impact of Cyclone Murasu, two boats were anchored for safety near Ramayapatnam Port on November 2 (Monday), while the third boat proceeded towards Nizampatnam Port.

The nine fishermen on the third boat departed from Nizampatnam to meet the other two teams in Ramayapatnam on November 3 (Tuesday). Due to a storm at sea and intense winds, their boat drifted towards the coast of Adani Krishnapatnam Port and capsized.

The nine were identified as Pakkirisamu Suriya (driver), Kuppan, Mohan, Rajesh, Murugan, Kuppusamy, Vijayakanth, Aravindh and Narayanan. While Narayanan was from Cuddalore, the remaining all were from Chennai.

Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu, who was in Kothapatnam to inspect the voting process for the local body elections, visited the place where the bodies of the fishermen washed ashore. ‘’The identification of the bodies will take place after the family members and officials from Tamil Nadu arrive,’’ he added.

“Further action regarding the transport of the bodies and bringing the capsized boat to the shore will be taken in consultation with the officials from Tamil Nadu,’’ the Collector said.

Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, along with the deceased fishermen's family members, reached the mortuary of RIMS Hospital in Ongole for the identification of the bodies.

Andhra Pradesh Fisheries Commissioner Rama Shankar Naik and District Collector P. Raja Babu accompanied the Tamil Naidu Minister. The family members identified four bodies. He said the bodies would be taken to Tamil Nadu after police investigation and post-mortem examination.

"I extend my gratitude to the Andhra Pradesh government for its cooperation. We hope to recover the remaining bodies soon," Mr. Wilson said.

Families’ plea

Families of the fishermen who are still missing have urged the State government to take steps on a war footing to find them.

Bharatheeswaran, son of Pakkiri, said his father had spoken to his mother on the evening of November 2.

“It seems the boat had developed a problem on November 3. We heard that the engine did not work, and water entered it. They had sought the help of nearby boats, and when one of them reached the location after three hours, the boat in distress was missing,” he said.

Chennai Mechanised Boat Owners’ Welfare Association president M.E. Raghupathi said that from the gathered information, the assumption was that the boat had been anchored at a bay in Kavali, where the cyclone made landfall. “Nobody can swim in the sea in such a situation. A team of Fisheries Department officials and fishermen have gone to Ongole GH. We have also called for divers from Thoothukudi, who will bring underwater cameras, to search for the boat.”

Community leader M.D. Dayalan said: “The boat should not have been allowed to leave the fishing harbour. Many boats do not have safety equipment. The department does not conduct surprise checks on boats to see if GPS equipment, life jackets, and equipment to signal distress are working. The government must take steps to search for the men, since if the body is not retrieved, the family will have to wait for seven years before getting the settlement,” he said.

Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Thursday announced a solatium of ₹7 lakh each to the families of the fishermen whose bodies had washed ashore, and directed that ₹2 lakh each be disbursed immediately. He also ordered arrangements be made to transport the bodies to Tamil Nadu at the government’s expense and hand them over to the families.

(With inputs from Deepa H. Ramakrishnan and R. Srikanth in Chennai)
